description: On January 1, 1970, Israel again attacks the East Ghor Canal to pressure Jordan to prevent Palestinian attacks in Israel from Jordanian territory.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Schmidt 1970

title: Ku Klux Klan poisons livestock water supply owned by black Muslim group in Alabama, US
description: Members of the Ku Klux Klan poison the water supply used for livestock on a farm owned by black Muslims in Ashville, Alabama. 30 cows are killed and at least nine others are sickened.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Neo-Nazis drop bombs in Maryland sewage plant
description: A group of teenagers associated with a neo-Nazi group attempt to spark racial conflict by dropping bombs into a sewage pumping station in Maryland, USA, an event they hope will be blamed on African Americans. Damage is caused to the pumping station.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Baltimore Sun 1970 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 197010020004

title: Pipeline bombed during a labor dispute in California
description: During a labor dispute, a pipeline carrying brine to the American Potash Plant in Trona, CA, is bombed, causing destruction of the pipeline and temporarily disrupting the town water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Committee on Government Operations United States Senate (CGOUSS) 1970 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Respon

title: Violent conflicts over use of China's Zhang River
description: Conflicts over excessive water withdrawals and subsequent water shortages from China's Zhang River have been worsening for over three decades between villages in Shenxian and Linzhou counties. In the 1970s, militias from competing villages fight over withdrawals. (See also entries for 1976, 1991, 1992, and 1999.)
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; China Water Resources Daily 2002

title: Water-cooling unit is bombed at a Louisiana country club
description: A water cooling unit is bombed at a country club in Louisiana, USA. Suspects are thought to be black nationalists seeking revenge. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Committee on Government Operations United States Senate (CGOUSS) 1970 ; New York Times, The 1970 ; Washington Post 1970 ; National

title: Britain expels Soviet agents reportedly planning to poison London's water supply
description: Britain expels 105 Soviet agents in 1971 after learning that plans existed for those agents to sabotage or disrupt London's water supply system by poisoning.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Douthit 1987 ; Harvey and Keatley 2014

title: Attempt to poison Chicago's waters
description: Two members of the right-wing "Order of the Rising Sun" are arrested in Chicago with 30-40 kg of typhoid cultures with which they allegedly planned to poison the water supply in Chicago, St. Louis, and other cities. Experts say the plan is unlikely to cause health problems due to water chlorination.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Eitzen and Takafuji 1997

title: India-Bangladesh Joint Rivers Commission
description: Indian PM Indira Gandhi and Bangladeshi leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman sign the Indo-Bangladesh Treaty of Friendship, establishing a Joint Rivers Commission (JRC) to cooperate on water sharing, flood control, irrigation, and cyclone management.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Statute of the Indo-Bangladesh Joint Rivers Commission (1972).

title: New York water threatened
description: Reported threat to contaminate water supply of New York City with nerve gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Purver 1995

title: OMVS Senegal River Basin Organization Founded
description: Senegal, Mali, and Mauritania establish the Organisation pour la mise en valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS), an innovative joint authority that treats the river as shared property, enabling development of Manantali and Diama dams.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Convention relative au statut du fleuve Sénégal (1972); OMVS Secretariat.

title: US bombs water works in Vietnam
description: United States bombs dikes in the Red River delta, rivers, and canals during massive bombing campaign.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Columbia Encyclopedia 2000a

title: German water supply threatened
description: A German biologist threatens to contaminate water supplies with bacilli of anthrax and botulinum toxin unless he is paid $8.5 million.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Jenkins and Rubin 1978 ; Kupperman and Trent 1979

title: Helmand River Treaty: Afghanistan-Iran
description: Afghanistan and Iran sign the Helmand River Water Treaty, allocating Iran 22 cubic meters per second (about 820 MCM/yr) from the Helmand. The treaty is never fully ratified or implemented, causing persistent disputes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Faizee, M. & Schmeier, S. (2023). Troubled Waters between Afghanistan and Iran; Treaty on the Helmand River (1973).

title: Inter-American Water Rights: US-Mexico Colorado River Salinity
description: Decades of US irrigation drainage return highly saline water to the Colorado River, devastating Mexican farms in the Mexicali Valley. The US and Mexico negotiate Minute 242 to the 1944 Treaty, committing the US to deliver Colorado River water at no more than 115 ppm salinity above Mexican levels.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; IBWC Minute No. 242: Permanent and Definitive Solution to the International Problem of the Salinity of the Colorado River (1973).

title: India-Bangladesh Farakka Barrage Declaration
description: India and Bangladesh issue a joint declaration to resolve the water-sharing dispute over the Farakka Barrage before its commencement of operations. A 1975 interim agreement follows, allowing India to operate feeder canals for short test periods.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Joint Declaration of the Prime Ministers of India and Bangladesh on Farakka Barrage Testing, New Delhi (1974).

title: Iraq threatens Syria dam
description: Iraq threatens to bomb the Euphrates dam (also known as al-Thawra or Tabqa dam) in Syria and masses troops along the border, alleging that the dam had reduced the flow of Euphrates River water to Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1994

title: Multiple attacks on water infrastructure in Puerto Rico
description: Striking workers are thought to be the cause of multiple attacks on various water infrastructure run by the Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewers Authority, a government-owned water agency. One attack destroys water pipes connected to two major refineries, while another leaves a large portion of the City of San Juan without running water for an entire day. The attacks are attributed to a group known as the Armed Forces for National Liberation, however no direct link has been made proving their connection.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New York Times, The 1974 ; Hewitt 2005 ; Sater 1981 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (ST

title: Iraq, Syria mobilize troops over drought tensions
description: As upstream dams are filled during a low-flow year on the Euphrates, Iraqis claim that flow reaching its territory is "intolerable" and asks the Arab League to intervene. Syrians claim they are receiving less than half the river's normal flow and pull out of an Arab League technical committee formed to mediate the conflict. In May Syria closes its airspace to Iraqi flights and both Syrian and Iraq reportedly transfer troops to their mutual border. Saudi Arabia successfully mediates the conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993 ; Gleick 1994 ; Wolf 1997

title: Locks and control devices on a Department of Water and Power control gate on a river in California are sabotaged in May 1975
description: Locks and control devices on a Department of Water and Power control gate on the Owens River, near Bishop, California are sabotaged during a dispute over groundwater pumping.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Walton 1992

title: Powerline insulators to Department of Water and Power water pumps on a river in California are shot out in September 1975
description: Insulators on a power line to the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power water pumps on the Owens River, California are shot out in an ongoing dispute over groundwater pumping by the city of Los Angeles.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Walton 1992

title: South Africa takes over Angolan dam
description: South African troops move into Angola to occupy and defend the Ruacana hydropower complex, including the Gove Dam on the Kunene River. Goal is to take possession of and defend the water resources of southwestern Africa and Namibia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Meissner 2000

title: Bacteriological agent used to poison groundwater and surface water in Mozambique
description: An unidentified bacteriological agent is found in groundwater and surface water sources in Mozambique. Sources report that the Rhodesian government had deposited the agent to target the black population in the country.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Gates diverting water to the Los Angeles Aqueduct from the Owens Valley are dynamited
description: Gates diverting water to the Los Angeles Aqueduct from the Owens Valley are dynamited, leading to 100 million gallons of water flows returning to Owens Lake.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sahagun 2013

title: Los Angeles, California, USA aqueduct gates are opened by a blow torch to fill Diaz Lake for recreational use
description: Los Angeles aqueduct gates are opened by unknown persons using a blow torch in order to fill Diaz Lake for recreational use.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Walton 1992

title: Militia chief shot in China's Zhang River conflict
description: A local militia chief is shot to death in a clash over the damming of Zhang River. Conflicts over excessive water withdrawals and subsequent water shortages from China's Zhang River have been worsening for over three decades. (See also entries for 1970, 1991, 1992, 1999.)
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; China Water Resources Daily 2002

title: Rhine Salt Pollution Treaty
description: Five Rhine riparian states (Germany, France, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Switzerland) sign the Convention on the Protection of the Rhine against Chloride Pollution, requiring France to reduce salt discharges from Alsace potash mines into the Rhine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Convention for the Protection of the Rhine Against Pollution by Chlorides, Bonn (1976); ICPR.

title: Explosions damage water system at British military base
description: Four separate explosions occur at several British military bases, one damaging the water system at Akrotiri (Santorini), an airbase near Limassol, in southern Cyprus, Greece.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Kariba dam on the Zambezi river is site of battle between Rhodesian and Zambian forces
description: Rhodesian and Zambian forces fight a 10?hour battle across the Zambezi River and a power station at the Kariba dam is attacked.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New York Times 1977

title: North Carolina reservoir poisoned
description: Contamination of a North Carolina reservoir with unknown materials. According to Clark: "Safety caps and valves were removed, and poison chemicals were sent into the reservoir....Water had to be brought in."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Clark 1980 ; Purver 1995

title: A water tank is poisoned in protest of airport construction in Japan
description: A water tank at a water purification plant is contaminated with oil and agricultural chemicals. The attack on the water supplies is in protest of the construction of an airport in Hokusol/Narita, Japan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Bombing of water plant in Puerto Rico cuts off water for 30,000
description: Puerto Rican nationalists are suspected in the bombing of a substation owned by Water Resource Authority. This incident leaves approximately 30,000 people in San Juan without electricity. This bombing is linked to a larger group of violent attacks on the state-owned Water Resources Authority.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sater 1981 ; Hewitt 2005 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 197801190007

title: Deaths of protestors and damage to construction of the Jonglei canal in Sudan
description: Demonstrations in Juba, Sudan in 1978 opposing the construction of the Jonglei Canal lead to the deaths of two students. In 1984, construction of the canal is suspended following a series of attacks on the construction site.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Suliman 1998 ; Keluel-Jang 1997

title: Machine gun used to attack the U.S. Embassy with goal of reducing cost of water and other necessary resources
description: The Popular Liberation Forces (PLF) uses a machine gun to attack the U.S. Embassy in El Salvador. This attack was stated by PLF to be part of their war against U.S. imperialism. Demands included the reduction in the cost of water, as well the cost of housing, fertilizer, rents, agricultural land, and electric power, as well as for the release of a number of prisoners assumed to be held for political reasons.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Devine 1981 ; RDWTI 2018

title: While battling insurgents, the Ethiopian military destroys basic civilian water wells and water sources
description: During the so-called "Secret Wars" in southeast Ethiopia, water wells are destroyed and poisoned by Ethiopian troops in an attempt to halt insurgents. The Ethiopian military is thought to have been advised in applying these tactics by Soviet and Cuban officials.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Human Rights Watch 2008

title: Equipment providing power to Los Angeles Department of Water and Power pumps on a river in California, USA is damaged
description: Electrical insulators are shot and damaged at a Southern California Edison site providing power to Los Angeles Department of Water and Power water pumps on the Owens River, California.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Walton 1992

title: Several different facilities owned by the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power are burned down, USA
description: A shack and platform at the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power well between Big Pine and Independence is burned down along with a house, barns, and shop at DWR land in Lone Pine, California.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Walton 1992

title: Attempted extortion of a casino in Lake Tahoe, Nevada, USA with threat to poison water
description: Attempted extortion of a casino in Lake Tahoe, Nevada with threat to poison water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness 2009

title: Government troops demolish water catchments in Somalia
description: Between 1980 and 1982, as part of President Barre's "scorched earth" policy in Somalia, government troops demolish water-points and berkads (catchments) in many of the towns and villages of Mudug and neighboring Nugal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Puntland Development Research Centre (PDRC) 2014

title: Military encounters between Cameroon and Niger over the recession of Lake Chad
description: Starting in the 1980s, rapid recession of Lake Chad draws Nigerian fishermen farther into Cameroonian territory, leading to several military encounters. By the 1990s, more than thirty Lake Chad villages founded by Nigerians are counted in Cameroon. In 2002, the border dispute goes to the International Court of Justice, which rules in Cameroon's favor.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Dimon 2012

title: Mozambique targets Cahora Bassa Dam in fight for independence
description: Regular destruction of power lines from Cahora Bassa Dam during fight for independence in the region. Dam targeted by RENAMO (the Mozambican National Resistance).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Chenje 2001

title: Niger Basin Authority Created
description: Ten Niger riparian states transform the River Niger Commission into the Niger Basin Authority (NBA) at Faranah, Guinea, with a broader mandate covering energy, water, agriculture, transport, and industry coordination.
countries: Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Chad
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Convention creating the Niger Basin Authority, Faranah (1980).

title: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, US water mains are deliberately contaminated with weed killer
description: Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States water mains are deliberately contaminated with weed killer.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness 2009

title: Soviet forces in Afghanistan destroy crops, irrigation sysems, and wells
description: In July 1980 Soviet forces destroyed dozens of villages south of Kabul during a two-week operation that included destruction of crops, irrigation systems, livestock, and wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Westermann 1999

title: ZACPLAN Zambezi River System Action Plan
description: Eight southern African states initiate the ZACPLAN process under UNEP to manage Zambezi River resources collectively, representing the first multilateral framework for the basin and laying groundwork for the eventual ZAMCOM agreement.
countries: Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNEP / SADC (1987). Agreement on the Action Plan for the Environmentally Sound Management of the Common Zambezi River System (ZACPLAN).

title: A Thai citizen dies from poison placed in drinking water by Vietnamese troops near the Kampuchean border
description: In March 1981, a Thai citizen dies from poison placed in drinking water by Vietnamese troops near the Kampuchean border; others are sickened.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Anderson and Van Atta 1984

title: Iran targets Iraq hydroelectric dam
description: Iran claims to have bombed a hydroelectric facility in Kurdistan, thereby blacking out large portions of Iraq, during the Iran-Iraq War.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993

title: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power in California, USA has equipment destroyed by arson
description: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power equipment, a frontloader, is destroyed by arson.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Walton 1992

title: Namibia targets Angola pipeline
description: Water infrastructure, including dams and the major Kunene-Cuvelai pipeline, is targeted during the conflicts in Namibia and Angola in the 1980s.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Turton 2005

title: Thai soldiers capture two Vietnamese trying to poison the water supply in a Kampuchean relocation camp in Thailand
description: In June 1981, Thai soldiers capture two Vietnamese trying to poison the water supply in a Kampuchean relocation camp in Thailand.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Anderson and Van Atta 1984

title: Bomb attack launched on Severn Trent Water Authority in protest over water taken from Welsh reservoirs
description: A bombing at the Birmingham headquarters of the Severn Trent Water Authority is claimed by the Workers Army of the Welsh Republic, as part of a demand the water agency pay more for water taken from Welsh reservoirs.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lockley 2022

title: Guatemalan forces more than 400 indigenous community members resisting forced migration from a new dam
description: In Rio Negro, Guatemala, between February 1982 and 1983, approximately 440 Maya Achi indigenous people, including hundreds of women and children, are killed by the Guatemalan Army and Civil Self-Defense Patrols in an effort to remove the community from an area slated to be flooded by the Chixoy dam. There are reports that the victims were tourtured and raped, as well. These killing became known as the Rio Negro massacres and efforts to bring justice to the survivors or investigate the perpatrators have been largely unsuccesful.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Levy 2000 ; Comisión para el Esclarecimiento Histórico 1999 ; Wikipedia contributors 2025c

title: Israel cuts off Beirut water
description: Israel cuts off the water supply of Beirut during siege.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Wolf 1997

title: Plan to poison Los Angeles water supply
description: Los Angeles police and the FBI arrest a man who was preparing to poison the city's water supply with a biological agent.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Livingston 1982 ; Eitzen and Takafuji 1997

title: An attempt was made to poison the water supply in Louisiana, United States with cyanide
description: An attempt was made to poison the water supply in Louisiana, United States with cyanide.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness 2009

title: Terrorists destroy US military barracks in Lebanon
description: An explosives-laden truck disguised as a water-delivery vehicle destroys a barracks in a US military compound, killing more than 300 people. The attack is blamed on Hezbollah with the support of the Iranian government.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2007

title: Terrorists plot to poison Israel water
description: The Israeli government reports that it had uncovered a plot by Israeli Arabs to poison the water in Galilee with "an unidentified powder."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Douglass and Livingstone 1987

title: A Los Angeles Department of Water and Power boat explodes under suspicious circumstances in California, USA
description: A Los Angeles Department of Water and Power boat on Mono Lake explodes under suspicious circumstances in continued violence over water diversions from the Owens Valley.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Walton 1992

title: Destruction of construction equipment at Atatürk Dam
description: During construction of the Atatürk Dam, the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) destroys construction equipment and nearly 1,100 vehicles, severely delaying the project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Glass 2017

title: Oregon water supply poisoned
description: Members of the Rajneesh religious cult contaminate a city water supply tank in The Dalles, Oregon, using Salmonella. A community outbreak of over 750 cases occurred in a county that normally reports fewer than five cases per year.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Clark and Deininger 2000

title: Water truck bombed in front of U.S. Embassy in Amman, Jordan
description: A water truck is destroyed when a bomb placed underneath it explodes. The truck was outside the U.S. Embassy in Amman, Jordan. Two people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; US Secretary of State 1986

title: Anonymous note threatens to contaminate New York City reservoirs
description: An anonymous letter writer threatens to contaminate New York City's water reservoirs with plutonium unless charges against a man accused of vigilantism for shooting four African American men in the New York subway are dropped. Testing detects minute levels of plutonium in the water but scientists cannot determine whether the threat to contaminate the New York City water supply was actually carried out or whether the sample was contaminated prior to receipt.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Johnston 2014 ; Bogen et al 1988

title: Cult plans to poison US waters
description: Law enforcement authorities discover that a small survivalist group in the Ozark Mountains of Arkansas known as The Covenant, the Sword, and the Arm of the Lord (CSA) acquired a drum containing 30 gallons of potassium cyanide, with the apparent intent to poison water supplies in New York, Chicago, and Washington, D.C. CSA members believe that such attacks would make the Messiah return more quickly by punishing unrepentant sinners. The objective appears to be mass murder in the name of a divine mission rather than to change government policy. The amount of poison possessed by the group is believed to have been insufficient to contaminate the water supply of even one city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Tucker 2000 ; Nuclear Threat Initiative (NTI) 2005

title: A plan to blow up the Atatürk Dam in Turkey is thwarted
description: Turkish police discover Syrian-backed terrorists designing a plan to blow up the Atatürk Dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Glass 2017

title: Lesotho coup supported by South Africa, partly to advance water agreement
description: South Africa supports a bloodless coup by Lesotho's defense forces. Immediately afterward, the two countries agree to share water from the Highlands of Lesotho, following 30 years of unsuccessful negotiations. There is disagreement over the degree to which water was a motivating factor for either party.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Inventory of Conflict and the Environment 2000b ; Mohamed 2001

title: South Koreans uneasy over threat posed by North Korean dam plan
description: North Korea's announcement of its plans to build the Kumgansan hydroelectric dam on a tributary of the Han River upstream of Seoul raises concerns in South Korea that the dam could be used as a tool for ecological destruction or war.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993

title: 19 police recruits in the Philippines die from poisoned water and candy from an unknown source
description: Nineteen Filipino police recruits die after drinking and eating water and candy from an unknown person.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; CBC News Online 2004

title: At least 12 police die in the Philippines after drinking poisoned water during a running race
description: At least 12 and up to 19 runners die after drinking poisoned bottled water during a race. The runners were members of the Philippine Constabulary.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Lack of water from drought contributes to onset of the Arab-Fur War.
description: The Arab-Fur War (1987-1989) between the Arab and Fur ethnic groups in Libya, is triggered in part by severe drought that strains farmer-herder relationships. Libyan leader Gaddafi sends drought relief supplies and weaponry to opposing sides.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bromwich 2018

title: Turkey-Syria Euphrates Water-PKK Agreement
description: Turkey and Syria broker a political agreement linking water policy to security: Turkey commits to releasing at least 500 m³/s of Euphrates water to Syria, while Syria agrees to stop supporting PKK Kurdish militants operating from Syrian territory.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Protocol on Matters Pertaining to Economic Cooperation Between Turkey and Syria, Damascus (1987).

title: A water tank is bombed in Pakistan, injuring 15
description: A bomb placed under a water tank explodes, injuring 15 people in Peshawar, Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Cubans attack the Calueque Dam in Angola, occupied by South African forces, during the Angolan civil war
description: Cuban and Angolan forces launch an attack on Calueque Dam, occupied by South African forces, via land and then air. Considerable damage inflicted on dam wall; the power supply from the dam is cut. Water pipeline to Ovamboland is cut and destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Meissner 2000

title: A bomb is discovered near a water pumping station in Israel
description: A large amount of dynamite is discovered near a water pumping station near Moshav Ramon, Israel prior to detonation. The detonation would have likely caused flooding and damage to agricultural land.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Alleged attempt to infect the water supply to a refugee camp with biological agents in Namibia
description: The Civilian Cooperation Bureau, a covert South African unit, is accused of an attempt to infect the water supply of a refugee camp in Dabora, Namibia, with cholera and yellow fever. The attempt is thought to fail due to the high chlorine content in the water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Water and other ecological threats used as justification for attack on cattle company
description: A fire is set in a cattle company building outside of Sacramento, California, causing hundreds of thousands of dollars in damage. An unidentified caller claiming to be part of Earth First! states he set the fire "because we are opposed to the livestock industry because it causes irreparable damage to the environment by putting chemicals in food and water and destroying natural habitat for wildlife."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; United Press International (UPI) 1989

title: Attacks on energy systems in Iraq leaves cities without water
description: During the Gulf War, targeted attacks on transformers and turbines at water-treatment plants leave whole cities, such as Basra, without water or wastewater treatment. And due to embargoes, parts needed to fix the plants are not available. It is estimated that at least 25 percent of water-treatment plants in Iraq do not have backup power supplies and are inoperable after electrical grids are damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Human Rights Watch 1991

title: Flows of water from Turkey's Atatürk Dam are threatened and used as a weapon of war
description: The flow of the Euphrates is interrupted for a month as Turkey finishes construction of the Atatürk Dam, part of the Grand Anatolia Project. Syria and Iraq protest that Turkey now has a weapon of war. In mid-1990 Turkish president Turgut Özal threatens to restrict water flow to Syria to force it to withdraw support for Kurdish rebels operating in southern Turkey.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993 ; Gleick 1995

title: Police report nine people are sickened by the intentional contamination of the water supply of a private apartment building in S
description: At least nine people in an apartment building in Edinburgh, Scotland report coming down with a diarrheal disease caused by Giardia lamblia. Investigators of the incident believe that the water supply to the apartment had been deliberately contaminated with fecal matter containing Giardia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: South Africa cuts off black community's water
description: Pro-apartheid council cuts off water to the Wesselton township of 50,000 blacks following protests over miserable sanitation and living conditions.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993

title: Violence over water competition kills 300 along Uzbekistan border
description: The Fergana Valley, shared by Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan, is especially vulnerable to violent eruptions over water and ethnicity. In 1990 an outbreak of violence in the Kyrgyz town of Osh on the border with Uzbekistan claims over 300 lives. The violence is provoked by competition for water, limited arable land, and ethnic tensions.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Khamidov 2001

title: 18 killed in Bengaluru, India after court order telling Karnataka to release water to Tamil Nadu on the Cauvery River
description: At least 18 people are killed in Bengaluru, India after a court order telling Karnataka to release water from the Cauvery River to Tamil Nadu sparked riots.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2023

title: British Columbia water supply threatened
description: A threat is made via an anonymous letter to contaminate the water supply of the city of Kelowna, British Columbia, with "biological contaminates." The motive is apparently "associated with the Gulf War." The security of the water supply is increased in response and no group is identified as the perpetrator.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Purver 1995

title: Chinese villages exchange mortar fire over water diversion
description: In December 1991, Huanglongkou village and Qianyu village exchange mortar fire over the construction of new water diversion facilities. Conflicts over excessive water withdrawals and subsequent water shortages from China's Zhang River have been worsening for over three decades. (See also entries for 1970, 1976, 1992, and 1999.)
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; China Water Resources Daily 2002

title: During Persian Gulf War, allied forces attack and destroy urban water and sanitation facilities in Basra, Iraq
description: During the Persian Gulf War, Allied forces target water and sanitation facilities in Iraq's second-largest city, Basra.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Vulliamy 1991 ; Middle East Watch (MEW) 1991a ; Middle East Watch (MEW) 1991b

title: Iraq destroys Kuwait desalination plants
description: During the Gulf War, Iraq destroys much of Kuwait's desalination capacity during retreat.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993

title: UN considers cutting river flow to Iraq
description: Discussions are held at the United Nations about using the Atatürk Dam in Turkey to cut off flows of the Euphrates to Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993

title: US destroys Iraq water systems during the 1991 Persian Gulf War
description: During the Persian Gulf War, Allied Coalition forces damage Baghdad's modern water supply and sanitation system "intentionally and unintentionally." Four of seven major pumping stations were destroyed, as were 31 municipal water and sewerage facilities in Baghdad "resulting in sewage pouring into the Tigris. Water purification plants were incapacitated throughout Iraq" (Arbuthnot 2000). Following the damage, the New England Journal of Medicine reports that, during the first eight months of 1991, childhood death in Iraq increases by 47,000 and the country's infant mortality rate doubles to 92.7 per 1,000 live births.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993 ; Arbuthnot 2000 ; Barrett 2003

title: US sanctions against Iraq target water systems
description: United States deliberately pursues policies that prevent repair and operation of Iraq's water systems through sanctions and withholding contracts.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nagy 2001

title: Violence erupts between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over use of India's Cauvery River
description: Violence erupts when Karnataka, India rejects an Interim Order handed down by the Kaveri Waters Tribunal, set up by the Indian Supreme Court. The Tribunal was established in 1990 to settle two decades of dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over irrigation rights to the Kaveri River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993 ; Butts 1997 ; Inventory of Conflict and the Environment (ICE) 2000a

title: Aral Sea Interstate Commission for Water Coordination
description: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan establish the Interstate Commission for Water Coordination of Central Asia (ICWC) to jointly manage Amu Darya and Syr Darya resources, responding to the Aral Sea crisis.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agreement on Cooperation in the Management, Utilization and Protection of Interstate Water Resources, Almaty (1992).

title: Canal on China's Zhang River bombed
description: In August 1992, bombs are set off along a Zhang River distribution canal collapsing part of the canal and causing flooding and economic losses in a continuation of three decades of violence with confrontations, mortar attacks, and bombings. Conflicts over excessive water withdrawals and subsequent water shortages from China's Zhang River have been worsening. (See also entries for 1970, 1976, 1991, and 1999.)
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; China Water Resources Daily 2002 ; Pietz 2015

title: Hungary and Czechoslovakia dispute over Danube
description: Hungary abrogates a 1977 treaty with Czechoslovakia concerning construction of the Gabčíkovo-Nagymaros project based on environmental concerns. Slovakia continues construction unilaterally, completes the dam, and diverts the Danube into a canal inside the Slovakian republic. Massive public protest and movement of military to the border ensue; issue taken to the International Court of Justice.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993

title: Russians attack Moldovan hydroelectric dam
description: In June, hostilities between Moldova and Russia in a short but intense conflict include a rocket-artillery attack on the hydroelectric turbines at the Dubasari power station on the Nistru (or Dniester) River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Malik 2005 ; Belitser et al 2009

title: Serbs cut off water and power to Bosnian cities
description: The Serbian siege of Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, includes a cutoff of all electrical power and the water feeding the city from the surrounding mountains. The lack of power cuts the two main pumping stations inside the city despite pledges from Serbian nationalist leaders to United Nations officials that they would not use their control of Sarajevo's utilities as a weapon. Bosnian Serbs take control of water valves regulating flow from wells that provide more than 80 percent of water to Sarajevo; reduced water flow to city is used to "smoke out" Bosnians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Burns 1992 ; Husarska 1995

title: Violent raids target water infrastructure between Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan
description: The Tyuyamuyun reservoir in the delta of the Amu Darya is a point of contention between Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. Violence occurs in 1992 over the re-direction of drainage waters and raids by both sides to cut off pipes and irrigation canals. Today, the Tyuyamuyun remains one of several disputed areas in continuing water dispute with Uzbekistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Votrin 2003

title: Water is used as a weapon in the dispute between Armenia and Azerbaijan
description: In a dispute over the Karabakh region, Armenia takes control of the Sarsang Reservoir in 1992. Subsequently, Azerbaijan claims Armenia is releasing water from Sarsang Reservoir to damage Azerbaijan territories with artificial floods and cutting off water for agricultural irrigation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ahmadi et al. 2023

title: Water supply to a Turkish air force base is poisoned
description: Potassium cyanide is discovered in lethal quantities in the water supply of a Turkish air force base. No one is poisoned prior to the discovery. The attack is attributed to the Kurdish Workers' Party.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Chelyshev 1992 ; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: A major dam on the Cetina River, Yugoslavia is attacked in the Croatian War
description: The 65-meter high Peru?a Dam on the Cetina River was Yugoslavia's second-largest hydroelectric facility before the country's breakup with the Croatian War beginning in 1991. On January 28, 1993, Serbian/Yugoslav army forces detonate explosives at the dam in an attempt to wipe out Croatian villages and the port city of Omi'. A successful Croatian counter-attack allows military engineers to reach the dam and release water on time to prevent it from bursting, saving an estimated twenty- to thirty-thousand civilians. Credit for preventing a dam burst is also given to British Marine Captain Mark Gray, a UN Observer, for opening gates to reduce water levels prior to the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993 ; Rathfelder 2007

title: Indonesian security forces kill four villagers protesting the construction of Nipah Dam, Madura Island, Indonesia
description: Indonesian security forces fire on villagers protesting the construction of Nipah Dam in Sampang Regency, in Madura Island of Indonesia's East Java province, September 25, 1993, killing four.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Tani and Ningsih 2024

title: Iran threatens West's water
description: A report suggests that proposals were made at a meeting of fundamentalist groups in Tehran, under the auspices of the Iranian Foreign Ministry, to poison water supplies of major cities in the West "as a possible response to Western offensives against Islamic organizations and states."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Haeri 1993

title: Iraq uses water to silence opposition
description: To quell opposition to his government, Saddam Hussein reportedly poisons and drains the water supplies of southern Shiite Muslims, the Marsh Arabs, or Ma'dan. The marshes of southern Iraq are intentionally targeted. The European Parliament and UN Human Rights Commission deplore use of water as weapon in region.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick 1993 ; National Geographic News 2001

title: Violence occurs over land use of a water catchment area in Kenya
description: In October 1993, violence erupts in the Narok district of Kenya's Rift Valley province. Maasai warriors attack immigrant Kikuyu settlers and massacre at least 17 of them, after Kikuyi settlers allegedly mutilated Maasai cattle. 16 more Kikuyus are killed in other parts of Narok and the rest of the Kikuyu population is forced out of the area and into refugee camps. Environmental concerns played a central role: a few months previously, the Narok County Council had declared Enosupukia, the site of the conflict, to be a water catchment area and decreed that all inhabitants, mostly transplanted Kikuyus, had to leave.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Cerami 2013

title: Aral Sea Central Asia Budget Pledge
description: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan, and Kyrgyzstan sign an agreement pledging 1% of their national budgets to fund Aral Sea restoration efforts, an unprecedented regional environmental commitment.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nukus Declaration of the Central Asian States on Aral Sea Basin Program (1994).

title: Israel-Jordan Peace Treaty Water Provisions
description: The Wadi Araba Peace Treaty between Israel and Jordan includes water-sharing provisions allocating Jordan 50 MCM/yr from the Sea of Galilee and assigning Jordan 75% of the Yarmouk River waters, representing the first formal water-sharing agreement between the two states.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Treaty of Peace Between the State of Israel and the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan (1994), Annex II (Water Related Matters); Gleick, P.H. (1994).

title: Moldova threatens Russian army's water
description: Reported threat by Moldovian General Nikolay Matveyev to contaminate the water supply of the Russian 14th Army in Tiraspol, Moldova with mercury.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Purver 1995

title: Rhine Action Programme Achieves Salmon Return
description: The Rhine Action Programme (RAP), launched by riparian states in 1987 following the Sandoz disaster, achieves its landmark goal of restoring salmon to the Rhine after decades of absence. The programme is considered one of the most successful international river restoration initiatives.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Commission for the Protection of the Rhine (ICPR) Salmon 2000 Report (1994).

title: Rhine Convention for Protection Enters Force
description: The Convention for the Protection of the Rhine (Bern Convention) is upgraded and the 1994 Rhine Action Programme agreed, building on the 1986 Sandoz disaster response to achieve river ecosystem restoration targets.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Convention on the Collection, Deposit and Reception of Waste Produced during Navigation on the Rhine and Inland Waterways, Rotterdam (1994).

title: Ecuador, Peru fight over Cenepa River
description: Armed skirmishes arise between Ecuador and Peru in part because of a border disagreement over the control of the headwaters of Cenepa River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Samson and Charrier 1997 ; Wolf 1997

title: Mekong River Commission Agreement
description: Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, and Vietnam sign the Agreement on Cooperation for the Sustainable Development of the Mekong River Basin in Chiang Rai, establishing the Mekong River Commission with principles of reasonable and equitable use of waters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agreement on the Cooperation for the Sustainable Development of the Mekong River Basin, Chiang Rai (1995).

title: Oslo II Accords West Bank Water Provisions
description: The Oslo II Interim Agreement between Israel and the PLO includes detailed provisions on Palestinian water rights in the West Bank, granting Palestine an additional 28.6 MCM/year and establishing a Joint Water Committee, but maintaining Israeli predominance over water allocation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Israeli-Palestinian Interim Agreement on the West Bank and the Gaza Strip (Oslo II, 1995), Annex III, Article 40 (Water and Sewage); Gleick, P.H. (1994).

title: India-Bangladesh Ganges Water Sharing Treaty
description: Indian PM H.D. Deve Gowda and Bangladeshi PM Sheikh Hasina sign a 30-year Ganges Water Sharing Treaty in New Delhi, the first comprehensive agreement establishing a formula to share dry-season flows at Farakka and recognizing Bangladesh's downstream rights.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Treaty Between the Government of the Republic of India and the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh on Sharing of the Ganga/Ganges Waters at Farakka (1996).

title: Orma and Degoodi clans wage war over scarce resources in Kenya
description: The Orma and Degoodi clans in Kenya wage war over grazing land and water due to a severe drought, with 10 fatalities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Salehyan et al 2014

title: Abkhazia cuts energy supplies to Georgia from the Inguri dam
description: Energy supplies to Georgia from the Inguri hydroelectric plant are cut by Abkhazia (a disputed republic at the intersection of Eastern Europe and Western Asia) in retaliation for Georgia rerouting telephone lines from Abkhazia through Georgia. The dam and power plant are situated at the shared border with the breakaway Republic of Abkhazia. Negotiations between Georgia authorities and Abkhazia also focus on demands that Georgia reimburse damage caused by an explosion at a substation on November 11 caused by Georgian saboteurs.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNCHR 1997

title: Bangladesh Nationalist Party strikes spark violence; demand to scrap Ganges River water-sharing treaty with India
description: General strikes called by Bangladesh's main opposition party, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), lead to sporadic violence with several injured on both sides, barricaded roads and rail tracks, damage to railway facilities, and stones thrown at trains. Among the key concerns are recent decisions concerning India, including an agreement on a landmark 30-year water-sharing treaty on the Ganges River that the BNP fears will help India impose "hegemony" in region. The BNP wants the water treaty scrapped.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kochanek 1998

title: Clash between police and students protesting the lack of water on campus in Nigeria, injuring three
description: Three students are seriously wounded in a clash with police at the University of Ibadan in Nigeria. Police are preventing students from protesting the lack of water and electricity on campus.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5286570

title: Malaysia threatens to cut Singapore's water
description: Malaysia supplies about half of Singapore's water and in 1997 threatened to cut off that supply in retribution for criticisms by Singapore of policy in Malaysia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Zachary 1997

title: Protest against water prices in Mauritania
description: The Mauritania government breaks up protests of water and electricity prices.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5014583, 5014584

title: Protests against plans to privatize water and sanitation services in South Africa
description: Congress of South African Trade Unions, South African Municipal Workers Union and the South African Communist Party marched on the Nelspruit council to protest against plans to privatize water and sanitation services.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5569692

title: Uzbekistan cuts downstream flow to Kazakhstan, prompting a riot by farmers
description: Uzbekistan raises regional tensions by cutting off 70 percent of flow downstream, threatening 100,000 hectares and prompting a riot by Kazakh farmers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hogan 2000a

title: Uzbekistani deploy troops to guard reservoirs along border with Kyrgyzstan
description: Continued serious water tensions between Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan lead to the deployment of 130,000 Uzbekistani troops on the Kyrgyz border to guard reservoirs straddling the two countries. Uzbekistan accuses Kyrgyzstan of releasing too much water from the Toktogul reservoir. Kyrgyzstan, through media leak, hints that in case the reservoir would be blown up, the resulting flood would sweep away Uzbekistan's Ferghana and Zeravshan Valleys.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Votrin 2003

title: Waterworks are sabotaged by armed groups in Mozambique
description: In Mozambique, unidentified armed groups sabotage waterworks and burn houses of civilians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5014627

title: Angolan rebels, government fight at dam
description: In September 1998, fierce fighting between UNITA and Angolan government forces broke out at Gove Dam on the Kunene River for control of the installation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Meissner 2001

title: Attack on water system in Algeria
description: A bomb placed by a group suspected to be affiliated with an extremist Islamic insurgency detonates near the Sidi Khaled water tower, Algeria, damaging a two-meter section of pipe. Four other similar attacks occur in Hassi R'mel, Ouled, Tolba, and Arzew.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; A.B. 1998 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 199802200004 ; RAND Databa

title: Attacks on water supplies during the Kosovo War leave tens of thousands without water
description: During the Kosovo War, several attacks over the course of two days in early 1998 leave tens of thousands of Albanians without water. The first attack on February 21, 1998 destroys a main waterline for the town of Kukës, Albania and 15 other villages. The second attack happens on February 22, 18 km away at Kolesjan village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; UN Environment Programme and UN Center for Human Settlements 1999

title: Clashes between rival tribes over water in Darfur, Sudan
description: Clashes between rival tribes (Rezaigat and Massalit) over water and grazing rights leave more than 100 people dead and about 45 villages gutted in West Darfur, Sudan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5328198

title: Congo rebels attack dam
description: Attacks on Inga Dam during efforts to topple President Kabila. Disruption of electricity supplies from Inga Dam and water supplies to Kinshasa, Congo.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Chenje 2001 ; Human Rights Watch 1998

title: Danube River Protection Convention Enters Force
description: The Convention on Cooperation for the Protection and Sustainable Use of the Danube River enters into force, establishing the International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River (ICPDR) involving 14 states and the EU.
countries: Germany, Austria, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, Ukraine
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Convention on Cooperation for the Protection and Sustainable Use of the Danube River (Sofia, 1994, entered into force 1998); ICPDR.

title: Four people are hospitalized after drinking poisoned water in Guinea
description: Four people are hospitalized after drinking water poisoned with acid and sold at the 28 September Stadium in Guinea, where the President held a final campaign rally.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5270449

title: Guerillas threaten Tajikistan dam
description: Tajik guerrilla commander Makhmud Khudoberdyev threatens to blow up a dam on the Kairakum channel if his political demands are not met.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; World Rivers Review (WRR) 1998

title: Major Puerto Rican aqueduct project is attacked
description: A group called the Boricua Popular Army (Macheteros) claims responsibility for the bombing of a major aqueduct construction project in Puerto Rico, stating the attack is the initiation of an effort to defend Puerto Rico's natural resources from the government. The explosion causes significant damage to the project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; US Department of Justice 1998 ; Associated Press (AP) 1999a ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terr

title: Members of a white supremacist group, The New Order, are arrested in Illinois with plans to poison water supplies with cyanide
description: A white supremacist group called The New Order plans to poison water supplies with cyanide, rob banks, and conduct murders and bombings in New York and Montgomery, Alabama. Members are arrested in sothern Illinois.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Los Angeles Times 1998

title: Militant attacks on water supplies leave one dead and many villages in the Abkhazia region of Georgia without water
description: Over the course of a few days, militant groups in the Abkhazia region of Georgia attack and damage numerous water-supply structures, leaving at least twelve villages without water. In addition, one person who is thought to be responsible for the placement of an explosive device on a water tower is killed when the device detonates.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Oil pipeline dynamited in Colombia, contaminating drinking water source for 200 families
description: The Caño Limón – Coveñas oil pipeline owned by Colombia Petroleum Enterprise is dynamited, causing oil to spill into the La Gritane stream, which supplies drinking water to approximately 200 families in rural Colombia .
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: South African military attack the Katse and Mohale dam sites in Lesotho during political instability there
description: On September 22, 1998, South African National Defense Forces attempt to secure the Katse and Mohale dam sites in the Lesotho highlands during a military intervention over the disputed 1998 elections and subsequent political instability. South Africa is heavily dependent on water and power from the Lesotho Highlands Water Project. Acting South African State President described the three objectives of the intervention as "to secure the Dam, restore order in the security establishment, and clear protestors from the Royal Palace." Many deaths and injuries were reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Likoti 2007

title: The Taliban Pashtun kill Hazaras in Afghanistan, throwing bodies down wells to poison the water supply
description: In 1998, Taliban Pashtun troops capture the Afghanistan city of Mazar-e-Sharif. Investigators say thousands of Hazaras are killed and hundreds of bodies are thrown down water wells to poison the water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; News and Jensen 2001

title: War between Eritrea and Ethiopia includes destruction of water systems
description: During the war with Ethiopia in 1998, water-supply systems in the mountainous region of Debub and Gash Barka in Eritrea are destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) 2009

title: Water line attack leaves 11 communities without water in the Negev area of Israel
description: Eleven communities in the Negev area of Israel are left without water after a main water line is attacked by an unknown group.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water pipeline connecting a marshland with an oil facility attacked in Colombia
description: A water pipeline that delivers water from San Silvestre marshland to the Ecopetrol Industrial Complex is attacked. The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) is presumed responsible.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water plants destroyed in Ethiopia-Eritrea war
description: Water pumping plants and pipelines in the border town of Adi Kuala are destroyed during the civil war between Eritrea and Ethiopia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) 2003

title: Water supply to Kukes, Albania and surrounding villages is shut off after an unnamed chemical agent is discovered
description: A chemical agent is discovered in the main waterline supplying the city of Kukes, Albania. The water supply is shut-off, impacting Kukes and the surrounding villages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Wells contaminated during Kosovo war
description: Contamination of water supplies/wells by Serbs disposing of bodies of Kosovar Albanians in local wells. Other reports of Yugoslav federal forces poisoning wells with carcasses and hazardous materials.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Schwartz 1999 ; Hickman 1999

title: Yemeni pipeline destroyed in attempt to pressure government to build water and power systems
description: Yemeni tribesmen, thought to be from the Jahm tribe, attack and destroy a pipeline in the Marib province in order to pressure the national government to build water distribution systems and power plants in their region.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: 100 bodies found in Angolan wells
description: One hundred bodies are found in four drinking water wells in central Angola.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Herald Tribune 1999

title: African nations fight over Zambezi island and access to water
description: Namibia and Botswana engage in a territorial dispute over Sedudu Island, or Kasikili Island, in the Zambezi River, or Chobe River, related to the location of the border and access to water. The International Court of Justice rules in favor of Botswana in 1999.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Court of Justice 1999

title: Bomb discovered at South African reservoir
description: A home-made bomb is discovered at a water reservoir at Wallmansthal near Pretoria. It is thought to have been meant to sabotage water supplies to farmers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Pretoria Dispatch Online 1999

title: Bomb explodes on Cavallo off the coast of Corsica, cutting off water supply
description: A bomb explodes on the island of Cavallo, off the coast of Corsica, causing a disruption to the local water supply. The attack was likely by the National Liberation Front of Corsica (FLNC), which seeks independence from France.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Chinese farmers fight over water
description: Around the Chinese New Year, farmers from Hebei and Henan Provinces fight over limited water resources. Heavy weapons, including mortars and bombs, are used and nearly 100 villagers are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; China Water Resources Daily 2002

title: Chinese man killed for speaking out against displacement of communities by the Three Gorges Dam
description: In March 1999, Lei Weidong is killed for his opposition to the Three Gorges Dam in China. Before his death, Mr. Weidong traveled to Beijing to protest the dam that would displace hundreds of thousands of people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Clashes between two villages in Mauritania over the control of a water hole
description: Clashes break out between the village of Djigueni and Missira in Mauritania over the control of a water hole for cattle. Clashes over water rights are common during the dry season.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5005903

title: Fighting breaks out over the use of a watering hole in Mali and two deaths are reported
description: Malian herdsmen in Missira-Samoura refuse to allow a horseman from Mauritania to use a watering hole. The Mauritanian horseman rides off and returns to the village with other men. Fighting breaks out and results in two people being killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5281066

title: Indonesian militia dump bodies in wells in East Timor
description: Militia opposing East Timor independence kills pro-independence supporters and throws bodies in water well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 1999

title: Injuries at protest in Bangladesh
description: Fifty people are hurt during strikes called to protest power and water shortages. Protests are led by former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia over decrease in public services and deterioration of law and order.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ahmed 1999

title: Lethal clashes between Malian herders and Mauritania clans over access to a watering hole
description: Thirteen people died in communal clashes in June 1999 along the border between Mauritania and Mali. Conflict started when herdsmen in Missira-Samoura village in west Mali refused to allow a Mauritania horseman to use a watering hole. The horseman returned with some of his clansmen, attacking the village on June 20, causing 13 deaths.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Edie Newsroom 1999

title: Major water pipeline in Zambia is bombed, cutting supplies to three million people
description: A water pipeline is bombed along the Great North Road in Lusaka, Zambia, cutting off water three million people. A total of sixteen bombs are reported to have exploded throughout the city of Lusaka, with damage targeted at water pipes, power lines, and the Angolan Embassy. At least one person is killed and two are injured. No one claims responsibility for the bombs, however, it is speculated that the attackers were seeking to discredit the Zambian government by causing chaos.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 1999 ; Associated Press (AP) 1999b ; Mulenga 1999 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and R

title: Multiple attacks on French utilities, including water, in one day
description: Reports find at least three attacks on utilities in the Hérault area of France, including one that damaged a water-supply pipeline.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: NATO strikes water facilities in Yugoslavia
description: NATO targets utilities and shuts down water supplies in Belgrade. NATO bombs bridges on Danube, disrupting navigation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 1999a

title: NATO targets dam in Kosovo
description: Belgrade reports that NATO planes had targeted a hydroelectric plant during the Kosovo campaign.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sadler and Clancy 1999

title: NATO targets water plants
description: Water processing plants are targeted, among other structures, in an air attack on Yugoslavia during the Kosovo War.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Wikipedia 2018

title: Nile Basin Initiative Established
description: Nine of ten Nile riparian states establish the Nile Basin Initiative (NBI) with World Bank backing, creating the first basin-wide institutional framework to promote cooperative development and management of Nile water resources.
countries: Ethiopia, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, DRC, Sudan, Egypt
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nile Basin Initiative Strategic Action Program; Dar es Salaam (1999).

title: Petrochemical and fertilizer factors attacked by NATO, leading to contamination of the Danube River
description: NATO attacks petrochemical and fertilizer factories in Pancevo, Serbia, claiming they are "dual use," producing chemicals and parts for both military and civilian uses. The attack leads to the extensive release of ammonia, ethylene dichloride, and other chemicals into the Danube River and contaminates the city's water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Schmetzer 1999

title: Puerto Ricans protest US Navy's water use
description: Protesters blocked water intake to Roosevelt Roads Navy Base in opposition to US military presence and Navy's use of the Blanco River, following chronic water shortages in neighboring towns.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New York Times, The 1999

title: Serbs cut off water to Pristina
description: Serbian engineers shut down water system in Pristina prior to occupation by NATO.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 1999b

title: Tajikistan releases water from Kairakum reservoir to cut water for cotton farmers in Kazakhstan; Kyrgyzstan cuts water to Kazakh
description: In summer 1999, Tajikistan releases 700 million cubic meters of water from the Kairakum reservoir without warning its downstream neighbors. Among other effects, this cuts water to cotton crops in southern Kazakhstan, causing significant losses to farmers. At the same time, Kyrgyzstan cuts flows to southern Kazakhstan in retaliation for Kazakhstan's failure to supply coal under barter agreements.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hogan 2000b

title: Taliban in Afhanistan cuts off vital water supply to Iran
description: During a 1999 drought, Taliban authorities cut off the flow of the Helmand River between Afghanistan and Sistan-Baluchestan, Iran, which relies on the Helmand as its only source of irrigation. The Iranian government allegedly responds by entering Afghanistan and building a series of diversion canals to restore flows. A 1973 water agreement between the two countries is never ratified and both Iran and Afghanistan have reported violations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Karimi and Hulpachova 2015

title: Villagers killed in Yemen water clash
description: Yemen sends 700 soldiers to quell fighting that claims six lives and injured 60 others in clashes between two villages fighting over a local spring near Taiz. The village of Al-Marzuh believes it is entitled to exclusive use of a spring because it is located on their land; the neighboring village of Quradah believes their right to the water was affirmed in a 50-year-old court verdict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al-Qadhi 2003

title: Water cooler spiked with chemical agent sickens seven law students
description: A water cooler spiked with potassium cyanide sickens seven law school students in Springfield, Massachusetts. Swastika-like graffiti around the water cooler draws speculation about the attacker.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Water for Luanda, Angola is cut off during conflict
description: In Angola, the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola attacks and occupies Catete, leaving Luanda without water. Additionally eight civilians and two FAA are killed and many others are captured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5557996

title: Water riots in Gujarat, India over control and access to water
description: Three people die and 20 are injured in December 1999 in Falla, Gujarat, India when the police open fire on 300 people protesting the state government's decision to reserve water from the nearby Kankavati Dam for Jamnagar, a neighboring town. The dam had become the only source of water for about 60 villages near Falla, and shortages and overdraft of groundwater contribute to a water crisis.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Financial Times Global Water Report (FTGWR) 2000 ; Centre for Science and the Environment 2000

title: Water tank in Istanbul, Turkey is attacked
description: A water tank is damaged from a petrol bomb thrown by unknown assailants in Istanbul, Turkey.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Anatolia 1999 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 199909280001 ; RAND Da

title: Water-supply pipeline is attacked in France
description: Explosives are placed along a water-supply pipeline by the Comité Régional d'Action Viticole in France. No injuries to people are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; France-Inter Radio Network 1999 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 199

title: Yugoslavia refuses to clear river debris
description: Yugoslavia refuses to clear war debris on Danube (downed bridges) unless financial aid for reconstruction is provided; European countries on Danube fear flooding due to winter ice dams will result. Diplomats decry environmental blackmail.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Simons 1999

title: A man is arrested for attempted poisoning of community water supply in Turkey
description: A man is arrested for attempted poisoning of the water supply for the village of Kurusaray, Turkey.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Aqueduct in Colombia is attacked
description: A bombing attempt occurs at an aqueduct in Colombia. The bomb does not detonate. The National Liberation Army is suspected in the attempt.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2000 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200

title: Australian hacker causes sewage spills
description: In Queensland, Australia, police arrest a man for using a computer and radio transmitter to take control of the Maroochy Shire wastewater system and release sewage into parks, rivers, and property.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gellman 2002

title: Central Asian nations cut off water to neighbors in ongoing dispute
description: Kyrgyzstan cuts off water to Kazakhstan until coal is delivered; Uzbekistan cuts off water to Kazakhstan for non-payment of debt.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Pannier 2000

title: Clashes between rioters and police over water shortages in Sudan leads to one death and many injuries
description: Sudanese rioters who are protesting against the failure of schools to reopen as well as water and electricity shortages clash with police who intervene to quell the riot. At least one student is killed and many are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5576946

title: Ethiopian killed in water fight
description: One man is stabbed to death during fight over clean water during famine in Ethiopia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sandrasagra 2000

title: French workers pollute river over labor dispute
description: In July, workers at the Cellatex chemical plant in northern France dump 5,000 liters of sulfuric acid into a tributary of the Meuse River after they are denied workers' benefits. A French analyst points out that this is the first time "the environment and public health were made hostage in order to exert pressure, an unheard-of situation until now."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Christian Science Monitor 2000

title: Israeli settlers are accused of intentionally releasing sewage to contaminate Palestinian agricultural fields in the West Bank
description: Israeli settlers from Efrat are blamed for deliberately releasing sewer water into Palestinian agricultural fields in the West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Kenyans battle monkeys for drought relief
description: A clash between villagers and thirsty monkeys leaves eight apes dead and ten villagers wounded. The duel starts after water tankers bring water to a drought-stricken area and monkeys desperate for water attack the villagers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2000 ; Okoko 2000

title: Luxury home burned to protest impact on watershed
description: The Earth Liberation Front (ELF) claims responsibility for setting a luxury home under construction on fire. Their written statement says they targeted the home because of its location in the Lake Monroe watershed, a drinking water supply for the town of Bloomington, Indiana that is in jeopardy from urban sprawl.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; Eco-Action 2003

title: Moroccan army destroys wells
description: Units of the Moroccan army destroy the wells situated in the municipalities of Guelta and Boujdour. Citizens usually use these wells to provide water for their sheep in the summer.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5001292, 5001293

title: Regional drought heightens tensions in Ethiopia and Kenya
description: The Ethiopian government says that regional drought is worsening conflicts at watering points and over access to pasture. The tensions are heightened by the presence of the Oromo Liberation Front (OLF), an Ethiopian armed opposition group said to be operating from Kenyan territory near the common border.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Norwegian Refugee Council/Global IDP Project 2002

title: Riots in northern China over use and allocation of water from Baiyang Lake
description: Civil unrest erupts over use and allocation of water from Baiyang Lake, in northern China. Several people die in riots by villagers in July 2000 in Shandong after officials cut off water supplies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Pottinger 2000

title: Riots over water privatization in Cochabamba, Bolivia
description: Massive protests, riots, and violence result from efforts to privatize the water system of Cochabamba, Bolivia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shultz and Draper 2009

title: Settlers attack a village in Palestine, injuring civilians and cutting water supply
description: In a village in Palestine, three Palestinians are injured by gunshots from Israeli settlers. The same settlers also cut the water supply to the village by damaging the pipes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Six deaths reported when officials in Guangdong, China blow up a water channel to prevent cross-border diversion of water
description: In August 2000, six die when officials in the southern province of Guangdong blow up a water channel to prevent a neighboring county from diverting water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Pottinger 2000

title: Students riot to protest water shortages in Kenya
description: Students riot to protest water shortages in Kenya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5273804, 5001531

title: Terrorist drill gets out of hand in California
description: A drill simulating a terrorist attack on the Nacimiento Dam in Monterey County, California got out of hand when two radio stations reported it as a real attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gaura 2000

title: Violent conflict in Afghanistan over access to water
description: Violent conflicts break out over water resources in the villages Burna Legan and Taina Legan, Afghanistan and in other parts of the region, as drought depleted local resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Cooperation Center for Afghanistan 2000

title: Water company is bombed to demand release of prisoners
description: A water company office in Ustaritz, France is damaged by a bomb thought to be placed in support of a group called the Basque Fatherland and Freedom (aka ETA). The attackers leave writing on the wall in the building demanding the release of ETA prisoners.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water storage facility is destroyed
description: Eritrea accuses Ethiopia of bombing the Red Sea port at Assab, saying several bombs are dropped on Assab, destroying a water storage facility on the outskirts of the town.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5267507

title: Water-supply tank for a condominium in Singapore deliberately contaminated
description: A water-supply tank is deliberately poisoned with kerosene and turpentine. Residents of the condominium complex in Singapore discover the contamination from the odor of their water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: A water tank car is destroyed by a landmine in Russia
