description: A water tank car is destroyed by a landmine in Grozny, Chechnya, Russia. A teenage girl is wounded in the explosion.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200108140011

title: An explosive device is detonated at Lhokseumawe Reservoir in Indonesia
description: A homemade bomb explodes at Lhokseumawe Reservoir in Aceh Province, Indonesia, with minor damage to the facility. The attack is attributed to the Free Aceh Movement.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: An explosive device is detonated at the Panauti hydropower plant in Khopasi, Nepal
description: Suspected Nepal communist party members detonate an explosive devise at the Panauti hydropower plant, causing around $500,000 in damages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: An inter-ethnic conflict between Macedonia and Albania includes a fight over control of the major water-supply reservoir
description: Macedonians and native Albanians in the border village of Radusa, Macedonia, fight to control the water reservoir that supplies water to Skopje, the nation's capital.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Fisher 2001

title: Bombing disrupts Lebanese water supplies
description: Water supplies to more than 20 towns are disrupted after a bomb explodes near the town of Baalbek in Lebanon.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; FBIS 2001 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200108270004

title: Chinese protestors block canal in protest over uncontrolled water pollution
description: In an act to protest the destruction of fisheries from uncontrolled water pollution, fishermen in northern Jiaxing City, Zhejiang Province, dam a large industrial wastewater canal for 23 days. The wastewater discharges into the neighboring Shengze Town, Jiangsu Province, killing fish and threatening public health.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; China Ministry of Water Resources 2001

title: Clashes between ethnic groups over access to water
description: Clashes occur between Pokomo and Wordei ethnic groups over access to a water fresh source in Kenya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5274071, 5274070, 5274069, 5274068

title: Deadly fight between Kenyan herders and farmers
description: At least 130 people are killed in a string of clashes between Pokomo farmers and Orma, semi-nomadic cattle herders over access to land and river water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2012a

title: Kyrgyzstan charges downstream countries for water provoking a natural gas cut off from Uzbekistan
description: In June 2001, the Kyrgyz parliament adopts a law classifying water as a commodity and announces that downstream countries would be charged for water. In response, Uzbekistan cuts off all deliveries of natural gas to Kyrgyzstan and accuses Kyrgyzstan of failing to honor an agreement to provide Uzbekistan with water in return for oil and gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hogan 2000a ; Khamidov 2001

title: Local community leader against the Babilonia hydro project murdered in his home in Honduras
description: A local community leader in La Venta, Honduras, is murdered in his home by six guards employed by a dam company, Energisa S.A. Carlow Roberto Flores had worked to oppose the Babilonia Hydroelectric Project in Sierra de Agalta National Park.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Graham 2001 ; International Rivers n.d.

title: Nepali soldiers stop rebels from targeting drinking water supplies
description: According to the Nepal Defense Ministry, soldiers repulse attempts by rebels to blow up the sources of Kathmandu's drinking water supplies at Shivapuri and Sundarijal. No details of these incidents are given.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; South Asian Intelligence Review 2001

title: Palestinians destroy water supply to Israeli settlements
description: Palestinians destroy water-supply pipelines to the West Bank settlement of Yitzhar and to Kibbutz Kissufim. The Agbat Jabar refugee camp near Jericho disconnects from its water supply after Palestinians loot and damage local water pumps. Palestinians accuse Israel of destroying a water cistern, blocking water-tanker deliveries, and attacking materials for a wastewater treatment project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Israel Line 2001a ; Israel Line 2001b ; Environment News Service 2001

title: Philippine water poisoned
description: The militant Islamist separatist group Abu Sayyaf threatens to poison the water supply in Isabela, a mainly Christian town on Basilan Island in the country's south. In October, residents in six nearby villages report water contamination from what smells like gasoline. Local officials respond by closing pipelines and bringing in drinking water by truck.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; World Environment News 2001 ; Fenton Helm and Dutter 2001

title: Protests over water shortages in Algeria
description: Angry protests take place in various communities of Ain Berda province, Algeria over gas, water and electricity shortages. Youths build barricades and block roads during these demonstrations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5241009

title: Residents riot over cut of water supplies in South Africa
description: Residents riot when officials in South Africa cut of water supplies to 1000 homes who are defunct on their payment. Police move in and disperse the crowd with rubber bullets.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4996607

title: Twenty people are killed over access to fresh water
description: Twenty people are killed in additional clashes between Orma and Pokomo ethnic groups over access to fresh water in Kenya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5274186

title: Two leaders of a water utility labor union assassinated
description: The president of the Codazzi Waterworks Labor Union, Aldo Mejia Martinez, is shot and killed by five unidentified people. Six months later, his successor, Engeniano Sánchez Díaz, is also murdered. The murders may be linked to a larger trend of homicides in Colombia of trade-union leaders and activists.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; Trade Union Confederation 2001

title: US bombs Afghan hydroelectric facility at Kajaki Dam
description: American forces bomb the hydroelectric facility at Kajaki Dam in Helmand province of Afghanistan, cutting off electricity for the city of Kandahar. The dam itself is not targeted.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2001 ; Parry 2001

title: Unrest over water shortages in Pakistan
description: Civil unrest over severe water shortages caused by the long-term drought. Protests began in March and April and continued into summer with riots, four bombs in Karachi (June 13), one death, 12 injuries, 30 arrests. Ethnic conflicts contribute as some groups "accuse the government of favoring the populous Punjab province [over Sindh province] in water distribution."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nadeem 2001 ; Soloman 2001

title: Water cut off in Macedonian conflict
description: Water flow to Kumanovo (population 100,000), Macedonia cut off for 12 days in conflict between ethnic Albanians and Macedonian forces. Valves of Glaznja and Lipkovo Lakes damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2001 ; Macedonia Information Agency 2001 ; Guardian, The 2001

title: "Unknown agent" released into water-treatment plant in Colombia
description: Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) releases an "unknown agent," presumably thought to be poisonous, in a water-treatment plant. No injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bogota Cambio 2002a ; Bogota Cambio 2002b ; Xinhua General News Service 2002 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and R

title: A man is arrested after threatening to dump mercury into local drinking water supply in Salem, Massachusetts, United States
description: A man is arrested after threatening to dump mercury into local drinking water supply in Salem, Massachusetts, United States.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness 2009

title: Algerians riot over water shortages
description: Algerians protesting against water shortages riot in the eastern coastal town of El Arrouch, Algeria, setting fire to buildings and vehicles.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2002

title: Bolivian irrigators and residents clash over water rights, with destruction of water delivery infrastructure
description: Tarata, Bolivia experiences violent confrontations between irrigators from the region of Arbieto and residents of the nearby town of Tarata. The dispute centers on the allocation of water among these users and new water infrastructure that took water from the Laka Laka dam. In October, irrigators destroy approximately two kilometers of water supply pipeline. In response, residents destroy part of a primary irrigation channel. After failed negotiations, the water system is damaged again in December in another confrontation between irrigators and village residents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bustamante et al 2004, Moriarty Butterworth and van Koopen 2004

title: Bomb explodes in water-utility office building in Corsica, France
description: A powerful bomb explodes in a water-utility office building on the Island of Corsica, France. The building is also graffitied with the nationalist slogan "Freedom for Patriots."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Bomb found in water pump station defused in Colombia
description: A bomb is found in a water-supply pump station along a canal, however it is defused prior to causing any damage to the system. The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) is blamed for the attempted attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Botswana authorities destroy wells of Kalahari Bushmen
description: Botswana's president Festus Mogae sends troops to the Kalahari Desert to destroy wells and empty water sources of indigenous Khoisan (also known as Bushmen), ostensibly in an effort to remove them from their ancestral lands and assimilate them into modern society. Critics blame the government of taking away water rights in favor of mining interests and labeled the government's actions a "siege." Botswana is condemned by international observers. Against expectations, a band of Bushmen retreat into the desert and survive for years with little outside assistance.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Workman 2009

title: Colombian rebels bomb dam
description: Colombian rebels in January damage a gate valve in the dam that supplies most of Bogota's drinking water. Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) detonate an explosive device planted on a German-made gate valve located inside a tunnel in the Chingaza Dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Waterweek 2002

title: Colorado eco-terrorists threaten water supply
description: Earth Liberation Front threatens the water supply for the town of Winter Park. Previously, this group claimed responsibility for the destruction of a ski lodge in Vail, Colorado that threatened lynx habitat.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Crecente 2002 ; Associated Press (AP) 2002

title: Deadly clash over water sharing in Kashmir, India
description: Two people are killed and 25 others injured in Kashmir, India, when police fire at a group of villagers clashing over water sharing. The incident took place in Garend village in a dispute over water from an irrigation stream.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2002

title: Drinking water in Libornia, Colombia is poisoned
description: Just one month after the poisoning of a water supply in another small town in Colombia, the water supply for the town of Libornia is poisoned as well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Drinking water poisoned in Pitalito, Colombia
description: The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) is accused of poisoning the town of Pitalito's water supply with heavy metals.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Far right-wing nationalists in South Africa plot to kill millions of black South Africans by poisoning water
description: A major plot to kill millions of black South Africans living in the townships near Johannesburg is discovered by the South African National Intelligence Agency. The attackers are a group of far right-wing white South Africans. Their plans consist of contaminating water supplies by pouring an agricultural chemical into reservoirs that supply four townships.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Four wells found with human remains in Cote d'lvoire
description: Conflict between the government of Laurent Gbagbo and opposing rebel forces leads to extensive violence and regional conflict. In late September 2002, there are reports of several mass graves discovered in the Bangolo. In Zeregbo and Bahably, four water wells are found with human remains. Early reports indicate that western rebel groups who captured the area killed the persons in the mass graves and wells between December 2002 and January 2003.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; US Department of State 2004

title: Gas line set on fire in a water treatment plant
description: A gas pipeline in a water treatment plant is set on fire by "People's Militias" in Dosquebradas, Colombia. One death and two injuries are reported in association with the event.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Indian military protecting reservoir attacked by terrorists
description: A camp of the Assam Rifles of the Indian military at Yairipok in Thoubal district with a mission to protect a water reservoir is attacked by suspected terrorists who fired grenades and other explosives on January 27. Later, a spokesman for the United National Liberation Front (UNLF) claims that the attack was carried out by its armed wing, the Manipur People's Army, which has been fighting for what it called an "Independent Manipur."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; South Asian Intelligence Review 2002

title: Inter-clan fighting of the Mudug region in Somalia occurs over resource scarcity
description: About 40 people are killed and 60 wounded in inter-clan fighting in the Mudug region of central Somalia. The violence is sparked by revenge killings over the deaths of eight fisherman, but a local elder, Muhammad Salad Du'ale, attributes the ongoing violence to the scarcity of water and grazing.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Puntland Development Research Centre (PDRC) 2014

title: Italy foils terror plot targeting water supplies
description: Italian police arrest four Moroccans allegedly planning to contaminate the water-supply system in Rome with a cyanide-based chemical, targeting buildings that included the United States embassy. Ties to Al-Queda are suggested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2002

title: Lesotho Highlands Water Project: South Africa-Lesotho
description: The Lesotho Highlands Water Project (LHWP) delivers first significant water transfers to water-scarce South Africa's Gauteng province from Lesotho highlands via transboundary tunnels, in exchange for royalties paid to Lesotho. A model example of water trade.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Treaty on the Lesotho Highlands Water Project Between the Government of the Kingdom of Lesotho and the Government of the Republic of South Africa (1986, Phase 1 operational 2002).

title: Multiple attacks on water towers in Pakistan
description: Two water towers are blown up in Jango Ghari, Pakistan, a tribal area, where several other similar attacks have occurred. The power systems atop the towers are destroyed in the blast as well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Nepal rebels blow up powerhouse
description: The Khumbuwan Liberation Front (KLF) blows up a 250 kilowatt hydroelectric powerhouse in Nepal's Bhojpur District, cutting off power to Bhojpur and surrounding areas. The damages take 6 months to repair and cost 10 million Rs (US $120,000). During 2002, Maoist rebels destroy more than seven micro-hydro projects, a water-supply intake, and supply pipelines to Khalanga in western Nepal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kathmandu Post, The 2002 ; Financial Times Global Water Report (FTGWR) 2002

title: Outspoken defender of the environment and settler rights, and opponent of the Belo Monte dam project, is assassinated in Brazil
description: In August 2002, Gilzan Teixeira Lima, a leader of a fight against the construction of the Belo Monte Dam project on the Xingu River in Brazil, is assassinated. He had received death threats for his defense of the environment and settler rights.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Plot to poison water and food supplies reported by Russian special forces
description: A plot by Chechen rebels to poison water and food supplies in Groznyy, Russia, is reported by Russian special forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Priest in Honduras murdered for speaking out against the Babilonia hydro project
description: A priest, Fredy Cornelia Benitez, is murdered in 2002 in Honduras for speaking out against the Babilonia Hydroelectric project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Protesters clash with police over water shortages
description: Clashes between protesters and police are reported in the east and south of Algeria, as well as in different neighborhoods of the capital, over water shortages. Streets are blocked and public buildings are burned.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5241129, 5241130, 5241131

title: Rival Ethiopian and Somali ethnic groups clash over access to water
description: Rival ethnic groups, the Afar (Ethiopia) and Issas (Somali), clash over scarce water in mid-2002. The scarcity is due to severe drought pushing Issas into Afar territory for use of their watering holes. The UN Emergencies Unit for Ethiopia says that "immediate political solutions are essential to negotiate conflict resolution between Afar and Issa communities over water and grazing land."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; The New Humanitarian 2002

title: Terrorist targets water systems in the United States
description: Papers seized during the arrest of a Lebanese Imam at a mosque in Seattle include "instructions on poisoning water sources" from a London-based al Qaeda recruiter. The FBI issue a bulletin to computer security experts around the country indicating that al-Qaeda terrorists may have been studying American dams and water-supply systems in preparation for new attacks. "U.S. law enforcement and intelligence agencies have received indications that al-Qaeda members have sought information on Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems available on multiple SCADA-related Web sites,' reads the bulletin, according to SecurityFocus. "They specifically sought information on water supply and wastewater management practices in the U.S. and abroad."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; McDonnell and Meyer 2002 ; MSNBC 2002

title: Violence over Cauvery River in India
description: Continuing violence over the allocation of the Kaveri River between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. Riots, property destruction, more than 30 injuries, arrests through September and October.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hindu, The 2002a ; Hindu, The 2002b ; PTI 2002

title: Violent clashes triggered over a hydroelectric project in Ecuador
description: A small community, San Pablo de Amali, in Bolivar province, Ecuador, resists a hydroelectric project on the local Dulcepamba River. The resistance by the community is generally peaceful, but some community members are arrested for acts of sabotage and destruction. In support of the developer, Hidrotambo S.A., the national government sends troops to the community on several instances, resulting in violent clashes. In 2012 the developer initiates construction. In 2015, the community claims that this construction causes severe flooding during a rain event, killing three local people, and destroying seven houses and 10 hectares of crop land. Judicial trials of community members are ongoing in 2019.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Carson 2019, Staberock and Lahidji 2016 ; Environmental Justice Atlas 2019 ; Observatorio del Cambio Rural n.d. ; Calvopiña 2016

title: Warehouse of drinking water project destroyed
description: A rebel group, called the Communist Party of Nepal-Maoists, destroys a warehouse of the Bijauri Drinking Water Project in Nepal, including 30,000 meters of polythene pipes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water company offices in Chile bombed in response to high tariffs for water
description: Three explosions occur at the offices of a water company, Aquas Andinas of Chile. The explosions are attributed to a group called Pueblo Reagrupado. Pueblo Reagrupado is thought to have placed the bombs in response to high tariffs for water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water pipe destroyed by explosion in Serbia
description: A water pipe that had been planned for a new water-supply system in Bujanovac, Serbia is destroyed by an explosion. An Albanian group is thought be responsible for the bomb.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water reservoir sustains minor damages from bombing in Colombia
description: The chief engineer of a water company reports minor damage from a bomb placed near a reservoir in Bogota by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water shortages cause riots in Algeria
description: Power outages and water shortages cause multiple days of rioting in Rouached, Algeria. 11 people are injured. Riot police intervene.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5241148, 5241147, 5241146, 5241143

title: Youths destroy local water, electric, and telecommunication facilities in Cote d'lvoire
description: On October 10, youths claiming to be members of the Group of Patriots for Peace (GPP) destroy facilities of the Ivoirian Water Distribution Company, the Ivoirian Electricity Company, and Cote d'Ivoire Telecommunications. Demonstrators say they were protesting the "free" supply of water, electricity, and telephone in rebel-controlled areas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; US Department of State 2004

title: A package with ricin and a note are found threatening to poison a local water supply in South Carolina, United States
description: A package with ricin and a note are found threatening to poison a local water supply in Greenville, South Carolina, United States.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness 2009

title: Al Qaeda threatens US water
description: Al-Qaeda threatens US water systems via call to a London-based, Saudi-owned magazine. The spokesman told the magazine that "al Qaeda [does not rule out] using sarin gas and poisoning drinking water in U.S. and Western cities."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2003a ; Waterman 2003 ; Washington Times, The 2003

title: Armed cadres kill Bangladesh Nationalist Party workers over resource dispute
description: Suspected armed cadres of the Purbo Banglar Communist Party (PBCP) kill six Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) workers at Naidighee village in Naogaon, on April 25. According to police sources, the incident appears to be a continuation of a long-standing dispute over nine government water reservoirs and khas (farming) land in the village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; South Asian Intelligence Review 2003

title: Bomb explosion breaks water main, cutting water supply for all of Baghdad, Iraq
description: Insurgents bomb a main water pipeline in Baghdad, Iraq, cutting all water supply and flooding neighborhoods. City engineers say this is the first strike against Baghdad's water system during the Iraq War, which began in March 2003. The bombing occurs around seven in the morning, when a blue Volkswagen Passat stops on an overpass near the Nidaa mosque and an explosive is fired at the six-foot-wide water main in the northern part of Baghdad, said Hayder Muhammad, the chief engineer for the city's water treatment plants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2003 ; Tierney and Worth 2003

title: Bomb found in water-supply facility in Ireland
description: A bomb is defused at a water supply facility in Keady, Ireland. The facility supplies about 10,000 homes with water. A group called the Continuity Irish Republican Army (CIRA) is suspected to be responsible for placing the bomb.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Bombs found at US bottling plant
description: Four incendiary devices are found in the pumping station of a Michigan water-bottling plant. The Earth Liberation Front (ELF) claims responsibility, accusing Ice Mountain Water Company of "stealing" water for profit. Ice Mountain is a subsidiary of Nestle Waters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2003b

title: Caño Limón – Coveñas pipeline attacked, spilling oil into stream and polluting water for 4,700 families; 972 attacks since 1985
description: A controversial pipeline is attacked once again, causing oil to spill into a local stream, polluting the water supply used by 4700 families. The Caño Limón – Coveñas pipeline has come under attack hundreds of times in an attempt by the local population to disrupt and halt natural resource extraction by multinational companies. One source reports that since the pipeline was built in 1985 it has been attacked 972 times.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; SourceWatch 2018

title: Colombian water plant bombed
description: A bomb blast at the Cali Drinking Water Treatment Plant kills 3 workers May 8th in Colombia. The workers were members of a trade union involved in intense negotiations over privatization of the water system.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Public Services International 2003

title: Darfur war triggered in part by disputes over control of water resources
description: The Darfur War is triggered in part by conflicts over the control of water and other natural resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bromwich 2018

title: Grenades are fired at a water reservoir plant in Kidapawan, Philippines destroying a piepline and disrupting water supplies
description: Two grenades destroy a water pipeline at a reservoir in Kidapawan, Philippines, disrupting water supply to approximately 100,000 residents. The Moro Islamic Liberation Front is accused of the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200303190005 ; U.S Department of Home

title: Group bombs a rural water supply office and other offices in India
description: A rural water supply office building is blown up along with other offices, in Parkal, India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Iraqi agents attempts to poison water at US base in Jordan
description: Jordanian authorities arrest Iraqi agents in connection with a botched plot to poison the water supply that serves American troops in the eastern Jordanian desert near the border with Iraq. The scheme involved poisoning a water tank that supplies American soldiers at a military base in Khao, which lies in an arid region of the eastern frontier near the industrial town of Zarqa.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Feuer 2003

title: Iraqi water treatment plant damaged
description: The Abu Nawas pumping station on the Tigris River, which supplies water to Sadr City and other treatment plants in Baghdad, is severely damaged during the 2003 conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) 2009

title: Israeli warplanes attack water systems in Gaza
description: Israeli warplanes hit water supply wells, pipelines, and wastewater treatment plants servicing hundreds of thousands of Palestinians in the Gaza region. Palestinian officials state that the attacks intentionally targeted the infrastructure, amounting to a war crime under the Geneva Protocol.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4991303

title: Man poisons water reservoir in Henan Province, China, sickening over 60 to boost water purifier sales
description: A man who sells water purifiers poisons a reservoir in Ruyang County, Henan Province, China, sickening at least 64 people. The man claims that he wanted to improve sales of his product.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Residents block highways in Algeria over lack of drinking water
description: A major cold wave and lack of electricity, gas, and drinking water has led residents of Ain Mlila, Algeria to block major highways until their demands are met.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4991269

title: Riots over lack of water services in Algeria
description: Rioters in Algeria armed with knives and molotov cocktails set fire to government buildings in protest over lack of electrical and water services.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5566892

title: Rockets are fired at Kajaki Dam, Helmand Province, Afghanistan
description: The governor of Helmand Province, Afghanistan reports that three rockets are fired at Kajaki Dam. 60 suspected Taliban are arrested for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Sa'ad and Dir clans fight over water and grazing in Somalia
description: Two days of heavy fighting in Mudug region of Somalia leave at least 43 people dead and over 90 injured. The fighting breaks out between the Sa'ad, Habar Gedir subclan and the Dir, and is concentrated in and around the villages of Towfiq and Awle, some 200 km east of Galkayo. As with the 2002 events, the clashes are triggered by revenge killings but the ensuing escalation of violence is also attributed to disagreements over water and grazing in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Puntland Development Research Centre (PDRC) 2014

title: Sudan targets water in civil war
description: The ongoing civil war in the Sudan has included violence against water resources. In 2003, villagers from around Tina said that bombings had destroyed water wells. In Khasan Basao they alleged that water wells were poisoned. In 2004, wells in Darfur were intentionally contaminated as part of a strategy of harassment against displaced populations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Amnesty International 2004 ; Schofield 2004 ; Bromwhich 2018

title: The Sudan government bombs wells in Furawiya, Sudan killing animals and destroying a well
description: The Sudan government bombs wells in Furawiya, Sudan killing hundreds of animals and destroying a well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Heffernan and Leaning 2006

title: Water bottles are intentionally contaminated in 20 different Italian cities, sickening more than 50 people
description: Around 50 people are sickened by water contaminated with either bleach acetone or ammonia in more than 20 different cities from across Italy. Authorities blame a "saboteur" or "copy-cat saboteurs" for these poisonings.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi and Murshid 2006

title: Water systems damaged in US-Iraq war
description: During the US-led invasion of Iraq, water systems are reportedly damaged or destroyed by different parties, and major dams are military objectives of the US forces. Damage directly attributable to the war includes vast segments of the water distribution system and the Baghdad water system, damaged by a missile.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNICEF 2003 ; Booth 2003

title: Women block water access to a naval base in Nigeria
description: A group of women in canoes protest safeguards on oil standards by blocking water access to a naval base in the Niger Delta, Nigeria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5294140

title: A bomb explodes at the Selaghat Dam, Nepal cutting electricity to the area
description: A powerful bomb explodes at the powerhouse of the Selaghat Dam, Bajura District, Nepal. No group claims responsibility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: A bomb explodes at the construction site for Dumarao Dam, Philippines
description: Suspected communists detonate a bomb at the construction site of the Dumarao Dam, Capiz province, Philippines.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Armed men attempt to gain access to the Zelenchuck Dam, Russia and are repelled, with one attacker injured
description: A group of three armed men attempted to gain access to the water intake area of the Zelenchuck Dam in the Karachay-Cherkessia Republic of Russia. Guards at the dam successfully repel the attack, wounding one attacker and arresting the others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Chinese engineers working on a dam are kidnapped, one is killed
description: Two Chinese engineers working on the Gomal Zam dam and a canal in Waziristan, Pakistan, are kidnapped by Pakistani militants seeking the release of six Pakistani comrades. During a rescue attempt, one of the two engineers is shot and killed, while the other is brought to safety.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; China Daily 2004b

title: Driver killed while transporting water in Iraq
description: A driver of a truck transporting mineral water in Mosul, Iraq is killed when his truck is set on fire.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; Reuters 2004c

title: Four people employed by the water and sewage department kidnapped in Kirkuk, Iraq
description: Three engineers and one contractor, employed by the city water and sewage board, are kidnapped in Kirkuk, Iraq. No reports could be found detailing the outcome of the kidnapping.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Government shuts off electricity and water supplies in northern Cote d'lvoire
description: On November 4, the army carries out "Operation Dignity" and mounts surprise attacks on Bouake, stronghold of opposition forces and the largest city in the north, shattering an 18-month ceasefire. The Government cuts off electricity and water supplies to the north the day before the attacks. They remain off for about a week.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; US Department of State 2005

title: Mexican farmers shot in duel over spring
description: Two Mexican farmers argue for years over water rights to a small spring used to irrigate a small corn plot near the town of Pihuamo. In March, these farmers shoot each other dead.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2004b

title: Militia attack village over land and water disputes
description: Boran militia attack Gabra village near the Ethiopian border. The attack is linked to long-running disputes over land and water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4985692

title: Militias smash water wells in Sudan
description: Janjaweed militias smash water wells and burn both food and seeds in the Jebel Marra area of Sudan. They also allegedly throw dead bodies into some open wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5576261

title: Missionaries working on a water project attacked in Mosul, Iraq
description: Four Christian missionaries from the U.S. are killed and one other seriously wounded when they are attacked while working on a water project in Mosul, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; Renaud and Johnson 2004

title: Murusade and Duduble subclans clash over water well in Somalia
description: Murusade subclan and Duduble subclan clash over a water well, with 23 fatalities. Separately, a dispute between the Dir and Marehan clans over control of water and grazing lands in Heraale leads to a death in October.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Puntland Development Research Centre (PDRC) 2014 ; The Somali Dir Clan's History: Codka Beesha Direed 2012 ; Salehyan et al 2014

title: Pakistan targets terrorists' water
description: In military action aimed at Islamic terrorists, including Al Qaeda and the Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, homes, schools, and water wells are damaged and destroyed in Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2004a

title: Police kill dam protestor in China
description: Tens of thousands of farmers stage a sit-in against the construction of the Pubugou dam on the Dadu River in Sichuan Province, China. Riot police are deployed to quell the unrest and one person is killed. Witnesses also report the deaths of a number of residents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lim 2004 ; Voice of America 2009

title: Police kill water protestors in India
description: Four people are killed in October and more than 30 injured in November in ongoing protests by farmers over allocations of water from the Indira Ghandi Irrigation Canal in Sri Ganganagar district, which borders Pakistan. Authorities impose curfews on the towns of Gharsana, Raola and Anoopgarh.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Indo-Asian News Service 2004

title: Protesters blockade a road over installation of pre-paid water meters in South Africa
description: Members of the Soweto Electricity Crisis Committee blockade a road in their city in protest of the installation of pre-paid water meters in their homes. Police use stun-guns to disperse them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4985178, 4985270

title: Rebels destroy offices of local water utility in Sudan
description: Rebels destroy several houses and the offices of the local police and water utility in Sudan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4987151, 4987157

title: Riots in prison over water shortage, Cote d'Ivoire
description: Riots occur at the main prison in Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire over a water shortage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5249959, 5249958, 5249956, 5249955

title: Riots over water shortage kill prisoners in Côte d'Ivoire
description: There are two incidents in early November at Abidjan's main jail, La Maison d'arrêt et de correction d'Abidjan (MACA), Côte d'Ivoire in which prisoners are killed. The first incident is sparked by a lengthy water shortage; prisoners reportedly had not had water for 5 days except for small rations of drinking water. At least 7 prisoners die and 30 are injured in the ensuing riots. U.N. human rights officials said they were investigating the riot and could not give a final death toll.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; US Department of State 2005

title: Riots over water shortages in Algeria
description: Riots break out in Algeria due to unemployment, water shortages, and resentment of the government. Protesters attack town halls and other administrative buildings.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5237320, 5237321, 5237322, 5237323, 5237324

title: Security staff of a public water system shot at while working
description: Bullets are fired at the security staff of a public water pumping station in Kosovska Mitrovica, Kosovo. Authorities blame Albanian extremists for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Several government agencies related to water and other services attacked
description: Over two months in 2004 in Nepal, the Communist Party of Nepal-Maoists bomb several government offices, including the Water Induced Calamities Control Sub-Division in Nadipur, Pokhara and the Groundwater Irrigation Project in Dang District.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Students protest over water shortages
description: Students protest over water shortages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5285986, 5285968, 5285957

title: Students riot over power cuts and water shortages in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Students riot over power cuts and water shortages in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
basin: Democratic Republic of the Congo Havzası
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5560713

title: Terrorists attempt to recruit workers at a US water utility to poison drinking water
description: The FBI and Homeland Security warn that terrorists are attempting to recruit workers at a US water utility to poison drinking water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness 2009

title: Terrorists bomb water pipe in India
description: Twelve Indian security forces are killed by an IED planted in an underground water pipe during "counter-insurgency operation in Khanabal area in Anantnag district.'
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Times News Network (TNN) 2004

title: The Sudan government and militias attack water systems in Furawiya, Southern Sudan
description: The Sudanese government and Janjaweed militia poison a well in Furawiya, destroy the sole pump for a communal well in Terbeba, and toss dead bodies down a well in Bendisi, southern Sudan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Heffernan and Leaning 2006

title: US Pentagon report raises possibility that Taiwan could target China's Three Gorges Dam as deterrence threat
description: A 2004 Pentagon report on China's military capacity raises the concept of Taipei adopting military systems capable of being used as a tool for deterring Chinese military coercion by "presenting credible threats to China's urban population or high-value targets, such as the Three Gorges Dam." China promptly denounces "a U.S. suggestion' that Taiwan's military target the Three Gorges Dam, leading the US to deny that it had so urged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; China Daily 2004a ; US Department of Defense 2004

title: US halts water projects in Gaza
description: The United States halts two water development projects as punishment to the Palestinian Authority for their failure to find those responsible for a deadly attack on a US diplomatic convoy in October 2003.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2004

title: Violence over water in Ethiopia
description: At least 250 people killed and many more injured in clashes over water wells and pastoral lands. Villagers call it the "War of the Well" and describe "well warlords, well widows, and well warriors." A three-year drought has led to extensive violence over limited water resources, worsened by the lack of effective government and central planning.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2004 ; Associated Press (AP) 2005 ; Wax 2006

title: Violent protests in South Africa
description: Poor delivery of water and sanitation services in Phumelela Township leads to several months of protests. No one is killed during the protests, but a few people are seriously injured, and municipal property is damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Centre for Development and Enterprise (CDE) 2007

title: Zambezi Watercourse Commission Agreement (ZAMCOM)
description: Eight Zambezi riparian states (Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe) sign the ZAMCOM Agreement establishing the Zambezi Watercourse Commission for integrated management of the basin.
countries: Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agreement on the Establishment of the Zambezi Watercourse Commission, Kasane (2004).

title: A bomb prematurely explodes at Mirani Dam in southern Pakistan, killing one attacker and injuring the other
description: Two militants attempt to detonate an explosive device at the Merani Dam Project offices in southern Pakistan, near Iran. The explosive device detonates prematurely, killing one attacker and injuring the other.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: A lawyer who advised people affected by the construction of a dam in Mexico is killed
description: A Mexican lawyer, Jaime Bracamonte Arias, who advised people affected by the construction of El Cajon Dam is killed in 2005 after years of receiving death threats.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: A mortar round hits a water facility in Iraq
description: A mortar round hits a water facility in Baghdad, Iraq, resulting in a disruption of water supply to residents serviced by the facility. No one claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200507010006

title: A rocket-propelled grenade is fired at the Haditha Dam
description: Insurgents fire a rocket-propelled grenade at Haditha Dam, Iraq. The grenade strikes power lines before detonating on the dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Assailants detonate a bomb at the Haditha Dam on the Euphrates River in Iraq
description: Assailants detonate a timed IED outside the central transformer room of the Haditha Dam on the Euphrates River in Iraq, damaging the dam. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Bomb destroys power source for local water system in Albania
description: A bomb explodes in the Margegaj village of Tropojë District in Albania, destroying a power source for the local water system. Several villages are left without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Bomb placed at a water station in Iraq explodes prematurely and kills both attackers
description: A bomb at a water station in Iraq explodes prematurely, killing the two men placing the bomb.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Car bomb near water services director kills one
description: A car bomb placed near the Kirkuk city water services director detonates, killing one person and injuring at least 17 others in Kirkuk, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Communist party in Nepal destroys a drinking water project
description: The Communist Party of Nepal-Maoists destroys a drinking water project in the District of Arghakhanchi, Nepal, disrupting water service to thousands of people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Euphrates-Tigris Initiative for Cooperation (ETIC)
description: Turkey, Syria, and Iraq establish the Euphrates-Tigris Initiative for Cooperation (ETIC) as a Track II platform for scientists and water managers to promote cross-border water dialogue, reflecting a limited rapprochement after decades of tension.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Euphrates-Tigris Initiative for Cooperation Charter (2005); Kent, S. (2008). Transboundary Water Governance.

title: Gunman take out electric lines, disrupting water service in Baghdad
description: Electric lines that provide power for water-supply services in Baghdad, Iraq are shot down by a gunman, causing a disruption to water services. These same power lines had been recently fixed after suffering from a similar attack in the months prior.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Gunmen attack civilians working on a water project in Iraq
description: Gunmen attack civilians working on a water project in Al-Faris, Iraq, killing 18 and wounding 22. No group claims responsibility for the shooting.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200507260001

title: Indian border guards and Bangladesh military clash over contruction of infrastructure on the Mahananda River
description: Indian Border Security Force (BSF) and Bangladesh Rifles (BDR) exchange fire over the construction of embankments on the Mahananda River. Indian officials argue the construction of a concrete embankment by Bangladesh will increase erosion on the Indian side and violate a 1975 agreement on border and river management between the two countries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) News 2005 ; Ramachandran 2006

title: Kazakhstan Kok-Aral Dam Saves North Aral Sea
description: Kazakhstan, with World Bank financing, completes the Kok-Aral dike and dam separating the North and South Aral Sea, successfully raising water levels in the northern section. Fish populations begin recovering after three decades of collapse.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; World Bank (2005). Syr Darya Control and Northern Aral Sea Phase-1 Project Report; Micklin, P. (2007).

title: Marehan and Garre clans clash over land and water rights in Somalia
description: The Marehan and Garre clans clash over land and water rights in Somalia, with 34 fatalities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Salehyan et al 2014

title: Over 90 dead in Kenya water fight
description: Police are sent to the northwestern part of Kenya to control a major violent dispute between Kikuyu and Maasai groups over water. More than 20 people are killed in fighting in January. By July, the death toll exceeds 90, principally in the rural center of Turbi. The tensions arise over grazing and water. Maasai herdsmen accuse a local Kikuyu politician of diverting a river to irrigate his farm, depriving downstream livestock. Fighting displaces more than 2000 villagers and reflects tensions between nomadic and settled communities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British_Broadcasting_Corporation_BBC_2005 ; Ryu 2009 ; Lane 2005

title: Over years of opposition to the La Parota dam, three local organizers are killed in Mexico
description: Between 2005 and 2007 three local organizers in Guerrero, Mexico, Tomas Cruz Zamora, Eduardo Maya Manrique, and Benito Cruz Jacinto, are killed for their opposition to La Parota Dam project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ojarasca 2012

title: Power station damaged, taking down some of Baghdad's water distribution system
description: A power station in Tarmiyah, Iraq is damaged by a fire, disabling a portion of Baghdad's water-distribution system.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Rocket lands near an Israeli national water company facility
description: A Qassam rocket lands near a facility belonging to the Israeli national water company, Mekorot, in the western Negev desert. There are no injuries or damages resulting from the strike.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200512120004

title: Six employees of a water utility found murdered inside the water treatment plant in Baghdad
description: Six employees of a water utility in Baghdad are found murdered inside a water treatment plant. The actual date of their deaths is not known.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Suspected Taliban militants lay explosives in an apparent attempt to cause failure of the Kajaki Dam in Afghanistan
description: Twenty suspected Taliban militants access the Kajaki Dam and began to lay explosives in an apparent attempt to cause a dam failure. NATO and Afghan troops arrest the militants prior to detonation of explosives.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Three Iraqis killed while driving water to an army base
description: A group of three Iraqi men are shot and killed while transporting water to a military base near Taji, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water pipeline attacked with bomb in Iraq
description: A bomb placed near a water pipeline explodes in Iraq, causing it to break. That same day, two nearby oil pipelines are also attacked.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water pipeline targeted in attack in Baghdad
description: A water pipeline is damaged by a targeted explosion, disrupting water services to approximately two million people in Baghdad, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; New Humanitarian, The 2005

title: 200 people attack home of Water Resource Minister in India
description: A group of around 200 people attack the home residence of Kamlesh Kumar Singh, the Jharkhand Water Resources Minister, in Kamgarpur, Palamu District, India. The minister is not home during the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: An explosion damages a water pipeline supplying water to parts of Sri Lanka's capital, Colombo and surrounding suburbs
description: An explosion damages a water pipeline that supplies water to parts of Sri Lanka's capital, Colombo, and surrounding suburbs. Tens of thousands of homes are without potable water as a consequence. No group claims responsibility but the act of sabotage occurs shortly after the Sri Lankan government reinvokes anti-terrorism legislation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200610120005

title: Armed clashes in Yemen over water well
description: Local media report a struggle between Hajja and Amran tribes over a well located between the two governorates in Yemen. According to news reports, armed clashes between the two sides force many families to leave their homes and migrate. News reports confirm that authorities had arrested 20 people in an attempt to stop the fighting.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al-Ariqi 2006

title: Bomb attached to police vehicle carrying water supplies injures three in Sri Lanka
description: Three police officers are injured after a bomb explodes from underneath a water truck in Vavuniya District, Sri Lanka.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Bomb explodes near water pump station in Pakistan
description: A bomb explodes near a water pump station in Quetta, Pakistan. No one is injured in the explosion.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: British soldiers are injured by mines at Kajaki Dam, Afghanistan
description: Five British soldiers are injured by land mines at Afghanistan's Kajaki Dam on the Helmand River. The mines were left over from the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Harding 2007

title: Dam protester executed in China
description: Chinese authorities execute a man who took part in protests against the Pubugou dam in Sichuan province in 2004 (see China 2004 entry). Chen Tao is convicted of killing a policeman, but is executed before legal appeals are completed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2006d ; Coonan 2006

title: Director of water project killed
description: The director of the Baqubah water project, Husayn Ali Atiyah, is killed by gunmen. The attack is considered part of a larger effort to undermine the Iraqi reconstruction process.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Drinking water supply for thousands destroyed in Nepal
description: Several drinking water supply reservoirs and pipelines that provide water for more than 20,000 people are destroyed by explosives in the Narayan and Jajarkot areas of Nepal. The Communist Party of Nepal-Maoists is suspected to be responsible for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Employee of Iraq's Ministry of Water Resources killed
description: An employee of the Ministry of Water Resources in Iraq is killed by a gunman.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Explosive device targeting a water main in Iraq detonates early, killing two, wounding one
description: An explosive device targeting a water main in Kirkuk, Iraq, detonates prematurely, killing two and injuring one of the attackers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Gas and water pipeline blown up by insurgents in Pakistan
description: A gas line and water pipeline in the Pir Koh - Dera Bugti District, Pakistan, is blown up by insurgents, resulting in the suspension of water and gas supply to adjacent areas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; South Asian Intelligence Review n.d.

title: Government water official killed in Iraq
description: A government official working with the water authority in Kirkuk, Iraq is killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Guinea Joins OMVS Senegal River Basin Authority
description: Guinea joins the Organisation pour la mise en valeur du fleuve Sénégal (OMVS) as its fourth member state, completing the basin's institutional framework by including the river's main headwaters state and enhancing cooperative management.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Treaty of Adhesion of the Republic of Guinea to OMVS, Bamako (2006).

title: Gunmen attack the drinking water treatment plant to the U.S. Ayn al-Asad base in Iraq
description: Gunmen blow up the pipes of a drinking water treatment plant running to the U.S. Ayn al-Asad base in Iraq. Clashes rage between the gunmen and members of the plant's security, and are followed by explosions that lead to the destruction of the plant's water pumps and power generators. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200604100025

title: Lebanon, Israel target water infrastructure in attacks
description: Hezbollah rockets damage a wastewater plant in Israel. Israeli counter-attacks damage water systems throughout southern Lebanon, including tanks, pipes, pumping stations, and facilities along the Litani River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Science 2006 ; Amnesty International 2006 ; Murphy 2006

title: Militants wound guards at a water-supply company in Algeria
description: Militants from the Salafist Group for Call and Combat attack a guard station at a water-supply company in Thenia, near Boumerdès, Algeria. Two guards are wounded in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Planted computer virus used to control chlorine output found in a water-treatment system in Pennsylvania, United States
description: An unknown individual plants a computer virus in a water-treatment system in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, United States to control chlorine output.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness 2009

title: Rocket attack damages a Mekorot water station, Israel
description: Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) claims responsibility for a rocket attack, which is aimed at Ashkelon, Israel, but lands in an industrial area just south of Ashkelon, damaging a Mekorot water station.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200602030011

title: Sri Lankan rebels cut water supplies
description: A major battle between the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (Tamil Tigers, LTTE) and the Sri Lankan Armed Forces takes place in July and August 2006 around the watershed of the Mavil Aru (Mother River) in the Kallar area of Trincomalee district. The Mavil Aru, a tributary of the Mahaweli River, supplies water to 20,000 villagers in the eastern Sri Lanka. The sluice-gates of the waterway are captured and closed by the LTTE, cutting off water supplies and leading to a major operation against them by the Sri Lankan military. The armed forces launch air strikes with the aim of capturing the waterway and sluice-gates, which was achieved on August 11, 2006.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2006b ; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2006c ; Gutierrez 2006

title: Sudanese militia attacks villagers concerned about the impacts of a dam, killing three
description: Militia of the Merowe Dam Militia Implementation Unit in the Sudan attack a gathering of villagers concerned about the community impacts of the dam at a school in Amri village, killing three farmers and injuring more than 50 others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bosshard 2009

title: Suspected terrorists kill a water tanker driver in Pakistan
description: Suspected terrorists shoot and kill a water tanker driver and his assistant in Dherdoni who supply water to security forces near the Afghan border in North Waziristan, Pakistan. No group claims responsibility for the attack, but the Taliban is blamed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200604100009

title: Taliban attack workers repairing the Kajaki Dam, Afghanistan
description: Soldiers, police, and workers at Afghanistan’s Kajaki Dam are attacked by Taliban insurgents in an effort to disrupt assistance programs and prevent people from cooperating with the government and foreign forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gall 2007

title: Two bombs explode at a water collection point in India
description: Two bombs detonate at a water collection point near a village in India. No one is injured from the explosions.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Two water truck drivers killed in Iraq
description: The drivers of a water truck are killed in Baghdad, Iraq by a gunman while driving for work.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Unsuccessful targeting of water pipeline In Baghdad, Iraq
description: A water pipeline in Baghdad is targeted by an explosive device placed nearby. However, the explosion does not damage the pipeline.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Violent water clashes in Somali
description: At least 12 people die and over 20 are wounded in clashes over competition for water and pasture in the Somali border region.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2006a

title: Water and gas supplies disrupted by explosion in Pakistan
description: Water and gas pipelines in Pir Koh, Pakistan are destroyed, disrupting the delivery of these supplies to nearby communities. The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) takes responsibility for the explosion.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water clashes kill 40 in Kenya and Ethiopia
description: At least 40 people die in Kenya and Ethiopia in continuing clashes over water, livestock, and grazing land. Fighting occurs in the southern Ethiopia in the region of Oromo and the northern Kenya Marsabit district.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2006

title: Water pipelines destroyed by rocket attacks and explosives in Pakistan
description: Several attacks with rockets and other explosives on pipelines that supply water to a gas plant in Dera Bugti, Pakistan, disrupt gas production.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; Dawn 2006

title: Water tank drivers killed in Pakistan
description: Two people driving a water tank in Pakistan are shot and killed. They had delivered water to security forces along the Afghan border.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water utility systems destroyed during conflict in Congo
description: During the long-running conflict in the Congo, many water-utility systems are attacked and destroyed. By 2006, the World Bank estimates that at least one-third of water utility installations have been looted and completely destroyed.
basin: Democratic Republic of the Congo Havzası
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Environmental Program (UNEP) 2011

title: World Bank Neutral Expert Rules on Baglihar Dam
description: World Bank-appointed Neutral Expert Professor Raymond Lafitte rules that India's Baglihar Dam largely conforms to the Indus Waters Treaty but orders minor design modifications to pondage capacity, a partial win for Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raymond Lafitte (2007). Baglihar Dam Expert Determination Report to World Bank.

title: A forced displacement campaign by the Ethiopian military includes destruction of water wells and other sources
description: During a violent, forced displacement effort by the Ethiopian military, water wells and other water supply sources are destroyed. The Ethiopian military is seeking to move people out of the country side and into larger towns and cities in order to continue their counterinsurgency fight against the Ogaden National Liberation Front. Numerous sources report executions of those who refuse to cooperate.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Human Rights Watch 2008

title: A former employee of a California canal system is charged with damaging a computer used to divert water to an irrigation canal
description: In the United States, a former employee of a California canal system is charged with installing unauthorized software and intentionally damaging a computer used to divert water from the Sacramento River to an irrigation canal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; McMillan 2007

title: A geologist working at the Hlaingbwe Dam, Karen Province, Myanmar is killed by a land mine
description: A geologist from the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand working at the controversial Hlaingbwe Dam on the Salween River in Myanmar is killed by a land mine near the project site.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: A review of long-term violence in Guatemala identifies more than 60 environmental activists killed
description: Research by a professor at the University of Regina, Canada, finds that between 2007 and 2017 at least 61 Guatemalan activists were murdered for their work protecting rivers, lands, and the people who depend on them for their livelihoods.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Granovsky-Larsen 2018

title: Attack on a water filtering station leaves at least 33 dead in Diyala, Iraq
description: An attack on a water-filtering station in the Al-Khalis District of Diyala Governorate in Iraq is thwarted by the Iraqi military and other forces, leaving at least 33 of the attackers dead. The number of deaths on the Iraqi side is not reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Attackers fire at the construction site of the Hlaignbwe Dam in Myanmar, killing a Thai worker
description: Unknown attackers fire mortars or artillery shells at the construction site of the Hlaignbwe Dam on the Salween River in Myanmar, killing a Thai worker. Attackers are suspected to be from the Karen National Union group.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Australian man murdered in fight over water restrictions
description: A 36-year-old Australian is charged with murder after killing a man during a fight over water restrictions in Sydney. A number of incidents have been reported following ten years of drought and water restrictions, leading scholars to suggest a "link between persistent urban water restrictions and civil unrest."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ABC News 2007 ; Crase 2009

title: Bomb placed on water meter kills four police officers in Colombia, while another under a car injures ten
description: A bomb placed on a water meter in Cielo Gonzalez Villa, Neiva, Colombia detonates, killing four police officers. On the same day, another bomb placed under a car detonates in front of a building occupied by the local mayor, injuring ten people. The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) is suspected of the crimes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018: Kraul 2007

title: Conflicts in Burkina Faso
description: Declining rainfall has led to growing fights between animal herders and farmers with competing needs in Burkina Faso. In August, 2007 people are forced to flee their homes by fighting in Zounweogo province.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA) 2007

title: Director-general of water projects killed by gunmen in Iraq
description: The director-general of water projects in Badush, Iraq is shot and killed by gunmen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Injuries at protest in Orissa, India
description: Thousands of farmers breach security and storm the area of Hirakud dam to protest allocation of water to industry. Minor injuries are reported during the conflict between the farmers and police.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Statesman News Service 2007

title: Israel's sanctions against Gaza cause water shortages
description: Israel's sanctions against Gaza cause water shortages and a growing public health risk. In particular, restrictions on fuel, spare parts, and maintenance equipment threaten the functioning of Gaza's already limited water and sanitation system.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Oxfam 2007

title: Mortar fired at water-treatment plant in Iraq
description: A mortar is fired at a water treatment plant in Baghdad, Iraq. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Protestors block main road in response to water diversion in Egypt
description: In 2007 and 2008, shortages of drinking water provoke demonstrations in towns and villages in the Nile Delta: participants speak of a "Revolution of the Thirsty." Protestors block the main coastal road after the regional water company diverted water from farming and fishing towns to affluent resort communities. Riot police are sent to quell the disturbances.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Marfleet 2011 ; Piper 2012 ; Salehyan et al 2014

title: Protests against the Kajbar Dam in Sudan turn violent
description: Villagers of ethnic minority Nubians set to loose their homeland in the Sudan stage protests against Kajbar Dam; four villagers are killed by government militia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bosshard 2009 ; International Rivers n.d.

title: Soldiers threaten to throw woman into a well and drown her if she does not comply
description: A 20-year-old woman reports that prior to being beaten by military forces, she was threatened with drowning in a well if she does not comply. This report is associated with reports soldiers guarding water holes and of other human rights abuses by the Ethiopian military from their campaign to defeat the Ogaden National Liberation Front.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Human Rights Watch 2008

title: Someone sabotages a Sacramento River water canal by installing unauthorized software and damaging a computer
description: Someone sabotages a water canal that diverts water from the Sacramento River, California, by installing unauthorized software and damaging a computer.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness 2009

title: Suspected Islamist separatists detonate an explosive at the Waeng Hydro Station in Thailand
description: Suspected Islamist separatists detonate an explosive at the Waeng Hydro Station in Thailand. The explosion damages the control station, but causes no injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Taliban fighters from Pakistan attack a major Afghanistan dam
description: At least 700 Taliban fighters cross from Pakistan into Afghanistan to attack Kajaki Dam, a major source of electricity, according to reports from a provincial governor.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2007

title: Tampering of bottled water in Toronto, Canada
description: A Toronto, Canada man previously accused of attempted murder and illegal possession of explosives is charged with eight more counts of attempted murder after allegedly tampering with bottled water, which he injected with an unspecified liquid.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Toronto Star 2007

title: The Kajaki Dam is the subject of fighting between coalition forces and Taliban insurgents
description: In February 2007, the Kajaki Dam is the focus of fighting between coalition forces and Taliban insurgents, as part of Operation Kryptonite. The intention of the operation was to clear the area around the Kajakai Dam of Taliban fighters so the power generation station could be reopened. The Taliban destroy or dismantle parts of the dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2007

title: Tigris River polluted after bomb strikes oil pipeline in Iraq
description: The Tigris River is polluted with oil after a bomb strikes a pipeline near Baiji, Iraq. The river supplies drinking water for nearby communities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Two people wounded by bomb at local watering hole in Algeria
description: Two people are wounded when a bomb explodes at a local watering hole in Jijel, Algeria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water distribution facility warehouse burnt down in Thailand
description: A warehouse of a water distribution facility is burnt down in Yala Province, Thailand. Islamic insurgents seeking independence from Thailand are the suspected arsonists.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Water pipeline and gas pipeline damaged by explosion in Pakistan
description: Water supply is disrupted when a water pipeline and nearby gas pipeline are blown up in Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Workers constructing water pipe attacked; two killed in Iraq
description: A bomb placed along a road kills two workers and wounds five others as they lay water pipes in Tal Afar, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Workers fixing a water pipe killed in Iraq
description: Two workers fixing a water pipe in Baghdad, Iraq, are killed in an event that is reported as either a drive-by shooting or a bomb explosion. The pipeline was being fixed from an attack a month earlier.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: A community organizer in Ecuador working to stop the Baba Dam is killed
