description: In Ecuador, community organizers against the Baba Dam receive death threats. One of the threats materializes when one of the organizers is found dead at the dam site.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: A local community in Peru takes control of dam outlet to prevent loss of water supply
description: Over 100 villagers and farmers from the local community near Lake Paron in Peru use force to remove employees and take over the outlet controls of the lake after the lake had been drained by nearly 50% by the operator of the controls, a subsidiary of Duke Energy International, for hydropower operations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Aiello 2009

title: Assailants attempt to damage a water pump outside of a refugee camp in Darfur
description: At the Hassa Hissa camp near Zalinjay, Gharb Darfur, Sudan, ten assailants attempt to damage a water pump outside of an internally displaced person (IDP) camp. The armed men open fire on the pump and set fire to the pump and five generators. The assailants fight with occupants of the camp, wounding one. No group claims responsibility, although it is widely believed the Janjaweed Militia is responsible.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200812010034

title: Assailants set fire to two water tanker trucks in Muqur, Badghis, Afghanistan
description: Assailants set fire to two water tanker trucks in Muqur, Badghis, Afghanistan, killing one driver, wounding two others and destroying the two trucks. No group claims responsibility, although the Taliban is widely believed to be responsible.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200806110020

title: Bomb detonates in front of drinking water office in Nepal
description: Unidentified persons detonate a bomb in front of the drinking water office in Tripureshwor, Nepal. No casualties or damage are reported, and no group claims responsibility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200804050020

title: China cracks down on Tibet with implications for wide regional water control and management
description: China launches a political crackdown in Tibet. At least some observers have noted the importance of Tibet for the water resources of China, though the political complications between Tibet and China extend far beyond water. As noted: "Tibet is referred to in some circles as the "world's water tower' ; the Tibetan plateau is home to vast reserves of glaciated water, the sources of 10 of the largest rivers in Asia, including the Yellow, Yangtze, Mekong, Brahmaputra, Salween, Hindus and Sutlej among others. By some estimates, the Tibetan plateau is the source of fresh water for fully a quarter of the world's population."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sharife 2008

title: Confrontations occur along border of Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan over water resources
description: Disputes over unclear borders and poor communications lead to a series of confrontations over water resources in a border area of Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. The confrontations with Kyrgyz border guards occur when villagers from Isfara Tajikistan cross into the southern Batken district of Kyrgyzstan to remove a dam blocking an irrigation canal preventing water from reaching the Tajik village of Hoja Alo. The dam is located in an area where the boundary line between the two states has not been agreed. Actions by Kyrgyzstan cut off irrigation water to Tajikistan during the spring growing season.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kadykeev 2008

title: Driver of a water tanker truck killed in Afghanistan
description: A driver of a water tanker truck owned by an aid agency is killed while driving. Local officials place blame on Taliban militants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Explosive device detonates destroying a tube well in Pakistan
description: At Kachhi canal project in Lund Nullah near Sui, Balochistan Province, Pakistan, unknown assailants detonate an explosive device destroying a tube well. No casualties or motive are reported. No group claims responsibility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200804190021

title: Four killed in Kenya over dispute over boreholes
description: Fighting over boreholes in arid northern Kenya kills at least four people as competition for resources grows in the drought-hit region between the Murulle and Garre clans in El Wak, Mandera District.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ali and Wallis 2008

title: Iraqi water station destroyed
description: A water station under construction is destroyed in an attack by an unidentified gunman. Explosives are also placed on the road near the project, injuring one person. The station was going to provide potable water to four villages that were at a distance from the Tigris River, east of Dalouiya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Berwani 2008

title: Militants blow up a section of a water pipeline in Iraq
description: Militants blow up a section of a water pipeline in Baghdad, Iraq. The explosion tears an 18-inch hole in the pipe that carries drinking water to Baghdad's Adhamiyah, Rusafa, and Karrada districts. No casualties are reported and no group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200810300021

title: Multiple civilians killed by remotely-triggered bombs targeting water trucks in Ethiopia
description: At least two water trucks being used to deliver supplies to the Ethiopian army are targeted by remotely-triggered bombs. At least four civilians are killed and another eight are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Niger Basin Water Charter Adopted
description: Heads of State of the Niger Basin Authority adopt the Niger Basin Water Charter at a summit in Niamey, promoting equitable and sustainable water resources management and entering into force in 2010.
countries: Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Chad
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Niger Basin Water Charter, 8th Summit of Heads of State and Government, Niamey (2008).

title: Riots break out in Somaliland when water drilling rig is removed
description: Riots break out after a water drilling rig that had been drilling water wells for one community in the capital is transferred by government authorities to the western part of the country. Five people died and fifteen are wounded in the demonstration.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Jama 2014

title: Security forces open fire on water privatization protesters in Mali
description: One person is killed and five injured when security forces open fire on protests over an attempt to privatize water services in Lere, northwestern Mali.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2008

title: Taliban threatens water supply dam in Pakistan
description: In October, the Taliban threatens to blow up Warsak Dam, the main water supply for Peshawar, Pakistan during a government offensive in the region.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Perlez and Shah 2008

title: Tipaimukh Dam, India is attacked by Hmar militants
description: Hmar People’s Convention-Democracy (HPC-D) militants attack and damage dam equipment installed at the Tipaimukh Multi-Purpose Hydel Project in the state of Manipur, India. The HPC-D said in a statement that the ongoing drilling work at the site is against the land, rights, and dignity of the Hmar people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nabi Dar and Alam 2022 ; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Unknown gunmen kidnap four Sudanese government drivers of the state water corporation
description: Unknown gunmen kidnap four Sudanese government drivers of the state water corporation in Um Tajok, Darfur and steal a drilling rig. It is not known if the kidnapped persons and drilling rig are returned.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200803200009

title: Unknown militants in Afghanistan attack an aid agency's water tanker
description: Unknown militants fire mortars at an aid agency's water tanker, then kill the driver and steal his tanker in an undisclosed location in eastern Afghanistan. No property damage is reported and no one claims responsibility for the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200805200002

title: Violent protests in Nigeria over the price of water
description: A protest over the price of water in Nyanya, Abuja, Nigeria results in violence, including the beating of water vendors.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yakubu 2008

title: Water aid workers kidnapped in Somalia
description: Five aid workers, employed by the charity Water for Life, are kidnapped at gunpoint in Somalia. This is one of the first instances of Somali natives being kidnapped, as well as one of the first instances of a woman being kidnapped.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018 ; New Humanitarian, The 2008

title: Water delivery pipelines destroyed in protest over water transfers in Yemen
description: Pipelines are destroyed in Yemen by locals protesting the extraction of water in Abyan for piping to Aden.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hall 2010

title: A bomb placed at water station kills six, including five children, in Khost City, Afghanistan
description: A remote control bomb placed at a water distribution station detonates, killing six, including five children, in Khost City, Afghanistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Pashtun Valley 2009 ; Blogger 2009

title: An improvised explosive device attached to a water tanker explodes in Iraq
description: An improvised explosive device attached to a water tanker in the al-Mahawii district of the Babel province explodes, wounding the driver. The blast causes severe damage to the tanker. No one claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200912110015

title: Assailants detonate an improvised explosive device targeting a civilian water truck
description: On Sunday morning, in Marawara, Konar, Afghanistan, assailants detonate an improvised explosive device targeting a civilian water truck, wounding four civilians and damaging one truck. No group claims responsibility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200903070013

title: Attack on electrical grid in Pakistan cuts off water for multiple water wells
description: Insecurity in northwestern Pakistan leads to a rocket attack on on the electrical grid cutting off 36 bore-holes that supplied water to Mingora town, Pakistan. Citizens resort to collecting water from contaminated surface-water sources, resulting in an outbreak of diarrhoeal disease.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNICEF 2021

title: Bomb damages water treatment plant, leaving community without water in Colombia
description: A bomb planted at a water treatment plant explodes damaging the plant and wounding two police officers in Villavicencio, Colombia. The town is left without water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Brazilian landowners fight with indigenous tribe over land and water
description: A dispute over water and land consider sacred by the indigenous Guarani-Kaiowa tribe begins with nearby landowners attempting to gain control over disputed land. The dispute continues until at least 2012 and leads to several deaths.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2012a

title: Drought and water inequities spark killings India
description: A family in Madhya Pradesh state in India is killed by a mob for illegally drawing water from a municipal pipe. Others run to collect water for themselves before the pipe runs out. Drought and inequality in water distribution lead to increasing conflict in the region. Indian media report more than 50 violent clashes in the state capital, Bhopal during May alone. Since January, 12 people are killed and even more injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Singh 2009

title: During kidnapping by Taliban in Afghanistan, water tank destroyed
description: A group of four employees of a construction company in Kunar province, Afghanistan are kidnapped by the Taliban. The kidnappers also destroy a water tank during the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Energy and Water Department attacked by suicide bombers, killing six and injuring dozens in Afghanistan
description: Six civilians die and approximately 30 others are injured when two suicide bombers attack the building of the Energy and Water Department in Khost City, Afghanistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; RAND Database of Worldwide Terrorism Incidents 2018

title: Environmental activist in a region flooded by Tucurui Dam killed in Brazil
description: After a region of Brazil was flooded by the Tucurui Dam, Raimundo Nonato do Carmo helped to lead the fight for environmental protection of the flooded and destroyed land. He was shot in a drive-by attack and killed in 2009.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Homemade bomb is planted inside the gates of the Metro Water District, Philippines
description: On Wednesday, ordnance experts defuse a homemade bomb planted on a bench inside the gates of the Metro Water District, a government-run building at Cotabato, Philippines. No damage or casualties occur. No group claims of responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 200904290018

title: Hydroelectric construction company hires armed private security to quell local opposition and violence in Guatemala
description: In the Q'anjob'al and Chug Territory of northern Huehuetenango, Guatemala, three proposed hydroelectric projects supported by the national government incite strong local opposition. The hydroelectric construction company hires armed private security personnel to quell confrontations and acts of vandalism and violence over three years.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Environmental Justice Atlas 2018

title: Local anti-dam activist in Colombia killed in his home
description: A community leader involved in anti-dam protests that threatened the Magdalena River in Colombia, Honorio Llorente Merendez, is shot and killed in his home in Puente Sogamoso.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Man killed in Mumbai, India protest over water cuts
description: Police clash with hundreds of Mumbai, India residents protesting water cuts. One man is killed and a dozen others injured. Mumbai authorities are forced to ration supplies after the worst monsoon season in decades.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Chandran 2009

title: North Korea dam release kills six in South Korea
description: Without previous warning, North Korea releases 40 million cubic meters of water from the Hwanggag dam, causing a flash flood on the Imjin River. In South Korea, at least 6 fisherman and campers are drowned. North Korea claims that the water had to be urgently released and promises to warn the South of future releases. South Korea fears that North Korea could use the water of the dam as a weapon during a violent conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Choe 2009

title: One dead in South Yemen protest over water cuts
description: At least one Yemeni is killed and three wounded in clashes with police in Aden in southern Yemen over the cutting off of water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2009

title: Police use live ammunition against demonstrators protesting water shortages in Somaliland
description: Police use live ammunition against demonstrators in the southern part of Hargeisa. Residents of Ahmed Dhagah district in Hargeisa, mostly women and children, take to the streets protesting severe water shortages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Somaliland Globe 2009

title: Suspected Maoists set fire to the power station at the Balimela Dam, India
description: Suspected Maoists set fire to the power station at the Balimela Dam, India, damaging equipment and water intake tunnels. The attackers say the attack is in retaliation for the failure to provide electricity and communications utilities to local villages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan threaten to contaminate local water resources
description: The Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) threatens to contaminate local water resources in a letter faxed to the Directorate of Military Lands and Cantonments in Rawalpindi, Pakistan. The letter stated that the TTP had procured 200 liters of a poisonous material that would be used to contaminate water sources and reservoirs unless the Army stopped military operations in South Waziristan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Roul 2010 ; Laskar 2009

title: Turkey-Iraq and Turkey-Syria Water MoUs
description: Turkey signs Memoranda of Understanding on water management with both Iraq and Syria, and jointly agrees with Syria to build a dam on the shared Orontes River in Hatay province, marking a diplomatic thaw in the Tigris-Euphrates basin.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Strategic Cooperation Council Protocols between Turkey, Iraq, and Syria (2009).

title: Village attacked in Ethiopian water supply conflict
description: Ethiopian Somalis attack a Borana community in the Oromia region over ownership of a new borehole being drilled on the disputed border between them. Three people from the Oromia village of Kafa are killed and seven injured, and the entire community driven from their homes. The drilling rig is destroyed, as well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2009

title: Water trucks contaminated with cyanide in Afghanistan
description: Water trucks supplying water to U.S. military forces in Afghanistan are contaminated with cyanide.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Afghan War Diary/Wikileaks 2009

title: 2010-2022: Violent dispute over corporate mine in Honduras national park leads to 100+ deaths and many arrests
description: From 2010 to 2022 in Honduras, a major violent dispute ensues over the development of a mine controlled by the Dinant Corporation in Carlos Escaleras National Park. The dispute leads to more than one hundred deaths, several attacks on community activists and environmentalists, and many arrests. The mine threatens land and water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Olson 2020 ; 2022

title: A series of attacks on hydropower facilities in Myanmar are reported, including on the Thawt Yin Kha Dam
description: Grenade attacks on the construction site of the Thawt Yin Kha Dam in Myanmar injure at least four. The attacks are claimed by the Karen National Liberation Army with the intent of destroying the project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: An improvised explosive device detonates at a potable water plant in Iraq
description: In the Abu Ghurayb neighborhood of Baghdad city, Baghdad province Iraq, two government employees are killed and another is wounded when an improvised explosive device detonates at a potable water plant. The amount of damage from the attack is unknown. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201012020006

title: Army troops in Colombia locate and defuse three bombs to be used against a town's aqueduct
description: Army troops locate and defuse three bombs suspected to be planted by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia's (FARC) 6th Front in Cajibio, Cauca, Colombia. According to authorities, the explosives were going to be used against the town's aqueduct. No casualties or damages are reported and no group claims responsibility for the attempted bombing attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201001280009

title: Bomb in water truck kills three in Afghanistan
description: A remote-controlled bomb hidden in a water truck kills three people, including two children, in the eastern Afghan province of Khost, which borders Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2009

title: Fighting in Pakistan over irrigation water
description: More than 100 are dead and scores injured following two weeks of tribal fighting in Parachinar in the Kurram region of Pakistan, near the Afghanistan border. The conflict over irrigation water began as the Shalozan Tangi tribe cut off supplies to the Shalozan tribe. Some report that al Qaeda may be involved; others claim sectarian violence is to blame as one group is Sunni Muslim and the other Shiite.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Express Tribune, The 2010 ; Associated Press (AP) 2010

title: Guatemalan mine protestors shot
description: Two unidentified gunmen on a motorbike shoot an activist protesting the impacts of mining on water quality and local water rights in Guatemala.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Amnesty International 2012

title: Gunmen kill two guards and detonate four explosives at the Baksanskaya Hydropower Plant, Russia, destroying two generators
description: Four gunmen attack a police station outside the Baksan Hydropower Plant, Russia, killing two facility guards and detonating four explosives, destroying two generators. A fifth explosive was later neutralized. Officials attribute the attack to the Baksan Dzhamaat group and two members are killed five days after the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Injuries and a death are reported during protests over water contamination from gold mining near Lake Conococha in Peru
description: Communities concerned with water contamination of Lake Conococha, both a water source and cultural icon, are met with violence from local police forces as they protest gold mining in the region. At least one person is reported dead and four others injured from the interaction.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Stark Guillen and Brady 2012

title: Local police find remains of Molotov Cocktails detonated at the Black Rock Dam, Connecticut, United States
description: Local police officials discover the remains of two devices that had detonated on an access road near the dam. Police identified the devices as Molotov Cocktails—IEDs made from gasoline-filled bottles. No injuries or damage to the dam are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Militants blow up a water supply tube-well
description: In Lakaro area of Mohmand, Federally Administered Tribal Areas, Pakistan, Tehrik-e-Taliban (TTP) militants blow up a water supply tube-well. TTP claims responsibility for the attack saying the tube-well is used for provision of drinking water to Security Forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201011040001

title: Militants blow up pump houses belonging to the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) and to the railways
description: On Monday, in the Karrampada area of West Singbhum, Jharkhand, India, suspected Communist Party of India - Maoist (CPI-Maoist) militants blow up two pump houses, one belonging to the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) and the other to the railways. Water supply is affected in the area as a result of the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201004190016

title: More than 30 armed men detonate an improvised explosive device at the electric transformer of a pump house in the Philippines
description: At night in Victorias City, Negros Occidental, Philippines, more than 30 armed men detonate an improvised explosive device at the electric transformer of Malago Pump House owned by the Victorias Milling Company sugar refinery before setting it on fire. The damage is initially placed at P400,000 ($9,246 USD). No casualties are reported. New Peoples Army militants claim responsibility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201010050009

title: Pakistan irrigation dispute kills 116
description: A water dispute in Pakistan's tribal region leads to 116 deaths. In early September, the Mangal tribe cut off the supply of irrigation water to lands used by the neighboring Tori tribe, leading to fighting.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; CNN 2010

title: Pakistani police fire on protesters who are demanding share of royalties from a new dam project, killing two
description: While a new dam is under construction in Pakistan, protests erupt in Chilas where people are demanding their share of royalties from the dam. Two protestors are killed, others are injured, and property of the state is damaged and destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ahmed 2010 ; International Rivers n.d.

title: Protestors over land and water killed and injured in India
description: At least three deaths and dozens of injuries are reported during protests over land and water given away for a power plant in Sompeta in Srikakulam district in Andhra Pradesh, India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hindu, The 2011

title: Severe flooding strengthens militant groups in Pakistan
description: Militant groups in Pakistan take advantage of severe flooding to reorganize and gain political power. Military resources in the country have been diverted to humanitarian relief efforts.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Waraich 2010

title: The Myitsone Dam, Myanmar is attacked by locals opposed to dam projects, killing at least one
description: Myanmar’s Myitsone Dam, in Kachin State, is the site of major local opposition to dam projects. In 2010, 10 bombs explode around the dam site, killing at least one Chinese worker. Construction is suspended by the Myanmar government in 2011 in response to a widespread opposition campaign.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nabi Dar and Alam 2022

title: Two unknown gunmen riding a motorbike fire upon the driver of a water tanker
description: On an evening in January, two unknown gunmen riding a motorbike fire upon the driver of a water tanker in Hariana Colony, Karachi, Pakistan. The driver, Noor Shah, is killed and the tanker rams into a moving auto-rickshaw with four people on board. Eight-year-old Unair dies and his younger brother is wounded. Both attackers escape. No group claims responsibility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201001310008

title: Unidentified militants detonate an improvised explosive device targeting a water tanker
description: On Thursday, in the town of al-Qaim in Iraq's Anbar province, a driver and two civilians are wounded and a water tanker truck is damaged when unidentified militants detonate an improvised explosive device targeting a water tanker. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201005060012

title: Violent confrontations occur in the West Bank over Israeli actions limiting water supply to new West Bank development
description: The construction and completion of a billion-dollar new middle-class Palestinian city of Rawabi in the West Bank is delayed for years while the Israeli government withholds access to basic water supplies. The delay is due, in part, to a larger dispute over the actions of the Israeli-Palestinian Joint Water Committee. In March 2015, a limited supply of water to Rawabi is finally approved, sufficient only for the 640 families that currently live there but far less than what will be needed for the expected 25,000 residents that the city will eventually house. Violent confrontations over this dispute occur regularly during this period.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shuttleworth 2015

title: Violent water protest in India
description: A protest about water shortages in the National Capital Territory of Delhi in India leads to violence. Erratic water supply and cutoffs in the Kondli area of Mayur Vihar in East Delhi causes a violent protest and several injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gosh 2010

title: Water disputes between Iran and Afghanistan escalate
description: Disputes over water between Iran and Afghanistan are escalating. One Afghan newspaper, Weesa, suggests that Iran blocked the transport of fuel oil to Afghanistan in 2010 as a means to put more pressure on the country over water. An Iranian editorial calls for bolder action by the Foreign Ministry and states that any aid to Afghanistan should be linked to "Iran's rights to water."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Aman 2013 ; Etedaalier 2011 ; Muhammadi 2011 ; Radio Free Europe 2011

title: A water tank is damaged by a homemade bomb in Pakistan
description: Sometime during the night between December 16 and December 17, 2011, a water tank is damaged by a homemade bomb in the area of Mandeo in the district of Bannu, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. No deaths or injuries occur. No claim of responsibility is reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201112170024

title: Drought contributes to tensions and the civil war in Syria
description: Severe political conflict in Syria has been aggravated by a multi-year drought gripping the region. More than 1.5 million people "mostly farmers and their families" have moved to cities and their outskirts. In 2008, US diplomats in Syria warn that the influx of rural people to cities "could act as a multiplier on social and economic pressures already at play and undermine stability in Syria." Political unrest begins in March 2011 in Dara'a, and soon escalates into civil war to overturn the regime of President Bashar al-Assad and the ruling Ba'ath Party.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mohtadi 2012 ; Worth 2010 ; Femia and Werrell 2012 ; Gleick 2014

title: Four famers killed in Tanzania over water resource dispute
description: Conflicts over water are increasing in the Pangani River Basin in northeastern Tanzania between farmers and herders over dwindling water resources. In 2011 in Mbuguni village, four farmers are hacked to death by angry Maasai morans (warriors) as they tried to stop a group of cattle from trampling on maize seedlings.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Makoye 2013

title: Gaddafi cuts of water to Libya's capital
description: During the 2011 Libyan Civil War, forces loyal to dictator Muammar Gaddafi gain control of a water operations center and cut off water supply to the capital. The system controls Libya's Great Manmade River, which is a system of pumps, pipes, and canals that brings water from distant aquifers to Tripoli and other cities. Half the country is left without running water, prompting the UN and neighboring countries to mobilize tanker ships to deliver water to coastal cities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Walton 2012 ; United Press International (UPI) 2011

title: Guards at the Machlagho Dam construction site in Afghanistan are attacked and killed
description: Armed militants attack and kill guards at the Machlagho Dam construction site in Afghanistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Hacker targets water plant in South Houston, Texas
description: A hacker targets a water plant in South Houston following earlier news (later discounted) of an electronic attack on an Illinois water plant, reportedly to raise awareness of concerns over lax security for critical infrastructure. The breach occurs after the attackers hack into supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) software used by the utility, and uses IP addresses that originated in Russia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mills 2011

title: Iran reportedly attempts to enlist the Taliban to blow up a dam on the Helmand River in Afghanistan
description: In 2011, a Taliban commander reportedly claims that Iran offered him $50,000 to blow up the Kamal Khan dam in Afghanistan on the Helmand River, shared with Iran.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Glinski 2020

title: Israel destroys Palestinians' water pumps and wells
description: Israel's military destroys nine water tanks in the Bedouin village of Amniyr in the South Hebron Hills, in the West Bank, Palestine. Later, soldiers destroy pumps and wells in the Jordan Valley villages of Al-Nasriyah, Al-Aqrabiyah, and Beit Hassan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Aburawa 2011

title: Israeli settlers destroy wells in attack on West Bank village
description: Israelis from nearby settlements attack Qasra, a West Bank village of 6,000, destroying crops and a water well. Attackers previously burned down a mosque and damaged hundreds of olive trees.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bsharat and Ramadan 2011

title: Militants set fire to a water well and two water pumps in Somalia
description: Militants set fire to a water well and two water pumps on the outskirts of Garbaharey, Gedo, Somalia. No casualties are reported and the attack causes an unknown amount of damage. No group claims responsibility, but the militant group al-Shabaab is thought to be responsible for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201108270005

title: Multiple attacks on Libyan water networks disrupt supply.
description: NATO bombs a plant that builds pipelines for the Great Manmade River project that carries water from southern groundwater to coastal cities. Major water networks are disrupted in this conflict, which affects access to safe drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene throughout Libya. Armed groups attack water wells cutting off water to civilians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2016

title: NATO attacks water pipe factory in Libya
description: NATO forces attack a factory that produces pipes for the "Great Man-Made River" water-supply pipeline near Brega, Libya, reporting that it was used as a base for military operations and the launching of missiles.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Center for Research on Globalization (CRG) 2013 ; Human Rights Investigations (HRI) 2011 ; Water Technology n.d.

title: Residential water tanks and water pipes in Dara'a, Syria are deliberately damaged by military and security forces
description: Residential water tanks and water pipes in Dara'a, Syria are deliberately damaged by military and security forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2011

title: Rocket-propelled grenades are fired at the Thawt Yin Kha Dam in Myanmar
description: Unknown attackers fire rocket-propelled grenades at the Thawt Yin Kha dam construction site in Myanmar.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S Department of Homeland Security 2012

title: Solomon Islands women attacked while fetching water
description: Amnesty International reports that women in the slums of the Solomon Islands must walk over a kilometer to fetch clean water and are "continually harassed, attacked, and raped." A survey shows that 92 percent of households do not have a tap in their home, and that local water sources are often polluted, forcing women to walk through areas which are unsafe.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Amnesty International 2011

title: Unidentified militants blow up a tube-well in Pakistan
description: On Friday, in Doog village in South Waziristan, Federally Administered Tribal Areas, Pakistan, unidentified militants blow up a tube-well, resulting in no casualties and causing an unknown amount of property damage. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201104010003

title: Unidentified militants blow up a water pump in India
description: In Mogahataburu village in West Singhbhum, Jharkhand, India, unidentified militants blow up a water pump, causing an unknown amount of property damage but resulting in no casualties. The specific motive for the attack is unknown; however, it is believed the bombing is to protest the ongoing operation against militants in Saranda forest. No group claims responsibility, but it is suspected that Communist Party of India-Maoist (CPI-M) militants are responsible.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201103180002

title: Yemen damages citizens' water tanks during uprising
description: Violence in Yemen's capital Sana'a leads to "acute water and power shortages, forcing residents to rely on power generators and buy water extracted from wells and sold on a thriving black market." The violence arose during the Yemeni uprising that occurred during the Arab Spring protests across the Middle East. During the violence, government soldiers shelled neighborhoods and destroyed many rooftop water tanks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shah 2012

title: A landmine explodes targeting a tanker providing water to Transitional Federal Government (TFG) soldiers, Somalia
description: A landmine explodes in Luuq town, Gedo Region, Somalia. The landmine is targeting a tanker providing water to Transitional Federal Government (TFG) soldiers. Three people are killed and an unknown number of people are injured in the attack. No group claims responsibility for the incident, although unnamed sources suspect Al-Shabaab.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201201150014

title: A water tanker is damaged when it is targeted by a roadside bomb
description: A water tanker is damaged when it is targeted by a roadside bomb in Khash Rod district, Nimruz province, Afghanistan. One person is killed and another wounded in the attack, for which no group claims responsibility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201203170018

title: Afghani terrorists poison water at girls' school
description: Up to 150 schoolgirls are reported sickened by poison in a school water supply in an intentional attack thought to be carried out by religious conservatives opposed to the education of women.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hamid 2012b

title: An explosive device detonates and damages a tube well and surrounding area in Pakistan
description: An explosive device detonates and damages a tube well, a transmission line, and a mosque in Lakki Marwat city, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan. There are no casualties reported, and no group claims responsibility for this incident. A school is also damaged in an explosion in the same location on this day.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201203150002

title: An explosive device detonates in a canal in the Philippines
description: An explosive device detonates in a canal in barangay Poblacion, M'lang town, North Cotabato province, Philippines. No casualties are reported in the blast. No group claims responsibility for this incident; however, police suspect the Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Movement (BIFM).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201208110008

title: An explosive device detonates near a water pipeline in Afghanistan
description: An explosive device detonates near a water pipeline in Pul-e-Alam district, Logar province, Afghanistan. Five people, including two Afghan police officers, are killed in the attack, and four people, including two Afghan police officers, are injured. No group claims responsibility; however, one person is arrested in connection with the incident and admits to remotely detonating the device.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201208010047

title: An explosive device planted in a water spring detonates as a group of children are grazing animals in Afghanistan
description: An explosive device planted in a water spring detonates as a group of children are grazing animals in Taywara district, Ghor province, Afghanistan. Seven children are killed in the blast. No group claims responsibility for the incident; however, sources attribute it to the Taliban.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201207240010 ; Shah 2012

title: An explosive device targeting a well in Pakistan detonates prematurely as the assailant is planting it
description: An explosive device detonates prematurely as the assailant is planting it in Wocha Khwara village, Federally Administered Tribal Areas, Pakistan. The device is targeting a fresh water well; the assailant is killed in the blast. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201205040033

title: Angry demonstrators protest over water supply in Tunisia
description: In June 18-19, demonstrators demanding a solution to a dried up water supply block the main road near Tozeur, Tunisia, leading to clashes with police.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Salehyan et al 2014

title: Assailants bomb a government water tank in Pakistan
description: Assailants bomb a government water tank in the Aka Khel area of Bara tehsil, Federally Administered Tribal Areas, Pakistan. There are no reported casualties; however, the water tank is destroyed in the blast. No group claims responsibility for the incident; however, police arrest one individual in connection with the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201212060017

title: Assailants fire a mortar round, striking a water facility
description: Assailants fire a mortar round, striking a water facility in Mosul city, Nineveh governorate, Iraq. One security guard is killed in the attack, and the facility is damaged. This is one of 32 coordinated incidents across Iraq on the same day. Al-Qa'ida in Iraq claims responsibility for the attacks, stating that they are in retaliation for the torture and genocide that Sunni civilians face in Iraqi prisons.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201202230016

title: Assailants open fire on security personnel escorting a water tanker convoy
description: Assailants open fire on security personnel escorting a Freeport Indonesia water tanker convoy in Mimika district, Papua province, Indonesia. There are no reported casualties, but the vehicles are damaged. This is one of two coordinated attacks on this convoy on this day, neither of which are claimed by any group.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201204140023

title: Attack on construction facilities at Turkish dams
description: 22 trucks are set on fire at dam sites in Turkey, in attacks attributed to Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) militants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Stratfor 2016

title: Brazilian landowners poison tribe's water
description: Brazil's federal police respond to reports that water used by the indigenous Guarani-Kaiowa tribe was poisoned by nearby landowners. The dispute began in 2009 and has led to the deaths of three tribesmen, who say the water runs through sacred land.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2012a

title: Chinese protestors challenge Japanese factory for discharging contaminated wastewater
description: In July, thousands of protesters take to the streets in Qidong, Jiangsu Province to challenge a pipeline from a Japanese-owned paper factory that would discharge contaminated wastewater into the sea, potentially polluting a nearby fishery, and contaminating drinking water. Demonstrators clash with police and there are reports of damages to government buildings, cars, and other property. Fourteen people plead guilty to encouraging the riot in which dozens of police are injured and the local Communist party chief is stripped half-naked.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Economy 2013 ; Okudera 2012 ; Associated Press (AP) 2013a

title: Colorado River Reaches Sea for First Time in Decades
description: The Colorado River has not reached the Sea of Cortez (Gulf of California) for most of the preceding decades due to upstream US and Mexican water extraction. Environmental flows negotiations between the US and Mexico under the 1944 Treaty continue.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; IBWC Minute No. 319: Interim International Cooperative Measures in the Colorado River Basin (2012).

title: Deaths in water conflicts in Tanzania
description: Violence between farmers and pastoralists expands in Tanzania's southeastern Rufiji valley, a region hit by drought. A farmer is killed in a conflict with a herdsman over access to water in the southern regions of Lindi and Mtwara. Five more people die and many more are injured in subsequent violence. According to local sources, violence has worsened during the prolonged drought.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Makoye 2012

title: Demonstrations turn violent over water and power shortages in Guinea
description: Demonstrations over water and power shortages in Conakry, Fria, and Dinguiraye, Guinea, turn violent, with dozens injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Crisis Watch Database 2014

title: Disgruntled Egyptian irrigators kidnap tourists
description: Farmers from the Abu Simbel region in Egypt hold over 200 tourists hostage to protest inadequate irrigation water. The farmers capture the tourists after they visit nearby monuments, but release them after officials agree to a temporary release of water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Egypt Independent 2012

title: Egypt and Sudan allegedly target Ethiopia dam
description: Information is leaked about an alleged secret agreement that would allow Egypt to build an air base in Sudan to attack the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD). Egypt is concerned that the dam, under construction in Ethiopia just upstream of Sudan on the Blue Nile, would reduce flows into its territory. The news reports, strongly denied by Egypt, claim that Sudan would allow Egypt to launch attacks if diplomatic efforts fail to resolve water sharing between Egypt and Ethiopia. The allegations are based on an internal 2010 email made available by Wikileaks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sudan Tribune 2012 ; Al Arabiya News 2012

title: Escalating rhetoric and disputes over dams in central Asia
description: Tensions escalate over two proposed dams in central Asia: Kambarata-1 in Kyrgyzstan and the Rogun Dam in Tajikistan. These dams could affect water supplies in the downstream nations of Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, and Kazakhstan. Uzbekistan's president, Islam Karimov, says the dams could cause "not just serious confrontation, but even wars."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Economist, The 2012

title: Ethnic conflict in Kenya fueled by water
description: Extensive violence over water is reported in Kenya, with approximately 50 deaths in clashes between farmers and cattle herders. The conflict is part of a long-running dispute between Pokomo farmers and Orma, semi-nomadic cattle herders, over land and water. The current conflict is being exacerbated by Kenyan and foreign investment in vast tracts of land for food and biofuel cultivation, putting pressure on local resources. (See also entry in 2001.)
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2012a ; Al Jazeera 2012

title: Farmers clash with police over water transfers from Isfahan to Yazd, Iran. A water diversion pipe is destroyed.
description: Farmers in Varzaneh clash with police and break a water pipe that transports 50 million cubic meters of water per year from Isfahan to the neighboring province of Yazd, Iran.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Karimi and Nasiri 2018

title: Four protesters against the Barro Blanco Dam are killed after blocking the Inter-American Highway in Panama
description: Three protesters, Mauricio Mendez, Frankline Javilla, and an unnamed person are killed by government forces as they are blocking the Inter-American Highway in Panama in protest of the Barro Blanco Dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Husband and wife are murdered in Mexico for their defense of local water resources
description: Ismael Solorio Urrutia and his wife Manuela Solis Contreras are killed, likely for their defense of water near their community in Buenaventura, Chihuahua, Mexico, and their opposition to the El Cascabel mining company, a subsidiary of Canada's Mag Silver Corporation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lira 2018

title: In Somalia, attackers shoot at and set fire to the town's water pump, destroying the only viable water source
description: Assailants attack the police station in El Adde town, Gedo region, Somalia. The assailants open fire on the station, causing the Transitional Federal Government (TFG) forces posted there to return fire. There are no reported casualties in the incident. The attackers also shoot at and set fire to the town's water pump, destroying the only viable water source. No group claims responsibility, but locals attribute the attack to Al-Shabaab, believing that the incident is prompted by the presence of Kenyan Defense Forces (KDF) in the town.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201206030027

title: Indonesian mobs battle over water source
description: Violence over access to a water source in Maluku, Indonesia. Rival mobs from two villages attack one another "with sharp weapons, guns and explosives" causing several deaths and injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Antara 2012

title: Injuries during protest over dam releases in India's Cauvery River
description: Thousands of farmers in Karnataka try to prevent the release of water from two dams (Krishna Raja Sagar and Kabini) on the Kaveri River. Injuries to protestors and police are reported. The water releases are ordered by the Indian Supreme Court, which requires Karnataka to deliver water downstream state of Tamil Nadu despite severe drought. The dispute continues later in the year when Karnataka again halts releases.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Walton 2012 ; Indian Express, The 2012

title: Iran is accused of efforts to prevent construction of Kamal Khan Dam, Afghanistan
description: Shakila Hakimi, a member of the Nimroz provincial council in Afghanistan, accuses Iran in 2012 of conducting an insurgency in order to prevent construction of the Kamal Khan Dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Aman 2013 ; Etedaalier 2011 ; Muhammadi 2011 ; Radio Free Europe 2011

title: Islamist kill dam guards in Afghanistan
description: Islamist militants execute militia members defending the Machalgho Dam in eastern Afghanistan. The dam is being developed for irrigation and local power supply. This dispute is one of several surrounding the international waters of Afghanistan, Iran, and Pakistan, which share several rivers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mashal 2012

title: Killings in water conflicts in Brazil
description: Northeastern Brazil sees growing conflicts after severe drought reduces water availability. News agencies report that one person a day is being killed from "water wars," which involve locals fighting over scarce supplies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Catholic Online 2012

title: Man with known opposition to a dam in Bukidnon, Philippines, is shot and killed
description: A man who is known for his opposition to the Pulangi V dam project in Bukidnon, Phillippines is shot and killed by two people on a drive-by on a motorcycle. Mr. Margarito J. Cabal was a utlity worker and had reported being followed by police cars in the days leading up to his murder.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; OMCT 2012

title: Militants block work and attack water systems at the Wular Dam construction site in India
description: Militants block work at the Wular Conservation Project (Wular Dam) construction site in the Baramulla District of India and attack and sabotage water systems, and flood protection works in northern Kashmir. They attack engineers and workers and detonate explosives at the unfinished Tulbul Navigation Lock/Wular Dam - a project opposed by Pakistan. Indian officials suggest that these militants may have been sent by Pakistan because of concerns that the project is in violation of Pakistani interests under the Indus Water Treaty of 1960. Sources said that eight of the 16 militants who stopped work of the Project are Pakistani nationals. India says the dam is not in violation of the Treaty and would, if completed, be used only for transportation purposes. Pakistan believes the Indian control over Jhelum waters has the potential to disrupt the Pakistan-Upper Jhelum Canal, Upper Chenab Canal, and the Lower Bari Doab Canal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hamid 2012a ; Ul Hassan 2012

title: Moroccan villagers cut off water supply to local mine fearing shortage and pollution
description: A group of Moroccan villagers, including many women and children try to stop the water supply to a local silver mine. They shut down some of the main wells that supply water for mining citing concerns about water allocation and pollution. The facility in Imiter, a Berber village nestled in the High Atlas mountains, has been accused of drawing more than its fair share of water and polluting what it uses.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Brouksy 2012 ; Alami 2014

title: One dead and two injured during a confrontation over a dam project in Guatemala, sparking protests
description: On May 1, 2012, two security guards hired by a dam-building company are suspected of shooting three community members from Santa Cruz Barillas, Guatemala. One of the community members, Andres Pedro Miguel, dies, and two others are injured. The community members had been actively working to prevent the dam from being built. The death of Sr. Miguel sparks protests across the region. The Guatemalan government responds with military force, raiding citizen homes and jailing dissidents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; DeLuca 2012 ; Hernandez 2013 ; Reynolds 2015

title: Organizer against dam projects in Honduras is killed in his home by police
description: Police shoot and kill Santos Alberto Dominguez Benitez, a community organizer against local dam projects in Intibuca, Honduras.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Redaccion El Heraldo 2012

title: Police kill gold mine protestors in Peru
description: Several incidents of protests, injuries, and deaths are reported in regions of Peru where residents oppose large mines because of concerns over water quality and water rights. Police kill four protestors in clashes over the proposed Canadian-operated $5 billion dollar Minas Conga gold mine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2012a ; Yeager 2012

title: Protestors burn buildings at Belo Monte Dam site, Brazil
description: Work on the controversial $13 billion Belo Monte dam is halted after protesters burn buildings at three dam sites.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Borisov 2012

title: Protestors concerned about water quality and water rights are injured and 2 killed at Peru's Tintaya mine
description: Protests because of concerns over water quality and water rights around the Xstrata Tintaya copper mine lead to two deaths and 50 injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Aquino and Wade 2012

title: Somali insurgents poison peacekeepers' well
description: Somali Al Shabaab insurgents poison a well and damage water infrastructure near the port city of Kismayo, Somalia. Insurgents are fighting against Kenyan peacekeeping troops participating in the African Union mission in Somalia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Wabala 2012

title: South Africans riot over water and power
description: Protesters in poor communities of Cape Town, South Africa riot over inadequate water and power. Hundreds burn tires, destroy cars, and throw rocks at police in anger over the lack of basic services.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Xinhua News 2012b

title: Syrian Civil War battle damages Aleppo pipeline
description: During the Syrian Civil War, the major pipeline delivering water to the city of Aleppo is badly damaged. The city of three million suffers severe shortages of drinking water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2012

title: Syrian government attack on Tremseh starts with the cutting of electricity and water supply
description: Syrian government attack on Tremseh, Syria on 12 July 2012 starts with the cutting of electricity and water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2012

title: Syrian government attack on al-Haffe cuts water and electricity
description: Syrian government attack on al-Haffe cuts water and electricity.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2012

title: Syrian rebels capture dam
description: In November, Syrian rebels fighting the government of President Bashar al-Assad overrun government forces and capture the Tishrin hydroelectric dam on the Euphrates River, after days of heavy clashes. The dam supplies electricity to part of Syria and is considered strategically important to the Syrian regime.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mroue 2012

title: The Taliban detonate a bomb at the Kapisa Dam, Afghanistan, killing three
description: The Taliban detonate an explosive device at the Kapisa Dam construction site, Afghanistan, killing three and injuring four more.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Three killed in dispute over wells in Somalia
description: In August 2012, fighting between two clans in the Lower Juba region of south Somalia kills at least three people and wounds five. Reports from the village of Waraq (near the border with Kenya) indicate that the dispute began over the ownership of new water wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shabelle Media Network 2012

title: Two explosive devices placed in a well are discovered and defused in Pakistan
description: Two explosive devices placed in a well are discovered and defused in Nar Raza Khan village, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan. No group claims responsibility for the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201208130026

title: Uzbekistan cuts gas over Tajik dam project
description: Uzbekistan cuts natural gas deliveries to Tajikistan in retaliation over a Tajik hydroelectric dam which Uzbeks say will disrupt water supplies. Gas flows resumed after a new contract is signed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kozhevnikov 2012

title: Villagers protest contaminated water in Egypt
description: Villagers from the Nile Delta province of Menoufia north of Cairo briefly lock the Egyptian health minister and a provincial governor inside a hospital room in protest over contaminated water caused hundreds of residents to fall ill. Egypt's state-run news agency MENA says the number of sick people reached more than 400. The two are released with police intervention.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2012b

title: Violence between camel herders and farmers over access to water and concerns about water contamination leave one dead in Kenya
description: Several farmers from Mwatate, Kenya are attacked, one killed, by camel herders after attempts to chase camels from agricultural land. The camel herders have moved to the area to find land and water for their stock. Farmers are also concerned about the potential spread of disease and pollution of the local water sources from camel feces and urine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mghenyi 2018

title: Violence over water in Nairobi, Kenya's slums
description: Violence, including several deaths, occurs during disputes over access to water in the poorest slums around Nairobi, Kenya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Njeru 2012

title: Violent conflict among Kenyan and Ugandan herders
description: Tensions lead to violence between Uganda and Kenya after Kenyan Pokot herdsmen cross the border seeking water and pasture. In October, the Ugandan government sends 5,000 soldiers to control violence among pastoralists from the two countries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bii 2012

title: Violent protests over food and water in Mauritania
description: Protests and violence over water shortages occur in the capital of Mauritania, Nouakchott. By July 2012, over 70,000 Malian refuges were seeking asylum in Mauritania, putting pressure on scarce food and water supplies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Taha 2012

title: Violent protests over water shortages in Egypt
description: Public protests over drinking and irrigation water shortages take place across Egypt. Several protests turn violent: in Beni Suef, one person is killed and many injured during a conflict over irrigation water; in Minya, villagers clash with officials over water shortages and water pollution; in Faiyum, hundreds of people protesting water shortages block a highway and set fires.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; OOSKANews Correspondent 2012

title: Violent protests over water shortages in New Delhi
description: Scuffles and protests break out around New Delhi during the summer of 2012 as residents surround water delivery trucks and fight over water. The summer is the hottest in 33 years, leading to extensive energy and water shortages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2012b

title: Water clash on border of Mali and Burkina Faso
description: A clash along the border between Dogon villagers from Mali and nomadic Fulani herders from Burkina Faso kills at least 30 people, after an earlier agreement to share water and pasture land was revoked. Chaos following a military coup in March is partly responsible for the breakdown in law and order in Mali.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Xinhua News 2012a

title: Water-related violence in South Sudan refugee camp
description: Violence breaks out at water points in the Jamam refugee camp in South Sudan. Medicines Sans Frontieres reports that as many as 10 refugees die every day because of water shortages at refugee camps in South Sudan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; McNeish 2012 ; Ferrie 2012

title: Women assaulted for attempting to take well water in India
description: Women from the village of Rasooh are reportedly assaulted for attempting to take water from a village well. The tensions over water are related to long-standing tensions between caste groups but have been worsened by drought and water shortage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sharma 2014

title: Workers at the Gomal Zam Hydroelectric Dam in Pakistan are abducted by Tehrik-i-Taliban
description: About 12 Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan fighters kidnap eight workers at the Gomal Zam Hydroelectric Dam, in the Murtaza Goth area of Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: A drinking water facility in Georgia, U.S., is attacked and the treatment settings are changed risking quality of tap water
description: In April 2013, the drinking water facility of a small town in North Georgia is attacked. The attackers gain access to the monitoring system and change the fluorine and chlorine settings, leading the management company to advise the 400 residents not to use the tap water for a few days.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Boubaker 2021

title: Algerian protestors and police clash at protest over water shortages
description: Nineteen people are arrested in Algeria's Setif region when clashes erupt between protesters and police during a demonstration against water shortages. Around 300 protesters march on the town hall in Bouselam to demand improved water supplies and other local improvements. Clashes broke out when the security forces attempted to access the building by force, with 19 people arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2013

title: Areas of Deir ez-Zor, Syria lose access to water when an armed group cuts supplies of food, potable water, and other essentials
description: Areas of Deir ez-Zor, Syria lose access to water when an armed group cuts supplies of food, potable water, electricity and fuel. The use of untreated water from the river resulted in health problems in the civilian population.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2013a

title: Armed gang sabotages main water pipeline in Yemen
description: An armed gang sabotages the main water pipeline from Sana'a to Ta'izz in al Hawjila, Ta'izz governorate on June 23.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Barakishnet 2013 ; Critical Threats 2013

title: Basic services, including water and electricity, are cut to settlements in southern Dara’a, Syria while under siege
description: Basic services, including water and electricity, are cut to settlements in southern Dara’a, Syria while they are under siege in early 2013.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2013b

title: Blockade causes shutdown of Gaza wastewater treatment plant
description: An Egyptian and Israel blockade of Gaza cut fuel supplies and causes a shutdown of Gaza's wastewater treatment plants, leading to massive overflow of sewage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al-Mughrabi 2013

title: Burundi Signs Nile CFA
description: Burundi signs the Nile Basin Cooperative Framework Agreement, bringing the total of signatories to six upstream states. The CFA remains contentious as Egypt and Sudan continue to withhold agreement.
countries: Burundi, Ethiopia, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nile Basin Initiative Official Communique on Burundi Accession (2013).

title: Car bomb targets water-supply systems in Colombia
description: A car bomb thought to be targeted at a community water supply detonates near an aqueduct. No group claims responsibility, however Colombian officials attributed it to the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201302060003

title: Chinese dam builders killed after attack by Uyghurs
description: Hundreds of Uyghurs are arrested following an attack on May 20th that led to the death of seven Han Chinese workers building a dam on the Karakash River in Hotan (in Chinese, Hetian) prefecture's Karakash (Moyu) county, China. Local officials ascribe the violence to land and water disputes and cultural differences between Han immigrants [to Xinjiang] and Uyghurs.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hoshur 2013

title: Clash between Kenyan herders and crop growers kills 56
description: Fighting between Borana herders and the crop-growing Burji community kills at least 56 people in 2013. The violence is rooted in historic clan rivalries as well as competition for water and pasture in the arid region. Clashes between the two communities date back to the 1960s and are related to disputes over the use of political power to take control of water and fertile land.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Khalif and Doya 2014

title: Colombian demonstration over water treatment plant turns violent
description: Violence breaks out in the town of Yopal, Colombia, which has been without water for nearly two years following the destruction of a water-treatment plant by a landslide. Demonstrations at government offices and offices of the water company lead to injuries and arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; United Press International (UPI) 2013

title: Demonstrators killed during protests over water shortages in Somaliland
description: At least two demonstrators are killed and others wounded in Somaliland when protests against water shortages are broken up by police firing live bullets. The shortages were caused by a work stoppage by private water vendors protesting new taxes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hasan 2013 ; Jama 2014

title: Egyptian politicians threaten sabotage of Ethiopian dam in a publicly broadcast meeting
description: During a publicly broadcast meeting hosted by Egyptian President Morsi, some meeting participants (Egyptian politicians) suggest sabotaging Ethiopia's dam on the Blue Nile.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ezzat 2013

title: Elsipotog Nation protests over fracking impact to water resources in Canada
description: Several injuries are reported and six police cars burned during a protest by members of the Elsipogtog First Nation in Canada over the impacts to local water resources from fracking operations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; CTV News 2013

title: Environmental activist Tomas Garcia is killed at peaceful protest of the Agua Zarca Dam project in Honduras
description: Environmental activist, Tomas Garcia, dies after being shot by the Honduran military during a peaceful protest of the Agua Zarca Dam project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers 2013

title: Farmers in Iran clash with police over water diversions
description: Hundreds of farmers in the town of Varzaneh, in Iran's Isfahan province, clash with police during a protest against the government's decision to divert water from the area to another province. Iranian media say farmers smash a pipeline carrying water from Zayanderud river to neighboring Yazd province in an effort to prevent the water transfer. Dozens are reported injured and more arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2013b ; Javedanfar 2013

title: Fight over control of water in Pakistan
description: In Karachi, rival sects of the Taliban fight for the control of water by controlling infrastructure and land.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hamid 2012a

title: Five killed at protest against lack of water at Indonesian prison
description: Protests against the lack of water and other basic resources at a prison in Medan, Indonesia leave five dead. Hundreds of convicts escape after the inmates set fire to the prison.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hariyadi 2013

title: Guatemalan community activist against mining and hydroelectric projects is killed
description: In Santa Elalia, Huehuetenango, Guatemala, Daniel Pedro Mato disappears and is found dead several days later. He was an indigenous community activist helping to organize against mining and hydroelectric projects in the region.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Islamic militants cut water supply to Timbuktu, Mali
description: Attacks by Islamic militants on utilities cut water supply to Timbuktu, Mali. There are also reports that Malian forces carried out executions in the conflict area near the towns of Sevare, Mopti, and Niono with bodies being dumped in water wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Formanek Smith-Spark and Netto 2013

title: Kyrgyz villagers block canal at border
description: A water and land dispute between villagers living on the border between Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan escalates when Kyrgyz villages block a canal to prevent water flowing to farmers on the Kazakh side of the border.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lillis 2013

title: Man displaced by dam project killed in Colombia for his opposition to additional projects
description: A man who is displaced by a dam, Nelson Giraldo, is shot for his opposition to further dam projects in Colombia. The Hidroituango dam project had displaced his family and many others from their home for around six months when he was shot.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Movimiento Rios Vivos 2013 ; International Rivers n.d.

title: Militants attack pumping station in Libya
description: Water for the capital of Libya, Tripoli is disrupted by an attack in southern Libya on a pumping station for the country's 'Great Man Made River' by militants loyal to former Libyan leader Muammar al-Gaddafi.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Stratfor 2013

title: Militias cut off water supplies to Tripoli
description: Militias cut off water supplies to Tripoli for several days in continuing unrest in the country.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hurriyet Daily News 2013

title: Pakistan and India clash over Siachen Glacier
description: Tensions continue between India and Pakistan over access to and control of the Siachen Glacier in Kashmir, with a demand by Pakistan that India withdraw troops stationed there.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Press Trust of India (PTI) 2013

title: Pakistani gunmen attack the Ghallanai Irrigation Dam site in Pakistan, damaging equipment and abducting civilians
description: About 12 Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan fighters attack the Ghallanai Irrigation Dam site, Pakistan and abduct at least four citizens, and set fire to construction equipment.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Protester killed after attending a rally against a dam in Panama
description: After attending a protest against the Barro Blanco Dam in Panama, Onesimo Rodriguez is killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Small dam is cyber attacked
description: U.S. authorities discover that Iranian hackers have successfully infiltrated the control system of a small dam in New York State. Due to work being performed on the dam, the hackers are unable to alter dam operations, however the event exposes the risks of cyberattacks on U.S. infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Berger 2016

title: Sri Lankan archbishop accuses army of killing unarmed protestors
description: The Catholic Archbishop of Colombo, Sri Lanka accuses the Sri Lankan army of shooting unarmed protesters and desecrating a church during demonstrations against water contamination. In the incident, at least six people are reported killed and more than 50 others wounded. Thousands of residents were protesting against the contamination of groundwater supply to 15 local villages, allegedly by chemical waste from a rubber glove factory.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al Jazeera 2013 ; Sun 2013 ; Wipulasena 2013

title: Syrian government forces and Hezbollah cut water to the town of Al-Quasayr during a seige
description: In May 2013, Syrian government forces and Hezbollah launch a major offensive on Al-Quasayr, controlling two water stations and cutting water to the town.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2013a

title: Tanzanian herders attempt to take control of water source
description: Conflicts over water continue in Tanzania between farmers and herders over dwindling water resources. In 2013, herders attempt to take over the central water source in the village of Makenya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Makoye 2013

title: The Syrian government drops barrel bombs in Dawar Qadi Askar, Syria, severing the main water supply line
