description: The Syrian government drops barrel bombs on 28 November 2013 in Dawar Qadi Askar, Syria, severing the main water-supply line.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2014a

title: The water tower and electricity generator in Masharah, Syria are shelled by government forces who impose a siege on the village
description: The water tower and electricity generator in Masharah, Syria are shelled by government forces who impose a siege on the village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2013a

title: Village water well destroyed in Somalia
description: The water well for a village in the Bay region is destroyed by an attack attributed to Al-Shabaab.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201312020003

title: Violence escalates over water in Yemen
description: The dwindling water supply from shared mountain springs leads to growing violence between Marzouh and Qaradh, Yemen. At least six deaths occur and many more are wounded in clashes since 2000. "Wherever in Yemen you see aquifers depleting, you have the worst conflicts," said Abdul Rahman al-Eryani, former minister for water and environment, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Friedman 2013

title: Water project employees kidnapped in Iraq
description: Four water project employees are kidnapped by assailants dressed as police officers. The outcome of the kidnapping is unknown and no group has claimed responsibility for the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201311190066

title: Water shortage causes riots in Jordan
description: The Syrian civil war and the displacement of refugees into Jordan contribute to a growing water supply crisis. In summer 2013, riots associated with water shortages are reported by the director of water utilities in Jordan's Mafraq governorate. He notes, "Mafraq was on fire. People burned tires in the street and closed the roads. There was tension over water in the past, but the Syria crisis has made it much worse."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Proctor 2014

title: Water shortage leads to local fighting in India
description: An acute water shortage in Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra, India leads to fights among locals and one death. The government expresses concern about large-scale public unrest due to a severe drought and major water shortages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Express News Service 2013

title: Water station in Egypt is attacked
description: A water station in Bir al-Abd, Egypt is attacked. No one is reported injured or killed. The attackers claim that the water station was built on their lands.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; MA'AN News Agency 2013

title: Water supply for the city of Kitchanga, Congo cut off resulting in deaths
description: The water supply for the city of Kitshanga, Congo is cut off in clashes between DRC armed forces and the Alliance des Patriotes pour un Congo Libre et Souverain (APCLS). The violence kills tens of civilians, including a humanitarian worker, wounds hundreds of people, and displaces thousands.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN News Service 2013

title: Water supply to the besieged town Muadamiyah, Syria is “cut off for weeks at a time” between April and December 2013
description: Water supply to the besieged town Muadamiyah, Syria is “cut off for weeks at a time” between April and December 2013.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2014a

title: Water tanker in Myanmar is attacked
description: Employees of the private company Assam Rifles are escorting a water tanker near the Manipur-Myanmar border when they are attacked with a remotely-detonated bomb. No one is reported injured, however the water tanker is damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Laithangbam 2013

title: A bomb damages a water pipeline in the city of Minva Al-Qamh, Egypt
description: A person is injured when an explosive device placed under a water pipeline is detonated in the city of Minya Al-Qamh, Egypt. The pipeline is not damaged. No one claims responsibility for the explosion.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201409270026

title: A leader of a Honduran indigenous organization opposed to the Agua Zarca Dam is killed; his son is also nearly killed
description: In July 2014, a leader of COPINH (Consejo Civico de Organizaciones Populares e Indigenas de Honduras), Tomas Garcia, and his son are attacked, killing Sr. Garcia and nearly killing his son. COPINH is an Indigenous organization that has been organizing people to oppose the Agua Zarca Dam in Honduras.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Solidarity Collective 2016

title: Armed bandits force villages to pay a 'water tax'
description: Drought in northern India causes local bandits to threaten to kill nearby villagers unless they deliver water to their rural hideouts. Twenty-eight local villages obey the order and take turns paying what the bandits call a daily "water tax.'
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Banerjee 2014

title: At least 30 people reported killed in attack on Haditha Dam, Iraq
description: At least 30 people are reported killed during an attack on a dam in the Haditha area of Iraq. No group claims responsibility for the attack but it is thought to have been carried out by Islamic State.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201412290031

title: Attack on an aqueduct in Colombia cuts off water for 16,000
description: An unclaimed attack on an aqueduct leaves approximately 16,000 people without water. The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) is blamed for the attack and criticized by a Colombian military general for causing a war crime by breaking international law that prohibits attacks on water systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Escobar 2014

title: Attack on water construction project in Iraq
description: Shots are fired at a checkpoint for an Iranian company working on a water project south of Kirkuk, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Aswat al-Iraq 2014a

title: Bombing injures two at water project in Iraq
description: Two people are injured when a bomb explodes near the center of the city Tuz Khurmatu at the town's water project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Aswat al-Iraq 2014b

title: Christian militias reportedly kill Muslim civilians
description: Continued sectarian violence in the Central African Republic between Muslim and Christian militias includes reports of Muslim civilians being killed and their bodies thrown down water wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lodge 2014

title: Civilians suffer violence, intentional water cuts along Georgia-Russia border
description: Despite continuing talks between Georgia and Russia following a 2008 war over South Ossetia and Abkhazia, violence continues in the region. Georgia says civilians along the line suffer violence and kidnappings, that school children are detained regularly by Russian troops, and that water and gas supplies are regularly cut off.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Independent Online 2014

title: Community activist organzing to block construction of the Agua Zarca Dam in Honduras murdered
description: Community activist, William Jacobo, in Rio Blanco, Honduras, is murdered. The Rio Blanco community was organizing to block the construction of the Agua Zarca Dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Coordinator of Honduran indigenous organization opposed to the Agua Zarca Dam attacked
description: A woman, Maria Santos Dominguez, serving as the coordinator of COPINH (Consejo Civico de Organizaciones Populares e Indigenas de Honduras) in Rio Blanco, Honduras, is attacked in her home. COPINH is an indigenous organization that has been organizing people to oppose the Agua Zarca Dam in Honduras.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Solidarity Collective 2016

title: Extensive damage to Gaza's water systems during the Israeli attacks on Gaza
description: Water and sanitation facilities in Gaza are heavily affected by the escalation of violence in 2014 with 63 water facilities damaged and 23 completely destroyed. More than 80 percent of the water wells in Gaza are estimated to not function with about 1.2 million people lacking access to water and sanitation services. Key sewage facilities are partially destroyed, including 60 percent of the treatment plants and 27 percent of the pumping stations, and 33,000 meters of water and wastewater networks are damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; World Bank 2014 ; GISHA 2014

title: Farmers and herdsmen clash over land and water access in Nigeria
description: In Nigeria, Tiv/Agatu farmers and Fulani herdsmen clash over access to grazing land and water points. In April 2014, President Goodluck Jonathan orders military operations in Benue, Nasarawa, and Plateau states in an effort to reduce the violence.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; All Africa 2014

title: Fisherman with connetions to organization opposing the Hidrosogamoso dam in Colombia dies from stabbing
description: A fisherman with connections to an organization working to oppose a dam in Colombia, Armando Caballero Toscano, is stabbed while walking to a friend's house. Mr. Toscano was the son of a leader of the local organization opposing the construction of the Hidrosogamoso Dam on the Sogamoso River in Colombia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Rios Vivos 2014

title: Four people killed and others injured in clashes over a dam project in Pakistan
description: In February 2014, four people are killed and another seven are injured in clashes between Pakistani communities over the construction of the Diamer-Bhasha Dam. The Pakistani government has failed to intervene in the dispute which has erupted between regional communities over who will be responsible for the construction and other aspects of the dam's administration.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; DAWN Correspondent 2016 ; Internataional Rivers n.d.

title: Free Syrian Army cuts off water supply to Wadi Barada
description: Syrian government forces are driven out of Wadi Barada's villages after the Free Syrian Army (FSA) cuts off water supply from Ain al-Fijah, a major spring serving the Damascus area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reznick 2016

title: Government reportedly bombs pumping stations in Aleppo, Syria
description: The water supply for the Syrian city of Aleppo is cut off in both regime and opposition-controlled areas. The city's water pumping stations are bombed, reportedly by the government, as are water distribution networks in opposition-controlled areas. In return, the Syrian Ministry of Foreign Affairs blames opposition forces for the water crisis.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bulos 2014 ; Syria Direct 2014

title: Groups attack Venezuelan water treatment plant
description: Unidentified groups attack the Bourgin water-treatment plant in Merida, Venezuela and contaminate the local supply with diesel fuel. The contamination is discovered through water-quality testing and the water supply to Merida is shut off for a short period for cleaning.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Pearson 2014

title: Haditha Dam on the Euphrates River is attacked
description: Reports from a military spokesperson from Iraq say security forces fought off militant groups trying to seize Haditha and a nearby dam on the Euphrates River. 40 militants are killed by the security forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Derechos Human Rights and Equipo Nizkor 2014

title: Honduran youth killed for supporting efforts opposing the Agua Zarca Dam
description: In October 2014, Maycol Ariel Rodriguez Garcia, a 15 year old indigenous youth from Honduras, was found dead. His death is thought to be connected to his involvement with anti-dam efforts in his community where indigenous Lenca community members have been working to stop the construction of the Agua Zarca Dam on Rio Blanco.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Solidarity Collective 2016

title: Hydroelectric power plant is attacked in Turkey
description: A hydroelectric power plant in Kars Province, Turkey is attacked by the Kurdistan Workers' Party. Three attackers are killed. The next day, three off-duty Turkish soldiers are killed in retribution.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Staff, Reuters 2014 ; Hurriyet Daily News 2014

title: ISIS cuts off water and electricity supply to Kobane, Syria ahead of their assault in September 2014
description: ISIS cuts off water and electricity supply to Kobane, Syria ahead of their assault in September 2014.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2015

title: Impaired electrical grid and water supply in Aleppo, Syria lead to a lack of potable water and sanitation
description: The Al-Nusra Front “deliberately impairs” the electrical grid and water supply in Aleppo, Syria between May 5-14th, leading to a lack of potable water and sanitation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2014b

title: In Texas, family feud over water well erupts in violence
description: A dispute over a water well leads to a violent assault with a sword and gun. Two men are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hlavaty 2014

title: Indigenous organizer supporting efforts to oppose Las Mintas Dam in Honduras shot and killed
description: Indigenous organizer, Pedro Perez, working in opposition of Las Mintas Dam is shot and killed in Honduras.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Insurgents seize Falluja Dam
description: Insurgents from Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) seize the Fallujah Dam in Iraq and close the floodgates to cause upstream flooding and to cut downstream water supply. The objective is to flood the area around the city of Fallujah to force government troops to retreat and lift a siege, while cutting water supplies and hydroelectricity generation for other parts of the country.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Coles 2014

title: Islamic State blocks access to water
description: In Iraq, Islamic State blocks access to water in the predominantly Christian town of Qaraqosh (also known as Bakhdida), take over farms and agricultural land, and expel most of the 50,000 residents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Security Council 2017

title: Islamic State contaminates drinking water supplies, Syria
description: Islamic State deliberately contaminates drinking water with crude oil in the Balad district of the Salahaddin Governorate. Poisoned water supplies are also reported from Aleppo, Deir ez Zor, Raqqa, and Baghdad.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Security Council 2017

title: Islamic State destroys water wells, pumps, and pipes in agricultural regions in Iraq
description: Farmers returning to their land in northwestern Iraq after the Islamic State (ISIS/ISIL) find widespread devastation to agricultural land, livestock, and machinery, including water pumps, wells, pipes and generators. One assessment by the Iraq Food and Security Cluster Partnership notes that of the 450 deep wells, only 50 are still useable. Another assessment by Amnesty International details the destruction of wells on the properties of more than 30 different farmers from across the country.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Joint Crisis Coordination Center 2015 ; Amnesty International 2018b

title: Islamic State fighters advance on Haditha Dam
description: Iraqi officials report that fighters with the Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) are advancing on the Haditha Dam, the second-largest in Iraq, raising the possibility of catastrophic damage and flooding. The ISIL militants are fighting for control of the Euphrates River dam, about 120 miles northwest of Baghdad and government forces were fighting to halt their advance. Army officers tell employees to stay inside and to be prepared to open the dam's floodgates if ordered to do so, one employee said.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Rubin and Nordland 2014

title: Islamic State forces take control of Mosul Dam
description: Mosul Dam in Iraq is taken over by Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) forces in August 2014. Over the next several weeks, Kurdish and US forces attack ISIS/ISIL in the region and retake control of the dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Maler 2014 ; Kreiter 2014

title: Islamic State uses Falluja Dam as a weapon
description: Islamic State closes the Falluja Dam floodgates and diverts water over an irrigation channel into a side valley, inundating land up to 100km away and placing parts of the city of Abu Ghraib under up to four meters of water. More than 10,000 houses and 200 square kilometers of farmland are flooded and extensive livestock killed. Water for millions of people in the cities of Karbala, Najaf, and Babil is cut off for a time.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Security Council 2017

title: Israeli missile hits water tank in Gaza, killing several
description: Several days of attacks on houses in Gaza by Israeli missles in July destroy water tanks and kill several occupants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2014

title: Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan security clash over border dispute
description: Security forces in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan clash over a border dispute. Among the targets of the violence, which leave security forces wounded on both sides, are a small dam and electricity substation inside Kyrgyzstan. The local grievances include disputes over access to pasture and water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Trilling 2014

title: Leader of opposition to the Tigre dam project in Honduras is found dead
description: A leader in the opposition to the Tigre Dam project, Justo Sorto, is found dead in Intibuca, Honduras. The dam is planned to be on a river the flows between Honduras and El Salvador.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Levees along the Shebelle River, Somalia are destroyed
description: Levees are destroyed along the Shebelle River in Somalia, in an attempt, sources claim, to make roads unusable by military forces. The attack is attributed to Al-Shabaab.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201409010003

title: Libyan tribal disputes include attacks on pumps and pipeline systems
description: Disputes between two tribes in Libya, the Zwai and Tebu, include attacks on power stations and power cut for the pumps that operate the 'Man Made River' pipeline system, leading to water shortages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Adel 2014

title: Militia burn and loot South Darfur refugee camp, destroying water wells
description: Armed Janjaweed militia burn and loot a South Darfur refugee camp, killing a local sheikh, injuring others, looting property and livestock, and destroying all water wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Radio Dabanga 2014

title: Multiple water projects are attacked in Iraq
description: In less than a week, several water projects are the targets of explosives, killing six employees of one of the water projects and damaging the infrastructure in Al-Shirqat District, Saladin Governorate, and Mushirfah, Nineveh Governorate, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201404090018, 201404130034

title: Organizer against corporate dam and mining projects killed in Mexico
description: A local leader opposing corporate hydroelectric and mining projects, Antonio Esteban Cruz, is killed in Mexico. Sr. Cruz was a leader of the Movimiento Independiente Obrero, Campesino, Urbano y Popular (MIOCUP) and had recently formed the Encuentro Nacional Indígena y Campesino (Ficam) to defend the land against corporate mining, gas pipelines, and dams.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Martell 2015 ; International Rivers n.d.

title: Over 1000 killed in Nigeria over access to land and water
description: Violence between farmers and herders kills over 1,000 people in 2014 in Nigeria alone, according to Human Rights Watch. At the root of this violence is the issue of access to land and water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; McAleer 2014

title: Palestinian water supply and wastewater system hit by Israeli war planes
description: Israeli warplanes hit water supply wells, pipelines, and wastewater treatment plants servicing hundreds of thousands of Palestinians in the Gaza region. Palestinian officials state that the attacks intentionally targeted the infrastructure, mounting a war crime under the Geneva Protocol.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Omer 2014

title: Pojom II hydroelectric project facilities in Guatemala is set on fire
description: The Pojom II hydroelectric project facilities are set on fire. This is one of three proposed hydroelectric projects in the northern Huehuetenango region of Guatemala that has been opposed by many of the local community.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Environmental Justice Atlas 2018

title: Protests against the construction of the Sivens dam in France turn violent, one protestor is killed
description: In 2014 protestors camped out to prevent the construction of the Sivens Dam on the Tescou River in southern France have multiple confrontations with police. On the night of October 26, one protestor, Remi Fraisse, is hit by a grenade thrown by the police and dies. His death prompts widespread protests across the country and shortly afterward, the regional government decides to halt the project completely.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Wikipedia contributors 2025b ; Cabrera 2014

title: Protests over spring diversion erupts in violence in Mexico
description: Protestors in San Bartolo Ameyalco on the outskirts of Mexico City battle anti-riot police during a protest to prevent the diversion of local spring water to a new development nearby. More than 100 people are injured, some seriously.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Becerra 2014

title: Protests over water shortages in South Africa turn violent
description: At least four people are killed in South Africa during protests over water shortages in the northern town of Brits.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sky News 2014 ; Maseko 2014

title: Riots over erratic water supply in Kitwe, Zambia
description: Kitwe's Wusakile and Chamboli townships in Zambia experience riots over erratic water supply. Residents engage police in skirmishes and eight people are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Zambia Daily Mail 2014

title: Russian shelling damages the Siverskyi Donets-Donbas canal and kills nine
description: Russian shelling of the pumping station of the 1st lift of the Siverskyi Donets-Donbas canal and other structures of the canal kills two and injures three. Over the course of several days, a total of nine people are killed and 26 employees of KP "Donbas Water Company" are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Donetsk Regional State Administration 2021 ; Ulytsky et al. 2018

title: Six dead including two children as protests against a dam project turn violent in Guatemala
description: Indigenous Q'equchi community members at risk of displacement from the Santa Rita hydroelectric dam in Guatemala are met with an esitmated 1,500 police sent to evict residents to allow dam construction to begin. At least six people, including two children are killed in confrontations related to the dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nelsen 2015 ; International Rivers n.d.

title: Three US citizens arrested for planning attack on water-treatment plants
description: Three men in the state of Georgia are arrested for planning to attack water-treatment plants, power grids, and other infrastructure in an effort to incite anti-government militias in the United States to fight the federal government. A criminal complaint charges them with conspiring to receive and possess firearms, specifically pipe bombs and thermite grenades. Thermite grenades are military-grade weapons typically used to destroy vehicles, weapons systems, and other equipment.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Brumback 2014 ; Rome News-Tribune 2014

title: Three people are killed in Mothutlung, South Africa in a protest over sabotage of local water pumps
description: Three people are killed during protests in Mothutlung, South Africa after the pumps supplying water are sabotaged, reportedly by private owners of water tankers who had paid kickbacks to municipal officials to cut the supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Water Integrity Network/Corruption Watch 2020

title: U.S.-led coalition launches airstrikes to protect dams from ISIS
description: A U.S.-led coalition launches a series of air strikes against targets of the Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) in areas around Mosul Dam, Fallujah Dam, and Haditha Dam in Iraq. U.S. aircraft destroy an ISIL-built earthen berm near the Fallujah Dam. This berm was built by ISIL to control downstream water supplies and to increase the flow of the Euphrates River into Abu Ghraib canals, flooding local Shiite neighborhoods in east Fallujah and forcing the locals to evacuate.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2014b ; Barnes 2014

title: Ukraine accused of cutting water supply to the North Crimea Canal
description: After Russia annexes Crimea from the Ukraine, they accuse Ukraine of cutting off the water supply in the North Crimea Canal, leading to a water shortage for Crimea's agricultural fields growing grapes, rice, maize, and soya. The canal delivers water from the Dnipro River in southern Ukraine and accounts for 80% of Crimea's water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2014a

title: Upper caste women in India reportedly restrict access to water sources
description: Tensions revive in the area of Jammu and Kashmir in early 2014 when upper caste women reportedly restrict access to higher-quality water sources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sharma 2014

title: Village clashes with police over spring
description: A confrontation over a water spring between 1,500 police and residents of a village on Mexico City's western outskirts leaves more than 100 police injured and five people arrested. It is the latest in a series of clashes over increasingly scarce water in the city, which draws much of its supply from surrounding states. Local governments say they are trying to extend municipal supply to the area; residents are afraid the objective is to take control over a local water source.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Stevenson 2014

title: Violence over access to water between neighbors in Kyrgyzstan leaves one dead
description: In Kyrgyzstan an Uzbek farmer is killed by his Kyrgyz neighbor who reportedly attacks him over access to irrigation water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Arnold 2018

title: Water construction equipment damaged in India
description: Maoists in Dharambandha, India claim responsibility for a bombing attack on a culvert and the excavation machine being used to build a canal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New Indian Express, The 2014

title: Water pipeline destroyed in South Sudan
description: Fighting around Malakal, in South Sudan, displaces thousands and leaves many dead. A military checkpoint and water pipeline to the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) compound and nearby Protection of Civilians area are targeted and destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; World Vision 2014

title: Water pipeline is damaged in Colombia
description: A water pipeline is damaged by an explosive device near the Pan-American Highway in Colombia. The attack is attributed to the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201407310004

title: Water purification plant in Fallujah attacked
description: At least two people die from a blast at a water purification plant in the city of Fallujah, in Al Anbar Province. More than 20 people are hospitalized from chlorine poisoning from the destruction of a water-purification chemical storage facility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201406130089

title: Water system in Donetsk, Ukraine damaged during conflict with Russia
description: During the conflict between the Ukraine and Russia, water systems for the city of Donetsk are damaged. The Donbas Water Company stops three pumping station from bringing water to the Siversky Donets-Donbas channel due to damages from the conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kiev Post 2014

title: Water tanks are destroyed in Khuza'a, Gaza by Israel military and a water treatment plant is bombed
description: Khuza’a town in Gaza is attacked by Israel Defense Forces. The electricity is cut and reports indicate that many water tanks on the rooftops of homes are attacked and destroyed by the IDF. The Israeli ground operation in Khuza’a also results in extensive damage to the water tower that serves the civilian population and to a water treatment plant.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Human Rights Council 2014

title: Water treatment facilities and a dam in the Ukraine are attacked
description: Gunmen fire at a water filtration center, causing an unknown number of casualties. Landmines are planted at a dam in Bakhmut (formerly Artemivsk district), Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine. The outcome of the attack is not reported and no group claims responsibility, although it is attributed to the Donetsk People's Republic.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201407140120

title: Water well attacked in Pakistan
description: Two schools and a solar-powered tube well are destroyed in a blast attributed to militants in the Mohmand Agency. No injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Newspaper Correspondent, The 2014

title: Water-supply reservoir is attacked in Ukraine
description: The regional water utility company in the Donetsk Oblast province of eastern Ukraine reports that the reservoir in rebel-controlled Horlivka has been hit by shells. Two injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Naharnet Newsdesk 2014

title: A Mayan community member known for protesting the K'anbalam River dam project is killed in Guatemala
description: A Mayan community member, Pascual Pablo Francisco, is found dead in March 2015 in the northern department of Huehuetenango, Guatemala. Sr. Francisco is known for opposing the construction of a dam on the K'anbalam River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reynolds 2015

title: A death is reported in ongoing farmer-herder conflicts in Tanzania
description: A group of Maasi cattle herders beat and kill a crop farmer in a conflict over water access. The farmer and his family had moved near the river because of changes in precipitation, making water unpredictable.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; DrinkLocal DrinkTap 2020

title: A local activist is injured during attempt to observe well digging operation by a private agricultural corporation in Peru
description: A local activist in Peru seeking to block corporate agricultural company, Agricola La Venta, from drilling wells is assaulted as she attempts to view a new well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; James 2015

title: A local environmental leader and mayor of Yagen, Peru is killed after protest over the Chadin II dam project
description: In Yagen, Peru, Hitler Rojas Gonzalez is shot and killed while walking home from a protest against the Chadin II Dam project. Rojas is the elected mayor of the town and local leader of environmental and social causes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: A member of the Gualinga indigenous community opposing a hydroelectric project is found dead in Honduras
description: A member of the Gualinga indigenous community, Juan Francisco Martínez, in Honduras is found dead in January 2015. He is thought to have been murdered for his opposition to a hydroelectric project on his community's territory.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; FIDH 2015 ; International Rivers n.d.

title: A water filtration plant in the Ukraine is damaged
description: During multiple attacks on the city of Shchastya, Ukraine, a water filtration station is hit. One person is killed and two others wounded during the attacks. While no group claims responsibility for the attacks, they are attributed to the Luhansk People's Republic.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201501140039

title: A water truck is damaged in Yemen
description: A water truck is damaged during the conflict in Amran District, Amran, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Air raid damages water well in Yemen
description: A water well is damaged during an air raid in Razih District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Air raid hits water well in Yemen
description: An early morning air raid hits a water well in Al Mokha District, Taizz, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Air raids damage water infrastructure in Yemen
description: Multiple air raids over the course of two days damage water wells and a water factory in Sihar District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Air raids damage water wells in Yemen
description: Multiple air raids over the course of a week damage water wells in Bakil Al-Mir and Hayran Districts, Hajjah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: An air raid damages a water tank in Yemen
description: A water tank is damaged in an air raid in Craiter District, Aden, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Andhra Pradesh and Telangana police clash over water releases from the Nagarjuna Sagar dam on the Krishna River
description: On February 13, 2015 in India, Andhra Pradesh police clash with Telangana police over the control of the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam in a water-sharing dispute over the releases of the Krishna River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Times of India 2023

title: Attack of a dam blocked in Iraq
description: In early January 2015 military troops in Iraq block an attack by IS militants that is attempting to destroy a dam and block a road connecting Diyala and the Shiite holy city of Sammara.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Xhinua_2015

title: Attack on water supply reservoir in Libya
description: A reservoir appears to have been the target of an attack by supposed Muslim fundamentalists in the city of Zintan, Jabal Al Gharbi district, Libya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201503050029

title: Attacks interrupt construction of Ilisu and Silvan dams, Turkey
description: At the end of 2014, work on the Ilisu Dam stops for four months after the armed wing of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) kidnaps two of the project's subcontractors. When construction resumes, the largely non-Kurdish workforce is escorted to the site by military tanks. Militants also target Diyarbakir's Silvan Dam by placing explosives on the roads leading into the site, and security threats in the region cause construction delays.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Stratfor 2016

title: Baloch Liberation Front fighters kill 20 working on Sohrab Dam in retaliation for military operations conducted in the area
description: Baloch Liberation Front (BLF) fighters shoot at construction laborers working on the Sohrab Dam, Balochistan, Pakistan, killing 20. The BLF stated that the attack was retaliation for military operations conducted in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Baloch Republican Army fighters in Pakistan abduct six construction workers from the Shadi Kaur Dam construction site
description: Baloch Republican Army fighters in Balochistan Province, Pakistan abduct six construction workers from the Shadi Kaur Dam construction site.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Bombing of an oil pipeline leads to contamination of water supplies in Colombia
description: Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels bomb an oil pipeline, causing it to spill 10,000 barrels of oil into the Mira River, leaving an estimated 150,000 people without drinking water. Colombian President Juan Manuel Santos declares a state of emergency in the state of Tumaco due to the spill.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Presstv 2015

title: China Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Mechanism Proposed
description: China proposes a 'Mekong River community of common destiny' in April 2015, aimed at institutionalizing Chinese leadership in Mekong governance alongside the MRC. Critics see it as China seeking to undermine the existing MRC framework.
countries: China, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Myanmar
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sanya Declaration of the First Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Leaders' Meeting (2016).

title: Citizen activist working to protect community control over water wells is murdered in Mexico
description: A citizen activist, Jose Isabel Cervantes Angeles, organizing on behalf of maintaining community control over water wells, is found dead inside of one of the wells in Coyotepec, Mexico, on April 18, 2015.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Clashes between pastoralists and farmers over water access.
description: Clashes continue between pastoralists and farmers over access to water and grazing lands in the face of severe drought. Water shortages have forced the herders to move to farmers' land for grazing, leading to clashes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Langat 2015

title: Community anti-dam activist shot and killed in Guatemala
description: In Jocotan, Guatemala, Dona Rosalinda Perez is shot and killed after five men enter her store. Dona Perez was known for community organizing against the Trest Marias Dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Cuts in water access trigger protests in Egypt
description: Residents of Giza block a road to protest ongoing water cuts. Police break up the protest with tear gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hamama and Charbel 2015

title: Egypt-Ethiopia-Sudan Declaration of Principles
description: Egypt, Sudan, and Ethiopia sign the Declaration of Principles on the GERD in Khartoum, establishing priority for downstream electricity purchase, a damage mitigation framework, and drought/low-flow procedures. However, the agreement lacks binding filling and operation rules.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agreement on Declaration of Principles between the Arab Republic of Egypt, the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia and the Republic of the Sudan on the GERD Project, Khartoum (2015).

title: Explosive devices discovered near water-treatment plant in Canada
description: Two small explosive devices are discovered near a water-treatment plant in Barrie, Canada. No one is injured and no suspects are identified in a report on the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Davidson 2015

title: Farmer kills herder's donkeys who compete for land and water in Tanzania
description: A Maasi herder loses their herd of donkeys when they are killed by a local farmer who sees the donkeys as competition for their land and water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; DrinkLocal DrinkTap 2020

title: Government water storage infrastructure is damaged in Yemen
description: A government-owned water storage unit is damaged in night-time air raids in Dhamar City District, Dhamar, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Human rights and environmental defender murdered over his opposition to over-exploitation of groundwater
description: Human rights and environmental defender, Alberto Almeida Fernandez, is murdered in a shopping center in Chihuahua, Mexico. Sr. Fernandez had opposed over exploitation of groundwater from the Flores Magon Ahumada Aquifer. Several of his legal actions to defend the aquifer had been successful in closing wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; OAS 2015

title: In Somalia, dozens are killed in local land and water disputes
description: Dozens are killed in clan-related violence in Somalia's Hiran region. Sources say the violence is related to tensions over access to water and pasture, as well as local politics.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2015a ; Horseed Media 2015

title: Indigenous movement leader of the Gualinga community opposing a dam project in Honduras is murdered -- the third in 2015
description: The body of indigenous movement leader in Honduras, Javier Vasquez Benitez, is found near his home. He is the third member of the Gualinga community to be murdered in 2015. He was a member of the Movimiento Indígena Independiente Lenca de la Paz - Honduras (MILPAH) and had been organizing the communitiy in opposition to a dam in their territory.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; FIDH 2015 ; International Rivers n.d.

title: Iranian border guards open fire on Afghan villagers accessing river water
description: A dispute over the allocation and rights to water from the Hari Rud River between Afghanistan and Iran leads to at least ten deaths when Iranian border guards allegedly open fire on Afghan villagers trying to collect river water. The river provides water for agricultural production in Herat province, Afghanistan, and to the downstream Iranian city of Mashhad, Iran's second largest city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Karimi and Hulpachova 2015

title: Irrigation canals are damaged in two attacks in Yemen
description: Two attacks spanning a week in Al-Marawi'ah District, Hudaydah, Yemen leave irrigation canals damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Islamic State attacks Iraqi security forces around Euphrates River dam
description: The Islamic State attacks Iraqi security forces and affiliated militiamen stationed around Adhaim dam on the Al Uzym River, north of Baghdad. Accounts differ as to the total number of deaths, however both sides suffer losses of life and numerous fighters are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; IANS 2015 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019. ID. 201501280049

title: Islamic State attacks Mosul Dam on the Tigris
description: An attack by Islamic State (IS) fighters on the Mosul Dam on the Tigris river leads to the death of 16 Kurdish Peshmerga soldiers. The dam provides electricity to part of the Anbar province, which was under IS's control at the time. In August 2014, the dam is seized by Kurdish and Iraqi government forces from IS, who had taken control of it weeks earlier. The 1,200 families who are said to have been operating the dam mostly fled when IS seized power in fear that the dam would be used to flood downstream communities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al Jazeera 2015 ; PakTribune 2015

title: Islamic State captures Tharthar Dam on the Tigris River
description: The Islamic State attacks and successfully captures Tharthar Dam near Fallujah, on the Tigris River in Anbar province, Iraq. The attack leaves 127 Iraqi soldiers dead. After capturing the dam, the fighters open at least one floodgate, affecting downstream communities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sabah and Alwan 2015 ; Alwan 2015

title: Islamic State cuts off irrigation water in Iraq
description: Following the capture of Ramadi Dam, the Islamic State cuts water for irrigation systems and treatment plants in the predominantly Shiite downstream provinces of Babil, Karbala, Najaf and Qadisiya, threatening Iraqi food production.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Security Council 2017

title: Islamic State shuts off water flow below Ramadi Dam
description: In June 2015, Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) militants shut off and redirect water flows below Ramadi Dam in order to facilitate military movements across the Euphrates River. As a result, communities downstream face water shortages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Alkhshali and Smith-Spark 2015 ; Coles 2015

title: Kosovo authorities shut off water to Pristina as preventative measure against a planned attack
description: A planned attack on the water supply in Pristina, Kosovo is prevented before its execution. The attack is intended to contaminate Badovac Lake, the largest water reservoir uphill of the city. As a preventative measure, Kosovo authorities temporarily shut off the water supply to tens of thousands of people in the capital after police arrest five suspects linked to Islamic State.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Guardian, The 2015

title: Local farmers burn a water pipe in attempt to stop groundwater pumping
description: Local farmers in Peru burn a plastic water pipe in an attempt to stop groundwater pumping by a corporate agricultural company Agricola La Venta.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; James 2015

title: Militants attack water-treatment facility in Philippines
description: Suspected New People's Army (NPA), Philippines militants hold up a water-treatment facility claiming that it had failed to pay "revolutionary taxes" to the NPA. No people are harmed, but armed guards are disarmed and additional items are taken from the personnel at the facility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Locsin 2015

title: Night air raid damages water project in Yemen
description: An air raid damages a water project in Harad District, Hajjah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Philippine town loses access to water after pipeline is bombed
description: A predominantly Muslim town in southern Philippines loses access to water after a group known as Abu Sayyaf is suspected in an explosion that damaged local water pipes. This group is said to be linked to al-Qaeda and/or at least inspired by al-Qaeda's strategy to attack water infrastructure in Iraq. The affected town is without municipal water for at least several days. In a possibly related incident a person guarding the water facility is killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Manilia Bulletin 2015 ; World Bulletin 2015

title: Revolutionary forces in Colombia blow up a water treatment facility
description: According to military officials, Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) "detonated a high power explosive device," destroying a water facility in the town of Algeciras, in southwestern Colombia, disrupting service to about 13,000 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2015b

title: Russian Federation forces bomb water-treatment facility in Aleppo, Syria
description: Russian Federation forces bomb the al-Khafsa water treatment facility in the city of Aleppo, reportedly mistaking it for an oil-production facility. The treatment plant draws water from the Euphrates River and is called "one of the most important in Syria, producing an average of 18 million liters of drinking water daily." According to UNICEF, "The bombing caused severe damage and cut off piped water supplies on which approximately 3.5 million people depend." Water pumping operations have since been partially restored, but more than 1.4 million people in rural Aleppo continue to suffer interruptions to their supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNICEF 2015 ; Triebert 2015

title: Saudi Arabia destroys a water bottling plant in Yemen; kills dozens
description: A plant is destroyed and 14 workers are killed in Yemen in an aerial bombing by a Saudi-led coalition. The Yemeni Defense Ministry claims the facility was a bottled water plant, while the Saudi-led coalition claims the facility was used to make bombs and train African migrants. Human Rights Watch finds no evidence the facility was anything except a bottling plant.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Fahim 2015 ; Human Rights Watch 2015

title: Second member of the Gualinga indigenous community opposing a hydroelectric dam is found murdered in Honduras
description: A member of the Gualinga indigenous community in Honduras, Silvestre Manueles Gomez, is brutally murdered in May 2015 near the border of the department of Intaibuca and La Paz. In this region there is a conflict between the owners of a hydroelectric company and the Indigenous community who oppose the dam because they say the permitting process violated their rights by failing to consult them. He is the second member of the Gualinga to be murdered in Honduras in 2015.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; FIDH 2015

title: Silvan Dam construction site attacked
description: A remotely detonated explosive on a road used for delivering supplies to the Silvan Dam construction site kills one civilian, a child. The bomb is thought to be planted by the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) and targeted at military vehicles.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Daily Sabah Turkey 2015

title: Small Peruvian town protests company's groundwater pumping
description: In a feud over water, farmers in the Peruvian town of Ocucaje challenge an effort by a company, Agricola La Venta, to start pumping from three wells. Water from the wells would flow through about eight miles of pipes to a farm that produces table grapes for export. Protesters set fire to plastic pipes and one protester is injured by company representatives during a dispute. The town is already struggling with serious water shortages and villagers are concerned that the pumping would further threaten water supplies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; James 2015

title: Soldiers guarding Turkish dam are attacked
description: Turkish soldiers guarding a hydroelectric dam are attacked with rockets and long-range gunfire by the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) in the Kulp district of Diyarbakir. One soldier is killed and three wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2015d

title: Spiritual leader opposing construction of dams in Guatemala is murdered one day after a court victory for indigenous people
description: A 70 year old Mayan spiritual leader known for supporting efforts to legally suspend the license for the construction of the Vega I and Vega II dams in Ixil territory, Guatemala, is murdered one day after the courts rule in favor of the indigenous groups. The courts found that the company that was issued the permits for the project had failed to consult the indigenous communities, making the permits invalid.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Abbott 2015

title: State water corporation is damaged in Yemen
description: A state water corporation is damaged in the conflict in Yemen, in Shibam Kawkaban District, Al Mahwit, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: State water utility infrastructure is attacked in Yemen
description: A state run water utility is a casualty to the conflict in Yareem District, Ibb, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Suspected ISIL attackers bomb the Adhaim Dam, Iraq, with at least 18 deaths reported
description: Suspected Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) suicide bombers detonate explosives-laden vehicles while other attackers open fire on Adhaim Dam, Iraq. At least 18 people (14 ISIL fighters) are killed and 23 people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Suspected ISIL attackers bomb the Haditha Dam, Iraq, killing at least 33
description: Suspected Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) suicide bombers detonate explosives-laden vehicles at the Haditha Dam, Iraq. At least 10 security force members and 23 attackers are killed; 16 security force members are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Suspected Kurdistan Workers' Party fighters set fire to construction equipment at the Kocali Dam, Turkey, construction site
description: Suspected Kurdistan Workers' Party fighters set fire to construction equipment at the Kocali Dam, Turkey, construction site.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Syrian rebel groups cut off water supply to Damascus
description: In August 2015, Syrian rebel groups cut off water from a spring in Ain al-Fijah, reducing water output to Damascus by 90 percent for three days and leading to water shortages and rationing. Rebels continue to periodically shut off the supply from the spring, resulting in water shortages in Ain al-Fijah and Damascus. Rebels threaten to blow up the spring if government forces enter the region.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reznick 2016

title: Terrorists bomb main water pipe into Aleppo, Syria
description: Fighters from Jabhat al-Nusra, the Syrian branch of Al-Qaeda, bomb the main pipeline carrying water to the city of Aleppo from the Euphrates River. More than 100 people are sickened by contaminated water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reznick 2016

title: Two Guatemalans fighting against the Hidro Santa Cruz dam project are killed
description: Two Guatemalan men, Cano Mateo Mateo and Alfredo Felipe Ramos, are killed in spring of 2015. They were members of a group that was actively involved in stopping the Hidro Santa Cruz Dam in Guatemala.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Two Mayan leaders accused of sabotaging a dam company are arrested in Guatemala
description: In March 2015, two Mayan leaders from Huehuetenango, Guatemala accused of sabotaging a dam company by damaging equipment and other property are arrested without a warrant. Their lawyer is allegedly beat by police after demanding a warrant.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reynolds 2015

title: Two demonstrators protesting a dam in Brazil are killed by a car that is driven into the group of protestors
description: Anti-dam demonstrators, Daniel Vilanova Dias and Leidiane Drosdroski Machado, are struck and killed by a car driven at a group of protestors protesting the Belo Monte hydroelectric plant in Vitoria do Xingu, Brazil. Another person is also injured by the same car.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Comissão Pastoral da Terra 2015 ; Global Witness 2024

title: Ukrainian town loses water supply
description: Most of the villages and towns in the southwest portion of the Luhansk region in Ukraine lose access to their water supply after fighting damages a water main.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2015c

title: Violent confrontation over a dam project leads to one being shot, eventually dying in Guatemala
description: A violent confrontation breaks out in Santa Eulalia, Guatemala, between citizens and municipal employees over a dam project. The municipal employees, which includes the mayor, shoot at the citizens who were part of a local radio station that broadcast in the Mayan Q'anjob'al language and allows people in opposition to the dam project to speak. Pascual Basilio Pascual Diego is shot and dies two months later in the hospital.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reynolds 2015

title: Water and land rights advocate shot and killed in the Philippines
description: Water and land rights advocate, Teresito Mula Labastilla, is shot and killed by two men on a motorcycle in Maramag, Bukidnon, Philippines. Mr. Labastilla advocated for water and land rights for farmers and indigenous peoples.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Task Force Detainees of the Philippines 2015

title: Water drilling rig is damaged during conflict in Yemen
description: A water drilling rig is damaged in Yemen, in the Haydan District, Saada.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water factory is hit in multiple air raids in Yemen
description: The Adhban water factory is hit during three air raids that occurred in August, in Sirwah District, Marib, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water infrastructure is attacked in Yemen
description: A water project in Al-Sharyah District, Al Bayda, Yemen is damaged. On the same day in Al-Mahabishah District, Hajja, water wells are also damaged in an air raid.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water pipe attacked in Egypt
description: A bomb explodes under a water pipe in al-Rahmaniya village, Abu Kebir, Sharqia governorate, Egypt.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al-Youm 2015

title: Water pipeline damaged in Pakistan
description: A water pipeline is damaged in a blast from an explosive reportedly placed by the Baloch Republican Army in Nokani, Balochistan province, Pakistan. No injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201502220004

title: Water plant in Colombia severely damaged in attack
description: A water plant near Algeciras, Colombia is severely damaged from an explosive, leaving approximately 13,000 people without services. The Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels are blamed for the attack. This attack on infrastructure comes after several other similar attacks on electrical plants and towers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Naharnet Newsdesk 2015

title: Water project is hit in air raids in Yemen
description: A water project in Majzar District, Marib, Yemen is hit during multiple evening air raids.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water supply well is attacked in Yemen
description: A water supply well attacked in Al-Ashah District, Amran, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water tank is damaged in an air raid in Yemen
description: A water tank is damaged in air raids in Sa'ada District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water tank is hit in an air raid in Yemen
description: A water tank is damaged in an air raid in Al-Sab'ein District, Capital, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water truck is damaged in Yemen
description: A water truck owned by an oil & gas company is damaged in the conflict in Haydan District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water trucks are damaged in conflict in Yemen
description: Water trucks are damaged during the conflict in Az Zuhrah District, Al Hudaydah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water well hit in air raid in Yemen
description: A water well is damaged during an air raid in Mustaba District, Hajjah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Yemen's civil war leaves millions without access to drinking water
description: The Yemeni Interior Ministry claims up to 4,000 people die annually from water-related violence including raids on wells and other fights over water access involving armed groups. A report from Yemen's pro-government newspaper estimates that 70-80% of conflicts in rural areas are about water. The UNFAO estimates that about 20 million Yemenis do not have access to drinking water because of the ongoing civil war.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Whitehead 2015 ; Almohsen 2015

title: 18 killed and 200 injured after reopening of the Munak canal, India
description: At least 18 people are killed and 200 injured after the Indian Army intervenes to reopen the Munak canal, which supplies New Delhi with three-fifths of its freshwater supply. The canal is shut down by economic protests in Harayana state. Sabotage of the canal left more than 10 million people in India's capital, Delhi, without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sethi 2016 ; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2016

title: A community leader representing families displaced by dam project killed in Sinaloa, Mexico
description: In Sinaloa, Mexico, Atilano Roman Tirado is shot and killed while hosting a local radio show. Mr. Tirado was a leader of the approximately 800 families that were displaced by the Picachos dam and were asking the Mexican government for compensation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: A severe drought sparked "water riots" in Northern KwaZulu-Natal
description: A severe drought in Northern KwaZulu-Natal sparks 'water riots' in the town of Jozini over access to water and in opposition to the installation of water meters. Violence erupts after a community protest, leading to the arrest of 23 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Stolley 2016

title: A water tank project is hit in air raids in Yemen
description: A water tank project and a water tank are hit during air raids in Harib and Sirwah Districts, Marib, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Air raids damage water project in Yemen
description: An air raid causes damage to a water project in Razih District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Air raids damage wells in Yemen
description: Five air raids leave wells damaged in Sirwah District, Marib, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Al-Awadh dam is damaged in air raid in Yemen
description: The Al-Awadh dam is damaged in an air raid in Radman District, Bayda, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: An unidentified group conducts an armed assault and attack on the Yasmak Dam construction site, Gumushane, Turkey
description: An unidentified group assaults the Yasmak Dam construction site in Gumushane, Turkey with rifles and shotguns.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Armed guards clash with farmers over drought-struck region of Bundelkhand, India
description: Armed guards and farmers clash over access to water from Jamunia River at the Bari Ghat Dam in the drought-struck region of Bundelkhand, India
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Das 2016, Niazi 2016b

title: Attack by the Islamic State on Tishreen Dam on the Euphrates River
description: Islamic State (IS) militants attack the Tishrin Dam on the Euphrates River in Syria. The attack is repelled with airstrikes. The following day a similar attack occurs during which at least 14 IS militants are killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lambert 2016

title: Attack on a local dam in India
description: A group of heavily armed militants fire blank rounds of bullets at a dam, creating panic among the locals. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nath 2016

title: Attacks on energy and water systems in Aleppo, Syria cut off water to two million residents
description: Two million people lack water supply in Aleppo, Syria after attacks on energy and water infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Domonoske 2016

title: Baloch Republican or Liberation Army fighters abduct and kill two laborers working at the Shadi Kaur Dam, Pakistan
description: Baloch Republican or Liberation Army fighters abduct and kill two laborers working at the Shadi Kaur Dam, Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Bombs detonated at hydroelectric power plant in East Java
description: Several explosive devices detonate at a hydroelectric power plant in Biltar, East Java, Indonesia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Jakarta Globe 2016

title: Colleague of Berta Cáceres, Lesbia Janeth, is also murdered for opposing the same dam
description: Four months after internationally known Honduran environmental activist Berta Cáceres is murdered, a second woman and environmental activist from the same organization is also murdered in Honduras. The second murdered woman, Lesbia Janeth, was working to stop the construction of a dam in La Paz, Honduras.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agren 2016

title: Dam and water driller are damaged by air raids in Yemen
description: The Al-Aqran dam and a water driller are hit during ongoing air raids in Nihm District, Sanaa, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Desalination company is hit by air raid in Yemen
description: An early morning air raid causes damage to a desalination company in Al Mokha District, Taizz, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Desalination plant is hit by air raids in Yemen
description: A desalination plant is hit during multiple air raids in Al Mokha District, Taizz, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Disruption of electrical system cuts power to water supply in Damascus, Syria
description: Attacks on Syrian electricity transmission stations cut power needed for water pumping to the eastern and western parts of Damascus. Authorities temporarily restore power five days later, but new fighting again cuts water to the city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNICEF 2016

title: Environmental activist with international recognition killed in Honduras
description: In 2016, Berta Cáceres -- a prize winning activist working to stop development of the internationally funded Agua Zarca hydroelectric dam on the Gualcarque river -- is murdered after years of death threats and state persecution linked to her campaign. In recent years hundreds of environmental activists have been killed in Latin America, including two of Sra. Cáceres colleagues.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Watts 2016, Lakhani 2017

title: Grassroots leader of efforts to stop hydroelectric projects in Brazil goes missing and is then found dead in a reservoir
description: A leader of the Movement of People Affected by Dams, Nilce de Souza Magalhaes, goes missing in January 2016 and is found dead six months later in the Jirau Dam reservoir. She had criticized Sustainable Energy Brazil, the organization leading a dam hydroelectric plant.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Brasil de Fato 2020

title: Guard at water well in the Sudan is attacked
description: A guard at water wells in the Um Burma area, Sudan is attacked and severely injured by paramilitaries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Dabanga 2016

title: Indigenous activist opposing a dam project is found dead in a suspicious suicide in Chile
description: An Indigenous activist, Macarena Valdes, is found dead in her home in Chile in an apparent suicide on August 2016. However, Valdes and her husband had been actively campaigning against the construction of a dam, including organizing blockades of the project. In 2018, prosecutors were foced to repoen the case when her family found a police report that implicated involvement of a man in her death.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; WCH 2016

title: Intentional attacks on water infrastructure in Syria
description: Control over power and water infrastructure and intentional attacks on that infrastructure are being used as weapons in the civil war in Syria. Officials estimate there has been a 50 percent reduction in access to safe water in the country since the war began.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Vidal 2016

title: Islamic State fighters destroy pipeline that provides water for eastern Mosul, Iraq
description: Islamic State fighters cut electricity to pumping stations and destroy a pipeline that provides water for eastern Mosul, Iraq, leaving more than half a million people without water. The group has intentionally cut off water supplies to various neighborhoods, according to a Mosul City Council official responsible for supervising the city's water and energy services.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Tawfeeq and Abdelaziz 2016, Laessing 2016

title: Islamic State militants raid Great Manmade River Project pumping station, Libya
description: Around 60 Islamic State militants raid the Great Manmade River (GMR) project station in Ash Shwayrif, southwest of Sirte. This system provides water to the Libyan Sahara and the northern cities of Benghazi, Sirte, and Tripoli.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Security Council 2017

title: Main water tank is damaged in Yemen
description: In Hayfan District, Taizz, a communities main water tank is damaged in the ongoing conflict in Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Massive opposition to project that threatens Indian heritage and water supplies
description: Hundreds of people are injured and arrested at protests over the construction of a major oil pipeline that threatens water quality on and near Native American lands. Massive opposition to the project developed in 2016 when the planned route reached the site of a Native American tribe called the Standing Rock Sioux, who say the plans threaten their heritage and local water supplies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; TheJournalie 2016

title: Millions of people in Yemen deprived of access to clean water
description: Attacks on water and power infrastructure throughout Yemen deprive nearly 20 million people of reliable access to clean water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ghobari and Browning 2016

title: Multiple attacks damage water tanks in Yemen
description: Water tanks are damaged over the course of several days in Kamaran District, Hudaydah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Municipal water infrastructure is attacked in South Africa in a corruption scheme to obtain contracts
description: In January 2016, Delangokubona "business forum" members, described as part of South Africa's "water mafia," lay siege to municipal infrastructure in KwaZulu-Natal threatening to kill stormwater teams and destroy infrastructure in an effort to get tenders without a bidding process.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Water Integrity Network/Corruption Watch 2020

title: Nelson Garcia, environmental activist in Honduras working to protect land and water rights, is assassinated
description: Nelson Garcia, an enviornmental activist working in Honduras to protect land and water was assassinated by unidentified gunmen. He was a member of Berta Caceres's indigenous group COPINH. She was murdered in 2015 as well for her opposition to the Agua Zarca Dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Garcia 2016

title: Oil pipelines are destroyed and used to contaminate the Tigris River and water supplies for downstream communities
description: In 2016, explosives are placed around the Baiji oil refinery north of Baghdad. Armed groups break the main pipelines to the refinery and divert the outflow to the Tigris River flowing towards Baghdad. Six downstream areas, including Baghdad, are affected by the oil pollution, leading to a shutdown of water supplies in those regions.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNICEF 2021

title: Opposition leader killed in South Africa after opposing threats to land and water
description: Environmental activist and opposition leader Sikhosiphi Radebe in South Africa is murdered after opposing industrial mining development that threatened community water and land.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Schneider 2016b

title: Protests against the building of dams on the Brahmaputra River in India
description: Protests against the building of dams on the Brahmaputra River in India's Himalayan state of Arunachal Pradesh turns violent, leading to two deaths and additional injuries. Both China and India have put forward plans for nearly 150 dams in the region, with major local opposition.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Third Pole, The 2016

title: Public officials taken hostage after an oil spill polluted local waters
description: An indigenous community in the Peruvian Amazon takes at least eight public officials hostage after an oil spill pollutes local water and lands. The Wampis community of Mayuriaga seizes a military helicopter and holds crew members and public officials in concern over inadequate emergency response plans.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Taj 2016

title: Pumping station is attacked in the Russia-Ukraine conflict, interrupting the water supply for 1.5 million people
description: A pumping station that is part of the Yuzhnodonbasskaya water pipeline is attacked. This pumping station provides water to 1.5 million people in the Donbas region, Ukraine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Strategic Foresight Group 2019

title: Rioting and looting over energy and water cuts in Venezuela
description: Rioting and looting in Venezuela over energy and water cuts leaves fifteen people injured, as severe drought effects on hydropower generation worsen energy availability and economic disruptions. President Maduro blames the crisis on the fall in global oil prices, a drought that has affected hydroelectric power generation, and political factors.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Polaco 2016

title: Riots over water in Bangalore, India
description: At least two people die and others are injured in riots over water in Bangalore, India in the state of Karnataka. The unrest starts when the Indian Supreme Court orders Karnataka to release water from dams on the Kaveri river to neighboring Tamil Nadu. Over 400 people were arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mortimer 2016, Gowen 2016

title: Scarce water supplies in drought regions of India spark violence
description: Scarce water supplies in drought-hit regions of India spark violence. As northern and central India suffer thorough severe drought and heat, police in Bundelkhand and several other regions including Tikamgarh are reporting a rise in violent, often deadly clashes over water. Indian police report that the fighting is getting more frequent and bloody, with numerous injuries and deaths reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Niazi 2016a

title: Several water pumps are hit by air raids in Yemen
description: Several water pumps are hit during two air raids in Baqim District, Sa'ada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Soqam dam damaged during air raids in Yemen
description: The Soqam dam in Sirwah District, Marib, Yemen, is damaged during air raids.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Stand-off over water rights and use resulting in death
description: In a standoff over water rights and land use, armed ranchers occupy a federal wildlife refuge in a protest that ends with one death and several arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Wiles 2016

title: Suspected Kuki National Front fighters fire blank bullets at the Lamlai Khullen-Maphou Dam, India
description: Suspected Kuki National Front fighters fired blank bullets at the Lamlai Khullen-Maphou Dam, India during an armed assault in an attempt to incite panic.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Threats to cut off supply of water in northwestern Tunisia
description: Residents of Fernana in northwestern Tunisia threaten to cut off the supply of water delivered by a pumping station to the capital, Tunis. They are protesting economic conditions and repeated water cuts that have sparked anger and protests among the local population. At least one death is reported. Water shortages are experienced in Sousse, Nabeul, Sfax, Kef, Siliana, Beja, Sidi Bouzid, Ben Arous, Medenine and Tataouine. Given the increasing number of protests, the Tunisian citizen's water observatory, Watchwater, warns against a possible "thirst uprising."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Massy 2016

title: Three water trucks struck in air raids in Yemen
