description: Three water trucks are struck in air raids in Al-Mahabishah District, Hajjah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Two dams are hit by air raids in Yemen
description: The Al-Hayathim dam and the Mahalli dam were both struck during air raids in Nihm District, Sanaa, Yemen in early December.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Two desalination plants are hit by air raids in Yemen
description: Air raids damage two desalination plants in Al Mokha and At Ta'iziyah Districts, Taizz, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Two people killed and many injured protesting arrest of anti-dam activist in India
description: On May 2, 2016 in India, two people, Tsering Tempa and Nyima Wangdi, are shot and killed by police while protesting the arrest of the anti-dam activist, Lama Lobsany Gyatso. Others at the protest are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Up to 4 million in Damascus lose water after attacks on Wadi Barada and Ain al-Fija springs, which serve 70% of the city
description: Up to four million people in Damascus, Syria suffer a loss of water services after springs outside the city are attacked. Water from the Wadi Barada and Ain al-Fija springs, which serve 70 percent of the Syrian capital, is cut off when water infrastructure is deliberately targeted.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hubbard 2017

title: Water barrier is damaged by air raid in Yemen
description: A water barrier is damaged by an air raid in Al-Qubaytah District, Lahj, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water driller is damaged by air raids in Yemen
description: A water driller is damaged by ongoing air raids in Arhab District, Sanaa, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water driller is damaged in air raid in Yemen
description: An air raid causes damage to a water driller in Sirwah District, Marib, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water driller is damaged over the course of four air raids
description: Four air raids cause damage to a water driller in Al-Safra'a District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water factory is struck during air raids in Yemen
description: The Al-Qis water factory is struck during two air raids in, Al-Hawta District, Lahj, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water pipeline is bombed in Turkey
description: A water pipeline is the target of an explosive device in Mardin, Turkey.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201604170038

title: Water pipeline is damaged in Pakistan
description: A water pipeline is damaged from explosions when it is misidentified as a gas pipeline, disrupting the water supply to a nearby village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nation 2016

title: Water project is attacked during air raids in Yemen
description: A water project is struck during an air raid in Kitaf Wa Al-Boqe'e District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water pump is damaged in Yemen
description: A water pump in Kitaf Wa Al-Boqe'e District, Sa'ada, Yemen, is damaged in the ongoing sub-national conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water pumping plant attacked in Syria

source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 351470

title: A locally organized blockade in protest of a dam project polluting a river is repeatedly attacked
description: Community members from Pajuiles, Honduras organize a blockade in protest of a dam project that is causing their local river to be polluted. People at the blockade are attacked several times over the course of a year with tear gas and other acts of physical violence. Some of the organizers are arrested and charged with usurpation and coercion.

description: An airstrike by coalition forces hits water and electricity stations in Al Kaniq, Hamdan, Sanaa, Yemen.

title: Airstrikes in Jahran, Dhamar, Yemen hit water systems
description: Airstrikes in Jahran, Dhamar, Yemen by coalition forces hit water and electricity systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 345190

title: Airstrikes in Yemen destroy water and electrical systems
description: Airstrikes by coalition forces over a few days hit water and electricity systems in Sanaa and Taiz, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 343986 & 344105

title: Airstrikes, shelling and sniper attacks damage water structures in Al Mohka, Yemen
description: Fighting in Yemen has damaged water infrastructure in several cities. Airstrikes, shelling, and sniper attacks in and around the town of Al Mokha have killed and injured scores of civilians and halted most services, including the main market and the water supply system.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ReliefWeb 2017a

title: Al-Aqran dam is hit during three air raids in Yemen
description: The Al-Aqran dam is hit during three air raids in Nihm District, Sanaa, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Al-Shabaab militants destroy water well in Kenya
description: Al-Shabaab militants destroy an important water well that had been drilled by the Kenyan army in the town of Lafey, Mandera County, leaving hundreds of residents without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kulan Post 2017 ; West 2018

title: Attack on Islamic State forces controlling the Tabqa Dam
description: A combined U.S. and Syrian force launches an attack in Syria on Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) forces controlling the Tabqa Dam, a "choke point" on the Euphrates River and source of hydroelectric power for the region, which has been under ISIL control. The bombs cause sever damage to the dam, stopping the flow of the river through it, threatening the integrity of the dam itself. Tens of thousands of civilians living below the dam are in immediate danger of complete destruction should the dam be overtopped. Before the dam is overtopped, upstream dams in Turkey cut water flow while the Tabqa dam engineers, under watch by opposing forces, restore operation to the dam. Revelations about the attack in 2022 confirm the US's involvement, identifying US Special Operations unit Task Force 9 as the perpetrator of the attack, even though the dam was on the US military's "no-strike list."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gibbons-Neff 2017 ; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2017 ; Phillips, Khan, and Schmitt 2022

title: Baloch Liberation Front fighters assault and injure two workers at the Shadi Kaur Dam construction site in Pakistan

title: Bomb damages water truck in Egypt
description: Islamic State fighters claim responsibility for bombs placed in a road that detonates, damaging a water truck and a tank in Sheikh Zuweid, North Sinai, Egypt.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 221401

title: Citizens protesting water cuts shut down local government in Algeria

source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 183728

title: Civilians protesting lack of access to water are reportedly beaten and tortured in Sudan
description: Five people from a citizen water committee and local police in El Fasher, North Darfur, Sudan, are reportedly beaten and tortured by military officers after asking the military to allow local residents to organize and take water from a local source. Residents stage protests against the violent reaction of the military.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sudanese Online 2017 ; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 318554

title: Clashes in Darfur between farmers and herders over water access result in deaths
description: At least 70 people have been killed in the past few months in clashes between farmers and herders over access to water resources and land in the southern part of Darfur.

title: Clashes over the ecological impacts of a proposed coal plant on aquatic ecosystems and fisheries
description: Protesters take to the streets in the center of Dhaka and more than 50 are injured in clashes over the potential ecological impacts of a proposed coal plant on aquatic ecosystems and fisheries. These actions follow on protests from 2016.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Schneider 2016a, Paul 2017

title: Community demonstrator murdered while protesting local hydroelectric projects
description: Don Sebastian Alonzo Juan, 72, is shot and killed while participating in a peaceful community demonstration in Yichkisis, village of San Mateo Ixtatan, Huehuetenango, Guatemala, against three local hydroelectric projects. The shots are reportedly fired by the private security guards hired by the hydroelectric project company.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Simon 2018

title: Community leader fighting for Afro Rights and protection of water resources killed in Honduras
description: A 73 year-old community leader in Honduras, Silvino Zapata Martinez, who fought for the rights of the Garifuna (Afro-descendant) community and campaigned to protect local water and land resources, such as the Masca River, is shot by gunmen and left to die.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; HRD Memorial n.d.-a

title: Conflict over water between two clans in Somalia kill at least 14 people
description: A conflict between two clans that started over the use of water and pastureland leaves at least 14 people dead and 50 others injured in Garowe, Nugaal, Somalia. Sources differ on the number of dead and the date of the violent clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 293947

title: Conflict over water quotas lead to two deaths in Iraq

source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 353965

title: Demonstration in South Africa over access to clean drinking water turns violent
description: A demonstration led by locals from the northwest village of Moeka, South Africa for clean drinking water turns violent. One protester is shot and killed and several homes are destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 302462

title: Demonstration over access to clean water turns violent
description: Demonstrations led by residents of Ketu South, Volta, Ghana, who are upset about the drying up of domestic groundwater wells, turn violent. Property is damaged and clashes between residents and police result in the death of one resident and the injury of two others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 227239

title: Demonstration over access to water and concerns about salary payments turn violent
description: Citizens from Crater, Aden, Yemen, demonstrate to demand salary payments and access to water and electricity services by blocking roads and setting tires on fire.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 345102

title: Environmental defender killed for activisim against Provenir II dam in Colombia
description: An environmental defender, Luis Edilson Arango Gallego, is killed in August 2017 near his home in Puerto Nare, Colombia. He had been recently working to defend the Samana Norte River and block the Provenir II hydroelectric plant from being built.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Universidad Nacional de Colombia n.d.

title: Ethiopian troops reportedly attack a water source in Somalia

title: Four people killed in clash over access to a water point in North Darfur, Sudan

title: Government forces in Yemen seize two major water wells; kill 12 Houthi

title: Gunfire exchanged during a water dispute in Somalia

title: Nearly 3 million people left without reliable access to water supplies in Ukraine

title: Protest over shortages of drinking water turn violent in Morocco

title: Protest over water outages, power cuts, and fees turns violent

title: Protests over water cuts turn violent in Tunisia

title: Protests over water outages turn violent in Sudan

title: Protests over water shortages turn violent in South Africa
description: Residents in South Africa protesting against water shortages are reported to have burned water tanks meant to help alleviate the problem.

title: Residents and police clash over lack of access to water in South Africa
description: Residents of Bushbuckridge, Ehlanzeni, Mpumalanga, South Africa, who claim to have asked for water for three years, stage a protest, including burning tires. Police respond to the protest, firing rubber bullets.

title: Three workers from the Saichang-Maphou Dam site are abducted and two are killed by suspected Kuki National Front fighters, India

title: Water drill is hit during air raid in Yemen

source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water for the Bari community, Somalia is cut off
description: Water for the Bari community in Somalia is cut off during a violent confrontation between militants that reportedly support Islamic State and Puntland security forces.

source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water project is hit during air raid in Yemen
description: A water project is hit during an air raid in Hamdan District, Sanaa, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water pumps destroyed in conflict over access to water in Mali
description: People identified as militants destroy several water pumps and a number of fields and seize cattle in Kewa, Djenne, Mopti, Mali.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 247138

title: Water tankers are destroyed in Yemen
description: Al-Qaeda affiliated militants are reported to destroy multiple water tankers that belonged to Houthis militants and the Yemeni Army in Wald Rabi, Al Bayda, and Lawdar, Abyan, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 347234, 347354

title: Water truck is damaged by air raid in Yemen
description: A water truck is damaged by an air raid in Al-Khawkhah District, Hudaydah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water truck is hit during air raid in Yemen
description: A water truck is hit during an air raid in Harf Sufyan District, Amran, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water truck near a market is hit during air raid in Yemen
description: A water truck is hit during an air raid near Hayran market, Hayran District, Hajjah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water well and desalination plant are hit during air raids
description: A water well and a desalination plant in Al Mokha District, Taizz, Yemen are hit during air raids.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water well attacked in Yemen during air raids
description: A water well is hit during air raids in Mawza District, Taizz, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water well is poisoned in Somalia, killing more than 30 people
description: Thirty-two people are reported killed and many others sickened from a poisoned water well in Masuubiye, Baidoa, Somalia. It is suspected that the well was poisoned by al Shabaab, a militant group affiliated with Al-Qaeda, in an attempt to prevent government soldiers from drinking the water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ikeji 2017

title: Well is hit during air raid in Yemen
description: The Al-Naysani well in Maqbanah District, Taizz, Yemen is hit during an air raid.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: 11 deaths attributed to ongoing conflict between herdsmen and farmers
description: Eleven are killed and 11 more injured during an attack by Fulani herdsmen on a farming community in Central Nigeria, ignited by the continuing conflict over land and water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2018a

title: A Guatemalan indigenous man involved in opposing dam construction projects is killed
description: Luis Armando Maldonado Marin, a known member of the Social Pastoral of the Earth, a local group actively opposing the construction of a dam, is shot and killed in Quetzaltenango, Guatemala. This is a region in Guatemala where many indigenous defenders are opposing hydroelectric projects.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Business & Human Rights Resource Centre n.d.-a

title: A Honduran lawyer who represents people protesting a hydroelectric dam is murdered
description: Honduran lawyer Carlos Hernandez is found murdered in Tela de Altantida, Honduras after committing to defend the town's mayor that was facing criminal charges for peaceful opposition to a hydroelectric dam project planned on the Jilamito River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: A UN mission collecting water for their base in South Sudan is attacked, injuring one Nepalese peacekeeper
description: On September 15th, an officer with the National Security Service of South Sudan fires at an UNMISS convoy collecting water for the UNMISS base in Yei, wounding a Nepalese peacekeeper.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7685832

title: A demonstration against the lack of water supply in Talara, Peru results in two injuries
description: On October 1, in Talara, Piura, Peru, hundreds of local inhabitants demonstrate against the lack of water supply in the area. Police clash with demonstrators by shooting rubber bullets and throwing tear gas, injuring two rioters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7378436

title: A dispute over access to water leads to one injury in India
description: On September 14, two families clash in Daria area of Chandigarh over getting water from a tap. A 17 year old girl was injured with a sickle in the fight.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7901182

title: A dispute over severe water shortage in the Hansi district of India leads to a clash causing a dozen injuries
description: On June 26, a violent clash occurs between two villages, Puthi Mangal Khan and Dhani Peeranwali, in Hansi district, India over acute water shortages. At least 12 people are reported injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5483096

title: A dispute over water distribution in Shikarpur, Pakistan leads to more than two dozen injuries
description: On July 15, 26 men sustain critical injuries in a clash between two groups of Sethar community in Batro area, Shikarpur, Pakistan over water distribution.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5936861

title: A dispute over water used for local mining in Chile leads to a demonstration, clashes with police, and injuries
description: On July 19, in Salamanca, Chile near Illapel (Coquimbo), around 60 residents of Cuncumen hold a demonstration calling for the end of water usage at the Los Pelambres mine. Police clash with demonstrators; eight injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7359974

title: A fight over a water point in Syria between government militias and Islamic State fighters results in multiple deaths
description: Regime and loyalist militia forces including Hezbollah clash with Islamic State fighters in the Tlul al Safa area of Syria over an important water point. Regime air and missile strikes kill at least four Islamic State fighters and an estimated 10 others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8114602

title: A fight over irrigation water in Pakistan kills two villagers and injures three more
description: On September 23, the Lanjar and Chandio tribes clash over irrigation water near Moro city (Naushahro Feroze, Sindh). Two villagers are killed and three are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5526747

title: A fight over the distribution of irrigation water in Pakistan injures seven
description: On August 18, two groups of the Bozdar tribe clash over distribution of irrigation water in Pir Barhi village, Sindh, Pakistan using sticks, rocks, and guns. Seven people are injured and hospitalized and one person arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4613013

title: A fight over water drainage in Pakistan kills one person
description: On September 23, two groups of the Kalhoro community clash over water drainage issues in Kholar, Sindh, Pakistan, killing one man.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8073481

title: A hydroelectric plant in Guatemala is destroyed in a dispute over local water control
description: On July 30, in Purulha, Baja Verapaz, Guatemala, community members occupy a hydroelectric plant, disarm local security, and destroy the infrastructure. The protestors claim that the hydroelectric plant is occupying lands of the community.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7342859

title: A large number of deaths are reported in attack on farmers by armed herdsmen in Nigeria over water and land resources
description: On a single day in Nigeria's Plateau state, an attack by armed herdsmen leaves dozens in farming communities dead. This attack is part of ongoing violence that is in part triggered by access to water and land resources. Reports vary in the number dead; one cites 200 and another, 86.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2018b ; Reuters 2018 ; McNeill and Akwagyiram 2018

title: A leader of local opposition to the Quadriver Mini Hydro Dam in the Philippines is murdered by assassins
description: A local leader of opposition to a dam project, Ricardo Pugong Manymi, is shot and killed by assassins in Tinoc town, Ifugao, Philippines. He is a known leader of the opposition to the Quadriver Mini Hydro Dam and of the Ifugao Peasant Movement, which seeks to defend human rights of the indigenous people of the Ifugao province.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Cimatu 2018

title: A local water system is damaged in a shootout between drug trafficking gangs in Brazil
description: On September 30, in Sao Goncalo, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil a shoot-out between drug trafficking gangs in the Minha Casa, Minda Vida complex of Joquei neighborhood damages the local water system, leaving residents without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7438702

title: A police station water tank is damaged in an attack on the station in India
description: On June 27, assailants throw a grenade at a police station in Pulwama district, Jammu and Kashmir, India. No people are injured, however the station's water tank is damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201806270018

title: A protest against a bill threatening water privatization in El Salvador is suppressed by government security forces
description: On June 14, 2018, students from El Salvador University and affiliates to the National Administration for Water Supply and Sewerage march to the Legislative Assembly in San Salvador City to protest a water bill that they claim aims to privatize water. Security forces use teargas to disperse the protesters. One injury is reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7344022

title: A truck carrying water tanks is used by suicide bombers in a failed attack in Syria
description: On January 18, a group of suicide bombers using a truck carrying water tanks in Aleppo, Syria is stopped by the Free Syrian Army. Members of the FSA kill three of the assailants and a fourth dies when he detonates his explosive device.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201801180025

title: A water filtration vehicle is attacked in Ukraine, five employees are injured
description: On April 17, a water filtration vehicle is attacked in Donetsk, Ukraine. At least five employees are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201804170026

title: A water project is attacked with explosive devices in Iraq
description: On October 4, a water project in Gharib, Kirkuk, Iraq is targeted and attacked with explosive devices. No group claims responsibility for the attack; however, sources attribute the attack to the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201810040002

title: A water tank and other farm items are damaged in an attack on a cowshed construction site in India
description: On August 15, a water tank, a tractor, and motorbike are damaged and several cows are injured in an attack on a cowshed construction site in Bara, Bihar, India. The Communist Part of India - Maoist claim responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201808150052

title: A water tanker is a casualty in one of seven attacks in Jharkhand, India on the same day
description: On May 29, seven related attacks occur across Jharkhand, India. A water tanker is a casualty in one of the attacks. The Communist Party of India - Maoist is suspected as the group responsible for the attacks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201805290033

title: A water tanker is damaged in an attack on a construction site in India
description: On March 2, a water tanker is damaged during an attack on a construction site near Kadambaguda, Odisha, India. One construction worker is kidnapped before being released a short time later.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201803020025

title: A water well and other structures are damaged by airstrike
description: Five farmers are killed in an airstrike while getting water from a pump in Al-Jah in Bayt Al-Faqih, Yemen. The water well, a mosque, and houses are damaged in the airstrike.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4598884

title: A well is damaged in an attack on Kenya Defense Forces in Somalia
description: On July 27, in an attack on Kenya Defense Forces soldiers in Dhamaso, Gedo, Somalia, a well and telecommunications equipment are damaged. No group claims responsibility for the incident; however, sources attribute the attack to Al-Shabaab.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201807270003

title: Air raid targets a water tanker
description: A Saudi-led coalition air raid is reported on Al Ghawl area of Nihm district, northeast of Sanaa city, allegedly targeting a water tanker. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5437331

title: Air raids are reported on a water rig
description: Two Saudi-led coalition air raids are reported on a water rig in Al Ammar area of Sadah border Governorate in northwestern Yemen. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5437334

title: Air raids are reported on water wells and reservoirs in Yemen
description: Five Saudi-led coalition air raids are reported on water wells and reservoirs across the Kamaran island in the north of Hudaydah Governorate, western Yemen. No casualties are reported but a large number of wells and reservoirs are destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5439301

title: Airstrike hits a water project in Yemen
description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike reportedly hits a water project in the Nushur area of Safra district, threatening to affect up to 10,500 people who rely on the water supplied by the project in Yemen. No injuries or fatalities are reported. This particular project has been hit three times by airstrikes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5438563

title: Airstrike targets a water project in Yemen
description: A Saudi-led coalition airstrike targets a water project in the al-Hamzat area of Sahar district, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5428241

title: Airstrike targets a water-transport truck in Yemen
description: A young girl is seriously injured by a Saudi-led coalition airstrike that targeted a water-transport truck in Ad Dhahi area of Hudayda, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5193162

title: Airstrikes damage water and sanitation infrastructure in Yemen
description: Airstrikes over several days in July in the city of Al-Hudaydah, Yemen, damage water and sanitation infrastructure, including many drinking water wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNOCHA and UNOCHA-Yemen 2018 ; Algohbary 2018 ; Al-Rodaini 2018

title: Al Shabaab diverts a river, forcing opposition to undefendable higher ground in Somalia
description: Al Shabaab, a group fighting to create an Islamic state in Somalia, diverts water from the Jubba River, causing a flood that forced Somali, Kenyan, and U.S. military forces to move to higher ground where they were later ambushed. One soldier from the U.S. was killed in the ambush.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Goldbaum 2018

title: An attempted theft of a water pump leads to an injury and arrest
description: On August 21 in Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil a man is beaten after he tried to steal a water pump. The man was arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7439535

title: An explosive device detonates at an oil pipeline, causing oil to pollute a local waterway in Colombia
description: On November 21, an oil pipeline is attacked in Boyaca, Colombia, polluting a local waterway with oil. No group claims responsibility; however, sources attribute the attack to the National Liberation Army (ELN).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201811210002

title: An oil pipeline is attacked multiple times, causing oil to flow into a local waterway in Colombia
description: On November 12, an oil pipeline is attacked four times in Arauca, Colombia, causing oil to flow into and pollute a nearby waterway. No group claims responsibility; however, sources attribute the attack to the National Liberation Army (ELN).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201811110002, 201811110030, 201811120

title: At least 8 more killed in ongoing conflict over access to water between farmers and herders, Mali
description: At least eight more people die in an ongoing conflict between the Fulani and Dogon communities in Mali near the town of Koro, sparked by access to water and grazing disputes. Since March 2018, the total death toll from this ongoing conflict is reported to be 25.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2018a

title: Attacks in Farah, Afghanistan are reportedly related to efforts by Iran to disrupt water projects in Afghanistan
description: Attacks in Farah in the western region of Afghanistan in early 2018 by the Taliban may, in part, be supported by Iran in an attempt to reduce Afghanistan's ability to pursue water dam infrastructure projects.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hussein and Jedinia 2018 ; Jerusalem Post, The 2018

title: Attacks on water infrastructure in the ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine cause water shortages for millions
description: Water shortages are reported by residents living in at least 20 communities near the line of conflict in the Donbas region of Ukraine. In spite of a ceasefire negotiated in 2014, the ongoing violence has damaged public utilities, leaving millions of residents without water for days and weeks at a time.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; REACH 2018 ; Protection Cluster 2018 ; Strategic Foresight Group 2019

title: Brothers murdered for opposing hydropower project in Guatemala
description: Neri and Domingo Esteban Pedro were found murdered near the San Andres hydroelectric project on the Yal Witz River in western Guatemala. The brothers were vocal opponents of the project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ramon 2018

title: Clans in Pakistan clash over water supply, killing one and injuring four
description: Machi and Wadhayo clans clash over water supply and agricultural lands on June 23 in Pakistan. A youth is killed and 4 others are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5525063

title: Clashes between tribesmen and pro-Houthi force over a water project
description: For the second consecutive day, clashes between Al 'Ukad tribesmen and pro-Houthi forces are reported in the Ridmah district of Ibb Governorate, Yemen. Clashes are reportedly initiated on September 24 as the tribesmen seize the weapons of a group of Houthi fighters to show their opposition to a water project. Injuries are reported on both sides but no fatalities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5440220, 5440187

title: Clashes expand between Tajik and Kyrgyz farmers over irrigation water
description: Clashes between farmers over irrigation water across the Tajikistan-Kyrgyzstan border escalate, with at least two instances involving armed guards to defuse the fights. One fight started over the installation of a water pump.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Arnold 2018

title: Clashes near a hospital in Hodeidah, Yemen damage building, destroy water tanks, injure patients; 149 killed in 24 hours
description: On November 11, fierce clashes between pro-Houthi and anti-Houthi National Resistance forces are reported in the direct vicinity of Al-Thawrah hospital in the south of Hodeidah city, resulting in damages to the building, including the destruction of its water tanks, and the injuring of many patients as they evacuated the hospital. On November 12, medics in hospitals across the city reported the death of 110 pro-Houthi fighters, 32 anti-Houthi fighters and 7 civilians over a 24-hour period.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8070171

title: Clashes over a water project in Yemen result in injuries
description: Clashes between Al 'Ukad tribesmen and pro-Houthi forces are reported in the Ridmah district of Ibb governorate, Yemen, over opposition to a water project. Injuries are reported on both sides.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6431623, 6431589

title: Conflicts over pasture land and water resources lead to violence
description: 14 people are killed in Northern Kenya, near Marsabit, after ongoing conflicts between two ethnic groups over land and water resources turns violent.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Abidi 2018

title: Desalination plant hit during air raids in Yemen
description: A desalination plant in Hays District, Hudayah, Yemen is hit during air raids.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Employees of Voda Donbassa are wounded during attacks on water systems in Ukraine
description: In April 2018, five Voda Donbassa (Donbas Water) employees are attacked and injured, resulting in the suspension of operations and evacuation of water sector employees and water shortages for nearly 380,000 civilians, particularly in Avdiivka, Yasynuvata, and Betmanove cities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; OSCE 2018

title: Environmental activist found dead near Kyiv, Ukraine
description: An environmental activist, Nikolay Yarema, is found dead near Kyiv, Ukraine. Yarema was known for his opposition to the seizure of the Svyatoshinsky Lake area, a well-forested northwestern part of Kyiv bordering the Nyvka River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; JAM news 2018

title: Environmental activist in India who worked to stop a dam on the Kali River is killed
description: An environmental activist, Ajit Maneshwar Naik, is killed by a masked assailant in Dandeli, in the state of Karnataka, India, where he worked. Naik had spent years fighting against the construction of what whould have become the seventh dam on the Kali River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Hemalatha 2018

title: Explosives detonate at a water plant in Iraq
description: On October 6, explosives detonate at a water plant in Abbasi, Kirkuk, Iraq. No group claims responsibility for the attack; however, sources attribute the attack to the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201810060046

title: Extensive violence reported over water scarcity in southern Iraq
description: In the province of Dhi Qar, Iraq, widespread clan clashes erupt due to water scarcity.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al Monitor 2018

title: Farmer injured in a clash with police in Varzaneh, Iran during a strike over access to water
description: A farmer reports losing sight in one eye and wounds from a pellet gun from a clash with police ignited by a strike over lack of water in Varzaneh, Iran.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Karimi and Nasiri 2018

title: Farmers in Qarneh, Iran destroy facilities diverting water from the city of Isfahan to neighboring Yazd province
description: In mid-November, angry farmers in Qarneh demonstrate against farming water shortages and destroy facilities diverting water from the city of Isfahan to the neighboring Yazd Province, Iran. The security forces clash with the rioters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6028843

title: Father and son are beaten to death in water dispute in Delhi, India
description: In Delhi during severe drought in 2018 a father and son are beaten to death in a water dispute.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Oaten and Patidar 2021

title: Four water wells are attacked in Libya
description: On December 9, four water wells are attacked in Libya. No group claims responsibility for the attacks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201812090005, 201812090006, 201812090

title: Government employees repairing a water pipeline are attacked in Iraq
description: On October 5, government employees from the Ministry of Transportation who are repairing a water pipeline are attacked in Shatt al-Arab, Basra, Iraq. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201810060039

title: Grenades are thrown and rounds are fired at a water pump house outside an Air Force post in India
description: On February 20, grenades are thrown and rounds are fired at a water pump house outside an Air Force post in Malangpora, Jammu and Kashmir, India. No injuries are reported and no group claims the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201802200026

title: Haryana, India villages clash over water and 12 are injured
description: Residents of one village in Haryana install a motor pump to draw water from a local water source, but residents of a nearby village object to it, leading to violent clashes, twelve injuries, and the destruction of the pump.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; The Kashmir Monitor 2018

title: Indigenous anti-dam activist killed in the state of Nayarit, Mexico
description: Indigenous anti-dam activist, Margarito Diaz Gonzalez is shot and killed in the state of Nayarit, Mexico. He opposed a dam that threatened the historic territories of the Huichol Indians, also known as the Wixarika.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Associated Press 2018

title: Indigenous leader in Mexico murdered for defending territory from mining and transmission lines from hydroelectric projects
description: In May 2018 , indigenous leader, Manuel Gaspar Rodriguez, is murdered in the middle of the night in Sierra Norte de Puebla, Mexico. Rodriguez was one of eight facing charges brought by the national electric utility company for participating in a blockade of transmission lines that were to be built in connection with several hydroelectric projects in his home territory.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; MiningWatch Canada 2018

title: Indingenous leader in Mexico known for opposition to hydroelectric projects in his region disappears
description: An indigenous leader in the Movimiento Agrario Indigena Zapatista (MAIZ) organization, Sergio Rivera Hernandez, goes missing on August 23, 2018. He had been active in working to protect the rights of indigenous communities in the state of Puebla, Mexico, where two dam projects were underway. As of September 2020, a judge ruled to acquit the three individuals who had been charged with his disappearance.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Front Line Defenders 2020

title: Injuries are reported during protests to demand potable water, food, and energy in Lara state, Venezuela
description: On December 17, in the Palavecino municipality in Lara state, Venezuela residents from several communities protest to demand the distribution of food, domestic gas, and potable water. State police officers use force against protesters by shooting pellets and tear gas to disperse the protest. Pregnant women and the elderly are reportedly beaten by police officers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7362053, 7362078

title: Injuries are reported when hundreds of students protest increases in water prices in Sulawesi, Indonesia
description: On November 30, hundreds of students protest increases in water prices in Watampone district, South Sulawesi province, Indonesia. Two students are injured by unknown attackers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7462749

title: Iranian security forces shoot at protesters, injuring one, at demonstration in Khorramshahr over lack of water
description: Protests over lack of drinking water supplies in Khorramshahr, Iran begin in front of government buildings. Social media posts of these protests include sounds of shots and cries and show security forces shooting at protesters. Only one protester is reported injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Euronews 2018b ; Associated Press (AP) 2018b

title: Iraqi female activist assassinated
description: An Iraqi activist, Su?ad al-?Ali, is assassinated while getting into her vehicle in Basra, Iraq. Mrs. Al-Ali had worked to bring better government services to her community, including safe and reliable drinking water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al Jazeera 2018a

title: Islamic State militants attack the Sarir water station in Libya and clash with government forces
description: In August, Libyan government forces clash with Islamic State militants near Haruj following an attack on the Sarir water station.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6738502 ; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 20180

title: Jaw Prison detainees routinely punished with water cuts in temperatures of up to 122°F, protesters attacked and sent to solitary confinement
description: In 2018, authorities at Jaw Prison in Bahrain reportedly impose water cuts lasting several days at a time during extreme summer heat, providing prisoners with only one cup of water a day, forcing them to drink toilet water. The prison is said to routinely use water deprivation as a form of punishment. In 2019 a prisoner is assaulted and placed into solitary confinement for protesting the outages, and in the same year a large police squad armed with dogs and shotguns is deployed to intimidate and attack prisoners demanding access to water, with their drinking water subsequently cut in retaliation. The issue continues as of 2024.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Americans for Democracy & Human Rights in Bahrain 2018 ; Bahrain Today 2019

title: Lack of access to potable water in the Dominican Republic leads to violent demonstrations
description: On July 9, 2018, shots are fired at the police station in Navarrete, Villa Bisono, Dominican Republic during a violent demonstration to demand improved access to potable water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7338609

title: Main water tank is targeted by military shelling
description: The main water tank of Durayhimi district, Yemen, which supplies most of the district in drinking water, is reportedly targeted by military shelling. Conflicting reports from local sources attribute the bombing to either pro-Houthi forces or Saudi-led coalition Apache helicopters that are targeting Houthi snipers near the tank. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5438816

title: Major dam and water source captured in Syria
description: The Afrin Dam, a major dam and water source on the Afrin River in Syria, is captured by Turkish forces and their Syrian militia allies, causing concern for the nearby communities that depend on the dam for water. These same forces are also in control of nearby Maydanki dam. Interruptions to water and electricity in communities dependent on these dams have occurred, along with reports of attacks on civilian centers and populations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Rudaw 2018

title: Man shot over access to water in Delhi, India
description: A man is shot in Sangam Vihar -- one of the poorest parts of Delhi -- during a dispute over water. The summer of 2018 sees one of the worst droughts in Dehli, India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Oaten and Patidar 2020

title: Member of an Indigenous rights organization in Mexico working to defend land and rivers is killed
description: In October 2018 a member of Comite de Defensa de Los Pueblos Indigenas (CODEDI), Noel Castillo Aguilar, is killed in Mexico. Aguilar was an active member in campaigns defending land and rivers in his home territory in the state of Oaxaca.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Davison 2018

title: Mexican farmers and white landowners clash over water
description: An alliance of local Mexican farmers storm the property of a white family living in Chihuahua state, Mexico, in frustration over what the farmers believe is an excessive use of water from the local river and aquifer. The clash results in one farmer being shot and other injuries to individuals on both sides of the conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kryt 2019 ; Mayorga 2018

title: More than 70 water systems damaged in Ethiopia related to violent conflicts
description: At least 76 water systems have been damaged by the ongoing conflict in the Oromia region of Ethiopia. The larger conflict leading to these casualties is between different ethnic groups and has displaced hundreds of thousands of people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNICEF 2018

title: Of 18 related violent attacks in one day in Thailand, one occurs at a waterworks authority compound
description: On May 20, 18 related violent attacks occur across Thailand. One of the 18 occurs at a Provincial Waterworks authority compound in Bacho, Narathiwat. No group claimed responsibility for the attack, however, the Barisan Revolusi Nasional are thought to be responsible.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201805200020

title: One death and several injuries are reported in a clash over wastewater drainage in India
description: On October 29, a woman is killed and 7 others wounded in a clash over a waste water drainage in Sheharmalpur village (Panipat, Haryana), India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5591751

title: One injury is reported when Israeli forces destroy a water pipeline in Kafr Qaddum, Palestine
description: On October 13, Israeli forces destroy a water pipeline in Kafr Qaddum sparking clashes with locals. An elderly woman is reportedly injured when she is hit with a tear gas canister.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5364594

title: One injury reported in protests in the Dominican Republic over access to potable water
description: On August 1, a woman is injured by gunfire during a protest in Navarrete, Bisono, Dominican Republic to demand access to potable water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7338616

title: One killed and several injured in fighting between farmers and herders in Tanzania over access to water
description: One person is killed and several police officers are injured in a fight over access to water resources between herders and farmers near the village of Dihida, Morogoro, Tanzania.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Makoye 2016

title: One person is killed during a protest to demand potable water and electricity in Bolivar state, Venezuela
description: On July 16, one person is killed in San Felix, Ciudad Guayana, Bolivar state, Venezuela during a protest to demand potable water and electric power in the city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7758571

title: Organizer of an encampment in protest of a dam project is killed by security forces in Honduras
description: An organizer of an encampment in protest of a dam project on the Jilamito River, Ramon Fiallos, is shot and killed by security forces in Arizona, Atlantida, Honduras. The community names a bridge in commemoration of him.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Walsh 2019

title: Over 230 people are sickened by poisoned drinking water in the conflict between Ukraine and Russia
description: Over 230 people are poisoned through contaminated drinking water in the town of Makiivka in the Donetsk region Ukraine. That water is thought to have been intentionally contaminated.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Strategic Foresight Group 2019

title: Police kill farmer and another community organizer who helped protect a local river in Honduras
description: A farmer who helped environmental organizers defending a local river, Geovanny Diaz Carcamo, is taken from his home in Pajuiles, Honduras, and killed by police in the middle of the night. His murder occurs one day after the murder of Ramon Fiallos, another community organizer who also worked in support of protecting a local river.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Lakhani 2018

title: Police shoot and kill a man protesting the Bonyunyu Dam project in Kenya
description: On January 9, 2018, Jomo Nyanguti is shot by police who are guarding surveyors mapping a dam site for the Bonyunyu Dam project in Kenya. It is reported that Nyanguti confronted the police officers and that three other people were arrested. Protestors are concerned that the dam will displace thousands of people from their ancestral lands and have stated that the project has moved forward without public consultation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Rivers n.d.

title: Prison inmates in Campeche, Mexico riot to protest lack of drinking water; two injuries are reported
description: On October 24, inmates of the San Francisco Koben Social Reintegration Center, Campeche, Mexico demonstrate against the lack of drinking water supply. They clash with the Penitentiary Police for about two hours until the Campeche State Undersecretary of Public Security mediates the riot. Two injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7648292

title: Pro-Hadi forces manage to take a water project
description: Pro-Hadi forces manage to take a number of sites after clashing with Houthi militias in the Alb area of Sadah, Yemen. According to the source, pro-Hadi troops take the areas of Mimna, Dhaher al-Burkan, Al Masirah, Water project, Al-Faridh, Qiraa'a, and the sniper outpost, all in the Alb area. No information on casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5428602

title: Pro-Houthi forces reportedly blow up a water tank
description: Pro-Houthi forces reportedly blow up the main water tank of Tuhayta as anti-Houthi forces are closing in on the city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5438269

title: Pro-Houthi forces reportedly destroy water collection tanks
description: Property destruction: Pro-Houthi forces reportedly destroy water collection tanks in Bani Zuhayr village west of Hays city in the south of Al Hudaydah Governorate. The tanks are reportedly the only source of water for the citizens of Hays district.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5429022

title: Protest to prevent oil pipeline that threatens water resources is met with violent arrests
description: Dozens of protestors are arrested and restrained, sometimes with violent tactics, as they physically resist the construction of a major oil pipeline in the United States. The protestors argue that the pipeline is proceeding illegally and that it threatens their water supplies as well as other resources that are vital to their way of life.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; L'eau Est La Vie Camp 2018 ; Zanolli 2018 ; Jamail 2018

title: Protests against poor water quality and services in Iraq lead to one death and several injuries
description: On July 10, hundreds of citizens in Al-Haritha, north of Basra, Iraq block a road in protest against poor services and the salinity of the water. One demonstrator is killed and several wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4623454

title: Protests by farmers over transfers of water from Isfahan to Yazd, Iran turn violent and cause damage to water transfer systems
description: Water systems used to transfer water from Isfahan to the neighboring province of Yazd are damaged multiple times by farmers protesting the loss of the water supply. Farmers blame the Iranian government for the lack of water in their region. Reports from social media show police officers attacking farmers associated with the destroyed pipes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Radio Farda 2018

title: Protests in Algeria for improved water supply and electricity leads to clashes with police and injuries
description: On July 22, residents of Ouargla, Algeria protest high electricity prices due to the heat wave and demand better access to tap water. Protesters clashed with police leading to several injuries. On September 15, protests expand and between 5,000 and 25,000 people demonstrate against inadequate water and sanitation infrastructure and a lack of jobs. This clash with police also leads to injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7969270

title: Protests in Iran over lack of water, mismanagement, and corruption around water lead to deaths of dozens
description: Ongoing protests against lack of water, mismanagement, and corruption around water are led by residents in small towns in western Iran. These protests gain more media attention as tensions escalate over time and may be linked to demonstrations from late 2017 and early 2018 that lead to the death of dozens of people. In 2018, at least nine environmental leaders are arrested, and one jailed environmentalist dies of alleged suicide.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Dehghanpisheh 2018

title: Protests in Iran over water shortages and poor quality lead to injuries. Deaths also reported by some outlets
description: In Iran, protests over the shortage and poor quality of drinking water turn violent as police open fire at rioters who throw stones and attack public buildings and banks. There are conflicting reports over the number of casualties; while Iranian officials deny any fatalities, they acknowledge that 11 people, including police officers, were wounded. Opposition websites report up to 4 fatalities among the demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6120737

title: Protests over water and electric services in South Africa turn violent and leave one police officer injured
description: On June 30, Dube Village residents block a highway, burn tires, and throw stones at the police demanding service delivery of water and electricity from eThekwini Municipality in Inanda. A police officer is injured during the protest.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8009004

title: Protests over water shortages turn violent in Iran
description: Water shortages in the southern part of Iran have caused protests, which turned violent with attacks on property and other infrastructure. Police action to break up the protests lead to several injuries and deaths.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Maclean 2018 ; Campbell 2018 ; Hameed 2018 ; Givetash 2018

title: Residents of Tall-e Kushk, Iran clash with police after water pumps are confiscated from well; one person is killed
description: In July, residents of Tall-e Kushk, Iran clash with police, objecting to the confiscation of water pumps from the wells in the village. One person was killed after the police fired a warning shot to disperse the rioters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6028698

title: Sanitation facility damaged in conflict in Yemen
description: A sanitation facility in Zabid District, Hudaydah is damaged in the ongoing conflict in Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Second environmental activist opposed to Gaya dam in the state of Puebla, Mexico, is murdered
description: A well known leader of local opposition to the Gaya hydroelectric dam in the Mexican state of Puebla, Adrian Tihuilit, is found dead in his car one day after he was reported missing. He is the second defender of human and environmental rights to be killed in the state of Puebla in two weeks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; HRD Memorial. n.d.-b

title: Seven people are hospitalized after a fight over sewage water in Pakistan
description: Neighbors clash over the issue of sewage water in the street in Gujranwala City, Pakistan on August 16. Seven people are hospitalized.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4613468

title: Seven people injured during dispute over irrigation water in Pakistan
description: Two groups in Jaffarabad District of Balochistan, Pakistan clash over an irrigation water dispute on June 25. Seven people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7699475

title: Suspected Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist fighters detonate bombs targeting the office of the Arun-III Hydropower Project, Nepal
description: Suspected Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist (CPN-Maoist-Chand) fighters detonate three bombs targeting the office of the Arun-III Hydropower project, Nepal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Suspected Muslim extremists attack the Djenne Dam construction site in Mali
description: Suspected Muslim extremists attack the Djenne Dam construction site, Mali, buring cranes, vehicles, generators, and construction materials.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Suspected Taliban fighters assault and attack the Kamal Khan Dam, Afghanistan, 13 deaths and 7 injuries
description: Suspected Taliban fighters assault and attack the Kamal Khan Dam, Afghanistan, killing twelve guards. One attacker is killed and seven are wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Suspicious circumstances around death of a young activist fighting water pollution in Ukraine
description: A young activist known for fighting industrial pollution of local reservoirs and for human rights, Mykola Bychkho, is found dead in the woods near his home in the township of Eskhar (Kharkiv oblast), Ukraine. Although local officals rule his death a suicide, the community disputes this claim and protests authorities to pressure them into further examination of his death. Bychkho had been successful at getting an environmental commission created in his efforts to fight the pollution of the local reservoir by various industries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Coynash 2018

title: Tank used to store water is by an airstrike
description: A tank used to store potable water is hit by a Saudi coalition airstrike in Kamaran district, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5440599

title: Tens of thousands admitted to hospitals from contaminated drinking water, inciting violence that leads to deaths and injuries
description: Tens of thousands fall ill from contaminated drinking water in Basra, Iraq. In response, citizen unrest escalates and protests turn violent, leaving at least 15 dead and hundreds injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Trew 2018 ; Al Jazeera 2018b ; Amnesty International 2018a

title: The Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist detonate an explosive at the powerhouse of the Arun-III Hydropower Project, Nepal
description: The Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist (CPN-Maoist-Chand) detonate an explosive-laden pressure cooker at the powerhouse of the Arun-III Hydropower Project demanding the Nepalese government use Nepali companies and labor during hydropower construction.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: The Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist detonate an explosive device at the dam site of the Upper Karnali Hydropower Project, Nepal
description: The Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist (CPN-Maoist-Chand) detonate an explosive device at the dam site of the Upper Karnali Hydropower Project, Nepal, demanding the Nepalese government use Nepali companies and labor during hydropower construction.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: The Donetsk Filter Station is attacked, affecting water supply to 350,000
description: Damage to the Donetsk Filter Station from shelling as well as gunfire directed at water station staff affects the reliability of water supply to approximately 350,000 people. This event is related to previous disruptions in water services from similar attacks in 2017.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Dymkovskyy 2018 ; UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA) 2018b

title: Two airstrikes hit a water dam
description: The Saudi-led coalition launches two airstrikes at Houthi forces in the Al Wahabiyah area in Al Sawadiyah district, Al Bayda Governorate, Yemen, hitting a water dam and killing a number of Houthi fighters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5441489

title: Two are injured during protests over water services in Miranda, Venezuela
description: On August 16, in Los Teques, Miranda, Venezuela a group of people build barricades using burning tires and garbage bags to protest problems with water services. The riots turn more violent when a group of people clash with the municipal police with firearms. Two police officers are injured. The police arrest a group of rioters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7361313

title: Two groups clash at the water plant in Muranga, Kenya, with damage to the water supply system
description: On August 27th, two groups clash at the water plant in Muranga, Kenya, with one group damaging the water supply at the plant.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5273940

title: Two killed while protecting water rights in Mexico
description: A father and son, Ramon Hernandez Nevarez and Anselmo Hernandez Andujo, are murdered while traveling together in Namiquipa, Chihuaua, Mexico. The two were farmers and known locally as water defenders, working to protect the Carmen River from over exploitation. The murderers have not been identified, however, it is thought that they were killed by people from an armed cartel called "La Linea."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lira 2018

title: Two men receive death threats for fighting against water wells in Chihuahua, Mexico
description: Two men, Martin Solis Bustamente and Eraclio Rodriguez, receive death threats for fighting what they see as the illegal construction and operation of water wells in the Carmen River Basin, Chihuahua, Mexico.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lira 2018

title: Two people are killed because of a dispute over a watercourse
description: Two people are killed and another is injured as a result of a tribal dispute over a watercourse in Bait Al-Hadi Village, Al-Qiblah, Ar Rujum District, Al-Mahwit Governorate, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5439644

title: Violence breaks out at a line waiting for water at a spring in Cape Town
description: Violence breaks out at a line waiting for water at a spring in a neighborhood in Cape Town after severe drought leaves the city with dwindling water supplies. After restrictions were imposed in early 2018, citizens have taken to collecting water from local springs, which are not counted in their water restrictions. In response to this violence, guards are posted at the spring and restrictions put on how much water can be collected.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Schlanger 2018 ; Chambers 2018

title: Violence in western Ethiopia, in part driven by shortages of water and land resources, displaces one million people
description: Violence in western Ethiopia displaces one million people. The violence is in part driven by shortages of water and land resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Amare 2019

title: Violence over irrigation water leads to at least one injury in India
description: On November 16, in Singanapalle village in Banaganapalle tehsil (Kurnool, AP), India, local political parties clash with each other over water pipes. One person is injured and hospitalized.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5592715

title: Violent clashes between farmers and police over access to water leave one dead in Kazeroon, Iran
description: One person is killed when police are sent to halt "illegal" water pumps Kazeroon, Iran, used by farmers and other villagers to access water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Euronews 2018a

title: War and soaring temperatures leave women and children water collectors vulnerable in South Sudan
description: War and soaring temperatures leave many rural communities in South Sudan with little or no local water sources. Women and children are subjected to violent attacks, rape, and murder when traveling to regional sources to collect water. Leaders report conflicts sparked by water shortages occurring between the many of the 60 different ethnic groups across the country.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Trew 2019

title: Water company truck hits landmine on the way to repair water pipes in Ukraine, injuring two
description: A water company truck driven by two employees strikes a land mine on its way to an emergency repair of damages to a water pipe due to attacks. Two water utility employees are injured. The water pipe services approximately 45,000 people with water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA) 2018a

title: Water coolers at a mosque are poisoned in Iraq
description: On December 5, an unknown assailant poisons water coolers at a mosque in Nasiriyah, Dhi Qar, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201812050004

title: Water dam hit during air raids
description: A water dam is hit during multiple air raids in Al-Sawadiyah District, Bayda, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water driller damaged in conflict in Yemen
description: A water driller in Baqim District, Saada is damaged in the ongoing conflict in Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water driller hit during air raid
description: A water driller is hit during an air raid in Al-Dhuha district, Hudaydah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water driller hit during air raid in Yemen
description: A water driller is hit during an air raid in Majz District, Sa'ada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water driller hit during air raids
description: A water driller is hit during multiple air raids in Sihar District, Sa'ada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water driller is hit during air raids
description: A water driller is hit during multiple air raids in Sihar District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water fountain damaged in air raid
description: A water fountain in Haydan District, Sa'ada, Yemen is damaged in an air raid.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water fountain is damaged in air raid
description: A water fountain in Haydan District, Saada, Yemen is damaged in an air raid.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water infrastructure attacked in Syria
description: Water infrastructure are attacked, along with health centers and hospitals, in an offensive by Turkey in the Afrin and Tal Rifaat districts in Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Rudaw 2018

title: Water project hit during air raid
description: A water project is hit during an air raid in Sihar District, Sa'ada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water project hit during air raid in Yemen
description: A water project is hit during an air raid in Al-Safra'a District, Sa'ada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water project is attacked and workers are killed and kidnapped by suspected militant group in Libya
description: In July 2018, Daesh militants are suspected of two attacks to workers of the Great Man-made River, a large water supply project that transports water from the Sahara desert to communities and agricultural fields in northern Libya. During the first attack four technicians from the Al-Hassouna plant are kidnapped, but later released. During the second attack two workers are killed and two guards are kidnapped.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; OOSKANews Correspondent 2018 ; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6743748

title: Water pump hit during air raid
description: A water pump is hit during an air raid in Sihar District, Sa'ada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water shortages in India lead to deadly fights between civilians and harassment of water company employees
description: Lack of water in cities across India -- due to drought, growing populations, and inadequate infrastructure -- leads to high tensions, resulting in at least two deaths when a fight breaks out between residents waiting in line at a water truck. Those working for the water companies with the responsibility of turning different water lines on and off, called "key men," are increasingly harassed by residents wanting to persuade them to keep their water on.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Abi-Habib and Kumar 2018

title: Water tank hit during air raid
description: A water tank is hit during an air raid in Haydan District, Sa'ada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water tank hit during air raid in Yemen
description: On December 10, a water tank is hit during an air raid in Kamaran District, Hudaydah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water tank is damaged in conflict in Yemen
description: A water tank in Al-Durayhimi District, Hudaydah is damaged in the ongoing conflict in Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water well digging machine is destroyed by airstrikes
description: In Sadah, Yemen, a civilian is injured and a water well digging machine is destroyed by 5 Saudi-led coalition airstrikes that hit in Farwah and Mahather areas of Sahar district.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5437994, 5437997

title: Water well hit during air raid in Yemen
description: On October 10, a water well is hit during an air raid in Bait Al-Faqih District, Hudaydah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water wells hit during air raids
description: Water wells are hit during multiple air raids in Kamaran, Hudaydah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Water wells project hit during air raids
description: A water wells project is hit during multiple air raids in Al-Hudaydah city, Al-Hudaydah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Well damaged in Al-Silw District, Taizz, Yemen
description: A water well in Al-Silw District, Taizz is damaged in the ongoing conflict in Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Well damaged in conflict in Hays District, Hudaydah, Yemen
description: A water well in Hays District, Hudaydah is damaged in the ongoing conflict in Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Workers at a pumping station in Libya are threatened by attackers with firearms
description: On December 18, attackers with firearms enter the Hasawneh pumping station and threaten workers in Jafara, Libya. No casualties are reported but valuables are stolen during the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201812180008

title: Xiangyang, China residents protest water and air pollution and clashes with police lead to injuries and arrests
description: On June 30, 2018, more than 1000 residents protest untreated wastewater discharge and groundwater contamination at a waste treatment plant in Xiangyang, China. Forty residents are arrested during clashes with local police; some residents are also injured and hospitalized.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7737107

title: 37 killed in herder-farmer conflict over water and land resources in Mali
description: Thirty-seven civilians are killed in the ongoing conflict between herders and farmers who are fighting over access to water and land resources in central Mali.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Press (AFP) 2019c

title: 50,000 people flee their homes in central Mali as conflict escalates over land and water
description: A series of massacres in central Mali, fueled by conflict over land and water resources, causes 50,000 people to flee their homes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Webb 2019

title: 600 residents in Honduras destroy mining equipment, clash with police over threats to water and forest; injuries reported
description: On August 16 in Yorito, Yoro, Honduras around 600 inhabitants destroy heavy machinery of the mining company Comercializadora de Agregados de Honduras S.A. (CEASA). During the conflict with police, multiple injuries are reported. The demonstrators oppose the operation of the mining company, which they consider threatens water sources and the forest. The territory is inhabited by Tolupan indigenous people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6957084

title: 9 water workers killed, 26 injured, in ongoing conflict in eastern Ukraine
description: Nine water workers are killed and 26 are injured since the start of 2019 through July in the ongoing conflict in the eastern region of the Ukraine. Additionally 58 sanitation facilities are damaged or destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNICEF 2019

title: A clash over access to a drinking water fountain leads to injuries and a demonstration in Pakistan
description: On September 10, police and Rangers resort to using batons and tear gas after supporters of three men who were injured during a clash over use of a water fountain blocked the road and demonstrated in Darya Khan Mari village, Sindh, Pakistan.
