source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5976848

title: A clash over water sharing leads to at least eight injuries in Pakistan
description: As reported on September 19, two groups clash after dispute about water sharing in the Multan district (Punjab), Pakistan resulting in injuries to at least eight persons.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6253244

title: A demonstration over water privatization and indigenous rights in Chile leads to a violent confrontation with police
description: On October 12, in Santiago, Chile a Mapuche demonstration over the defense of indigenous territories and the privatization of water leads to a violent confrontation with police and the destruction of public facilities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7819398

title: A dispute over sewage water discharge leads to one death in India
description: On March 18, in Kalakkad (Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu), India, a dispute over sewage water discharge leads to one death.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5600470

title: A dispute over sewage water discharge leads to two deaths and four injuries in India
description: On March 30, two groups clash over the drainage of dirty water in Lisana village (Rewari, Haryana), India. Two persons are killed and four others injured in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5601051

title: A dispute over the use of water resources turns violent in Kyrgyzstan
description: On June 9, about 30 residents of Ak-Suu, Kyrgyzstan reportedly attack a couple because of conflicts over water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6195499

title: A dispute over water drainage in Pakistan results in seven injured
description: On September 9, two groups from Tamma village attack each other with batons, sticks, and stones over a dispute about water drainage in their village near Islamabad city, Pakistan. Seven people are injured when one of the groups rammed their SUV against the other group's car.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5976857

title: A dispute over water rotation in Pakistan leads to one death
description: On August 29, two groups of the Marri community attack each other with axes over a water rotation dispute in Dilshad village near Golarchi town, Pakistan, resulting in one fatality.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5932538

title: A dispute related to access to clean water in Haiti leads to multiple deaths and arrests
description: On July 1, shots are fired at protestors demanding clean drinking water, killing two near Petite-Riviere de Nippes and Anse-a-Veau, Haiti. Unidentified people fire back, killing four more. Some of the initial attackers are arrested by police.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7018063

title: A fight between farmers and pastoralists at a water source in Kenya results in serious injuries
description: On September 20th, in Mkocheni village, Kenya, a fight between farmers and herders over access to a water source results in serious injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6013277

title: A fight over restoration of a drinking water tap in AP, India injures eight
description: On October 28, Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and Yuvajana Shramika Rythu Congress Party activists clash over the restoration of a drinking water tap in Santakaviti village (Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh), India, injuring eight.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6332030

title: A fight over the price of water leads to deadly clashes in Sudan
description: A woman was killed in a dispute over the price of water in El Gedaref, Sudan. This violent clash triggers more fighting between familial groups, leading to at least eight more deaths and dozens of injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Dabanga 2019

title: A former employee takes control of a Kansas-based water company's computers to remotely to alter the treatment of drinking water
description: In March 2019, the public water utility in Ellsworth County, Kansas, is the target of malicious action by a former employee who takes control of the company’s systems remotely to alter the treatment of drinking water intended for the population.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Boubaker 2021

title: A grandmother and her grandson are beaten when seeking water from a private well
description: A grandmother and her grandson in Badhauli village, Sultanpur, UP, India insist on being allowed to use a private well to get water. The well owner refuses and sends men to beat the grandmother and grandson with sticks, injuring them both. The owner is concerned that his well cannot provide water to the entire village and therefore, he does not want to provide water to anyone.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Indo-Asian News Service 2019 ; ACLED ID: 6071375

title: A gunfight over the sharing of irrigation water in the Mangal area of Pakistan kills six and injures three others
description: On July 7, members of two Pashtun tribes Pakha Khel and Maduzai exchange gunfire over a 40-year-old dispute regarding sharing of irrigation water in Mangal area of Pakistan. Six people are killed and three others sustain injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7259519

title: A man is beaten to death for allegedly stealing a water pump in Rajasthan, India
description: On September 21, a Dalit man is beaten to death by locals for allegedly stealing a water pump at Ghatoli village (Jhalawar, Rajasthan), India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6014039

title: A man is stabbed by his neighbor over a water sharing dispute in India
description: A man is stabbed by his neighbor over a water sharing dispute in Chennai, India. Current drought and water supply management problems have led to lack of water for millions living in the city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2019

title: A projectile is launched at a desalination plant in Saudi Arabia
description: On June 19, a projectile is launched at a desalination plant in Shuqaiq, Jazan, Saudi Arabia. Houthi extremists claim responsibility for the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201906190010

title: A protest over delays to repair of water and sanitation infrastructure in Pakistan leads to injuries
description: On August 16, locals reportedly attack and injure four Water and Sanitation Authority staff at Gulberg Colony in Multan city, Punjab, Pakistan over delays in repair work.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5931854

title: A violent demonstration over access to water in Panquehue, Chile ends in the destruction of a local water system
description: A group of citizens demonstrated violently in Panquehue, Chile in the Valparaiso Region. The group destroyed water facilities used for farming claiming that drought and industrial use is leading to water shortages for local residents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6939510

title: A water dispute in Pakistan results in one death and other injuries
description: On June 26, two tribal sub-clans attack each other with weapons and knives over a water dispute in Jangal Pir Alizai, Balochistan, Pakistan resulting in one fatality and injuries to two others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5545782

title: A water system is destroyed in an attack in the Philippines
description: On May 4, Cambalidio, Camarines Sur, Philippines is attacked; while no casualties are reported, a water system is destroyed in the incident. No group claims responsibility; however, sources attribute the attack to the New People's Army (NPA).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201905040041

title: A water tank and a vehicle are damaged in an attack on a House Assembly member in Zimbabwe
description: On August 21, House Assembly member Caston Matewu is fired upon, in Nyameni, Mashonaland East, Zimbabwe; a water tank and a vehicle are damaged but no casualties are reported. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201908210017

title: A water tank and windows are damaged during an attack on a polling center in Afghanistan
description: On September 28, a water tank and several windows are damaged during an attack on a polling center in a female high school in Fayzabad, Jawzjan, Afghanistan. The Taliban claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201909280054

title: A water tank is targeted in an attack on the Somali National Army in Somalia
description: On June 9, a water tank is targeted in an attack on the Somali National Army by Al-Shabaab, near Wanlaweyne, Lower Shebelle, Somalia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201906090020

title: A water tanker is damaged in an attack on a convoy in Somalia
description: On December 10, an explosive device detonates targeting a convoy in Isbartiba, Mogadishu, Somalia, causing an unknown number of casualties and also damaging a water tanker. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201912100031

title: A water well is shelled causing material damages in Yemen
description: On January 5th, pro-Houthi forces shell a mosque and a water well in the Al Jabaliyah area of At Tuhayat district, Yemen, causing material damages. No injuries nor fatalities are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5183989

title: A woman is killed in a clash over the sharing of drinking water in Kurnool, India
description: On May 10, in Kurnool district (Andhra Pradesh), India a woman is killed during a clash between two families over sharing of drinking water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5188422, 5197337

title: Afghan police attack Taliban militants trying to destroy a water well; seven deaths are reported
description: As reported on August 9, Afghan police forces attack Taliban militants trying to destroy a water well in Almar district, Faryab. Seven militants are killed and nine are wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6821820

title: Air raid hits water truck and causes four civilian fatalities in Yemen
description: On March 4, a water truck is hit in an air raid in Al-Sawadiyah District, Bayda, Yemen. Four civilians are also killed in the raid.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Airstrike hits water tank in Saada, Yemen
description: On July 9, an airstrike by Coalition forces hits a water tank in Razih District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Al Shabaab militants flood a highway and ambush Somali soldiers who arrive to cut off the water
description: On October 11, Al Shabaab militants ambush Somali military soldiers after they arrive to close the water gate of Hawaadley water storage opened by the militants to flood the highway between Bal'ad and Jowhar.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6023755

title: An irrigation water dispute kills one in Pakistan
description: On July 23, the family of members of a Junejo community individual who was killed in a irrigation water dispute burn tires, block Sukkur-Larkana highway, and hold a sit-in along with the victim's body in Shikarpur district, Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5669080

title: An unidentified group sets fire to machinery and leaves an explosive device at a hydropower project in Nepal
description: An unidentified group of attackers set fire to machinery and leave an explosive device at the Solukhola Dudhkoshi Hydropower Project in Bhadaure, Nepal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Armed clash erupts over water and grazing land near Afmadow, Somalia
description: On January 16 an armed clash erupts between Bartire and Mohamed Zuber clan militias over water and grazing land near Afmadow town. There are several casualties on both sides during the clashes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6134960

title: Assailants attack schools, houses, trucks transporting drinking water and other infrastructure in Yemen
description: In early March, assailants use guns to attack schools, houses, trucks transporting drinking water, and other infrastructure in Al-Abaysa, Hajjah, Yemen. No group claims responsibility for the incident; however, sources attribute the attack to Houthi extremists.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201903080004, 201903090040

title: At least 11 people are killed in a conflict over access to water between pastoralists and farmers near the Kenya-Ethiopia border
description: A deadly flight between farmers and pastoralists over a watering point near the Kenyan-Ethiopian border leaves eleven people dead, two injured, and four missing.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Charles 2019

title: At least 12 people are injured in a clash over rainwater drainage pipes in Haryana, India
description: On April 19, two groups of residents clash over the laying of rainwater drainage pipes in Mollewali village in Pinjore sub-division (Panchkula, Haryana), India. At least 12 injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7417707

title: At least 50 people are injured in Bangladesh in a dispute over a local water body
description: On August 6, at least 50 people are injured in a clash between two groups of villagers at Modhurapur village, Bangladesh over a local water body. Police fire tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse the crowd.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5928658

title: Attempt to plant an explosive device in a water channel in Yemen results in one death
description: On January 11, assailants attempt to plant an explosive device in the Qamt water channel and open fire on security forces in Taizz, Yemen. One assailant is killed. No group claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201901110035

title: Caste violence in India continues, with access to water and water resources being regular triggers or casualties of conflict
description: Marginalized socioeconomic groups, known as "Dalits" in the Hindu-based caste system, experience threats, torture, and violence when seeking access to water in Maharashtra, India. Dalit women are targets of violence in particular. Additionally, water sources used by Dalits are at times purposely contaminated with human excrement.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ghanekar 2019

title: Chilean social unrest tied to cost of living -- including water and power -- and inequality turn violent
description: Protests in Chile include general civil unrest and reflect dissatisfaction in social and economic inequality, including the price of water and other utilities. Protests grow and turn violent with thousands injured and several dying during clashes with security forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2019

title: Clash over water shortage in Clifton, Karachi injures 7, including 2 police officers; 40+ demonstrators arrested
description: On July 28, at least five people are injured in a clash between local activists, government representatives, and local political parties in Clifton town, Karachi, Pakistan over shortage of water and failure to maintain city's sewerage. Police intervene to disperse the demonstrators and arrest more than 40 demonstrators. Two police officers are also injured in the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7546083

title: Conflict over local drinking water leads to two injuries in Nepal
description: On May 19, a group of people beat up a couple in Khamari locality of Siranchowk Rural Municipality near Gorkha, Nepal for blocking the registration of the drinking water source of the village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7161427

title: Demonstrators in Tunisia wreck water pipes to a neighboring town, protesting water service interruptions
description: Around July 3 in Jelma, Tunisia, demonstrators wreck water pipes delivering water to neighboring towns, demonstrating against water service interruptions.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5578770

title: Demonstrators protesting over water, electricity, and jobs attacked by Iraqi security forces, with over 100 deaths
description: Iraqi citizens publicly demonstrating to protest ongoing water, electricity, and job challenges are met with violent repression by Iraqi security forces. Over 100 people are killed within the first seven days of protests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Karam and Abdul-Zahra 2019

title: Disputes between herders and farmers over access to water lead to growing violence in Chad
description: Herders and farmers who used to coexist peacefully are now inflicting deadly wounds on each other over fights driven by water shortages in the Sahel region of Chad.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2019a ; AFP/VOA 2019

title: During one of four attacks in the area, water tunnels and bridges are blown up in Yemen
description: On May 29, water tunnels and bridges are blown up in one of four attacks in Ad Dali, Yemen. No group claims responsibility for the incident; however, sources attribute the attack to Houthi extremists.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201905290035

title: Eco-vandalism disrupts water diversions
description: A water diversion system in the Colorado Rocky Mountains near Berthoud Pass is vandalized, disrupting water deliveries for several days. The act is suspected to be linked to ongoing tensions over water diversions from the Colorado River basin to Denver and other Front Range communities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Smith 2019

title: Eight people are injured in a fight over water in Pawai, Madhya Pradesh, India
description: On June 5, residents of Pawai village (Panna district, Madhya Pradesh), India attack each other following a dispute over water. Eight people were injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5214069

title: Explosive device detonates near a water facility in Iraq, killing one civilian
description: On July 9, 2019, an explosive device detonates near a water facility in Shirqat, Saladin, Iraq, killing one civilian. No group claims responsibility for the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201907090008

title: Farmers in the Punjab, India fight over irrigation water. One injury is reported
description: On July 21, farmers fight in Lubanianwali village (Muktsar, Punjab) after a farmer stops rainwater flow from a pipe. One person is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5668459

title: Farmers protesting the diversion of the Zayandehrud River damage diversion water pipes
description: In October, a group of farmers in Isfahan, Iran demonstrate against the diversion of Zayandehrud River to other provinces; some demonstrators damage the water pipes of the diversion infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6060356

title: Farmers stop the main water pumping station in El Hamma, Tunisia, disrupting local drinking water supply
description: On July 22, farmers hold a demonstration and stop the main water pumping station in El Hamma, causing disruptions of drinking water in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5663171

title: Fatalities and injuries are reported in a clan fight over access to water wells and land
description: On January 15, clan militias in Somalia fight over water wells and land in the area. There are reports of fatalities and injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6134973

title: Five are hurt when a car hits them during a demonstration over lack of drinking water in Miranda state, Venezuela
description: On April 10, five are hurt when a car tries to run them down during a demonstration demanding water in San Diego de los Altos, Los Teques, Miranda state, Venezuela.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6942434

title: Five people are injured in a clash over sharing irrigation water in India
description: On February 22, five persons are injured in a clash between two groups of farmers over sharing irrigation water at Singhi village near Bolpur (Birbhum, West Bengal), India. They use bamboo sticks and crude bombs in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5599166

title: Four are injured in a fight over water supply in Kurnool, AP, India
description: On November 16, four persons are injured in a clash between villagers and local leaders belonging to the Yuvajana Shramika Rythu Congress Party over drinking water at Kalvabugga (Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh), India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6698873

title: In Chittoor, India, five people are injured in a dispute over a panchayat (village council) water connection
description: On April 27, in Gudupalle Mandal area (Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh), two groups clash over a panchayat water connection at Alugumanupalle. Five persons are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5604612

title: In an attack on a convoy escorting food and water supplies, at least three are killed and one injured in Burkina Faso
description: On June 24, in an attack on a convoy escorting food and water supplies in Burkina Faso, at least three people are killed and one is injured. No one claims responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201906240011

title: India responds to deadly attack by threatening to curtal water deliveries to Pakistan
description: An attack by a Pakistan-based group that killed at least 40 Indian soldiers has worsened tensions between the two countries, prompting Indian leaders to threaten to curtail water deliveries from rivers flowing into Pakistan. Curtailment of water deliveries could undermine the 1960 Indus Water Treaty, which stipulates the sharing of water resources between the two countries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al Jazeera 2019 ; TheNewArab 2019 ; Johnson 2019

title: Indigenous activist killed at home for opposing Proyecto Integral Morelos, which threatened local water resources
description: Samir Flores Soberanes, an indigenous environmental activist from Mexico, is killed in his home for his opposition to the Proyecto Integral Morelos, a thermoelectric plant and pipeline that threatened local water and land resources. The Moreles state prosecutor claims that the murder has nothing to do with the thermoelectric plant project. The People's Front in Defense of the Land and Water for the states of Morelos, Puebla and Tlaxcala (FPDTA) state that the only enemies that Soberanes had were those involved with the project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agren 2019

title: Indigenous women murdered for their resistence to hydropower projects and land grabs in Omoa, Honduras
description: In September and October 2019 at least six women from the indigenous Garifuna communities in coastal Honduras are murdered for their resistance to government-backed land decisions and hydropower projects that affected their territory. One of the six, Mirna Teresa Suazo Martinez, was the president of the board of trustees in the Masca community of Omoa.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; AWID 2020

title: Injuries are reported during demonstrations against the lack of water and electricity in Caracas, Venezuela
description: On March 31, a protest is held in San Jose de Cotiza, in Caracas, Venezuela to protest blackouts and the interruption of water services. The protest is met by officials of the Faes, the National Guard, and armed militias of the ruling party. Two people are reportedly wounded by bullets.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7556979

title: Injuries are reported during demonstrations against the lack of water and electricity in Maracay, Venezuela
description: On March 31, residents of Maracay, Aragua state, Venezuela protest blackouts and the lack of water. Five are wounded amid demonstrations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6942744

title: Israel reportedly cuts off water supplies to approximately 1500 Palestinians
description: Palestine News Network reports a water shut off to 17 Palestinian communities in Hebron, West Bank. The report suggests that the shut off was a purposeful act by Israel to force the movement of local Palestinians out of their homes to make room for more Israeli settlements.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sputnik 2019

title: Israeli settlers reportedly flood Palestinian-owned olive groves with sewage
description: On October 27, Israeli settlers flood Palestinian-owned olive groves in the village of Deri al Hatab east of Nablus, Palestine with sewage water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6330660

title: Kenyan school water tank poisoned
description: A water tank at a primary school in Kirinyaga County, Kenya, is vandalized and poisoned. No one was harmed by the poisoned water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Munene 2019

title: Local residents in Mat, Albania clash with police over the construction of a hydroelectric plant
description: On October 26, residents of Zall Gjocaj village in Mat, Albania clash with police while demonstrating against the construction of a hydroelectric power station. The residents are worried about local water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7000567

title: Man threatened and killed for working land claimed to be owned by a hydropower company in Honduras
description: A man is threatened and killed in March 2019 for working on the land that was allegedly owned by DESA, the hydropower company in Honduras responsible for the Agua Zarca Dam project. The man, Olban Adonay Gómez García, was the son of a leader of the community resistance to the Agua Zarca hydroelectric project that is associated with the murder of Berta Caceras and several of ther local activists.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Business & Human Rights Resource Centre n.d.-b

title: More than 130 killed in Mali in conflict between hunters and herders over land and water
description: More than 130 people are killed in the conflict between hunter and herder communities in Mali. In this instance, Dogon hunters are accused of attacking Fulani herders.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; TRT World 2019 ; Insiders Newsletter 2019

title: Mortar shells are fired severely damaging a water tanker
description: Pro-Houthi forces reportedly fire mortar shells near the city of Hays in the south of Hodeidah Governorate, western Yemen. Several houses and a water tanker are severely damaged by shrapnel. At least one civilian is injured in the shelling.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4567255

title: National leader Dilma Ferreira Silva, working for policy reform to support people affected by dams, is murdered in Brazil
description: The leader of an effort to establish national policy in Brazil that would guarantee the rights of people affected by dams, Dilma Ferreira Silva, was murdered, along with her husband and their friend, in March 2019. Sra. Silva had been personally displaced by a dam in her childhood and had spent her life advocating for rights for her family and the river.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Agenzia fides 2019

title: Numerous fights, including attacks on water tankers, break out over access to water in Madhya Pradesh, India during severe heat
description: Water shortages in Madhya Pradesh, India intensify during a heat wave, leading to numerous violent conflicts among Indian civilians. In one instance in Khajrana a water truck driver is beaten. In another instance in Panna, eight people are injured during a fight. The local government responds to the violence by ordering police to escort water trucks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Times of India 2019

title: On two days in May, assailants set fire to water tankers and other vehicles at construction sites in India
description: On May 8 and again on May 12, assailants set fire to water tankers and other construction vehicles and a building in Maharashtra, India. Maoists are suspected to be responsible for the attacks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201905080014, 201905120043

title: One Israeli killed and two others injured at a spring in the West Bank
description: A homemade bomb explodes at a spring, killing an Israeli teenager and injuring her father and brother. Springs in the occupied West Bank area have become hotspots for conflict between Israeli and Palestinian citizens who both visit during the summer while seeking to cool off from the heat.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Chronicle News Service 2019

title: One death and eight injuries reported in a dispute over grazing and water access in South Sudan
description: On April 15th, clashes break out between pastoralists in the area of Manya , South Sudan in an apparent dispute over grazing and water access in the area. One person dies and eight are injured in the violence.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7212045

title: One death and several injuries are reported during a protest over lack of water and other services in Sao Paulo, Brazil
description: On July 18 in Valinhos, Sao Paulo, Brazil approximately 400 people protest the lack of water and inadequate school and health assistance in the Marielle Vive Camp. A supporter of Jair Bolsonaro drives a truck through the crowd, killing an elderly man and injuring five people, including a journalist.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6925533

title: One death is reported in an armed clash over control of water in Bangladesh
description: On August 21, an eight-year old boy is killed in an armed clash between two groups over the control of water body in Kulaura Upazila, Maulvibazar, Bangladesh.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5928720

title: One death is reported in dispute over water at a public tap in Andhra Pradesh, India
description: On July 15, a woman is killed during a clash over water between two groups at a public tap in the Srikakulam district (Andhra Pradesh), India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5615664

title: One death reported in a fight over water in southern India during a severe heat wave
description: In Tamil Nadu, India, a 33 year old man dies as the result of a fight that broke out over water. India is experiencing a heat wave with temperatures reaching higher than 50 degrees C/120 degrees F.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2019b

title: One farmer is killed and three others injured in armed clash over access to water in Bangladesh
description: On March 16, a farmer is stabbed and killed and three others injured in an armed clash between two groups of villagers at Dhaki village, Mithamain, Bangladesh over a water body dispute.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5587875

title: One injury is reported in a fight over drainage water in Devsar town, India
description: On July 5, two families fight over a water drainage issue in Devsar town (Kulgam, Jammu and Kashmir), India. One injury is reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5549508

title: One man is killed and his son injured in a dispute over drawing water in Maharastra, India
description: On October 6, two men attack a Muslim father and son over drawing water from a nearby tap in Ghatkopar (Mumbai Suburban, Maharashtra), India. The father dies of his injuries at a hospital.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6024805

title: One man stabs six others in a fight over water shortages in Ranchi, India during severe heat wave
description: In Ranchi, India, one man stabs six other people due to water shortages. India is experiencing a heat wave with temperatures reaching higher than 50 degrees C/120 degrees F.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Agence France-Presse (AFP) 2019b

title: One person is killed during a protest over the lack of water in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa
description: On February 27, protesters blocked a road in Umzimkhulu, KwaZulu Natal, South Africa protesting the lack of water. Two protesters are shot and one killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 4557854

title: One person is killed in a clash over the distribution of irrigation water in India
description: On April 8, a youth was killed during a clash between groups from two villages in Shopian district (Jammu and Kashmir), India over the distribution of irrigation water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5602334

title: One person is severely injured in a water dispute in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, India
description: Around June 8, a youth is attacked with baseball bats by unidentified people in Gwalior (Madhya Pradesh) over a water dispute. The victim sustains severe injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5220363

title: One reported killed during protests over the lack of water and power services in Zulia state, Venezuela
description: On April 5, in Santa Rita, Zulia state, Venezuela a man is shot dead by police and military officers during a protest demanding basic services such as electric power and potable water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7758755

title: Pakistan claims India's unexpected release of water from a dam is an act of war
description: India releases water from a dam on the River Sutlej, causing moderate flooding downstream in Pakistan. India claims that the release is a "routine exercise" during monsoon season. The release and resultant flooding are seen as an act of war by Pakistan. This incident adds to the already strained relations between the two countries which have been at odds since February 2019 when 40 Indian parliamentary police were killed by a suicide bomb in Kashmir.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2019

title: Pastoralists in Morocco fight with local residents and destroy water supply infrastructure
description: On November 11, in Toumliline, Morocco, pastoralist nomads attack residents of the area with rocks and sticks, resulting in the destruction of water supply infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6859342

title: Protestors trying to stop the diversion of floodwaters in Iran clash with Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps; one protestor dies
description: On March 4, clashes break out between Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) forces and protestors trying to stop the diversion of floodwaters in Dashte Azadegan, Iran. One protestor reportedly dies after being shot by IRGC forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5553643

title: Protests over water, electricity, and university fees in the Democratic Republic of Congo turn violent; four deaths reported
description: Students from the University of Lubumbashi demonstrate over water, electricity, and fees. The demonstrators barricade roads, block access to the university, and burn tires and vehicles. Police forces opened fire on the demonstrators, killing three. A police officer also dies after being hit by a police car.
basin: Democratic Republic of the Congo Havzası
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7844120

title: Seven people injured during dispute over water supply in Rajasthan, India
description: On June 6, residents of two villages near Kishangarh Bas (Alwar district, Rajasthan), India clash with each other following a dispute over water supply in the neighborhood. Seven people were injured in the fight.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5214126

title: Several people are injured in a fight over a water tanker in Delhi, India
description: On June 10, two groups of residents clash over a water tanker in Delhi-Mehrauli (South Delhi, National Capital Territory of Delhi) injuring several people. The state has been facing water shortages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7550619

title: Shelling and airstrikes destroy water supply systems in Tripoli during ongoing war in Libya
description: Heavy shelling and airstrikes between April and June of 2019 destroy water infrastructure in Tripoli, Libya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) 2019

title: Shrapnel damages a water pipeline, leaving more than three million people without water
description: Shrapnel from an exploding shells damages a pipeline in the Siverski Donetsk-Donbass channel near Horlivka, Ukraine. The damages leave 3 million civilians on both sides of the conflict with either unreliable or no water supplies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNICEF 2019

title: Six Dalits are injured in a clash over access to drinking water in Mainpuri, India
description: On May 28, six Dalits, a marginalized socioeconomic group, were injured in an attack in Mainpuri (Uttar Pradesh), India over drinking water from a tube well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5210722

title: Six injuries are reported in a dispute over water in Mundera, Madhya Pradesh, India
description: On June 8, locals residents attack each other following a dispute over water at Mundera village of Lavkush Nagar Tehsil (Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh). Six people are injured in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5214204

title: Six people are injured and one killed in a dispute over irrigation water in Uttar Pradesh, India
description: On October 15, two groups of villagers from Kataura and Pradhan Paksha, Uttar Pradesh, India clash over irrigation water. Six persons are injured. The dispute continues in late October and a death is reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6363134, 6331745

title: Six police officers are injured during demonstrations demanding the restoration of water services in South Africa
description: Around October 16, 2019 residents from Tshikota, South Africa demonstrate, demanding the restoration of water service in their area. Six police officers are injured and 12 demonstrators are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6331456

title: Suspected Boko Haram fighters assault the Alou Dam, Nigeria killing 20
description: Suspected Boko Haram fighters attack the Alou Dam in Nigeria, killing at least 20 civilians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Suspected New People’s Army fighters set fire to construction equipment at the Kaliwa Dam construction site, Philippines
description: On February 8, assailants set construction equipment at a dam construction site on fire in Maysaysay, Quezon, Philippines. No group claims responsibility; however, sources attribute the attack to the New People's Army (NPA).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201902080001 ; U.S. Department of Home

title: Suspicious circumstances surround the death of a legal advocate who opposed a dam in Indonesia
description: In October 2019, Golfrid Siregar is found dead. Environmental activists argue that Siregar had been targeted for his work as a legal advocate and that suspicious circumstances of his death indicate that he was in fact murdered. Siregar's most recent work included the filing of a lawsuit accussing the North Sumatra government of forging a signature to allow for the permitting of a dam in the region.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Karokaro 2019

title: Ten are injured in a dispute over irrigation water in Pakistan
description: On July 6, two groups of Janwri community attack each other with sticks and metal rods over the rotation of water in Gharo village, Pakistan. Ten men are injured during the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5555813

title: The Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist (CPN-Maoist-Chand) detonate three explosive devices at the Arun III Dam’s powerhouse, Nepal
description: The Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist (CPN-Maoist-Chand) detonate three explosive-laden pressure cookers at the Arun III Dam’s powerhouse, Nepal, damaging a generator.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: The Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist detonate an explosive device at the Upper Karnali Hydropower Project dam in Nepal
description: he Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist (CPN-Maoist-Chand) detonate an explosive device at the Upper Karnali Hydropower Project dam construction site in Nepal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: The destruction of a water plant leads to clashes in Yemen, killing and injuring many
description: On November 26, clashes are reported between 'Abidah Al-Qaz'ah tribesmen and Islah-affiliated pro-Hadi forces after tribesmen established a roadblock to demand compensation for a water factory that was damaged in an airstrike and killed the son of the factory's owner. On November 28, reports alleged that 20 people were killed, most of them civilians, and 85 others injured in the clashes that lasted for several days. Fatalities spread over three days.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7002983, 7002984

title: The water supply to Tripoli, Libya is cut off during war
description: The water supply serving Tripoli, Libya's capital city, is cut off by gunmen that force employees managing the system to turn off the flow of water. The war is between Libya's National Army and UN-backed forces and has been ongoing since 2014.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Elumami 2019

title: Three people injured in a dispute over access to drinking water in Kyrgyzstan
description: In July, violence over access to drinking water is reported in the Iskrinsk district, Chui region of Kyrgyzstan. Several people are reported hospitalized.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6196207, 8359742

title: Turkey forces destroy Syrian power lines, leaving a city without water
description: The Syrian city Al Hasakeh is left without water after Turkish military forces destroy power lines in the area. The attack also leaves at least 11 civilians dead and causes damage to other infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Save the Children 2019 ; British Broadcasting Corporation 2019

title: Turkey takes control of Syrian water system in Allouk and interrupts water supply
description: Turkey and Turkish-backed forces take control of the Allouk water station in northeastern Syria in October 2019. The water station, near the town of Ras al-Ain (Serekaniye), serves 460,000 people in al-Hasakeh governorate. Water pumping has been interrupted several times since the start of the year, with the latest interruption on March 29, 2020. Officials say the interruptions are a tactic to force Kurdish-led authorities to supply electricity to areas under Turkish control.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Human Rights Watch 2020

title: Two are injured in a dispute over access to water in Uttar Pradesh, India
description: On August 7, two persons are injured in a clash between two families in Bhadri village (Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh), India over taking water from a tap.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7046512

title: Two are injured in a fight over irrigation water scheduling in Pakistan
description: On June 22, unidentified men attack and injure two people over irrigation water rotation scheduling, in Hamo Pota village, Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5545720

title: Two are killed and one injured when an explosive device detonates targeting police transporting water in Afghanistan
description: On July 13, a explosive device targeting a police truck transporting water detonates, killing two and injuring one in Miya Nishin district, Kandahar, Afghanistan. No group claim responsibility for the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201907130028

title: Two deaths and multiple injuries reported in violence over irrigation water in two villages of India
description: On August 4, two villages clash over sharing irrigation water for their crops in the villages of Sagar and Panchagochhia, India. Two people are killed and 15 injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7091216

title: Two groups exchange gunfire, killing two, over irrigation water in Pakistan
description: On September 22, two groups exchange fire over a dispute about irrigation water use in Maidan Khwar area of Upper Dir district (KP), Pakistan resulting in two fatalities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6013987

title: Two herders are killed at water points in Kenya
description: On March 24th, two herders are killed at water points at the border of Isiolo and Garissa counties, Kenya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6360549

title: Two injuries are reported during protests over the lack of access to water in Pietermaritzburg, South Africa
description: On May 20, residents from Henley Village, Pietermaritzburg, South Africa demonstrate over lack of access to water. Police use rubber bullets and teargas to disperse the crowds. Two demonstrators are injured and one is hospitalized.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8008775

title: Two men are seriously injured in clash over access to water in India
description: Two men are seriously injured in a clash over water in Krishna Nagar Colony, India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Times of India 2019

title: Two people accused on stealing water pumps are beaten in Guatemala
description: On June 27, in Zona 8, Mixco Town, Guatemala, two people who allegedly stole water pumps are beaten by a group of local inhabitants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7410510

title: Two people are injured in a water dispute in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, India
description: In early June, a clash over water occurs between two groups in Indore (Madhya Pradesh), India. Two people are injured in the encounter.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7418605

title: Two people shot while protesting water and electricity shortages in Caracas
description: Two people are shot by police and paramilitary groups responding to the protests of citizens who have been without electricity or water for several weeks as a result of ongoing political fighting at that national level in Venezuela.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hernandez and Zuniga 2019

title: Uganda Ratifies Nile CFA
description: Uganda becomes the fourth country to ratify the Nile Cooperative Framework Agreement in August 2019, marking continued consolidation of upstream riparian states under the new legal framework that challenges Egypt and Sudan's colonial-era allocations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nile Basin Cooperative Framework Agreement Deposit of Ratification Instrument by Uganda (2019).

title: Vehicles and machines at a water pipeline construction site are burned in India
description: On September 28, vehicles and machines at a water pipeline construction site are burned in Masenar, Chhattisgarh, India. Maoists are suspected to be responsible for the attacks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; National Consortium for the Study of Terrorism and Responses to Terrorism (START) 2019 ID. 201909280055

title: Violence between Hindu and Muslim farmers over irrigation water in Uttar Pradesh, India leads to one injury and two arrests
description: Around July 15, Hindus and Muslims clash in Semra village (Agra district, Uttar Pradesh), India over a farm field water channel. Two people are arrested and one injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 5999090

title: Violence erupts in rural Ghana between Chokosis and Bimobas communities as groups fight over land and access to water resources
description: In Chereponi district, Ghana, houses are burned to the ground, animals are killed, and many flee as violence erupts along ethnic lines between Chokosis and Bimobas peoples who are fighting over land and water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; GhanaWeb 2019

title: Violence in northwest Syria damages civilian infrastructure including 29 individual water systems
description: From January through July 2019 violence in northwest Syria leaves civilian infrastructure damaged and destroyed including at least 29 water stations serving approximately 610,000 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; US Agency for International Development 2019

title: Violence over access to local water leads to gunfire and injuries in India
description: On April 17, two rival groups, including a local official, clash at Kotla Doom village (Amritsar, Punjab) in a dispute over a village pond water/land. Both groups accused the other of gunfire, with two persons injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7047279

title: Water pipeline for Amman Jordan sabotaged
description: The Disi Water Conveyance Project, a pipeline sending over half of the water supply to Amman, Jordan, and the surrounding area, is sabotaged over 60 times in 2019, at times disrupting supply for five days. Rural communities that are experiencing extremely high rates of unemployment are thought to be behind the sabotage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Namrouqa 2019

title: Water resources engineers from the Iraq Ministry of Water Resources are attacked while opening waterways to flood a marsh
description: An team of engineers working on flood prevention from the Ministry of Water Resources in Missan Province, Iraq is attacked by an unidentified armed group while opening waterways to turn a flood into the areas of the central marsh. One death and one injury are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7098106

title: Water shortages linked to child kidnappings in South Sudan
description: Local authorities cite water shortages as a growing influence on the number child kidnappings in the Boma region of South Sudan. When there is a water shortage, shepherding communities spend more time on the move seeking water for their livestock, but, as a side business, they will also abduct children who can then be resold for profit.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Trew 2019

title: Water station serving 80,000 people damaged in Syria
description: A water station in Basida, Idlib Governorate, Syria, serving 80,000 people is damaged by ongoing violence.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA) 2019

title: Workers clash over a water connection in Pakistan, injuring one
description: On March 3, workers of PPP and PTI clash in Liaquatabad town, Karachi, Pakistan over water connections. At least one individual is reported injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7551668

title: A Palestinian water network is damaged by Israeli settlers
description: On December 13, a group of Israeli settlers from the Maaoun settlement attack a Palestinian's house and damage a water network in Sarura area of Yuta village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7448036

title: A clash over the installation of water tanks at a reserve in Chiapas, Mexico results in at least 10 injuries
description: On October 25, in the municipality of San Cristobal de las Casas, Chiapas, Mexico in the Gertrude Duby reserve, a clash is reported over the installation of water tanks in the reserve. At least 40 people participate, shots are fired, and at least 10 people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7621187

title: A clash over water and land kills one and injures three in Somalia
description: On June 21, militias from the Leelkayse and Majeerten clans clash in the Deeralay area, Mudug, Somalia over water and land. One person is killed and three others injured in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7213222

title: A demonstration against the lack of water services in Senegal leads to injuries and arrests
description: On June 22, 2020, residents demonstrate in Koumpentoum town (Koumpentoum, Tambacounda) against a lack of running water. One gendarme is severely injured and several demonstrators are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8017144

title: A demonstration over the shutdown of drinking water facilities in Manipur, India results in multiple injuries
description: On December 7, demonstrations over the shutdown of drinking water facilities in Manipur, India results in multiple injuries of police and demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7413746

title: A dispute over drinking water stalls in Maharashtra, India leads to two deaths and one injury
description: On April 27, two people die and one is seriously injured during a clash between two Muslim groups in the Shivaji Nagar slums of Govandi town (Mumbai city, Maharashtra), India over drinking stalls.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7077556

title: A dispute over irrigation water leads to a clash between conflicting political parties in Nepal
description: On August 28, a clash related to watering paddy fields leads to dozens of injuries between cadres of Nepali Congress and JSPN at Kachanari village in Bariyarpatti, Nepal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7197635

title: A dispute over the control of local water resources turns violent in Bangladesh Two deaths and over 50 injuries are reported
description: In late December, a dispute over control of local water resources between Shantipur village and Prajarkanda village in Itna Upazila (Kishoreganj), Bangladesh turns violent during local arbitration. Two people are killed and over fifty injured in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7461903, 7461933, 7461933

title: A dispute over water distribution in Budhal city, India leads to three injuries
description: On May 19, a dispute over water distribution in Budhal city (Rajouri district, Jammu and Kashmir), India leads to three injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7118264

title: A dozen injuries are reported in violence over access to water for cattle in Chad
description: Around June 1, youth militias from Kouri Bougoudi and Sakine, Chad clash over water for their cattle at Hadjar Hadid (Ouaddai). A dozen people are reported injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7121551

title: A fight in Kenya between two clans over a watering point leaves one dead, 18 injured
description: A fight erupts between two clans in the town of Arbeqarmso, Kenya, over a watering point. The incident leaves one person dead and 18 others injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Makong 2020

title: A fight over access to water in the Al-Qatri camp for displaced persons in Syria leads to one death
description: On May 15, a civilian is killed during clashes between displaced people in Al-Qatri camp near Idlib, Syria. Clashes erupted after residents of the camp lost access to water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8086067

title: A fight over the laying of water pipes in Puri district, India kills two and injures more than ten
description: On October 11, a fight over the laying of water pipes in Dimirisena village in Brahmagiri, Puri district (Odisha), India kills two and injures more than ten.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7253949

title: A fight over the rotation of irrigation water in Pakistan injures eight
description: On September 12, a clash takes place between the Chandio and Solangi communities over the rotation of water in Zahra Machhi village in Radhan, Pakistan. Both groups attack each other with sticks, injuring eight men.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7220582

title: A major riot breaks out between Kyrgyz and Uzbek nationals over access to water; more than 200 people are hospitalized
description: On May 31, a riot breaks out between dozens of Kyrgyz and Uzbek nationals over access to water sources near the village of Chechme on the border with Uzbekistan. Rioters hurl rocks at each other while setting properties on fire on both sides of the border. 200 Uzbek citizens are hospitalized in Sokh enclave including 13 with gunshot wounds; 25 Kyrgyz villagers are taken to the hospital in Kadamjai district with injuries of various degrees.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7119482

title: A police officer kills one in a dispute over water in Brown's Town, Jamaica
description: On December 14, near Brown's Town, Saint Ann, Jamaica, residents set tires on fire after an off-duty police officer shoots and kills someone in a dispute over water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7448913

title: A protest in Mexico against the cost of water services turns violent; at least 16 people are injured
description: On May 14, in San Miguel de Allende, Guanajuato, about 80 people block a street to demonstrate against the cost of water service. About 100 municipal and state police intervene and 16 people are reported injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7627646

title: A protest over the lack of water services in Senegal turns violent and demonstrators and police are injured
description: On May 30, residents demonstrate in Cap Skirring in Oussouye, Ziguinchor, Senegal against the lack of running water. They burn tires on the roads. The gendarmerie forces fire tear gas and live ammunition to disperse them; demonstrators reply with stones. Three demonstrators and three gendarmes are severely injured. 16 people are also arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8017603

title: A water dispute between farmers in Kazakhstan turns into a riot, injuring 12
description: On May 29, a water dispute between farmers near the town of Zhetisay of Turkistan region of Kazakhstan turns into a riot resulting in a dozen injuries. Police arrest two rioters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7125505

title: Afar and Somali forces clash over water and pasture land, killing at least 11
description: Around March 12, at least 11 people are killed during armed confrontations between Oromo and Afar pastoralists in the Bordeda (Mieso) area, Ethiopia over water and pasture.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7772237

title: Afghan security forces transferring water targeted by assailants
description: In Kandahar, Afghanistan Afghan border security forces are attacked by assailants while transferring water. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202002220023

title: An attack on a water pumping station in Libya cuts of the water supply to 2 million people in the capital of Tripoli
description: An armed group attacked a control station at Shwerif, Libya, cutting off the water supply to more than 2 million people in the capital Tripoli. The UN condemns the attack as "reprehensible."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al Jazeera 2020

title: An environmental activist in Honduras who protested an open-pit mine that would contaminate the Guapinol River is assassinated
description: In October 2020, a member of the El Guapinol community in Honduras who participates in the protests over the development of an open-pit mine that would contaminate community water sources of the Guapinol River is shot and killed in his own home. (See also events of 2018.)
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bruess 2020

title: Armed clash between Husen and Reer Garaad militias in Sanaag, Somalia over pasture and water disputes injures six
description: On June 27, an armed clash is reported between a Husen Sub-Clan militia and Reer Garaad Sub-Clan militia, both from the Warsengeli clan, Sanaag, Somalia. The motive of the clash is believed to be disputes over pasturelands and water resources. At least six people are injured in the clan clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7153500

title: At least one injured in explosion en route to repair water pipe in Yebyu, Myanmar
description: At least one person on their way to fix a water pipe is injured when an explosive device is detonated in Yebyu, Myanmar. A related attack occurs in Yebyu on the same day. Sources suspect the Karen National Union is involved.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202003110027

title: Attacks on water and sanitation systems in the Donbas region of the Ukraine cut off water services for civilians
description: A resumption of aerial attacks between the Ukraine and Russia in the Donbas region again target water and sanitation systems, leaving civilians without running water in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ritter 2020

title: Attempted arson at irrigation construction site in Baleguian, Philippines
description: An attempted arson occurs at an irrigation construction site. A subsequent clash with security forces leaves an unknown number of assailants injured. Sources attribute the attack to the New People’s Army.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202009290017

title: China Opens Mekong Water Releases During Drought
description: In response to downstream protests and diplomatic pressure, China agrees in 2020 to share real-time data on upstream Mekong dam operations and releases water from its Yunnan reservoirs to alleviate drought conditions in Lower Mekong riparian states.
countries: China, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Myanmar
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lancang-Mekong Cooperation (LMC) Ministerial Declaration on Hydrological Data Sharing (2020).

title: Clashes in Lebanon over water, electricity and energy shortages lead to injuries and arrests
description: On January 13, demonstrators in Sidon city, Lebanon protest the crises in the country, including lack of water, electricity, gasoline, diesel, and gas. Clashes between rioters and military forces are reported, leaving five people injured and several arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7924726

title: Clashes over shared water point kills at least 10 in northern Uganda
description: Clashes between South Sudanese refugees and local community members in Tika village near the Rhino refugee settlement in northern Uganda over access to a shared water source leave at least 10 dead, 19 injured, and several missing.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Athumani 2020

title: Clashes over water resources in Yemen result in eight deaths and additional injuries
description: On May 1, clashes between Al Tilan and Al Dahshal Ba al Harith tribal militias over water resources in Al Ghiwayl valley of Usaylan district (Shabwah), result in eight deaths and additional injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7074385

title: Deaths and injuries reported in a clash over the use of a water pump in Burkina Faso
description: On July 11, members of Lobi and Dogosse communities clash over the use of a water pump for a Lobi customary rite in Tako-Yoyora (Loropeni, Poni), Burkina Faso. Three people are killed, two injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8016768

title: Deaths are reported in protests over a mine that would contaminate local water sources in Honduras
description: Beginning in 2011, members of the community of El Guapinol, Honduras, protest the development of an open-pit mine that would contaminate their water source, the Guapinol River. In 2018, the group protesting set up an encampment that after several months is violently broken up by security guards. One protestor is shot and killed and others are arrested and put in jail. In October, 2020, another member of the community who participates in the protests is shot and killed in his own home.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bruess 2020

title: Demonstrations against a proposed privatization of the drinking water system in Mexico leads to injuries and arrests
description: On November 30, in Chignautla, Puebla, Mexico, hundreds of residents demonstrate against the proposed privatization of the drinking water system. The demonstration turns violent. The municipal police intervene with pepper spray; the demonstrators react by looting and burning the municipal presidency. Arrests and injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7619803

title: Demonstrations in Chile over land and water rights lead to conflicts with the police, injuries, and arrests
description: In November 2020, demonstrations in the Los Rios region of Chile over land and water rights and other water concerns lead to conflicts with local police and arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7303190

title: Demonstrators in Gheyzaniyeh, Iran are injured while protesting water outages
description: On May 25, police shoot tear gas and rubber bullets at demonstrators in Gheyzaniyeh, Iran demonstrating against frequent outages of water. Several injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8055724

title: Demonstrators storm a desalination plant in Tunisia, disrupting local potable water supply
description: On September 23, demonstrators storm a desalination plant in Nagga, Kebili, Tunisia and interrupt the provision of potable water in the region to demand the pavement of a public road in their village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7233824

title: Egyptian hackers claim responsibility for a cyberattack on dam operations at the Ethiopian Grand Renaissance Dam
description: Egyptian hackers launch a cyber attack on Ethiopian water systems in June 2020. On a Facebook page maintained by the hackers, they allude to Egyptian opposition to the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile. The attack is carried out as the reservoir behind the dam is being filled despite the lack of an agreement between Egypt and Ethiopia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mahmoud 2020

title: Engineers and customary chief kidnapped on way to repair water piping system destroyed by attack
description: Three engineers working for the water distribution network of Ngongo and a customary chief are kidnapped in Mwanga, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo. The abduction occurs en route to repair a water piping system that was destroyed by assailants in an earlier attack. Their fate is not known. Sources attribute the attack to the Patriotic Resistance Front in Ituri.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202009210037

title: Environmental defender killed along with two of his family members in conflict over a dam in Patuca, Honduras
description: Gunman kill Jose Antonio Teruel, an environmental defender in the Patuca community in Honduras, in part due to his connection to a conflict between a power company and the community over a dam. During the murder, which occurs in his home, his sister and her husband are killed as well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Business & Human Rights Resource Centre. n.d.-c

title: Explosion outside water station near Naanaah, Iraq, injures at least one
description: An explosive device is detonated in front of the central water station near Naanaah, Iraq, injuring at least one station employee. A related bombing occurs in this area on the same date. No group claims responsibility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202006140013

title: Farmers break into La Boquilla dam in Mexico in opposition to water releases to the United States
description: The National Guard and the army are deployed to La Boquilla Dam in October after protesters occupy it in protest of proposed water releases to the United States.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mexico News Daily 2020

title: Fighting in Libya continues to include attacks on water supply infrastructure
description: Fighting between the Libyan National Army (LNA) and the internationally recognized Government of National Accord (GNA) leads to cuts in water and power to Tripoli when gunmen storm a control room, cutting water flows from the Great Manmade River Project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2020

title: Four are injured during protests in Cojedes, Venezuela over lack of public water services, including water
description: On September 29 in San Carlos, Cojedes, Venezuela, residents protest the lack of basic public services such as water, electricity, and gas. GNB and CPNB officers arrest 12 individuals. Four people are injured by state security forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7238578

title: Four are injured in a land and water dispute in Thanamandi, India
description: On March 1, four people attack a family in Thanamandi (Rajouri district, Jammu and Kashmir), India over a land and water dispute. Four members of the family are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6985035

title: Four injuries reported in a dispute over irrigation water rotations in Pakistan
description: On July 3, a clash takes place between two groups from the Janwri and Dhalo communities over rotation of water in Abdul Hakeem Dhalo village in Radhan, Pakistan. Four men are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7155626

title: Gunmen attack water and sewage workers in Cukurca, Turkey
description: Assailants carrying firearms and rockets attack water and sewage employees in Cukurca, Turkey, injuring two. No group claims responsibility, but sources believe the Kurdistan Workers’ Party to be behind the assault.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202006250007

title: In Guyana, security guards protecting a water pump used to flood land as weapon against squatters are attacked
description: On October 15 in Success, Demerara-Mahaica, Guyana, two armed men attack a security guard protecting a water pump controlled by the Guyana Sugar Company. The company is accused of using the water to flood land to drive squatters out.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7248742, 7248743

title: In a caste dispute, over two dozen Dalit are attacked with acid for using a handpump for water in Jhansi, India
description: On August 25, a mob attacks and injures over two dozen Dalit people with acid in Basaar village in Jhansi (UP), India over using a handpump for water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7198760

title: Injuries are reported during a protest in Yaracuy, Venezuela demanding better potable water services
description: On September 26 in Chivacoa, Yaracuy, Venezuela, around 60 people demonstrate to demand better basic services including potable water. National Guard and police fire tear gas after rioters destroy the headquarters of the Mayor's office. An unknown number of people are injured and arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7758267

title: Injuries are reported in a demonstration over access to improved water and electricity in Guinea
description: On July 14, residents demonstrated in Siguiri town (Siguiri, Kankan), Guinea to demand better electricity and water supply. Security forces fire tear gas to disperse them, injuring several people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7163509

title: Israel detects and thwarts a cyberattack on water systems
description: Israeli authorities link Iran to an attempted cyberattack aimed at disrupting water supplies in at least two locations in Israel in late April 2020.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Warrick and Nakashima 2020

title: Israeli forces damage drinking water tanks while trying to disperse Palestinian protestors
description: On May 15, Israeli forces use live fire, rubber bullets, and tear gas to disperse Palestinians protesting settlement policies in Kafr Qaddum. Two drinking water tanks are damaged during the event.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7096535

title: Mexican military forces and farmers clash over water releases from a dam
description: Farmers protest at the Las Virgines dam in northern Mexico where water is being held to repay a water debt to the U.S. Several hundred overtake control of the dam, causing property damage estimated at $4.6 million. The farmers say that without the water, they will no longer be able to farm.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2020a, AP News 2020

title: Multiple cyber-attacks on Israel water infrastructure
description: Several cyberattacks on Israeli water infrastructure are reported by the Israeli Water Authority. The attacks are aimed at agricultural water pumps in the Upper Galilee and on water and wastewater treatment systems in the central part of the country. No mention is given of who carried out the attacks, but previous similar attacks were attributed to Iranian hackers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; MEM 2020

title: Nine indigenous leaders in the Philippines opposed to dam projects are killed during a police raid
description: Philippine National Police (PNP) and the Criminal Investigation and Detetion Group (CIDG) raid what they claim to be homes of armed members of the new People's Army (NPA) on the island of Panay in the Philippines. During the raid, the police claim that they were shot at and were acting in self defense when they shot and killed nine people. The police also made 16 arrests and claimed to find firearms and explosives in the raided homes. The people who were arrested contested the police account, saying that the police raided the homes at 4 am when the people in the homes were sleeping and deny that any of the people shot at the police or resisted arrest, and that the firearms and bombs were planted by the police. Human rights and environmental groups across the country point out that the nine killed were indigenous leaders of Tumanduk communities working to stop two dam projects in their ancestral lands on the Jalaur River and Panay River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Aguirre 2021

title: Nine people are reported injured in a clash over wastewater in Fazilka district, Punjab, India
description: Around September 2, a clash in Ramnagar Urf Jatwali village of Fazilka district (Punjab), India over waste water injures nine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7197913

title: Officials inspecting the flow of water in Gulkani, Haryana, India are attacked. Seven injuries and 50 arrests are reported
