description: On July 1, around 50 people attack officials inspecting the flow of water into a pond in Gulkani village, Jind (Haryana), India. Seven policemen and officials are injured and 50 arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7156068

title: One death and multiple injuries reported during protests over lack of potable water and other services in Sucre, Venezuela
description: On September 30 in Cariaco, Sucre, Venezuela, residents block a road to demand basic services including potable water, gasoline, gas, food, and electric power. State police officers arrive to disperse the group of people but are received with stones. One person is killed during the demonstration and an unknown number of people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7238587

title: One death and several injuries are reported during a clash between farmers and pastoralists in South Sudan
description: On February 22, farmers from Kuajiena county, South Sudan attack armed pastoralists from Tonj at a water point, leading to a firefight which kills one and wounds between three and five people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7685894

title: One death is reported in dispute over control of water in a refugee camp in Bangladesh
description: On September 3, a dispute over access to water between Rohingya refugees and residents of the Chakmarkul Rohingya Camp (Teknaf, Cox's Bazar) in Bangladesh leads to a death.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7198825

title: One injured during protests demanding water in Trujillo, Venezuela
description: On May 11, in Carvajal, Trujillo, Venezuela, residents protest to demand water and are met with force by Special Action Forces (FAES). One person is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7100483

title: One injury reported in a fight in Garhi Khairo, Pakistan over irrigation rotations
description: On August 5, a clash takes place between two groups of the Buledi community in Jnai Wandh village in Jacobabad, Sindh, Pakistan over rotation of water, causing injuries to one.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7198232

title: One man is shot during protests in Miranda, Venezuela to demand potable water services
description: On August 26 in Cupira, Miranda, Venezuela, residents protest to demand basic services including potable water and are met with force by municipal police. One man is severely injured with a bullet.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7185224

title: One person reported killed in clash over water in Kupwara, India
description: On August 3, two families clash at Kacchama village in Kupwara city (Kupwara district, Jammu and Kashmir), India over a water dispute. One person is killed in the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7200256

title: Over 100 injuries reported in a clash over access to water in local villages in Bangladesh
description: On December 18, two groups of villagers clash at Baniachong Upazila (Habiganj), Bangladesh over control of a water body. Over 100 people are injured in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7461913

title: Protestors injured in Tripoli, Libya, while protesting water shortages and other deplorable living conditions
description: Several hundred people hold a protest of deplorable living conditions, including from water shortages, in Tripoli, Libya. Some protestors are injured from shots by security forces working to disperse the demonstrations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Aslan 2020

title: Protests against the water crisis in Pernik, Bulgaria turn violent, injuring at least 32 people
description: On January 27, at least 300 residents in Sofia protest the water crisis in Pernik and clash with police. Police use tear gas and at least 32 people, including two police officers, are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6770918

title: Protests in Algeria for improved water supply and energy leads to clashes with police and injuries
description: On February 26, 2020, police forces and rioters clashed in Draa El Caid, Algeria over gas and water services, resulting in the injury of two police officers and several dozen rioters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6977786

title: Protests in Caxito, Angola for improved water supply leads to clashes with police and injuries
description: On August 5, 2020, people stage a demonstration in Caxito (Dande, Bengo, Angola) in support of employees who had not received their wages and against the lack of water supply in the region. Police used tear gas and live fire to disperse the demonstrators. Injuries and arrests are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8016224

title: Seven killed in clan dispute over land and water in Mandera, Kenya
description: Around November 20, Garre and Murle clans clash over pasture land and water in Yado village, Mandera, Kenya. At least seven people are killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7395780

title: Seventeen people reported injured in a dispute over irrigation water scheduling in Pakistan
description: On February 6, a clash erupts between two groups of the Gaho community, Kumb town, Pakistan, over water rotation. Both groups attack each other with sticks and axes injuring 17 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6863610

title: Several killed in a fight over a watering point in Marsabit, Kenya
description: In mid-June, herders clash over a watering point in Marsabit, Kenya. Several fatalities are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7129928, 7129714

title: Several killed in an attack on a dam in Afghanistan
description: Several military personnel are killed and others wounded during an attack on a dam, Machalugu village, Paktia province, Afghanistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Pettersson et al. 2021 ; Sundberg and Melander 2013

title: Shelling damages Siverskyi Donets-Donbas water pipeline, Ukraine
description: Shelling reported at the Siverskyi Donets-Donbas water pipeline in contested areas of eastern Ukraine (June 2020). The pipeline delivers water to people in the region from the Siverskyi Donets River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sheldon 2020

title: Six deaths reported in clashes over the use of water wells in Chad
description: In January, members of the Arab and Boulala communities clash in the area of Djokhana (Dababa, Hadjer-Lamis), Chad over the usage of water wells. Six people were reportedly killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6876190

title: Six police officers killed and two wounded in attack at irrigation dam in Qala-e Fath, Afghanistan
description: An attack on a police outpost guarding an irrigation dam leaves six officers dead and two injured. Sources suspect the Taliban are responsible, but they deny the claim.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202010240001

title: Sniper shoots and wounds civilian fetching water in al-Rawdah, Yemen
description: A civilian is injured after being shot by a sniper while attempting to fetch water. Sources attribute the attack to Houthi extremists.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202008170036

title: Soldiers wounded, water pumps and transformers destroyed in attack on Popular Mobilization Forces checkpoints in Al-Wehda, Iraq
description: An attack on Popular Mobilization Forces checkpoints leaves at least two soldiers injured and destroys several water pumps and transformers. Sources believe the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant to be behind the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202009160012

title: Suspected Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist fighters detonate an explosive device at the Arun III Hydropower Dam, Nepal
description: Suspected Communist Party of Nepal–Maoist (CPN-Maoist-Chand) fighters detonate an explosive device at the Arun III Hydropower Dam construction site, Nepal, damaging a generator.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: Suspected New People's Army fighters conduct an armed assault on the Igbaras Hydropower Plant, Philippines
description: Suspected New People's Army fighters conduct an armed assault on the Igbaras Hydropower Plant, Iloilo, Philippines, with automatic/semi-automatic rifles. An unknown number of attackers are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; U.S. Department of Homeland Security 2023

title: The Sudanese Armed Forces clash with Amhara militants after the Ethiopians try to make use of river water in Sudan
description: On May 28, Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) clash with Amhara militia in the area of Barakat Norein, Sudan, after the SAF refused to allow the Ethiopians to make use of river water in the area. The area is claimed by Ethiopia. One Ethiopian militiaman is wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7770242

title: The curtailment of water and electricity after cyclone Amhan leads to protests in Budhal, India. One injury is reported
description: On May 26, a mob attacks police and Trinamool legislators in Kolkata city (Kolkata district, West Bengal), India while calling for restoration of electricity and water supply affected by cyclone Amphan. One injury is reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7118952

title: Three Afar militiamen shot by Somali forces in Garbo Ciise, Ethiopia amid ongoing clashes over water and grazing rights
description: In late January, three Afar communal militiamen are shot and wounded by Somali ethnic forces in Garbo Ciise (Adaytu), Ethiopia. Clashes over grazing areas, water, and other resources are common in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7677367

title: Three deaths and four injuries are reported in a gunfight over irrigation water rotation and money in Pakistan
description: On July 7, a clash takes place between two groups of the Bhangwar community near Kandhkot city, Pakistan over water rotation and money. Both groups fire at each other, killing three men and injuring four others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7161589

title: Three injuries and two deaths are reported in a dispute over drainage water in Madhya Pradesh, India
description: On January 12, two unidentified groups fire at each other in Gwalior (Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh) India over the flow of drainage water, leading to two deaths and three injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6746005

title: Three youth collecting water are injured when attacked in South Sudan
description: On November 14, three youth collecting water from the river Horse are wounded by armed militia in Torit county, South Sudan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7307215

title: Two deaths are reported when Syrian militias fight with smugglers during a raid on water tankers
description: On March 29, QSD forces clash with smugglers during a raid on water tankers in the town of Thiban in Deir-ez-Zor, Syria. Clashes result in at least two deaths and additional wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8087309

title: Two farmers kill their neighbor in a dispute over sharing water from a well in Madhya Pradesh, India
description: On February 26, two farmers beat to death their neighbor in Majhgawan village (Chhatarpur, Madhya Pradesh), India during a dispute on sharing water from a well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 6980136

title: Two groups clash over irrigation water in Pakistan, with severe injuries to two people
description: On May 8, two groups of Solangi community clash over water rotation in Mirpurkhas city, Pakistan. They attack each other with weapons, resulting in severe injuries to two men.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7085556

title: Two killed during widespread protests at La Boquilla dam that diverts water to the United States from Mexico
description: Two are killed a gunfight with Mexico’s military police near several days of protest in La Boquilla, Chihuahua, at a dam that diverts water to the United States. Mexicans in the northern state of Chihuahua are angry at water being diverted across the border hurl Molotov cocktails and rocks at security troops, and occupy the La Boquilla dam, closing the sluice gates.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gonzalez 2020 ; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7622818

title: Two police officers killed and one injured while carrying water from a well in Mirza Ali, Afghanistan
description: An assailant opens fire on police officers carrying water from a well in Mirza Ali, Afghanistan, killing at least two and injuring another. No group claims responsibility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202004270008

title: Violent protest at Las Virgenes dam, Chihuahua, Mexico over water releases
description: Demonstrators at the Las Vírgenes Dam in Chihuahua, Mexico burn several government vehicles, block railway tracks and set fire to a government office and highway tollbooths to protest the release of water from local dams to meet treaty obligations with the United States.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associate Press (AP) 2020

title: Water distribution workers abducted in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
description: Employees of a Ngongo water distribution organization are abducted and later released unharmed. Sources attribute the incident to the Patriotic and Integrationist Forces of the Congo.
basin: Democratic Republic of the Congo Havzası
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202009140028

title: Water supply network damaged in attack on Palestinian-owned land in Khallet Ad-Dabi, West Bank
description: Assailants damage a water supply network, attack a home and set fire to more than 400 olive trees during the incident. Sources attribute the attack to Israeli Settlers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; START 2025 ID. 202012130036

title: Well-known businessman and environmental activist kidnapped and killed in Veracruz, Mexico
description: In October 2020 a local businessman and environmental defender, Miguel Vazquez Martinez, is kidnapped in Tlapacoyan, Veracruz, Mexico. His body is not found until 2021. He was known for over 15 years of organizing to prevent hydroelectric projects on local rivers and he founded a local environmental defense organization that had filed injunctions to try to prevent some dam projects from progressing.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Pradilla 2020 ; infobae 2021

title: White supremacists in the United States plot to poison water supplies
description: In secret surveillance, the US Federal Bureau of Investigation records neo-Nazis recruiting members and plotting terrorist acts including poisoning water supplies in an effort to ignite violence. Seven arrests were made.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; MacFarquhar and Goldman 2020

title: 'Stop Line 3' protest related to water in US turns violent; demonstrators light fires, smash windows; arrests made
description: On March 11, about 100 people gather for a 'Stop Line 3' demonstration in Portland, Oregon, United States in support of abolishing ICE, protecting water rights and quality, and against the proposed Line 3 oil pipeline expansion. The demonstration turns violent when around 50 to 60 demonstrators light fires, smash windows, and pull protective plywood off a federal courthouse. Federal officers fire tear gas and chemical munitions to disperse the crowd resulting in injuries and arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8073113

title: 11 people are reported shot in a fire fight over access to water in Guinea
description: On May 17, villagers of Dankakoro and Banfelebougou villages, Guinea engage in fire fights around Dankakoro village over access to a disputed water point. 11 people are shot and injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7993103

title: A Brahmin group assaults Dalit community members over drawing water from a shared well in Malarh, India
description: On July 9, a Brahmin caste group assaults Dalit community members at Malarh village in Udhampur district (J&K), India, over drawing water from a shared well. Several Dalit community members are injured in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8383819

title: A Nevada-based wastewater plant is targeted with malware that affects the SCADA system, USA
description: In March 2021, a Nevada-based wastewater plant is targeted with an unknown malware strain that affects the SCADA system.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ahmed 2021

title: A Palestinian-owned water spring near Hebron is sealed by Israeli military forces
description: On November 4, Israeli military forces seal a Palestinian-owned water spring east of Bayt Ummar, Hebron, West Bank, to prevent farmers from using it.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8623420

title: A Water Resources Department staff member was assaulted by farmers in Punjab, India over the alleged theft of irrigation water
description: Around July 9, a staff member of the Water Resources Department, Punjab, India is attacked and injured by farmers in Lualaba village (Nabha, Patiala district), when stopped from allegedly stealing water from canals.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8391970

title: A clash over a proposed water project in Al Ashah, Yemen results in three deaths and one injury
description: On September 5, clashes erupt between Sufyan and Al Usaymat tribesmen in Al Ashah, Yemen over a water project that Houthi forces are planning in a contested area between the two tribes. The clashes result in three fatalities and one injury.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8532662

title: A clash over access to water between different ethnic groups in Cameroon leads to at least 22 deaths and hundreds of refugees
description: On December 9, armed men from the Musgum and Massa ethnic groups clashed with Arab Choas in Kousseri town (Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord), Cameroon over the ownership of a water spot. At least 22 people were killed over three days; hundreds of people are displaced to N'Djamena in Chad.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8686676, 8686675, 8686675

title: A clash over shortage of drinking water, illegal fishing, and lack of electricity leads to two injuries in Pakistan
description: On August 17, a demonstration in Gwadar city, Pakistan against water shortages, illegal fishing, and electricity cutoffs leads to a clash injuring two people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8476686

title: A conflict over control of and access to water results in one death to a child collecting water in Yemen
description: On October 24, 2021, clashes between Abu Shusa tribesmen and Sabara tribesmen supported by Houthi forces result in the death of a child in Wadi Mawr (Al Maghrabah, Hajjah), Yemen as the child was getting water from the area. According to one source, Houthi forces prevent citizens from other tribes from collecting water in the area claiming that it is within 'Hashemite property'.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8611596, 8611736

title: A demonstration in France over the construction of irrigation tanks leads to the destruction of water infrastructure and a clash
description: On November 6, demonstrators gathered in Cramchaban, France to protest the construction of 19 irrigation tanks in the area. They damage water pumps, burning equipment, and empty a water reservoir. Police respond with tear gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8648986

title: A dispute between local residents and farmers in Tarata, Bolivia over the use of water lead to at least two injuries
description: On August 18 in Tarata, Cochabamba, Bolivia locals and irrigation farmers clash near La Angostura dam after a blockade was implemented by the workers. The blockade was set up to demand the use of the water from the dam to irrigate land in the region. Local residents argue the water should be used for tourism and local fish farming activities. At least two injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8431728

title: A dispute over canal water in Okara, Pakistan kills two and injures three
description: On October 9, two people are killed and three are injured when armed men fire bullets at a family in Okara, Pakistan, allegedly over a canal water dispute.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8601883

title: A dispute over the construction of an irrigation water canal in Pakistan leads to two deaths and one injury
description: On July 9, farmers shoot and killed two other farmers and injure one other in Faisalabad, Pakistan, over the construction of an irrigation water canal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8391862

title: A dispute over the diversion of flood waters for irrigation in Nepal leads to 15 injuries
description: On June 26, a group of locals, including a ward chairperson, clash with others in Maulapur municipality, Nepal over diverting flood water into local fields. 15 people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8374863

title: A dispute over the rotation of water results in injuries in Pakistan
description: On July 25, two groups of the Khuhawar community attack each other with sticks, injuring one man in Sarang Khuhawar village, Pakistan. The dispute is over rotation of water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8413325

title: A farmer is killed in a dispute over irrigation water in Punjab, India
description: On July 25, a farmer is attacked and killed by his neighbors in Kamal Wala village (Fazilka district, Punjab), India, over a water canal dispute.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8413274

title: A fight over a drinking water well in Xudun, Somalia kills at least ten people
description: On April 16, a fight over a drinking water well between militias in the Dhabar-Dalool village near Xudun, Somalia kills at least ten people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7875383

title: A fight over a water reservoir near Baxdo, Somalia kills two and injures three others
description: On June 5, two clan militias fight over a water reservoir near Baxdo village, Galgaduud, Somalia. Two people are killed and three others are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8069450

title: A fight over a water well in Wadi al Barkani, Yemen injures six
description: On January 8, unknown militias clashed in Wadi al Barkani, Yemen over a water well, injuring six people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7450122

title: A fight over access to a water well escalates into extensive violence in the Upper Nile state of South Sudan, killing at least 1
description: On January 3rd and 4th, a fight over water access at a well escalates in the disputed border town of Meganis, Upper Nile, South Sudan. 17 are killed across two days of fighting and more than 20 are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7454070, 7454072

title: A fight over the rotation of irrigation water in Pakistan injures four
description: On March 4, a clash takes place between two groups of the Bohra community over the rotation of water injuring four men in Pir Chandam village, Shikarpur, Sindh, Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7739499

title: A fight over the use of irrigation water in the Punjab, Pakistan injures at least eight
description: On May 6, at least eight people are injured in a clash between two groups of villagers in Bahawalnagar district (Punjab), Pakistan over the usage of irrigation water in the village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7973977

title: A man is killed in a clash over irrigation water in the Punjab, Pakistan
description: On October 8, a man was shot dead during a clash between two groups over irrigation water at Gagar village, Punjab, Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8602001

title: A man who tries to rob a water pump in Mexico is beaten by local residents
description: On December 10, in Oaxaca de Juarez, Mexico a man is undressed, beaten, and tied up after he tries to rob a water pump.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8688493

title: A pastoralist is killed and four others injured in a dispute over land and water near Kismayo, Somalia
description: On September 17, suspected Awramale clan militia shoot and kill a pastoralist from Majeerteen clan in the vicinity of Kismayo town, Somalia, in a dispute over water and land. Four other injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8565318

title: A pipeline carrying water to a joint Myanmar-China mine is bombed by a militia group opposed to the Myanmar military regime
description: On September 9, in Salingyi township (Yinmarbin district, Sagaing region), Myanmar a water pipeline transporting water from the Chindwin River to the Myanmar Wanbao and Myanmar Yangtze copper mines (a joint venture between China and a Myanmar military-owned holding company) is bombed by a local militia group. The group stated that the bombing was carried out because China had been ignoring the 'desires of Myanmar people for democracy and backing the military junta.'
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8537392

title: A protest in Afghanistan over lack of clean drinking water and other services results in three deaths and more than 40 injuries
description: On June 8, 200 demonstrators in the city of Fayzabad, Badakhshan, Afghanistan protest inadequate security and a lack of electricity and clean drinking water. The demonstrators clash with police, throwing stones and wood at security forces and setting fire to a tax collection office building. Three demonstrators are killed and 43 others were wounded after police responded by shooting.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8071621

title: A protest in Trelew, Argentina over environmental and water concerns of a mining project turns violent
description: In December 2021 in Trelew (Chubut), Argentina, a group protests the approval of the mining project in Chubut's province, demand the law's repeal and improved protection of water. Multiple government buildings are set on fire; police respond with tear gas and rubber bullets; more than 30 injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8702468, 8702001, 8702000, 8702958

title: A social activist protesting inadequate water service is shot and killed in Mexico
description: On September 7, in Cuernavaca, Morelos, a social activist is shot and killed by two armed men in his house in Colonia Antonio Barona, Mexico. The victim led several protests to demand water service and created groups to prevent the Federal Commission of Electricity from suspending electricity to the wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8532287

title: A water dispute in the Chui region of Kyrgyzstan results in at least one hospitalization
description: On June 23, a resident of Iskra village near Tokmok city in the Chui region of Kyrgyzstan is assaulted by the villagers from a neighboring town following a water dispute. One hospitalization is reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8359742

title: A water project in Al Hudaydah, Yemen is attacked
description: On June 16, Houthi attack the Al Khamiri water project in Hays city (Al Hudaydah), Yemen. According to the source, the work on the water project is interrupted by the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8165518

title: A water station is destroyed near Ar-Raqqa, Syria
description: On July 17, an IED planted by an unidentified armed group in Beir Al-Hashim in Ar-Raqqa detonates inside the well project and renders the water station inoperable.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8395035

title: A water well is damaged after Houthi forces target civilian farms in Al Hudaydah, Yemen
description: On November 4, Houthi forces target civilian farms in At Tuhayat district (Al Hudaydah), Yemen, with mortars damaging a water well. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8629246

title: A worker at a wastewater treatment plant in California, U.S., remotely uninstalls software needed for safe operation
description: In January 2021, a worker at a company providing services to the Discovery Bay, California, wastewater treatment plant remotely accesses the plant’s computers and uninstalls software critical to operating the facility’s network and protecting its water treatment systems, including water filtration, water pressure, and chemical levels maintenance. He is arrested, tried, and convicted.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; United States Attorney's Office 2024

title: Airstrike hits rural water and electricity authority in Sana, Yemen
description: On September 12, an airstrike hits a rural water and electricity authority in Al-Thawrah District, Sana, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: An attack on a water tanker delivering water to pastoralists affected by drought in Somalia kills four
description: On December 2, an unidentified group attacks a water tanker delivering water to pastoralists affected by drought near Buulo Xaaji village, Lower Juba, Somalia. Four people are killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8673592

title: An attempt to steal water from a government-owned water channel leads to gunfire and injuries in Pakistan
description: On September 9, officials of an irrigation department are attacked in Faisalabad, Pakistan after refusing to let people steal water from a government-owned channel.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8541019

title: An unidentified group destroys a water plant providing water in Libya
description: On July 29, an unidentified armed group blows up water station 353 on the Man-made River near Ash Shwayrif (Al Jabal Al Gharbi), Libya, disrupting water supply to Bani Walid, Misrata, Khoms, and Zliten.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8403559

title: Another nine indigenous leaders, also opposing a dam project, are killed in the Philippines by police
description: Three months after the killing of nine Indigenous leaders on Panay Island—deaths that human rights advocates link to opposition against two dam projects—a similar tragedy unfolded in the Philippines. On what became known as “Bloody Sunday,” joint raids by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and Philippine Army (PA) targeted Indigenous people accused of being communist insurgents. The raids resulted in six arrests and nine deaths, including environmental activists Puroy Berhemedo de la Cruz and Randy Pulong Berhemedo de la Cruz of the Dumagat Sierra Madre group, who had campaigned for Indigenous rights and against the Kaliwa Dam project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; International Federation for Human Rights 2021 ; Business & Human Rights Resource Centre n.d.-d

title: Anti-dam activist receives death threats before his murder in Oaxaca, Mexico
description: An anti-dam activist, Fidel Heras Cruz, receives a death threat before being murdered in January 2021 in the state of Oaxaca, Mexico. He had also been opposed to commercial sand and gravel extraction that damanged the river bed. Follwing this murder, the Mexican government confirmed that the hydroelectric project would continue.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Associated Press 2021

title: Armed assailants attack police in Shadegan, Iran amid water shortage protests, killing one officer and injuring three others
description: On July 24, unidentified armed assailants open fire on and injure four policemen in Shadegan city (Khuzestan), Iran. The attack occurs in the context of continued tension and protests over water shortages. One police officer dies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8425789

title: At least six killed in clan disputes over land and water in Garbatulla, Kenya
description: On January 9, militias from the Ajuran and Borana clans fight over land and water in the vicinity of Eldera village, Garbatulla, Kenya. At least six people are killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7499757

title: At least three are killed in a clash over the distribution of water in Pakistan
description: On July 8, at least three people are killed in a clash including exchange of gunfire over water distribution in Dera Ghazi Khan city, Punjab, Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8383559

title: Attacks on water systems in Ethiopia have cut off water supply to thousands of people
description: Throughout the conflict in Tigray, Ethiopia, water infrastructure has been attacked, causing communities to lose access to safe water access. Water pumps have been destroyed, and equipment has been looted.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Action Against Hunger 2021

title: Azerbaijan and Armenian forces clash over water
description: On December 8, 2021, the Ministry of Defense of Armenia report that military forces of Azerbaijan open fire on a car belonging to the military of Armenia transporting water in the South-Western part of the Armenia-Azerbaijan border.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8691565

title: Border guards from Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan exchange fire over a water source, killing dozens and wounding hundreds
description: Between April 28 and 30, 2021, border guards and rioters from Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan exchange fire over the control of a water canal and pumping site along the Isfara River. Several dozen casualties and hundreds of hospitalizations were reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7931294, 7931294, 7971544 ; Auyezov et al 2021

title: Civilians fetching water are killed by Islamic militants in Mozambique
description: On October 22, Islamist militia attack and kill several civilians fetching water in Lumumua, Mozambique.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8611892

title: Clashes between fishers and ranchers over water displace thousands between Cameroon and Chad
description: Clashes between Mousgoum fishermen and Arab Choua cattle ranchers over water usage displace at least 11,000 civilians between Cameroon and Chad in August 2021.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Voice of America News 2021

title: Clashes in Missiska, Cameroon over water and land kill 45, injure 74; 19 villages burned, 40 abandoned after cattle deaths
description: In the village of Missiska in the Logone Birni division, northern Cameroon, violent clashes over water and land use erupt when a basin dug by Musgum fisherfolk trapped and killed cattle belonging to Arab Choa herders. The conflict kills at least 45 people and injures 74 others. At least 19 villages are burned down and 40 others abandoned by the inhabitants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Crisis Group 2024

title: Clashes occur among herders, farmers, and fishers, northern Cameroon
description: Clashes among herders, farmers, and fishers break out over water and land in the village of Ouloumsa, Logone-Birni town, Far North, Cameroon.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Crisis Group 2024

title: Community organizer and river defender murdered in Guerrero, Mexico
description: A community organizer and river defender, Isaías Elacio Palma, is murdered in March 2021, in Cacahuatepec in the state of Guerrero, Mexico. His son had been murdered in 2018 for defending the environment as well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; González Chacón et al. 2022

title: Conflicts over water in Cameroon between ranchers and fishermen kill at least 40 people
description: Tens of thousands of citizens of Cameroon flee bloody conflicts over water between cattle ranchers and fishermen in the region bordering Chad and Nigeria. The conflict kills at least 40 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kindzeka 2022

title: Deaths and injuries are reported in a fight over water supply in Pakistan
description: On July 27, two groups exchange fire killing two people and injuring seven in Tangoo Basi, Pakistan, over a water supply line.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8413382

title: Deaths are reported in demonstrations in Khuzestan, Iran over electrical outages, water shortages, and the transfer of water out
description: In mid- to late-July, protestors clash with police and other security forces in Bandar e Mahshahr, Susangerd, Ahvaz, Izeh, and Aligudarz (Khuzestan), Iran over repeated and prolonged electrical outages, water shortages, and the transfer of water from Khuzestan to other provinces. Explosions and gunfire are heard and several demonstrators and at least one policeman is reported killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8394011, 8394012, 8394005, 8394006, 8394007, 8394000, 8394002, 8733596

title: Demonstrators in Kiev, Ukraine rally against renewal of water supplies to Crimea, resulting in violent clashes with police
description: On August 14, activists demonstrate in Kiev against the implementation of the Steinmeier formula on Donbas conflict settlement and the renewal of water supplies to Russia-occupied Crimea. The demonstrators provoke clashes with police using tear gas, tires, and other items. Eight officers are reportedly injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8471091

title: Eight are killed and many injured in a fight over a water well in Al Yatmah, Yemen
description: On February 13, 2021, militias affiliated with the Juayd Tribe and the Al Hussein tribe, and soldiers from the pro-Hadi 7th brigade in Al Yatmah (Khabb wa ash Shaaf), Yemen clash over a water well. The clashes result in eight fatalities and dozens of injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7697066

title: Extensive attacks on Gaza disrupt water supplies for 800,000 people
description: Around 800,000 people in Gaza lack regular access to piped water in the wake of the 11-day fighting in 2021 that damages around half of the water network or cuts off electricity required for the water system, says the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). Gaza municipality authorities say in a statement that 290 water-supply facilities, including the only desalination plant in northern Gaza, are damaged during the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; The Water Diplomat 2021 ; UNICEF 2021 ; Humaid 2021

title: Farmer/pastoralist violence over land and water lead to at least one death in Baringo region of Kenya
description: On August 5, an unidentified communal militia shoot and kill a pastoralist in the Embosos area in Arabal village, Marigat, Baringo, Kenya. At least 38 cattle are stolen from pastoralists in search of pasture and water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8461043

title: Farmers in Isfahan, Iran clash with police over water shortages and diversions of water from the region
description: On May 25, farmers demonstrate in Isfahan, Iran over issues stemming from shortages and lack of access to Zayandehrud River water. A conflict with police result in several injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8056330

title: Farmers protest lack of access to water and droughts in Isfahan, Iran. Several protesters are injured
description: On July 4, farmers protest in front of the Isfahan provincial governorate building in Iran over lack of access to water and droughts affecting the Zayandehrud River. Police reportedly intervene, beating and injuring several protesters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8375665

title: Farmers protesting water shortages and drought are beaten and arrested in Shaban village, Iran
description: On September 1, farmers protest water shortages and drought in Shaban village near Nahavand city (Hamadan), Iran. They are confronted by police who beat them and make several arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8425500

title: Farmers rally in Isfahan, Iran over water shortages; police use tear gas and rubber bullets, dozens injured, 60+ arrested
description: On November 26, farmers and supporters rally at the dried Zayandehrud riverbed and throughout the streets of Isfahan, Iran demanding the government address water shortages. Police attacked the demonstrators with tear gas, rubber bullets, and batons, and make between 60-214 arrests; the internet is shut down, and the city is put under security lockdown. Dozens of demonstrators are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8734218 ; Fassihi 2021

title: Five people are injured in a clash over the waters of the Longone River, Cameroon.
description: Arab Choa people from Malia and Toukoumaya villages clash in a land and water dispute around Waza, a town in Logone-et-Chari. Five people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Crisis Group 2024

title: Four are killed and eight injured in a fight over the distribution of irrigation water in Pakistan
description: On August 1, two groups from the communities of Chandio and Bohar, Pakistan exchanged fire, killing four people and injuring eight, over the distribution of irrigation water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8477231

title: Four river defenders from Paso de la Reina in Oaxaca, Mexico, are murdered within the span of a month
description: Four river defenders from the 500 person community of Paso de la Reina in Oaxaca, Mexico are murdered within the span of a single month, March 2021. The four include Raymundo Robles Riano, Noe Robles Cruz, Gerardo Mendoz Reyes, and Jaime Jimenez Ruiz. This is the same community where a pervious murder of an anti-dam activist occurred in January of the same year.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Muñoz Ramirez 2021

title: Hacker successfully manipulates chemical treatment systems at a Florida water treatment plant adding dangerous levels of sodium
description: A hacker gains control of a small water treatment plant's chemical dosing computer program, causing the addition of dangerous amounts of sodium hydroxide to the community drinking water system. Staff spot the cyberattack and prevent contaminated water from being released to the community.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation 2021c

title: Hackers use a ransomware variant against a New Jersey-based wastewater treatment facility, USA
description: In September 2021, threat actors use a ransomware variant against a New Jersey-based wastewater treatment facility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ahmed 2021

title: Honduran environmental activist protesting construction of a new dam is shot and killed
description: An environmental activist from the town of Nueva Granada, Honduras is shot and killed. He and his fellow community members had been protesting the construction of a new dam on the Ulua River in Honduras.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bruess 2021a, Al Jazeera 2021b

title: In Maine, U.S., a wastewater facility’s computer is attacked by ransomware, forcing the system to be shut down
description: In July 2021, a ransomware attack is launched against a Maine-based wastewater facility’s SCADA computer forcing the automated system to be shut down and run in manual mode.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ahmed 2021

title: Injuries are reported during a protest in Peru demanding the resumption of potable water and sewage services
description: On March 2, in Las Lomas, Peru, protestors block the Sullana highway that leads towards the International Bridge with Ecuador to demand the resumption of a potable water and sewage works that have been paused for eight years. Police intervene with tear gas and the demonstrators fight back rocks. An unknown number of injured citizens are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7730854

title: Injuries are reported in a clash between farmers and miners over the Arque River in Bolivia
description: On October 23, in Capinota, Cochabamba, Bolivia farmers and mining workers from Sicaya clash for control of Arque river and a watershed. Drought and a dispute over water for mining are the main issues. Three people were injured in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8613014

title: Injuries are reported in a dispute over water wells and land near Qorilow village, Somalia
description: On June 25, Hassan Gaab clan militia clash with Cosoble Ali militia in Qorilow village, Somalia over water wells and land in the area. The injured are rushed to Warshikh town for medical attention.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8366959

title: Islamic State militants destroy a water tanker in Egypt
description: On July 17, 2021, Islamic State militants target a water tanker with an IED in Sheikh Zuwayid (Al Shiekh Zuwaid, North Sinai), Egypt, destroying it.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8394438

title: Israeli forces demolish a medical unit, water well, and under-construction mosque in Hebron, West Bank
description: On August 25, Israeli military forces demolish a medical unit, water well, and an under-construction mosque west of Yuta town, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8425979

title: Israeli forces destroy Palestinian agricultural facilities, including water tanks, near the Maskiyot settlement, West Bank
description: On November 1, 2021, Israeli military forces demolish Palestinian-owned agricultural facilities including sheds, water tanks, and solar cells in Khirbat Al Maytah west of Maskiyot Israeli settlement, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8623408

title: Israeli forces destroy a water tank in Al Khadir, the West Bank
description: On November 1, 2021, Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian water tank in Al Khadir (Bethlehem, West Bank) for not having a building permit.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8623409

title: Israeli forces destroy a waterdistribution network near Hebron in the West Bank
description: On October 25, Israeli military forces bulldoze a water distribution network and a road that links Palestinian villages with Musafer Yuta, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8610568

title: Israeli forces dismantle and destroy residential tents and water tanks of Palestinian farmers in Umm al Jamal, West Bank
description: On November 7, Israeli military forces dismantle and destroy residential tents and sheds, including three water tanks, belonging to Palestinian farmers in Umm al Jamal, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8643190

title: Israeli military cut down Palestinian olive trees and destroy a water well in Birin, West Bank
description: On December 14, 2021, Israeli military forces raze 120 olive trees belonging to Palestinians in Birin, West Bank and destroy a water well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8697574

title: Israeli military forces confiscate West Bank Palestinian agricultural equipment, including five water tanks
description: On 1 December 2021, Israeli military forces confiscate Palestinian-owned agricultural equipment in Khirbet ar Ras al Ahmar, West Bank, including tractors, vehicles, and five water tanks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8670817

title: Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian water well in Nilin; a protest results in multiple injuries
description: On November 29, 2021, Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned water well in Nilin (Ramallah and Al Bireh), West Bank used for agricultural purposes. A protest against the destruction results in multiple injuries from rubber bullets and tear gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8670809, 8670820

title: Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned house and a water well near Hebron
description: On December 7, 2021, Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned house and a water well in Abu Khashabeh, Hebron.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8687926

title: Israeli military forces demolish agricultural facilities including a water well in the West Bank
description: On August 11, 2021, Israeli military forces demolish agricultural facilities, including a water well, caravans, and agricultural rooms in Mosafer Yuta, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8425870

title: Israeli military forces destroy a Palestinian agricultural water tank near Jenin, West Bank
description: On August 9, Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned agricultural water tank used for farming near Yabad, Jenin, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8425855

title: Israeli military forces destroy a Palestinian irrigation water tank in Nablus, West Bank
description: On July 15, Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned water container of 500 cubic meters in Bayt Dajan, Nablus, West Bank, which was used for irrigation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8384463

title: Israeli military forces destroy a water-distribution system near Bayta in the West Bank
description: On September 17, Israeli military bulldozers raze all roads and a water distribution system leading to Jabal Subeih in Bayta town (Nablus) to prevent access to the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8544295

title: Israeli military forces destroy an agricultural structure and water well in Bethlehem, West Bank
description: On August 4, 2021, Israeli military forces demolish five Palestinian-owned agricultural store rooms and a water well in Wadi Rahhal, Bethlehem, West Bank, on the pretext of not having building permits.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8426789

title: Israeli military forces destroy irrigation water pipes in the West Bank
description: On July 6, Israeli military forces raid the village of Al Jiwaya, Hebron, West Bank and uproot water pipes used for irrigation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8375906

title: Israeli military forces raze a Palestinian irrigation system near Khirbat Atuf, West Bank
description: On November 28, 2021, Israeli military forces raze a Palestinian water network (four kilometers long) used for agricultural purposes in Khirbat Atuf, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8670806

title: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian olive trees and irrigation systems in Wadi Qana, West Bank
description: On June 23, Israeli settlers uproot 10 olive trees and ruin water containers and an irrigation network in a Palestinian-owned farm in Wadi Qana, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8266764

title: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian olive trees and steal a water pump in Nablus
description: On June 28, 2021, Israeli settlers from the Ahya settlement uproot Palestinian-owned olive trees and steal a water pump and electric wires in the village of Jalud, Nablus.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8366309

title: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian orchards and irrigation systems in Nablus, West Bank
description: On July 2, Israeli settlers uproot 84 Palestinian-owned fruit trees and destroy irrigation pipes and water containers near the settlements of Shilo and Shvut Rachel in the lands of the village of Qaryut, Nablus.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8366312

title: Israeli settlers destroy agricultural equipment, including water tanks in Shufah, West Bank
description: On November 21, settlers from Avnei Hefetz break into a Palestinian-owned agricultural warehouse in Shufah village, West Bank, and destroy agricultural materials and water tanks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8658862

title: Israeli settlers from the Yitzhar settlement damage a Palestinian-owned water well
description: On November 6, Israeli settlers from the Yitzhar settlement damage a Palestinian-owned water well in the Nabeaa Sufli area, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8643182

title: Kajaki Dam in Afghanistan is attacked by the Taliban
description: Kajaki Dam on the Helmand River in Afghanistan, which provides power to more than three million people including the cities of Kandahar and Lashkar Gah, is attacked by the Taliban.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; France24 2021

title: Kiowa and Cheyenne demonstrators rally in Taos, New Mexico against water pipeline; one injured during protest
description: On February 24, demonstrators from Kiowa and Cheyenne Tribes rally at a construction site in Taos, New Mexico against the construction of a water pipeline in protest of how the Abeyta Water Rights Settlement is being implemented. A demonstrator is injured
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7751534

title: Landmines intended to disrupt the Al Hudaydah city water-supply pipeline in Yemen are defused
description: On August 13, the National Resistance forces engineering team defuse Houthi landmines planted around a water pipe near the Red Sea Mills company in Al Hudaydah, Yemen. According to the source, the mines were going to disrupt city water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8429149

title: Local villagers and farmers tear down an earthen dam on the Dez River, Khuzestan, Iran in opposition to water diversions
description: On June 14, local villagers and farmers tear down an earthen dam on the Dez River near the Dehkhoda Sugarcane Development Company, Seffak (Khuzestan), Iran in opposition to the diversion of water from the river.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8419552

title: Major clash over water kills more than 30 in Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan dispute
description: At least 31 people are killed, scores injured, and 10,000 evacuated after a dispute over access to water and water facilities leads to major clashes on a disputed Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan border.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; British Broadcasting Corporation 2021a

title: Mauritanian protests over water shortages and electricity cuts result in injuries and arrests
description: On July 2, the Mauritanian police use tear gas to disperse hundreds of residents of Kobenni, Mauritania protesting regular water shortages and electricity cuts affecting the city. One policemen is injured and several people are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8535238

title: Militants sabotage electric lines near Ouorou, Burkina Faso, disrupting water access
description: In December militants sabotage the electric lines and destroy a water pump near Ouorou (Toeni, Sourou), Burkina Faso cutting off the water supply to the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8706915, 8687475

title: Militias in Somalia kill two in a dispute over water and grazing land
description: On December 20, militias fighting over water and grazing land kill two from Hawadle clan near Banyaaley village, Hiraan, Somalia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8707004, 8707086

title: Multiple deaths and population displacements reported in clash between clans in Basuke, Marsabit, Kenya
description: Around December 25, Degodia and Borana ethnic militias engage in an armed clash over scarce water and pasture at Basuke, in Marsabit county, Kenya. 11 people are killed and over 300 families are displaced by the conflict into Basir town in Wajir.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8704831

title: Multiple deaths are reported in violence over access to water between pastoralists and local militia in South Darfur, Sudan
description: On March 1, Fellata pastoralists clash with Masalit militia in Gereida, South Darfur, Sudan after a member of the Fellata was killed at or near a water source. 11 more deaths are reported with another 36 wounded across two days of violence.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7732214

title: Multiple injuries are reported during demonstrations over cutoffs of water and electricity in North Darfur, Sudan
description: On April 11, students in El Fasher, North Darfur demonstrate against poor living conditions including the interruption of water and electricity. Rioters block main roads and set fire to tires and at least six members of the armed forces and several students are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7875058

title: One death is reported in a dispute over the control of a local water body in Bangladesh
description: On October 3, armed assailant(s) shoot and kill a person at Digdair village in Tarail Upazila (Kishoreganj), over the control of a local water body.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8590865

title: One death is reported in a fight over access to a water point in the village of Malual Deng Ngor, South Sudan
description: On April 16, two groups of women armed with sticks fight over access to a water point in the village of Malual Deng Ngor in Yargot payam, South Sudan. One woman dies in the incident and five are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8073672

title: One farmer is killed in a dispute over canal water irrigation in Punjab, India
description: On September 23, a group of men allegedly attack a farmer and his son in Amarpura village (Abohar, Fazilka district, Punjab), India, over a canal water irrigation dispute. The farmer died.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8568685

title: One killed and others injured in clan clashes over grazing land and water points in Marsabit, Kenya
description: On January 13, armed gunmen from Dasenaach ethnic militia clash with a Gabra ethnic militia over a grazing zone and watering point in Sibiloi National Park in Madho Dimtu village, Marsabit, Kenya. One person is killed and two others injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7810248

title: Palestinians destroy water pipes that provide water to Israeli settlements near Nablus in the West Bank
description: On July 5, Palestinians destroy water pipes that provide water to Esh Kodesh and Migdalim settlements near Qusra, Nablus, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8375870

title: Protest over lack of irrigation water in Azerbaijan leads to at least one injury
description: On September 28, 2021, residents of Nabatkend, Ortamugan and Kolpu villages of Saatly region of Azerbaijan protest the lack of irrigation water and control of water by "Baku oligarchs." Police intervene and injure a protester who was transported to the hospital.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8581293

title: Protesters demanding improvements in water, sewage, and electrical services in Najaf, Iraq are attacked, injuring at least one
description: On July 31, dozens of people protest to demand improvements in basic services such as water, sewage, and electricity in Najaf city, Iraq. Unknown militants attacked the protesters with knives, injuring at least one protester.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8459077

title: Protests in Araucania and Biobio, Chile over water rights and hydro plant spark clashes, equipment destruction, and arrests
description: In November 2021, demonstrations in the Araucania and Biobio regions of Chile over water rights, a local hydroelectric power plant, and other water concerns lead to conflicts with local police, destruction of equipment from the Rural Drinking Water Project, shootings, and arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8627617, 8604869

title: Protests in Cangandala, Angola for improved water and electricity supply leads to clashes with police and injuries
description: On September 25, 2021, protests in Cangandala (Cangandala, Malanje, Angola) to demand water and electricity are met with violence. Three injuries and eight arrests are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8586839

title: Report that Ethiopian National Defense Forces conducted an airstrike against the Tekeze Dam
description: On November 30, the Ethiopian National Defense Force conduct an airstrike in the Tekeze area targeting Tigray People's Liberation Front forces, in Asgede, Tigray, Ethiopia. The TPLF claim the government attacked Tekeze dam; the government deny the accusation and warn members of TPLF not to release the water from the dam. Casualties due to the airstrike are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8696304

title: Report that Hamas turns water pipes into homemade rockets to attack Israel
description: A representative of Islamic Jihad boasts that his group improvises weapons from everyday materials, including water pipes, to make rockets to attack Israel.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2021

title: Residents in Kerman, Iran clash with police over wells drilled on their lands to transfer water to other regions
description: On December 25, residents demonstrate in Shamsabad village (Kerman), Iran in protest over wells being drilled on their lands to transfer water elsewhere. Police clash with the protesters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8734377

title: Residents in Lumas, Albania protest against the use of a local water source, leading to at least one severe injury
description: On May 21, locals protest in Lumas, Albania against the use of a water source for municipal purposes. The police use force when residents block the road severely injuring one protester.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8005374

title: Residents in Senegal protesting bad water quality refuse to pay their bills and beat up water company representatives sent to cu
description: On March 22, residents beat up representatives of the Sen'Eau national water distribution company in Mbacke, Diourbel, Senegal as they try to suspend the distribution of water to residents who had not paid their bills in protest of bad water quality.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8011591

title: Russian warplanes destroy an agricultural water pumping station near Idlib, Syria
description: On July 3, Russian warplanes launch airstrikes on the water pumping station in al Rouj area in Idlib, destroying the station that served over 3500 hectares of farmland. No fatalities or injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8380745

title: Sabotage of water infrastructure by the "water mafia" is reported in Kwa-Zulu Natal, South Africa
description: Acts of sabotage and vandalism on water infrastructure are reported in 2021 in Kwa-Zulu Natal, South Africa so that water tanker contracts can be signed in growing corruption in South Africa's water system.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Jacobs 2024 ; Water Integrity Network/Corruption Watch 2020

title: Sabotage to water infrastructure occurs in Hasawna, Libya
description: Around July 13, an unidentified armed group carries out acts of sabotage to damage water infrastructure in Hasawna (Wadi Ashshati, South), Libya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8385887

title: Saudi-led air raids target the Rural Electricity and Water Authority in Aththaorah district, Yemen
description: On October 21, Saudi-led coalition air raids targeted Aththaorah district, Yemen, striking the Rural Electricity and Water Authority. The Saudi-led coalition claims to have struck Houthi sites used for launching drones and ballistic missiles in Sanaa.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8611555

title: Saudi-led air raids target the Water and Rural Corporation in Yemen
description: On December 9, Saudi-led coalition air raids again target the Water and Rural Corporation in Aththaorah district, Yemen, damaging civilian property. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8687755

title: Shelling by rebel forces in Donetsk, Ukraine cause blackouts and one village to loose water supply
description: On August 11, the NAF rebel forces fire mortars at the governmental positions near Novomykhaylivka, Donetsk, Ukraine. As a result of the shelling, one Ukrainian soldier is injured, and the territory of the farm and the power transmission line are damaged, causing blackouts of settlements and leaving Novomykhaylivka village without water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8471752

title: Six are injured during a protest in Peru demanding improved potable water and sewage services
description: On January 11, in Tumbes, Peru, citizens of Cerro Blanco block a highway to demand improvement of the potable water service and sewage system. Police forces intervene and six citizens are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7497018

title: Spokesperson for organization opposed to La Parota Dam in Mexico is kidnapped and never found
description: An activist and spokesperson for the Consejo de Ejidos y Comunidades Opositoras a la Presa La Parota (The Council of Ejidos and Community Opposing the Parota Dam), Vicente Iván Suástegui Muñoz, is kidnapped while driving his taxi cab in Acapulco, Mexico in 2021. Sr. Muñoz had been defending land and water since 2003. His brother, Marco Antonio Suástegui Muñoz, is murdered in 2025 after a multi-year effort to bring justice to his brother's disapperance. The Parota Dam would affect 24 rural communities and displace approximately 25,000 people in the Mexican state of Guerrero.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Wikipedia contributors 2025a

title: Taliban attack a dam in Afghanistan
description: The Salma hydroelectric dam is attacked by Taliban rockets. The dam, in western Heart province, is one of the largest in Afghanistan and provides irrigation water and electricity. The dam was completed in 2016 with the assistance of India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lalzoy 2021 ; Opinion Express 2021

title: The main water pipeline diverting water from Isfahan to Yazd, Iran is destroyed by farmers and residents
description: Around July 31, farmers and residents destroy the main water pipeline from Isfahan to Yazd around Isfahan, Iran.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8426482

title: The water supply for a factory is destroyed by opponents of the government regime in Myanmar
description: On December 11, in Myaing township, Magway, Myanmar, members of the People's Revolutionary Army burn down and destroy water supply for a local factory. Locals said the military controlled the factory and soldiers were working there.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8758925

title: Two communities in Ciudad de Mexico clash over water infrastructure, with several injuries reported
description: On July 20, in Ciudad de Mexico - Xochimilco, residents from two mountain communities clash with each other over a water project in San Mateo Xalpa. The confrontation was between supporters and opponents of the water work in the Cola de Conejo tank. Several people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8393753

title: Two killed in protests over water shortages in Iran
description: Two men are killed during growing public protests over water shortages in Khuzestan province in southwest Iran. The shortages are occurring during the worst drought in 50 years, with protests in several cities and towns over residential and agricultural water cuts and power blackouts.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al Jazeera 2021a ; British Broadcasting Corporation 2021b

title: Two men are killed, three injured in a clash over irrigation water rotation in Pakistan
description: On April 29, a clash takes place between the Mangrio and Nohani communities over the rotation of water. Shots are fired, killing two men and injuring three others in Tando Allahyar city, Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7933859

title: Unknown assailants attack an Iraqi security force during release of irrigation water from the Sabla River
description: On December 6, unknown militants attack a security force in Rifai district of Thi Qar province, Iraq. The attack takes place while the Iraqi force is providing security during the release of irrigation water from the Sabla river.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8685837

title: Villagers in Mexico fight over access to water supplies, with injuries and arrests
description: On January 13, in Huejutla de Reyes municipality, Hidalgo, a clash between the communities of Coxhuaco II and Xiquila over access to water leads to injuries and arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7618375

title: Violence breaks out again between Choa Arab ranchers and Musgum fishers and farmers over access to water in northern Cameroon
description: Clashes break out in northern Cameroon between Choa Arab and Musgum groups following a dispute over dwindling water resources in the Logone River, a tributary to Lake Chad. The violence then spread to neighboring villages, leaving 10 villages burned to the ground.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; United Nations News 2021

title: Violence over access to water leads to one death and two injuries in Cameroon
description: On May 18, villagers fight in Waza village (Logone-et-Chari, Extreme-Nord), Cameroon over access to a water point. One person is killed, and two others injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8010460

title: Violent clash over access to water in Lebanon leaves at least one injured
description: On January 18, Msheik and Hjula clans clashed over access to water using guns and RPGs in Hai el Lailaki, Baabda, Lebanon. At least one injury is reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 7918867

title: While in search of pasture and water, militias clash with police at Laikipia Nature Conservancy, Kenya, killing at least one
description: On July 31, militias clash with police at the Laikipia Nature Conservancy in Wangwaci village in Ol-Moran town, Laikipia, Kenya. One officer is killed. The militias invade several ranches in the conservancy in search of pasture and water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8460925, 8460922

title: 106 towns in the Kherson region of Ukraine are left without water after Russian attacks on energy and water infrastructure
description: 106 towns in the Kherson region of Ukraine are left without water services in April 2022 after Russian attacks on energy and water systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023

title: A Colombian water and sewerage company is bombed
description: In Saravena, Arauca, Colombia, members of the FARC group bomb the local water, sewage, and sanitation communal company of the municipality.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. COL9608

title: A caste dispute in India over irrigation water leaves two injured
description: In a caste dispute in UP, India, an upper caste mob beat up a Dalit group and attempt to strip a Dalit woman, in a clash over watering their fields. Two injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND115654

title: A clash over the distribution of drinking water injures six in Chattradev, Nepal
description: A clash over the distribution of drinking water injures six in Chattradev, Nepal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. NEP18865

title: A farmer is killed and two others injured in a clash at Satpakia, Bangladesh, following an altercation over allocation of water
description: Rivals groups clash at Satpakia village, Bangladesh, following an altercation over giving water to rice fields. A farmer is killed and two others are injured in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BGD23118

title: A political demonstration in Brazil turns violent and demonstrators break water pipes and damage the water and sanitation system
description: On November 18, 2022, in Ariquemes (Rondonia), Bolsonaro supporters protesting the result of the October 30th damage the city's water and sanitation system by breaking water pipes, causing a shortage in water supply in six neighborhoods.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BRA61203

title: A protest over bottled water company exploitation of groundwater is broken up by Mexican police and national guard
description: State police forces and national guard disperse protesters in Cholula de Rivadavia, Puebla, Mexico, who had been occupying the facilities of the Bonafont water bottling company since March 22, 2021. The protesters denounced the overexploitation of the aqifers, leaving neighboring towns without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX56613

title: A violent demonstration over the lack of access to drinking water in Beni Ayat, Morocco leads to injuries
description: A group of demonstrators attack and injure journalists covering a protest in Morocco over access to drinking water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MOR5500

title: A water tanker is attacked by Al Shabaab militants in Somalia killing ten and injuring 15
description: On January 1, Al Shabaab militants detonate a remote-controlled IED, targeting an Ethiopia forces water tanker near Feerfeer village, Somalia. Al Shabaab claims ten soldiers are killed and 15 others injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8705165

title: A water tanker is destroyed and four soldiers are injured in Al Shabaab attack in Somalia
description: Al Shabaab militants target government security forces convoy with a water tanker, injuring four and destroying the water tanker in Afgooye, Somalia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM37537

title: A water-supply facility is destroyed during a protest in India over access to healthcare for prisoners
description: CPI-Maoist cadres attack construction workers and destroy a water supply transformer in Giridih city, India during a call for healthcare facilities for prisoners.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND105473

title: A water-supply station in Syria is attacked by Turkey
description: Turkish forces shell the water station of Al Hishah in Ar Raqqa governorate, Syria, rendering it inoperable.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR98396

title: Activists protest in Angola against the lack of water
description: Activists protest in Lobito, Angola, against the lack of water in the city. Police arrest seven activists and reportedly beat them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. ANG3639

title: Airstrike hits water tanks in Saada, Yemen
description: On November 1, an airstrike hits water tanks in Sa'ada District, Saada, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Yemen Data Project ND

title: Al Shabaab bombs a water source borehole near Belet Weyne, Hiraan, Somalia
description: Al Shabaab detonates an improvised explosive device at a water source borehole and destroys houses from the Hawadle clan near Belet Weyne, Hiraan, Somalia. Al Shabaab was targeting clans supporting government operations in the region.
