source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM38197

title: Al Shabaab destroys houses and water wells in near Maxaas, Somalia
description: Al Shabaab destroys houses and water borehole in Ceel-Jiqoow village near Maxaas town, Bulo Burto, Somalia
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM38027

title: Al Shabaab explosive attack kills eight African Union Transition Mission peacekeepers and destroys water tanker in Somalia
description: An improvised explosive device planted by Al Shabaab is used to attack a convoy of the African Union Transition Mission peacekeepers in Somalia, killing eight soldiers and destroying a water tanker.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM38688

title: Al Shabaab militants destroy water pumps in Hanan, Galgaduud, Somalia
description: Al Shabaab militants set several houses on fire and destroy water pumps in Hanan village, Cadaado, Galgaduud, Somalia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM37607

title: Al Shabaab militants detonate an improvised explosive device at a water source borehole in Somalia
description: Al Shabaab militants detonate an improvised explosive device at a water source borehole and destroy houses of civilians near Maarsomage and Qaayib, Galgaduud, Somalia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM37669, SOM37672

title: An attack on a water truck in Burkina Faso was accompanied by a threat to attack all water systems
description: Gunmen set fire to a water truck in the Centre-North region of Burkina Faso. Assailants made it clear they did not want to see water trucks on that road again. All water trucking activities, currently the only way to provide emergency water assistance to the residents, were halted, according to the Norwegian Refugee Council.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; News24 2022

title: An attack partly destroys three spillways and the roadway on the Kakhovka Dam on the Dnipro River
description: An attack in November 2022 partly destroys three spillways and the roadway on the Kakhovka Dam on the Dnipro River, leading to a decrease in water levels in the Kakhovske Reservoir, threatening water supply in regional cities, reducing water available for the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, and hindering Ukrainian advances across the river.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick et al. 2023 ; Shevchuk and Vyshnevskyi 2022

title: An attempt to cut off the power supply of a water well in Morelos, Mexico, is met by violence
description: Residents in Chamilpa, Morelos, Mexico, seize a van from the Federal Electricity Commission after employees try to cut off the power supply of their water well. The residents also held the workers from the state-owned company and threatened to set the unit on fire.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX56127

title: An attempt to divert water on the Mahakali River at the Nepal-Indian border is met with violence extending over several weeks
description: An attempt to divert water on the Mahakali River at the Nepal-Indian border because of construction is met with violence in Khalanga town, Darchula district, Nepal. The dispute extends over several weeks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. NEP14812, NEP10091

title: An explosion at a water pandal in Myanmar injures two
description: In Hlaingtharya township, Yangon, Myanmar, an explosion at a water pandal injures two.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR32899

title: An explosive planted at a Syrian water tank kills one and destroys the tank
description: An explosive planted by an unknown group explodes at a Syrian state water tank in Al Baghala, Homs, destroying it and killing one soldier.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR99003

title: Armed group in Chiapas, Mexico, kills two men reportedly trying to poison a water well in an ongoing land conflict
description: A Santa Martha community armed group near Atzamilho, Chiapas, Mexico, shoot and kill two men reportedly trying to poison a water well. The attack is related to an ongoing land conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX66055

title: Armed rebel group in Indonesia damages water-supply system for a military post
description: The TPNPB, the armed wing of the Free Papua Organization, damage the water pipes of the Indonesian military forces post in Jenggernok, Papua province, Indonesia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IDN7770

title: Around 100 farmers in Tacna, Peru clash over ownership of a water well in the sector
description: Around 100 farmers of the Huerto de Olivos Fronteras Vivas association, Tacna, Peru, clash over ownership of a water well in the sector.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PER5220

title: At least one death and multiple injuries reported in ongoing clashes in Sanaa, Yemen, over control of a water source
description: In extended clashes, Bani Buays and Bani Habar tribesmen fight in Bani Ahkam, Sanaa, Yemen, over the control of a water source, killing at least one and injuring four.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM74752, YEM74753

title: Attack on a water well during dispute in Somalia beween Al Shabaab and Hawadle clan
description: Al Shabaab militants burn and destroy houses, including destroying a water borehole in a dispute between Al Shabaab and the Hawadle clan, Bulo Burto, Somalia. About 60 household are displaced.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM37492

title: Attack on energy system providing water for five villages in Morocco
description: An unidentified group destroys power generators used to pump water for five villages and a school in Toumliline, Sidi Ifni, Guelmim-Oued Noun, Morocco.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MOR6279

title: Attack on water pumping station in Dori, Burkina Faso, disrupts local water supply and kills four
description: Presumed Islamic State Sahel militants attack a police position at the water pumping station in Yakouta, Seno, Burkina Faso. Four policemen are reported killed, two wounded, and two missing and the water supply to the town of Dori is disrupted.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO7476

title: Attack on water pumps and systems in Burkina Faso, with seven reported deaths
description: Ongoing violence between presumed Jama'at Nusrat al Islam wal Muslimin militants and volunteer fighters in Burkina Faso, with extensive sabotage of water systems. On March 14, at least seven people are reported killed in Arbinda, with violence also in the town of Djibo.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO6755, BFO6811

title: Attack on water systems of the Great Man-Made River in Libya
description: An unidentified armed group destroys infrastructure at four different stations belonging to the Man-Made River in Wadi al Washkah, Libya, causing significant water loss.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. LBY11094

title: Attacks leave 40 towns in the Mykolaiv region without water services
description: In May, attacks leave 40 towns in the Mykolaiv region of Ukraine without water services; 30 water-supply systems are damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023

title: Attacks on Kremenchuk and Dnipro dams in Ukraine in October 2022
description: Russian missile attacks (in October 2022) are aimed at the Dnipro Hydroelectric Power Station in Zaporizhzhia, Dniester Pumped Storage Power Station in Chernivtsi Oblast, and Kremenchuk Hydroelectric Power Plant in Svitlovodsk in Kirovohrad Oblast. [The Dnipro hydroelectric plant near Zaporizhzhia is attacked in December 2022 and again in February 2023.]
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Wilk and Zochowski 2022 ; Harding et al. 2022 ; BBC News 2023

title: Bomb blast in Myanmar at drinking water tank
description: Bomb blast in Pyapon, Ayeyarwady, Myanmar at drinking water tank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR32209

title: Bomb planted by unknown armed group explodes at water station in Dara, Syria
description: A bomb planted by an unknown armed group explodes in a water station near Kharab Shahem town in Dara, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR109439

title: Cameroon separatists ambush a convoy of water trucks, killing one soldier
description: Ambazonian separatists ambush a military convoy with explosive and engage in a firefight with the soldiers in Cameroon, killing one soldier and destroying two trucks from the national water production company, Source du Pays.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. CAO5831

title: Chernihiv loses centralized water due to attacks on infrastructure
description: Chernihiv is left without centralized water supply due to attacks on electrical and water service systems (April).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023

title: Clan dispute over access to water and land leads to three deaths in Somalia
description: Ogaden-Mohamed Zubeyr Clan militia clashes with Marehan clan militia near Dif, Lower Juba, Somalia, in a dispute over access to water resources and grazing land. Three people and several animals are killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM36987

title: Clash between two groups in Karachi City, Pakistan, over government efforts to stop illegal water connections, injures six
description: A clash takes place between two groups when the Karachi Water and Sewerage Board takes action against illegal water connections in Karachi City, Pakistan. Six people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK76903

title: Clash in Madhya Pradesh, India over communal water resources
description: Two groups of villagers clash in Nowgong, Madhya Pradesh, India, over communal water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND107585

title: Clash on the Afghanistan-Pakistan border injures at least two after Pakistani forces allegedly attempt to divert floodwaters to
description: At least two are injured in an armed clash between Taliban and Pakistan security forces on Spin Boldak-Chaman border, Kandahar, Afghanistan. The clash starts after Pakistani forces allegedly attempt to divert floodwaters towards Afghanistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. AFG64722

title: Clash over land and water injures five in West Bengal, India
description: Two groups clash over land and water issues in Kumarsanda, Murshidabad district, West Bengal, India, injuring five.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND116979

title: Clashes erupt between unknown gunmen and Syrian Democratic Forces after attack on Zir water facility in Deir ez Zor, Syria
description: Clashes take place between unknown gunmen believed to Islamic State members and Syrian Democratic Forces after a water facility in Zir, Deir ez Zor, Syria is attacked.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR107078

title: Community members in Johannesburg, South Africa threaten contractors, fire shots, demand illegal water connections
description: Community members threaten Joburg Water contractors and fire gunshots in Johannesburg, South Africa, demanding permission for illegal water connections.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF18108

title: Conflict over mining and water pollution in Guyana has led to threats and violence against local villagers
description: Threats and violence are reported in conflicts between villagers and miners over illegal gold mining in indigenous communities in Guyana that is contaminating local waters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Papannah and Sutherland 2022

title: Conflict over use of government-controlled water pipeline in India leads to violence
description: Three rioters assault a female Sarpanch, head of the Panchayat, and her family members in Gunga village, Madhya Pradesh, India, after she warned the rioters for misusing a government water pipeline.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND106862

title: Continuing attacks in Kharkiv cut off water supply for major sections of the city
description: In May, continuing Russian attacks in Kharkiv, Ukraine cut off water supply for major sections of the city. More than forty multi-story buildings in Kharkiv are left without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023

title: Deaths and injuries during a clash in Sudan over a water project on the Atbara River
description: Two unspecified clan militias clash in El Birma area, Aroma, Sudan, over a water project on the Atbara River. Two people are killed and seven others injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SUD16891

title: Deaths and injuries reported in fight between Garre and Degodia clans over water and pasture lands in Banissa, Kenya
description: Nine are reported killed and several injured in a fight between Garre and Degodia clans over water and pasture lands in Banissa, Kenya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KEN9774

title: Demonstrations and vandalism of a major water tunnel project in Nepal over concern about local water supplies
description: Local demonstrations against the Dahchok-Sisnekhola Tunnel project in Chandragiri, Nepal, over concern it has dried up the local drinking water include vandalization of the offices of the Nagdhunga Tunnel Project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. NEP14922

title: Destruction of the sewage treatment plant in Vasylivka leads to contamination in the Kakhovske reservoir
description: The Russian destruction of the sewage treatment plant in March 2022 at the town of Vasylivka in Zaporizhzhia oblast leads to sewage contamination of the Kakhovske Reservoir.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick et al. 2023 ; Shevchuk et al. 2022 ; Interfax Ukraine 2022

title: Dispute over irrigation water leads to 10 injuries in Bangladesh
description: At least 10 people are injured in a clash between two groups from villages of Kaishalarbagh and Bagabaria in Sonaimuri upazila, Noakhali, Bangladesh over canal water dispute.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BGD21766

title: Egyptian hackers attack the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam in an effort to trigger downstream flooding and power failures
description: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile is attacked in February 2022 by Egyptian hackers with the motto “Black Pyramid War” in an effort to trigger downstream flooding and power failures.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Goud 2022

title: Environmental defender and local leader of opposition to dam projects on the Rio Verde is found dead in Oaxaca, Mexico
description: The environmental defender and local leader of the Consejo de Pueblos Unidos por la Defensa del Rio Verde, Filogonio Martínez Merino, is found dead in Santiago Jamiltepec in the Mexican state of Oaxaca. He had been part of the local resistence to two dam projects on the Rio Verde.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; CIVICUS Monitor n.d.

title: Environmental water defender Yuli Velasquez attacked by gunmen in Colombia
description: Environmental water defender Yuli Velasquez, president of Fedepesan [the Federation of Santander Fishers for Tourism and Environment], is attacked by gunmen in Colombia in 2022; her bodyguard is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Patterson 2022

title: Extensive French protests and sabotage of water basin in a protest against agricultural and industrial water use during drought
description: During March 2022, numerous groups, including the 'Executive Committee of Regional Water Protection,' the collective 'Stop Bassines,' and the Peasant Confederation protest the creation of water basins for industrial agricultural irrigation. Various protests, including between 5000 and 7000 people near the end of March, sabotage water basins and damage pump stations in Nouaille-Maupertuis and La Rochenard, France. Gendarmerie forces use tear gas to disperse a group of demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. FRA16071, FRA16070, FRA16603

title: Farmers vandalize and burn Champadevi hydropower office in Nepal over water diversion
description: Farmers vandalize and burn the office of the Champadevi hydropower project in Siranchok, Nepal, to protest the diversion of their irrigation water towards the hydropower project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. NEP21122

title: Fighting between Bani Fadol and Bani Badr militias over a water station in West Kordofan, Sudan leaves two dead and 13 injured
description: Fighting breaks out between Bani Fadol militia and Bani Badr militia in multiple locations in West Kordofan, Sudan, following a dispute over a water station. Two are killed, and 13 people are wounded across two days.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SUD18570, SUD18571

title: Gates on the dam at the Mironovsky reservoir are damaged, causing downstream flooding on the Luhan River
description: Russia accuses the Ukrainian armed forces of destroying the gates on the dam in May 2022 at the Mironovsky reservoir near Svitlodarsk to slow the Russian advance across the Luhan River toward Svitlodarsk in the Bakhmut Region of Donetsk Oblast.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kadam 2022 ; Izvestia 2022

title: Gates on the dam on the Oskil reservoir are destroyed, causing flooding in Svyatogorsk, Ukraine
description: In April 2022, gates of the dam on the Oskil reservoir in the Kharkiv area are destroyed, releasing water from the reservoir and causing the level of the Siverskyi Donets River to rise, flooding Svyatogorsk. The reservoir provided water for the Donbas region.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kolodezhna and Vasyliuk 2022 ; Petrenko 2022

title: Grenade blast in water tank leaves 40 families without water in Potrerito, Valle del Cauca, Colombia
description: Three unidentified individuals detonate a grenade in a water tank in Potrerito, Valle del Cauca, Colombia, leaving around 40 families without drinking water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. COL18785

title: Herder-pastoralist violence over access to water in Kenya kills one and injures others
description: Suspected Pokot pastoralist militias attack herders watering animals at the Arabal river, Baringo county, Kenya. One person is killed; two others injured, and close to 40 cattle stolen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KEN8106

title: Houthi fighter kills civilian in Yemen in a water project dispute
description: A Houthi fighter shoots and kills one civilian in Razih district, Sadah, Yemen, over benefits from a water project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM77165

title: Houthi forces attack water infrastructure in Yemen
description: Houthi forces in Yemen target water infrastructure in Al Haymah, Al Hudaydah, Yemen damaging it.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM71958

title: Houthi forces attack water supply and desalination infrastructure in a series of missile attacks on Saudi Arabia
description: In a series of attacks, Houthi forces fire cruise missiles at Saudi Arabia's Ash Shuqayq Water Desalination Plant, Ad Darb, Jizan, and at the National Water Company in Dhahran Al Janub, causing damages to both facilities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAU23182, SAU23191

title: Houthi forces fire upon residents in Yemen, injuring three women and two children in a dispute over water wells and land
description: Houthi security forces fire upon residents of Iyal Husayn, Arhab, Sanaa, Yemen, injuring three women and two children in a dispute over water wells and agricultural land.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM75962

title: Houthi forces kill two farmers and injure three in water well dispute in Al Hudaydah, Yemen
description: Houthi forces shoot and kill at least two farmers and injure three others in Bani Ubaqah in Bajil district, Al Hudaydah, Yemen when Houthi forces attempt to seize civilian lands and dig a water well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM77714

title: In January 2022, the Taliban cut flows of water to Iran and the Hamoun wetlands from the Helmand River
description: in January 2022, the Taliban divert the Helmand River south, cutting the flow of water to Iran and the Hamoun wetlands.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Iran International 2022

title: In a dispute over digging a water well, Houthi forces and local residents exchange gunfire in Yemen
description: Houthi forces and local residents exchange fire in Bayt al Yazidi, Damt, Ad Dali, Yemen, after Houthi forces raid over a disagreement on digging a water well. No fatalities or injuries but Houthi forces kidnap eight residents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM76032

title: Injuries are reported in a demonstration in South Africa over water shortages
description: Residents of several farms and townships in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, set tires on fire and block the entrances to Umzinto in a demonstration against water shortages in the region. During the demonstration, a private security officer opens fire and injures three people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF16158

title: Islamic State Sahel militants kill 30 civilians in Talataye, Mali, and destroy homes, markets, and water wells
description: Islamic State Sahel militants kill at least thirty civilians from the Dawsahak, Tuareg, Djerma, and Songhai communities in Talataye, Mali, and destroy houses, markets, water wells, and more.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MLI7156

title: Israeli forces and settlers raze Palestinian land, uproot olive trees for Ariel Settlement water networks
description: Israeli military forces and settlers raze Palestinian-owned land and uproot 50 olive trees near Zawiya village, Salfit, West Bank, to set up water networks for the Ariel settlement (September).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16476

title: Israeli forces demolish a Palestinian-owned water well and olive trees near Hebron in the West Bank
description: On 13 February 2022, Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned water well, and uproot olive trees in Bayt Ummar, Hebron, West Bank, under the pretext that they were located near Israeli settlements.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE14007

title: Israeli forces destroy water pump in Nablus, West Bank, cutting water supply to over 20,000 Palestinians in multiple villages
description: Israeli military forces destroy a central water pump that supplies water to several villages, including Burin, Madama, Asirah, and Urif, Nablus, West Bank, cutting water supply to more than 20,000 Palestinians (October).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE17073

title: Israeli forces raze Palestinian street to construct a water line to serve Israeli settlements near Zawiya, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces raze part of a Palestinian-owned street near Zawiya, Salfit, West Bank, to construct a water line serving Israeli settlements.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE29987

title: Israeli military and settlers destroy Palestinian water systems in Birin, Hebron in the West Bank
description: Israeli military forces and Israeli settlers destroy a water network and water tanks and confiscated water pumps and electrical cables belonging to a Palestinian in Birin village, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE14239

title: Israeli military demolish Palestinian agricultural facilities in the West Bank, Palestine, including a water tank
description: On January 4, 2022, Israeli military forces demolish Palestinian-owned agricultural facilities in Ibziq, West Bank, including a water tank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8697398

title: Israeli military demolishes Palestinian house and water well in Hebron, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces demolish a Palesinian house under construction and a water well in Farsh al Hawa, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE18153

title: Israeli military demolishes Palestinian-owned agricultural facilities, including water well, near Hebron in West Bank
description: Israeli military forces demolish Palestinian-owned agricultural facilities, including a water well, in Al Frihat area near Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE17451

title: Israeli military demolishes water well, shop, and fence in Qalqas Village, Hebron, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces demolish a water well, a shop selling car parts, and a fence at the junction of Qalqas village, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE18399

title: Israeli military destroy Palestinian water pipelines and uproot palm and citrus trees near Jericho, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces uproot 166 palm and citrus trees, destroy water pipelines, and confiscate fences belonging to Palestinian farmers in Awsaj, north of Jericho, West Bank (August).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16254

title: Israeli military destroy structures, including water well, near Hebron, Palestine
description: Israeli military forces demolish structures, including a water well belonging to Palestinians, northeast of Hebron city, West Bank, under the pretext of not having a building permit.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE15332

title: Israeli military destroy the water well used for water supply in Bayt Lid, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces destroy a Palestinian-owned water well used for the entire town of Bayt Lid, Tulkarm, West Bank, and backfilled it with rocks and concrete.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE15403

title: Israeli military destroy water supply line in the West Bank
description: Israeli military forces raze Palestinian-owned lands and destroy a water supply line in Kafr Qaddum on the West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE13629

title: Israeli military destroys Palestinian water tank near Jericho, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces destroy a Palestinian-owned water tank used to water agricultural lands in Marj Naajah village, Jericho, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE14963

title: Israeli military destroys Palestinian water well in Ras Atiya, West Bank, and block farmers from using the water
description: Israeli military forces destroy a Palestinian-owned water well in Ras Atiya, West Bank, and block farmers from using the water for agricultural purposes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE15294

title: Israeli military destroys two Palestinian water wells in West Bank
description: Israeli military forces destroy two Palestinian-owned water wells in Al Ras, West Bank, by filling them with concrete.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16463

title: Israeli military destroys water pipes at the spring in Duma Village, Nablus, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces destroy Palestinian-owned equipment, including water pipes and barbed wire, at the water spring of Duma village, Nablus, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE15693 ; Middle East Monitor 2022

title: Israeli military forces and settlers destroy Palestinian water wells near Hebron and Nablus in the West Bank
description: Israeli military forces demolish and raze four Palestinian-owned water wells near in Khallet ed Dabaa, Hebron, West Bank on February 2nd, in order to construct settlement projects in the area. Two days later, Israeli settlers destroy a water well in Qaryut village, Nablus, West Bank, and pollute the well with chemicals.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE13815

title: Israeli military forces demolish Palestinian-owned agricultural facilities in Al Khadir, West Bank, including a water well
description: Israeli military forces demolish Palestinian-owned agricultural facilities in Al Khadir, Bethlehem, West Bank, including a water well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16174

title: Israeli military forces demolish a water well and house in Khallat al Mayyah in the West Bank to forcibly evict Palestinians
description: On 15 February 2022, Israeli military forces demolish a water well and a house in Khallat al Mayyah village, Hebron, West Bank, to evict the Palestinian residents from the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE14027

title: Israeli military forces destroy Palestinian water systems and land near Salfit and Tubas in the West Bank
description: On 10 February 2022, Israeli military forces raze Palestinian-owned lands in Sarta village, Salfit, West Bank, to construct a water supply pipeline for a nearby settlement. They also destroy retaining walls and uproot more than 160 trees. That same day Israeli military vehicles and tanks destroy a Palestinian-owned water network, agricultural roads, and crops during their military exercise in Jordan Valley near Bardalah, Tubas, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE13874

title: Israeli military forces destroy a Palestinian agricultural water distribution network in al-Awsaj, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces destroy a water distribution network and fence on Palestinian agricultural land in al-Awsaj village, north of Jericho city, West Bank (September).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16457

title: Israeli military forces destroy a Palestinian water well and grape trees in Al Khadir, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces destroy a water well and uproot 55 grape trees belonging to Palestinian farmers in Al Khadir village, Bethlehem, West Bank (August).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16257

title: Israeli military forces destroy a Palestinian water well and olive trees near Bethlehem in the West Bank
description: Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned water well and uproot 20 olive trees belonging to a Palestinian in Tuqu village, Bethlehem, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE15905

title: Israeli settlers and soldiers destroy water wells, tanks, and agricultural facilities in West Bank villages; clashes ensue
description: In mid- to late-June 2022, Israeli settlers and soldiers destroy a water well in Qaryut village, Nablus, West Bank, fill another well with stones near Yabad, Jenin, demolish a pond used to water grapes in Bir Zayt, water tanks and agricultural facilities in Al Quds-AzZaayyim village, and destroy a water network, trees, and agricultural facilities in Ibziq. Clashes erupt between the soldiers and Palestinians. Several Palestinians suffered from tear gas inhalation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE15594, PSE15606, PSE15612, PSE15611, PSE15621, PSE15518

title: Israeli settlers break into a water well in Qaryut, Palestine, and clash with local residents
description: Israeli settlers under the protection of Israeli soldiers break into a water well in Qaryut village, Nablus, West Bank, and clash with Palestinian who confronted them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE15085

title: Israeli settlers damage water well in West Bank; injure several, sparking protests with 50 more injured
description: Israeli settlers under the protection of Israeli soldiers break into a water well in Qaryut village, Nablus, West Bank in late April and early May, and damaging the well and polluting the water with unknown materials. Three days later Israeli settlers, under the protection of Israeli military forces, physically assault Palestinians at a water well in the same area injuring several, including a 14-year-old child who sustained fractures, followed by a major Palestinian protest where 50 more are injured by the Israeli military.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE14813, PSE14833, PSE14935, PSE14590

title: Israeli settlers demolish Palestinian agricultural water well in Dura and damage water networks in Dayr Istiya, West Bank
description: A group of Israeli settlers demolish a Palestinian-owned agricultural water well in Dura town, Hebron, West Bank, and water and sewage networks in Dayr Istiya village, Salfit, West Bank in July 2022.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE29770, PSE29769

title: Israeli settlers demolish Palestinian-owned facilities, including water tanks in West Bank, to advance settlement projects
description: Israeli settlers demolish Palestinian-owned facilities, including solar cells and water tanks in Al Farsiyah, Tubas, West Bank, in an attempt to advance settlement projects (October).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16887

title: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian water network, vandalize pond, and loot water pump in Bayt Dajan, Nablus, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers destroy a Palestinian-owned water supply network and vandalize a pond, both used for farming east of Bayt Dajan, Nablus, West Bank. Also, settlers loot a water pump from the land (September).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16183

title: Israeli settlers destroy solar cell units and damage water tanks belonging to Palestinian farmers in Al Farsiyah, West Bank
description: A group of Israeli settlers destroy solar cell units and damage water tanks belonging to Palestinian farmers in Al Farsiyah, Tubas, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE17154

title: Israeli settlers destroy water network irrigating Palestinian agricultural lands near Tubas, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers destroy a water network distributing water to more than 300 dunams of Palestinian agricultural lands in Al Farsiyah, Tubas, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16080

title: Israeli settlers flood Palestinian lands near Hebron, West Bank, with sewage
description: Israeli settlers release sewage water onto Palestinian agricultural lands in Bayt Ummar, Hebron, West Bank, damaging a vineyard.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE29995

title: Israeli settlers flood Palestinian lands near Majdulim in the West Bank with sewage and wastewater
description: Israeli settlers from Majdulim settlement, West Bank flood Palestinian-owned lands with sewage and wastewater, causing material damages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE14078

title: Israeli settlers from Eli destroy Palestinian water networks and spring in Nablus Village, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers from Eli destroy Palestinian-owned water networks and a spring in As Sawiyah village, Nablus, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16700

title: Israeli settlers in violence against Palestinian energy, land, and water resources in Salfit, West Bank (April)
description: Israeli settlers break into Palestinian agricultural lands in Dayr Istiya village, Salfit, West Bank, and vandalize solar cells and a water tank in late April 2022.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE26064

title: Israeli settlers seize Palestinian land near Ain As Sakout, West Bank in order to control water wells
description: Israeli settlers seize Palestinian-owned lands near Ain As Sakout, West Bank, to control the water wells in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE15935

title: Israeli settlers vandalize the water supply network in the West Bank, causing water cuts
description: Israeli settlers vandalize the water supply network in Kisan, Bethlehem, West Bank, causing water cuts.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE16272

title: Israeli settlers vandalize water tanks in Birin, Hebron, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers set fire to building supplies and vandalize water tanks belonging to Palestinians in Birin (Hebron, West Bank).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE14527

title: Israeli settlers, under the protection of Israeli soldiers, clash with Palestinians after raiding a water well
description: Israeli settlers, under the protection of Israeli soldiers, clash with Palestinians after raiding the water well of Qaryut village, Nablus, West Bank. Soldiers fire stun grenades and tear gas canisters toward Palestinians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE17616

title: Kyrgyz-Tajik border clash at disputed Golovnoy water facility leaves one Kyrgyz guard dead
description: A firefight between Kyrgyz and Tajik border guards on the disputed perimeter at the Golovnoy water distribution facility in Ak-Sai, Batken, Kyrgyzstan kills one Kyrgyz serviceman.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KGZ1697

title: Large protest in Iraq over lack of irrigation and drinking water is met by police using live ammunication to disperse the demons
description: Hundreds in Maysan, Iraq, protest lack of irrigation and drinking water, demanding better public services. Police uses live ammunition to disperse the demonstration.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IRQ39884

title: Locals in Balochistan protest for rights and clean water; clashes with police leave one officer dead, complex set on fire
description: Locals hold a demonstration in Gwadar city, Balochistan, Pakistan, demanding rights for the people of Gwadar, clean drinking water, and an end to fishing trawlers. The demonstrators besiege the residence of the deputy commissioner and other offices. Police lob tear gas shells and fire shots to disperse the protesters. One policeman is reported killed, and a police complex is set on fire.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK80310, PAK80336

title: Major portions of Kharkiv are left without water by attacks on water and energy systems
description: More then than 100 multi-story buildings in Kharkiv are left without water by Russian attacks on water and energy systems during the Russia-Ukraine war (April 2022).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023

title: Mali militias and the Russian Wagner group attack Mopti, Mali, killing three and sabotaging a water tower
description: Militias from Forces Armées Maliennes, Dan Na Ambassagou, and the Russian paramilitary group Wagner, attack the village of Yalema, Mopti, Mali, killing three and sabotaging a water tower.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MLI6831

title: Many towns in Donetsk, Ukraine are cut off from water supplies during the Russia-Ukraine war
description: 37 towns in the Donetsk are cut off from water supplies; 27 water-supply systems are damaged; 40 percent of the water-supply system in Mariupol is damaged (April).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023

title: Mexican farmer threatened and then murdered for his connection to a hydroelectric project development
description: A farmer, Francisco Vázaquz Domínguez, is threatened and then murdered in Ayala, Morelos, Mexico, for his role as a land owner and connection to Asociación de Usarios del Río Cuautla (ASURCO). ASURCO is a water user association that had been involved in decisions related to hydroelectric power and other water projects. He was threatened by the president of the association before being murdered.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Global Witness 2024 ; Agua Para Todos 2022

title: Militants attack villages in Mali, killing four and destroying water infrastructure
description: On January 3, ISWAP (Greater Sahara) militants attack the villages of Labodji, Doreye, and Oussadia, in Gao, Mali. Four people are killed, houses burned, and a water tank is destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8704892

title: Militants attack water administration building in Turkey
description: Halklar?n Birle?ik Devrim Hareketi militants attack the building of the Turkish state's water administration with improvised explosive devices in Kayapinar, Diyarbakir.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. TUR26795

title: Militants destroy a water pumping station in Burkina Faso, cutting water deliveries in several quarters in the regional capital
description: Presumed Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin militants destroy a water pumping station in the village of Zorkoum, Sanmatenga, Burkina Faso. The sabotage cuts water deliveries in several quarters in the regional capital of Kaya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO8156

title: Militants destroy water company machinery in Burkina Faso
description: Presumed Jama'at Nusrat al Islam wal Muslimin militants destroy national water company machinery in the town of Djibo, Burkina Faso.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO6658

title: Militants destroy water pumps in Burkina Faso
description: Presumed Jama'at Nusrat al Islam wal Muslimin militants destroy three water pumps in the village of Singtanga, Sanmatenga, Burkina Faso.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO6567

title: Militants in Burkina Faso attack government infrastructure, including drinking-water-supply pipes
description: Presumed Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin militants blow up a police station, gendarmerie, the mayor's office, the prefecture, and drinking-water-supply pipes, and burn several trucks in the town of Kouka, Burkina Faso.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO8104

title: Militants in Burkina Faso attack water pumping station in Djibo; soldiers kill two
description: Presumed Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin militants attack a checkpoint and fire gunshots at a water pumping station in the town of Djibo, Burkina Faso. Soldiers responding to the attack kill two militants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO8021

title: Militants in Burkina Faso destroy water systems
description: Presumed Jama'at Nusrat al Islam wal Muslimin militants set off explosives and destroy a water pump and two water towers in the village of Hamkane, Arbinda, Soum, Burkina Faso.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO6497

title: Militants in Mali attack a village, damaging the water tower
description: Militants in Mali attack the village of Tadjalalt, Ansongo, Gao. The militants loot and burned the medical dispensary and damage the water tower. The village is part of the Tuareg Kel Essouk community.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MLI6196

title: Militants in Mali destroy water pumps and rice fields
description: Presumed Jama'a Nusrat ul-Islam wa al-Muslimin militants destroy water pumps and rice fields in Kouna, Mopti, Mali.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MLI6807

title: Militants in Pakistan kill one, injure two soldiers repairing a water-supply line
description: An IED planted by unidentified militants in Bara Banda area, Lower Dir, Pakistan, kills a soldier and injures two more. The blast took place while the soldiers were repairing a water-supply connection from a natural spring.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK77445

title: Military forces clash with rioters in raids to stop water and power network violations in Al Badiya al Wosta, Jordan
description: Military forces clash with rioters during raids into several areas in Al Badiya al Wosta, Jordan, to stop and control violations against water and power networks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. JOR996

title: Myanmar military bombs two villages after water is cut off from a military camp
description: After the blockade of a watercourse used by military forces in Kwi Lon Taing, Myanmar, the military attacks the Kwee Lel Te and Kee Lel Ywar Thit villages of Kyainseikgyi, Kayin.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR33240

title: Myanmar military raids a village and destroys water pumps and other property
description: Myanmar military raids Hput Hlaing village (Sagaing region), destroying motorcycles, solar boards, water pumps, and other valuable items belonging to the villagers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR39640

title: One farmer is killed and another injured in a dispute over access to water in Uttar Pradesh, India
description: The village head/Pradhan in Imlia, Balrampur, Uttar Pradesh, India, shoot two farmers in a dispute over taking water from government tube well, killing one and injuring the other.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND111652

title: One injured in protest over water shortages in Polokwane, South Africa
description: Community members in Polokwane, Limpopo, South Africa protest against water shortages. Demonstrators barricade the N1 with rocks and one person is reported hit by a police vehicle and hospitalized.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF17828

title: One killed in clash in Somalia over water resources
description: Pastoralists from Dhulbahante clan militia clash with Majeerteen-Issa Mahmud militia in Fadhiyar near Garowe, Somalia, in a dispute over water resources. One person is killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM37981

title: One killed; one injured in dispute over access to canal water in Haryana, India
description: A dispute over access to canal water leads to one killed and one injured in Sultanpur village, Haryana, India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND109351

title: One person is killed in India in fight about access to water from a community tap
description: A 45-year-old woman in south Dehli, India is stabbed to death following a fight about filling water from a community tap.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Times of India 2022

title: One person is shot during a clash between two groups of villagers in Nagsosha, Bangladesh, over water-logging
description: One person is shot during a clash between two groups of villagers in Nagsosha, Natore, Rajshahi, Bangladesh, over water-logging issue in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BGD22797

title: Palestinian and Israelis clash in the West Bank after soldiers prevent Palestinians from digging a water well near Jenin
description: Palestinian rioters clash with Israeli military forces during a raid in Dhaher al-Abed, Jenin, West Bank, after soldiers attempted to prevent Palestinians from digging a water well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE14093

title: Palestinian property, including a water well, is destroyed by the Israeli military to build a road
description: Israeli military forces destroy Palestinian-owned properties in Battir, Bethlehem, West Bank, uprooting 370 olive trees, demolishing a retaining wall and water well, and razing Palestinian lands to build a road.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE13509

title: Palestinian property, including water wells, are destroyed by the Israeli military
description: Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned house and two water wells in Mosafer Yuta, Hebron, West Bank, for the benefit of settlement projects.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE13517

title: Palestinians clash with Israeli settlers and soldiers over Qaryut water spring
description: Palestinians clash with Israeli settlers and soldiers who broke into the water spring of Qaryut village, Nablus, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE17114

title: Physical conflict erupts between two clans over control of water resources and water services in Sidon, Lebanon
description: Physical conflict erupts between workers, drivers and owners of two different Water Associations and clans, Al Salim and Al Aafara, in Sidon, Lebanon over control of water resources and client competition.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. LBN14072

title: Police beat and arrest over 20 residents of Hamadan, Iran, protesting ongoing water shortages
description: Residents of Hamadan, Iran, protest an ongoing water shortage. Police attack protesters and make over 20 arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IRN19645

title: Presumed Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin militants sabotage a water pumping station near Tiben, Burkina Faso
description: Presumed Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin militants sabotage a water pumping station near the village of Tiben, Sanmatenga, Burkina Faso.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO8571

title: Protest against long-term water cuts in Democratic Republic of Congo turns violent
description: Mwetu Mwa Kele activists demonstration in Tshikapa, Tshikapa, Kasai, Democratic Republic of Congo, against a two-year water cut. Police disperse the protest using tear gas and firearms, injuring four.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. DRC25294

title: Protest in Guatemala City, Guatemala with blocked roads and a violent confrontation with police over lack of water services
description: People in Guatemala City, Guatemala, block roads to demand reconnection of water services in their communities, protesting they've been ignored by the water company. Violence occurs when police arrive to evict demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. GTM5011

title: Protest in Hamadan, Iran, over water shortages and government mismanagement with at least one injury reported
description: Around 200 residents protest in Hamadan, Iran, over ongoing water shortages, protesting government mismanagement of the situation, and cuts in water supply during severe drought. Police and protesters clash when the police attempt to disperse the gathering. Injuries are reorted.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IRN19661 ; RFE/RL 2022a

title: Pumping stations in Lysychansk are damaged by attacks in the Russia-Ukraine war
description: Water supply to the south part of Lysychansk is cut off after attacks on the water pumping stations “Lisova Dacha”, “GTV,” and “Sumischena.” (April 2022)
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023

title: Pumping stations on the Popasna water pipeline are damaged, cutting water supply to a million people
description: The pumping station and first lift of the Popasna Water Pipeline sustain heavy damage, cutting off water supplies for around one million people in early May. The station pumps water from the Siverskyi Donets River to several settlements in the north of the Luhansk Region, including Popasna, Zolote, Hirske, Pervomaisk, Kadiyevets, Alchevsk, Khrustalny, Antratsyt, as well as in the villages of Toshkivka, Chekhirovo, Loskutivka, Pidlisne, Vovcheyarivka, Madoriazantseve, Lysychansk.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sheldon 2022

title: Regional special forces shoot protesters opposing water well drilling in Shilabo, Ethiopia, killing two and injuring seven
description: Regional special forces shoot into protesters who had gathered to oppose the drilling of a water well in a cattle grazing area near Shilabo, Ethiopia, killing two and injuring seven others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. ETH9567

title: Residents and farmers destroy intake pipes that drew water from a river and transferred it to a dam in Kenya
description: Residents and farmers from eight villages destroy intake pipes that drew water from a river and transferred it to Ragati dam, Mathira East, Nyeri, Kenya in demonstration against the move by the Mathira Water and Sanitation Company, Mawasco. The pipes cut the flow of water to domestic users and irrigators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KEN9500

title: Residents in Mpumalanga, South Africa assault construction officials during a protest against water project corruption
description: Cottondale Village residents, Mpumalanga, South Africa, barricade a road with burning tires and pipes meant for a water distribution project in protest over corruption. There are reports that rioters assaulted the construction company officials. The police arrested two suspects.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF17521

title: Residents of Ibague, Colombia, protest against a water cut and the lack of drinking water supply
description: Residents of La Pola neighborhood, Ibague, Colombia, protest against a water cut and the lack of drinking water supply for weeks, demanding the reconnection of services. At least one injury reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. COL10698

title: Residents of Lysychansk, Ukraine collecting water are attacked by Russian forces, killing ten and injurying more than 20
description: Russian army fires on residents in Lysychansk who had come out to replenish supplies of drinking water, June 2022. At least ten deaths and 21 injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Aretem Lysohor Luhansk 2022b

title: Residents of Zabol, Iran attack the trucks of Afghan traders during a demonstration to demand more water from the Helmand River
description: In growing tensions over the shared Helmand River, residents of Zabol, Iran attack the trucks of Afghan traders near the border during a demonstration to demand more water from the Helmand River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Faizee and Schmeier 2023 ; Radio Free Europe 2023

title: Russia is blamed for deliberately cutting off the water supply to Mykolaiv city
description: Russian forces are blamed for deliberately cutting off the water supply of Mykolaiv in April by sabotaging the water pipeline from the Dnipro River, based on satellite imagery and data from intelligence sources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Zhuhan and Ibrahim 2022

title: Russia reportedly attacks the Dnipro hydropower plant in December 2022
description: The Dnipro hydropower plant near Zaporizhzhia is reportedly attacked by Russia in December 2022.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; BBC News 2023

title: Russian and Ukrainian forces blame each other for shelling of an industrial area that cuts off water for several cities
description: Russian and Ukrainian forces blame each other for shelling the industrial area of Enerhodar, Zaporizhzhia. The shelling cuts off the water supply in several districts of the city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR73678

title: Russian attack on water and energy infrastructure cuts utilities to Kharkiv in northeastern Ukraine
description: The mayor of Kharkiv reports that a Russian strike on an infrastructure facility knocks out power and water to much of the city in northeastern Ukraine in mid-September 2022.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kramer 2022

title: Russian attack on water distribution pipeline in Luhansk, Ukraine
description: Russian forces shell Sievierodonetsk, Luhansk, Ukraine, damaging a water distribution pipeline.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR55854

title: Russian attack on water processing systems in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine
description: Russian forces shell and mine water-processing systems in Verkhnia Krynytsia, Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR55865

title: Russian attacks on water systems cut water supply to one million people in the Luhansk region
description: The entire Luhansk region is left without central water supply due to destruction of electricity stations in early May 2022. This Russian attack cuts the water supply to a million people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023 ; Aretem Lysohor Luhansk 2022a ; Rothrock 2022

title: Russian forces attack Siverskyi Donets-Donbas water pipeline
description: Russian forces attack the Siverskyi Donets-Donbas water pipeline providing water to the city of Donetsk, February 2022.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; CEOBS 2022a

title: Russian forces attack a dam on the Siverskyi Donets River draining the reservoir and causing flooding
description: Russian forces attack the Oskil dam on the Siverskyi Donets River in the Kharkiv region, draining the reservoir and causing flooding (July 2022).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Belousova 2022

title: Russian forces cut off access to water and electricity to the city of Sievierodonetsk, Ukraine
description: Russian forces destroy electricity and water lines near Sievierodonetsk, Luhansk. Severodonetsk is cut off from access to electricity and water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR54814

title: Russian forces damage the Karlivka water purification station
description: Russian forces shell civilian and military infrastructure near Karlivka, Donetsk region, damaging the Karlivka water purification station.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR65264

title: Russian forces destroy a dam in Donetsk, flooding the town of Raihorodok
description: The Russians blow up a dam during their retreat in Donetsk Oblast in October 2022, flooding the settlement of Raihorodok.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Tyshchenko 2022

title: Russian forces shell Kharkiv water systems, with numerous deaths reported
description: On 7 March 2022, Russian military forces shell the city of Kharkiv destroying energy facilities, pipelines, and water systems. Numerous civilians as well as servicemen are reported wounded and killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR52922

title: Russian forces shell Kupiansk and Kharkiv, Ukraine, damaging water pipe and civilian infrastructure
description: Russian forces shell Kupiansk and Kharkiv, Ukraine, damaging a water pipe and other civilian infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR89226

title: Russian forces shell Shevchenkove in Mykolaiv, Ukraine, damaging power station and water tower
description: Russian forces shell Shevchenkove community in Mykolaiv, Ukraine, damaging a power distribution station and a water tower.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR79341

title: Russian forces shell Zelenodolsk, Ukraine, cutting off water and electricity
description: Russian forces shell Zelenodolsk, Dnipropetrovsk, Ukraine, cutting off water and electricity.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR56258

title: Russian forces shell the Kherson, Ukraine water utility, killing one
description: Russian forces shell the Kherson, Ukraine water utility, resulting in the death of one civilian.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR83383

title: Russian missile attack damages a water-supply plant and kills two in Sievierodonetsk, Luhansk, Ukraine
description: Russian forces clash with Ukrainian forces in Sievierodonetsk, Luhansk. Russian forces fire Grad missiles, damaging a water-supply plant. Two people die, four are wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR53519

title: Russian missile attack near a Ukrainian nuclear plant also shuts down a nearby hydropower plant
description: Russian missiles strike near the Ukrainian Pivdennoukrainsk nuclear plant, also known as the South Ukraine Nuclear Power Plant. The attack damages a hydroelectric power station near the nuclear facility, forces the shutdown of one of the plant’s generators, and causes partial power outages in the area (September 2022).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Santora 2022

title: Russian missile attack on an oil depot in Kalynivka, Ukraine contaminates water resources
description: A Russian missile attack on an oil depot in Kalynivka, Ukraine leads to water contamination at a fish farm and pond about 30 kilometers (about 18 miles) southwest of Kyiv, also threatening the Irpin River (March 2022).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Voice of America 2022

title: Russian missile attack on the Pechenihy dam
description: In September, 2022, Russian missiles attack the Pechenihy Dam in Pechenihy on the Siverskyi Donets River, Kharkiv Oblast.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; OSINT 2022

title: Russian troops destroy Ukrainian dam that blocked water to Crimea
description: In late February, Russian troops invading Ukraine destroy a concrete dam built by Ukraine in 2014 to cut off water to Crimea after Russia annexed that region. The canal was originally built to provide water from the Dnipro River to Ukraine's Kherson region and Crimea.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2022

title: Russian warplanes attack the water station near Idlib, Syria damaging the water system and injuring at least one
description: On January 2, Russian warplanes conduct airstrikes on the vicinity of Sijer - Bqesemtoh town water station near Idlib, Syria, damaging the pipes and rendering the station inoperable. At least one worker at the water station is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. 8699619

title: Russians bomb water supply system in Kherson, Ukraine
description: Russians bomb water supply system in Kherson, Ukraine, March 1, 2022.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Verkhovna Rada 2022

title: Saudi-led air raids on a water drilling rig in Yemen kills one and injures two
description: Saudi-led coalition air raids strike a water rig in As Safiyah, Al Jawf, Yemen, killing 1 laborer and injuring 2 more.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM71446

title: Saudi-led forces attack water infrastructure in Yemen
description: Saudi-led coalition air forces attack water infrastructure in Tamrah, Yemen, destroying it and interrupting water delivery services.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM70714

title: Saudi-led forces attack water reservoirs in Sadah, Yemen
description: The Saudi-led coalition air force attacks water reservoirs in Saadah district, Sadah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM70500

title: September 2022 Russian missile strike on Karachunov dam in Kryvyi Rih causes flooding, cutting water to 100+ homes
description: A September 2022 Russian missile attack on the Karachunov dam at the Karachunivske Reservoir on the Ingulets River in the city of Kryvyi Rih destroys water gates and causes a flood and the loss of water supply to a hundred residential buildings.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick et al. 2023 ; Golowanow 2022 ; Gettleman 2022 ; United Kingdom MoD 2022 ; Novaya Gazeta Europe 2022

title: Seven deaths are reported in clashes over irrigation water and agricultural land in Yemen
description: Clashes over irrigation water and agricultural land take place between Kaut and Abu Ahmad tribesmen in As Sudah district, Amran, Yemen. The clashes result in seven fatalities and two injuries, over 21 - 23 July.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM75092, YEM75081, YEM75078

title: Several are injured in a clash between police and demonstrators in Ciudad de Mexico in a protest over a water system
description: Several people are injured in a clash between police and demonstrators in Ciudad de Mexico, Xochimilco. Residents are protesting hydraulic works of the Actopan collector and denouncing the misuse of water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX68032

title: Several towns in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine lose water services due to attacks
description: Russian attacks leave the towns Huliaipole and Stepnohirsk in the Zaporizhzhia region without water services (April). The town of Polohy is partly without water services. No wastewater treatment is available in Vasylivka and Stepnohirsk due to damage to water systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023

title: Shortage of water in Samba, India, leads to violent demonstration
description: Women hold a demonstration and vandalize government offices at Samba, India, over shortages of water supply in their area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND114528

title: South Sudanese refugees are attacked at Um Sangour, Sudan, in a dispute over access to the waters of the Nile
description: South Sudanese refugees are attacked by local residents at Um Sangour camp, White Nile state, Sudan, in a dispute over access to the waters of the Nile. Gunshots are fired in the air, with property, including a school, destroyed and looted, with no precise information on casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SUD16980

title: Suspected Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin militants sabotage water installation in Sebba, Burkina Faso
description: Suspected Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin militants sabotage the National Office of Water and Sanitation water installation by destroying the generator in the town of Sebba, Burkina Faso.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO8392

title: Suspected Somali camel herders injure two farmers near Tseikuru, Kenya, in a fight over grazing land and watering points
description: Suspected Somali camel herders injure two farmers in Masungwa area of Tseikuru, Kitui, Kenya, in a fight over grazing land and watering points.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KEN9410

title: Suspected Somali herders invade farms and destroy water points in Kilifi, Kenya
description: Suspected Somali herders invade farms in Magarini, Kilifi, Kenya and destroy some water points.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KEN9543

title: The Israeli military demolish a Palestinian water tank used for irrigation in the West Bank
description: Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned water tank used for agricultural purposes in Furush Bayt Dajan, Nablus, West Bank, to maintain the Israeli control over water resources in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE13877

title: The Pechenihy Dam on the Siverskyi Donets River is damaged during the Russia-Ukraine war
description: Two gates and the roadway over the Pechenihy Dam in Pechenihy on the Siverskyi Donets River (the main tributary of the Don River) in the Kharkiv region are blown up by the Armed Forces of Ukraine in order to widen the Siverskyi Donets River, and make it difficult for the Russians to encircle the city of Kharkiv (February 2022).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick et al. 2023

title: The Russian military bombs a water pumping plant in Chernihiv, Ukraine, killing four
description: The Russian military bombs one of the Chernihiv pumping stations, March 14, 2022. Four people, including station employees, are killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Suspilne News 2022

title: The water supply to the city of Basra, Iraq, is attacked
description: Unidentified militants sabotage the Bidaa canal in Basra province, Iraq, threatening the water supply for the city of Basra.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IRQ40184

title: Thee soldiers from the Myanmar military are killed while repairing a water system for a military camp
description: Myanmar military repairing a water system for a military camp are attacked in Hpruso, Kayah, Myanmar, killing three soldiers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR42388

title: Thousands protest large basin irrigation project; violent clashes with 1,500 police leave 60+ officers, 50 demonstrators injured
description: Between 4,000 and 7,000 people from a wide range of community, environmental, and political groups demonstrate against the large basin project being built to irrigate fields in times of drought. Around 1,500 police officers and six helicopters are deployed to meet them and a violent confrontation injures more than 60 police officers and 50 demonstrators. A pipeline is cut.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. FRA19929, FRA19930

title: Three killed in dispute over control and distribution of drinking water in Mexico
description: Violence over the control, distribution, and sale of drinking water in San Gregorio, Cuautzingo, Mexico, leads to three deaths and one injury.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX59573

title: Turkish attack on drinking water system in Ar Raqqa, Syria
description: Turkish military shells the town of Al Hishah in Ar Raqqa, Syria, damaging the drinking water station.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR104350

title: Turkish forces fire rockets at the water station in Fatsa, Syria
description: Turkish forces fire rockets at the water station in Fatsa, Ar Raqqa, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR98628

title: Two families in Syria clash over water for agricultural lands
description: Clashes take place between two armed families over the watering of agricultural lands in Al-Hessan village in Deir ez Zor, Syria. One injury is reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR98737

title: Two killed in attack on tractor delivering water to Pakistan military in Balochistan, Pakistan
description: Balochistan Liberation Army militants detonate a landmine targeting a tractor carrying water for Pakistan forces in Khost, Balochistan, Pakistan, killing two.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK75154

title: Ukrainians flood lands north of Kyiv in an effort to stop an armored assault on Ukraine's capital
description: In late February 2022 at the start of the expanded Russia-Ukraine war, the Ukraine military intentionally flood lands north of the capital, Kyiv, by destroying a hydraulic structure near Kazarovichi village. This leads to the inundation of the floodplain of the Irpin River with water from the Kyivski Reservoir, helping to stop a Russian armored assault.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Gleick et al. 2023 ; Mundy 2019 ; Kucharski 2022 ; Kramer 2022

title: Underwater pipeline supplying water to Aegina, Greece, is damaged by sabotage
description: According to the Attica Regional Authority in Greece, unidentified assailants use explosives to damage the underwater pipeline that supplies water to the island of Aegina. The incident reportedly occurred near the village of Perani, 300 meters off the Coast of Salamina at a depth of 14 meters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. GRC3705

title: Unidentified armed group targets water-transport truck with explosive device in Marib, Yemen
description: An improvised explosive device planted by an unidentified armed group targets a water-transport truck in Marib, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM77511

title: Unknown gunmen, believed to be Islamic State members, attack Asayish water truck in Syria, killing 1 and injuring 2
description: Unknown gunmen believed to be Islamic State members target an Asayish water truck in Karama, Syria, killing 1 Asayish member, and injuring two others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR109397

title: Violence over a water project in Kassala, Sudan kills two and wounds seven.
description: In the city of Kassala, Sudan, a violent incident at the end of March results in two deaths and seven injured in a conflict over a water project. Authorities impose a security cordon around the affected area and arrested eight alleged perpetrators and on April 6, negotiators sign an accord between the Beni Amer, Habab, and Sibarat tribes to put an end to the conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; The Water Diplomat 2022

title: Violence over access to water in Sanaa, Yemen results in one death and one injury
description: Bani Habar tribesmen attack and clash with Bani Buays tribesmen in Arhab, Sanaa, Yemen, over the control of a water source. The clash results in 1 fatality and 1 injury.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM74750

title: Violence over access to water in a canal in Bangladesh leads to one death and several injuries
description: One person is killed and at least 7 injured in a clash between two groups at the Madhusudanpur canal, Bangladesh, in a dispute over water sharing.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BGD21381

title: Violence over water in Nigeria between Fulani pastoralists and Aworo farmers lead to three deaths
description: Aworo community members kill three Fulani pastoralists in Ogun, Nigeria. The pastoralists were accused of destroying farms and water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. NIG23299

title: Violence reported between pastoralists and farmers over access to water sources and land near Chomboro in South Sudan
description: Armed pastoralists, possibly Bor Dinka, fire upon Lokoya children bathing at a water source in the area of Chomboro, Eastern Equatoria state, South Sudan, wounding one. A local official has claimed that 2,810 people were displaced from the area, in heightened tensions between pastoralists from Jonglei state and residents in parts of Eastern Equatoria state over water and land.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SSD8286

title: Violent demonstration in Chilpancingo de los Bravo, Guerrero, Mexico, over access to water services leads to injuries
description: A violent demonstration in Chilpancingo de los Bravo, Guerrero, Mexico, over access to water services leads to injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX68765

title: Violent demonstration in Karachi City, Pakistan over water connections, injuring one
description: Violent demonstration in Karachi City, Pakistan, over water connections to a private hospital. Demonstrators scuffle with police forces, injuring one.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK77479

title: Violent demonstration in Sindh, Pakistan, against the diversion of water from farmers, with multiple injuries
description: Farmers stage a demonstration near Khairpur Nathan Shah, Sindh, Pakistan, to demand irrigation water be diverted to the lands of the 'influential people.' Police clash with the demonstrators: farmers pelt stones and the police retaliate with gunfire, injuring 25 people, including 5 police.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK75801

title: Violent demonstration over lack of potable water in Gedaref, Sudan
description: Demonstrators stage a protest in Gedaref, Sudan, demanding access to potable water. Security forces beat and arrest some of the protesters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SUD17429

title: Violent demonstration over lack of potable water in Peru
description: Residents of at least ten settlements of Veintiseis de Octubre in Peru, damage the offices of the EPS Grau potable water company to complain about the lack of potable water services.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PER4015

title: Violent demonstrations in Brazil over water shortages
description: Violent protests in Esmeraldas, Minas Gerais, and Serra, Espirito Santo, Brazil, with burning obstacles in protests against a shortage in water supply. One demonstrator is reported injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BRA51402, BRA51428

title: Violent protest in Argentina in a demonstration against a mining project and threats to water resources
description: In a violent protest in Andalgala, Catamarca, Argentina, against the MARA mining project and threats to water resources, the Agua Rica company offices are set on fire.
