source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. ND ARG9974

title: Violent protest in Musina, South Africa, over chronic water shortages
description: Over several days, rioters barricade streets with burning tires and riot in Musina, Vhembe, Limpopo, South Africa to demonstrate against chronic water shortages. Police intervene and shoot rubber bullets and live ammunition, injuring at least one, and rioters throw stones at the police. Several arrests are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF16688, SAF16691, SAF16736, SAF16739

title: Violent protest over contaminated water and inadequate water supply in Maharastra, India
description: Around a dozen Shiv Sena members in Nagpur, Maharastra, India, ransack the offices of the Orange City Water Pvt Ltd. and manhandle a senior company official during a protest over contaminated and low-pressure water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND110466

title: Violent protest over lack of water and electricity in schools in Gedaref, Sudan
description: Students of Azza and Al Sir schools in Gedaref, Sudan, stage a protest and close the national road in a demonstration against the lack of water and electricity. Security forces fire tear gas to disperse the crowd and beat protesters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SUD18034

title: Violent protest over lack of water services in Monterrey, Mexico
description: Protestors in Monterrey, Nuevo Leon, Mexico, block a road to demand water services and some are assaulted by drivers opposed to the blockade.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX61830

title: Violent protests over pollution from mining in Bolivia
description: Residents of Oruro, Bolivia, block a highway to demand the closure of a mine in their neighborhood due to water pollution. In a counter-demonstration, mining workers of Bolivar, Totoral, and Avicaya areas, march through the city detonating dynamite and attempting to enter the building of the Oruro Regional Government.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BOL3221

title: Water access clash injures two in Mallah community, Badin, Sindh, Pakistan
description: A clash over access to water takes place between two groups of the Mallah community, Badin, Sindh, Pakistan, injuring two.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK79350

title: Water basins are damaged in France in a protest over the use of water during a drought
description: Members of a group of gardeners, fishers, and 'water stream lovers' damage large water reserve basins in Pouille, France, denouncing the use of water during a drought.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. FRA18320

title: Water cut provokes violence in Candelaria, Colombia
description: A group in Candelaria, Valle del Cauca, Colombia, demonstrate against an eight-day water cut and vandalize the town hall and mayor's office. Arrests are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. COL11102

title: Water pollution from mining in Madagascar prompts violent protests from local fishers
description: Local fishers attack soldiers and block a road leading to the QMM mining company in Fort Dauphin, Taolagnaro, Madagascar, in a demonstration to force the company to meet demands to stop water pollution. 30 soldiers are taken hostage by the group, 5 soldiers are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MAG2216

title: Water station in Syria is attacked
description: An unidentified armed group targets the water station of Thiban with heavy machine guns and rockets in Deir ez Zor governorate, Syria, causing extensive damage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR98401

title: Water supply canal is attacked in Zlitan, Libya
description: An unidentified armed group damages water canal in Zlitan, Almargeb, Libya, cutting available water supplies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. LBY11088

title: Water supply for five towns in the Luhansk region of Ukraine is cut off
description: Water supply for five towns in the Luhansk region is cut off in April, including Rubizhne, Popasna, Hirske, Sievierodonetsk, and part of Lysychansk.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shumilova et al. 2023

title: Water truck is targeted by Syrian government forces, injuring three
description: Syrian government forces target a drinking water truck in Idleb countryside with a guided missile, injuring 3 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SYR103918

title: Women protesting against water prices in Comoros clash with police
description: Women demonstrating against the payment of water bills from the National Company for the Exploitation and Distribution of Water in Comoros clash with police, who respond with tear gas. At least 6 women and two children are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. COM50

title: A Pennsylvania water authority, with several other organizations, is the victim of a cyberattack by Iran-affiliated hackers
description: In November 2023, an Iranian-linked group, "Cyber Av3ngers," targets multiple organizations, including a small Pennsylvania town's water provider. Earlier this year, a Russian-linked "hactivist" group attempted to disrupt operations at several Texas utilities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Whisnant 2024 ; Associated Press (AP) 2023

title: A Peruvian congress member is attacked in a dispute over the construction of a potable water and sewage project
description: On 26 June in Arequipa, Peru, a congress member is attacked with rocks, bottles, and dirt by residents of Apipa in a dispute over the construction of a potable water and sewage project in the Cerro Colorado district. Police intervene with tear gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PER8287

title: A building of the water-supply company in Donetsk, Ukraine is attacked
description: A Russian report says Ukrainian Armed Forces strike the building of the water-supply company in the Petrovsky district of Donetsk (March 22, 2023).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; War in My Eyes 2023

title: A clash between two clans in Somalia kills one and leads to the destruction of houses and water reservoirs
description: Dhulbante clan militia in Somalia set fire and destroy houses and water reservoirs belonging to Habarjeco clan in Boodhlay village, Ceerigaabo, Sanaag. One civilian is killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SOM42908

title: A clash in Kenya between Samburu militia and Isiolo herders over grazing land and water access leaves one dead, 5 injured
description: A confrontation occurs between suspected Samburu militia and an unidentified militia group, described as Isiolo herders, near Archers Post, Samburu East, Kenya. The clash arises from disputes over grazing land and access to watering holes for livestock, resulting in one fatality and five injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KEN10941

title: A community water system in Ireland is hacked, cutting water supply to 180 households for two days
description: In December 2023, a community-owned and managed water system in Ireland is hacked and a computer controller is disabled, cutting water supply to 180 households for two days. The hackers stated the equipment was targeted because it originated in Israel.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Quinn 2023

title: A dam in Sudan is attacked and damaged during fighting between Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces
description: In November 2023, attacks on the Jebel Aulia Dam in Sudan during fighting between Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces damage the infrastructure, cut its ability to regulate water levels and deliveries, and threatens dam collapse.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; IHE Delft 2024

title: A dispute among water pipe operators leaves one dead, one injured in Mexico
description: Two armed individuals traveling on a motorcycle shoot workers in a dispute over water pipe operators in Chalco de Diaz Covarrubias, Mexico. One person is killed and one injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX82111

title: A political clash turns violent in India over the failure to complete an irrigation project in Andhra Pradesh
description: On August 4, members of the YRS Congress Party and the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) clash in Beemaganipalle village on the outskirts of Punganur town, Andhra Pradesh, India in protests over unfinished irrigation projects. Police resort to lathi-charge and teargas to disperse the mobs. Police vehicles are set on fire and several TDP members and officials are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND137690

title: A political clash turns violent in India over the failure to complete an irrigation project in Telangana
description: On November 14, members of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) political party assault members of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) including the Nalgonda District President in Nellikal village Telangana, India, while the BJP was demonstrating against the BRS for not completing the Nellikal Lift irrigation project as promised.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND144736

title: A suspected Al Shabaab gunman fires on a water tanker in Kenya
description: A suspected Al Shabaab gunman fires on a water tanker near Nguni market, Kenya (Mwingi Central Sub- County, Kitui). The driver managed to escape unhurt and one of the tanker's front tires was punctured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN12795

title: A violent conflict erupts in Chiapas, Mexico over the control and allocation of water from a spring
description: Around 80 residents from Tunapaz, Chichabantelja, Chiapas, Mexico protest the lack of an agreement for the distribution of water from a local spring in Chic'habantelja on December 3. Some protestors start shooting in the air, open a ditch in the road, and cut off electricity service. The rioters also throw stones and sticks at their neighbors resulting in at least eight indigenous people injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX81847

title: AQAP militants target water tanker with IED in Mudiyah district, Abyan
description: Al Qaeda in the Arab Peninsula (AQAP) militants target a water tanker belonging to Southern Transitional Council (STC) 13th Saiqa Brigade forces in Mudiyah district, Abyan, with an IED, injuring one STC fighter and damaging the truck.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM80890

title: Al Shabaab attack kills two civilians and destroys water points in Sirirale, Somalia
description: An improvised explosive device planted at two water points by Al Shabaab detonates, killing two civilians, injuring one, and destroying the two water points in the Sirirale area near Baardheere village, Hiraan, Somalia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM39476

title: Al Shabaab attack results in 350+ camel deaths and water contamination in Ceel Xeero Village, Somalia
description: Deadly Al Shabaab assault claims lives of over 350 camels and pollutes water sources in Ceel Xeero Village, Bulo Burto, Somalia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SOM39239

title: Al Shabaab detonates IED at water borehole in Ceel Qoxle village, Galgaduud, Somalia
description: On September 13, Al Shabaab detonates an IED at a water source borehole in Ceel Qoxle village, Ceel Buur, Galgaduud, Somalia, destroying a water truck. The same day Al Shabaab detonates an IED at a water source borehole and destroys houses and water wells in Ceel Garas village, Dhuusamarreeb, Galgaduud, Somalia, targeting civilians from the Habar Gedir clan. The militants claim the US destroyed the water wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SOM42259 ; SOM42258

title: Al-Qaeda militants in Abyan target military vehicles with IEDs, including a water truck, in Imbaqirah, Mudiyah
description: Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula militants target military vehicles of 'mercenaries' in Imbaqirah, Mudiyah, Abyan, with three improvised explosive devices, including a water truck.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM80258

title: An environmental activist and defender of water and agroecology is fatally attacked in Mexico
description: An environmental activist and researcher defending water and agroecology, Alvaro Arvizu Aguiniga, is attacked with an axe at the Center for Sustainability of the Sierra Nevada Incalli Ixcahuicopa (CENTLI) in Tlalmanalco de Velazquez, Mexico, and dies. Assailants also intimidate his wife and collaborators, beating and tying them up. Aquiniga has advocated for a new General Water Law for over a decade.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX75608 ; Scholars at Risk Network 2023

title: An unidentified drone attacks a water tower in Vyazovoye, Russia
description: An unidentified drone attacks a water tower in Vyazovoye, Russia. No casualties occur.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. RUS9799

title: Armed Israeli settlers from Avigail settlement attack Palestinian home in Al Mefqara, damaging water containers and solar panels
description: Armed Israeli settlers from the Avigail settlement attack a Palestinian home in Al Mefqara village near Massafer Yuta (Hebron, West Bank) breaking solar energy panels, damaging water storage containers, and chopping down fruit bearing trees.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE37063

title: Armed bandits attack Olng'arua primary school in Isiolo, Kenya, setting fires, vandalizing property, and stealing a water pump
description: Armed bandits from neighboring villages attack Olng'arua primary school in Leparua, Isiolo, Kenya, setting vehicles on fire, vandalizing classes and a residential building, and damaging water tanks and a biogas digester. They also steal a motorcycle and a water pump.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KEN11518

title: Armed group sabotages sewage network in Al Khums, Libya, causing contamination
description: An unidentified armed group sabotages a sewage network in Al Khums, Al Marqab, Libya, resulting in a water leak and area contamination in early September.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. LBY11333

title: Armed group's attack on oil pipeline in Ricaurte, Narino, Colombia, results in oil spill, contaminating local water sources
description: An armed group damages an oil pipeline in Ricaurte, Narino, Colombia, causing an oil spill that pollutes local water sources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. COL19335

title: Armed individuals in Haiti open fire on a convoy of vehicles related to water and sanitation. No one is injured but vehicles are
description: In Croix-des-Bouquets, Ouest, Haiti, armed individuals open fire on a convoy of vehicles belonging to the National Directorate of Drinking Water and Sanitation, in the Beudet area. No one is injured but vehicles are damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. HTI5433

title: Armed man kills one and injures another over water tank dispute in Adinah Village, Yemen
description: An armed man kills one man and injures his son in Adinah village, Ad Dali, Yemen over a water tank dispute.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM81065

title: Armed men attack police in Guanajuato, Mexico amid water control dispute
description: Armed men in pickups shoot at police near Water Committee, Rincon de Tamayo, Guanajuato, Mexico, possibly due to Municipal Water Board control of community wells.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX69743

title: Armed men occupy Municipal Water Company in Mixco, Guatemala, abduct employees and open fire on police
description: In Mixco, Guatemala, unidentified armed men occupy the Municipal Water Company of Guatemala City (Empagua) and abduct employees. As police forces arrive to reestablish water services, the armed men opened fire on them and flee the company's facilities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GTM7750

title: Assault on Water Resources Department staff in Diyala Province, Iraq
description: Two individuals attack Water Resources Department staff in Diyala province, Iraq, while they are dismantling unauthorized structures along waterways. Law enforcement apprehends the attackers, and casualties remain uncertain.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IRQ45201

title: At least 50 people are injured in a clash about the control and management of water and flooding in Sylhet, Bangladesh
description: On 14 June, locals from several villages burn tires and stage a demonstration against flooding in the area of Sylhet Sadar upazila (Sylhet), Bangladesh. They clash with locals from another village using indigenous weapons, when the latter opposed the decision to cut a raw canal on the side of the road to allow temporary water drainage. At least 50 people are injured, including police personnel, during the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BGD24696

title: Attack by Israel on the system providing energy for the Gaza Central Wastewater Treatment Plant
description: In November, Israeli air strikes destroy part of the energy production system, including solar panels, that provided energy for the Gaza Central Wastewater Treatment Plant, opened in April 2021 with the help of EU funding. The plant served 11 communities and one million people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Zwijnenburg 2023c

title: Attacks on water systems in Western Oromia, Ethiopia
description: In Western Oromia, Ethiopia, an attack and looting in June 2023 damages health posts, a hospital, and other facilities, including a water reservoir, causing a water-supply shortage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Addis Standard 2023

title: Azerbaijani forces wound civilian attacking water truck in Martakert region
description: On September 3, Azerbaijani forces fire small arms and grenade at a water truck near Chankatagh in the Martakert region, wounding one civilian.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. AZE18586

title: Baloch separatists set machinery on fire and abduct workers laying down a water pipeline in Pakistan
description: On 7 June 2023, Baloch separatists set fire to machinery and abduct five workers laying a water pipeline for a private company in Gaza area of Kalat district, Balochistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK134663

title: Balochistan Liberation Front strikes army water-supply post in Balochistan, Pakistan
description: Members of the Balochistan Liberation Front launch an assault on the Pakistan army's water-supply post in Gawak town, Kech, using rockets and heavy weapons.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK81223

title: Boko Haram and ISIS militants attack fishing communities, killing 7, abducting 25, and forcing thousands to flee
description: Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province militants launch over a dozen attacks on fishing communities as part of the longstanding land and water disputes in the northern part of Logone-et-Chari division, abducting around 25 people and killing at least seven. Thousands flee to the southern parts of the division.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Crisis Group 2024

title: Boko Haram militants clash with gendarmerie forces and overturn a water tower in Extreme-Nord, Cameroon
description: On September 11, Boko Haram militants, JAS faction, clash with gendarmerie forces at the military outpost in Nguetchewe, Extreme-Nord, Cameroon, resulting in three deaths. The militants overturn a water tower during the conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CAO7792

title: Caste violence kills one Dalit man for using a public tap to drink water in India
description: In mob and caste violence on November 27, several people assault and kill a man from the Dalit community in Sathra village, Uttar Pradesh, India for using a public tap to drink water. One person is arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND145392 ; The India Express 2023

title: Civilians at a water well in Al Fitahab, Sudan are attacked, killing one
description: Civilians at a water well in Al Fitahab, Sudan are attacked by RSF artillery, killing one, wounding 6.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD23360

title: Clash between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu in Thanjavur, India over Cauvery river water release with 197 arrests
description: CPI members protest in front of central government offices in Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu, India) against Karnataka for not releasing Cauvery river water to Tamil Nadu and demand the government solve the issue. Police clash with protestors and arrest 197 people, including 152 men and 45 women.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND139229

title: Clash erupts as Palestinian protesters confront Israeli forces and settlers over water well usage in Qaryut Village, Palestine
description: In Qaryut village, Nablus, West Bank, Palestinian protesters confront Israeli military forces and settlers, triggered by settlers' intrusion for utilizing the village water well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE31044

title: Clash over equitable distribution and access to potable water infrastructure in Bolivia
description: Residents of Palacio Tambo San Lucas, Bolivia clash with residents of Japo in an ongoing issue around a potable water system from a river in Japo that would only benefit Palacio Tambo. Several residents were injured and three residents from Japo are reported missing.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BOL5035

title: Clash over water pollution in India, leaves over 30 injured as villagers confront each other and police intervene with tear gas
description: Villagers from Konsakhul and Leilon, India, clash over water pollution concerns. The clash escalates into a confrontation, with both sides throwing stones. State police intervene, using tear gas to restore order. Over 30 people sustain injuries in the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND129166

title: Clash over water rotation and access injures one person in Sindh, Pakistan
description: A clash takes place between two groups of the Chachar community, injuring one person in Muhammad Hashim Chhachhar village, Sindh, Pakistan, over the rotation of water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK82630

title: Clash over water sharing in Kashmore leaves one dead and 14 injured
description: Two groups of the Jakhrani tribe in Malgazari village, Kashmore district, Kashmor, Sindh, clash over water sharing for agricultural lands, attacking each other with axes, clubs, and bricks, resulting in one death and 14 injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK84039

title: Clash over water supply in South Africa, leads to shootings and injuries
description: A group of protestors demanding water supply clash with local authorities in Charlestown, Newcastle, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Three people are shot and hospitalized.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF19005

title: Clashes between Baggara tribal militias over water canal dispute injure woman in Deir ez Zor, Syria
description: Clashes between two Baggara tribal militia families in Jneineh, Deir ez Zor, Syria over a water canal injure a woman with a stray bullet, with no fatalities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR115452

title: Clashes erupt on World Water Day march demanding improved water services in Merida, Yucatan, Mexico
description: On World Water Day, March 23, 2023, around 100 people march in Merida, Yucatan, to demand improved water services. The demonstrators clash with state police, resulting in one police officer being injured. Authorities arrest four individuals.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX72281

title: Clashes in Al Quds, West Bank: Palestinian rioters throw Molotov cocktails, Israeli police respond with tear gas and wastewater
description: On September 25, Palestinian rioters throw Molotov cocktails and clash with Israeli police who raided Al Quds - Isawiya, Al Quds, West Bank, Palestine. Police fire stun grenades, tear gas, and spray wastewater at the rioters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE36384

title: Clashes over land and water disputes at Qurnat as Sawda peak, Lebanon leave three dead
description: Two armed clashes between Tawk clansmen and Bqaa Safrine militiamen at Qurnat as Sawda, Al Danniyeh, Lebanon result in two deaths. The army intervenes, killing one militiaman and arresting 19 individuals while seizing weapons and ammunition. Clashes in the area have been over land and water disputes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. LBN14910

title: Clashes over water dispute in Ar Raqqa, Syria injure six
description: Clashes among Fakheth Al 'lyat tribal militiamen in Karama, Ar Raqqa province, Syria over watering agricultural lands injure six people, with no fatalities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR114966

title: College students in South Africa protest water, book, and student card shortages; set fire to vehicle and water tank
description: College students in eSikhawini, uMhlathuze, KwaZulu-Natal, protest demanding solutions for the shortages of water, books, and student cards on the campus. Demonstraters set fire to a college vehicle and a water tank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF18431

title: Community in Santa Cruz Pueblo Nuevo blocks highway demanding water solutions to water shortages
description: In Santa Cruz Pueblo Nuevo, Mexico, residents block the Tenango-Ixtapan de la Sal highway, protesting water shortages caused by alleged theft by a group from San Pedro Tlanixco, prompting state police intervention with tear gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX75167

title: Community members from Aquixcuatitla, Hidalgo, Mexico abduct a public official and clash with police in a dispute over a drinkin
description: In Huejutla de Reyes, Hidalgo, Mexico community members from Aquixcuatitla abduct a public official from the Huejutla de Reyes municipality in a dispute over the drinking water pumping system electricity contract. Police rescue him and clash with the rioters, who attack them with machetes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX81030

title: Confrontation erupts as Palestinians clash with Israeli forces during raid on the water spring in Qaryut Village, Nablus, Palest
description: Palestinians and Israeli military forces clash after Israeli raid on the water spring in Qaryut village, Nablus, West Bank. Soldiers use stun grenades and tear gas canisters, leading to several injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE31755, PSE32094

title: Coordinated attacks target water supply company in Natal, Brazil, with Sindicato do Crime suspected
description: Unidentified individuals in Natal, Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil target a local water supply company, setting fire to its facilities and a vehicle in the Cidade da Esperanca neighborhood. These coordinated attacks occur across the state for ten days, with the Sindicato do Crime organization believed to be responsible.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BRA68951

title: Darfur militia burns 17 villages, seizes water sources, and displaces civilians in Bielel, South Darfur, Sudan
description: Militants, identified as the Darfur communal militia, burn 17 villages in Bielel, South Darfur, Sudan, and seize the local water resource. Civilians are displaced from these 17 villages and an additional 12 neighboring villages to refugee camps.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SUD19973

title: Deadly three-day attack by ethnic militia over access to water in Mekenisa Kebele, Oromia, Ethiopia
description: Ethnic Somali militias in Mekenisa kebele, East Hararge, Oromia, Ethiopia, attacks ethnic Oromo civilians for three days blocking their access to drinking water, resulting in four deaths and nine injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. ETH9828, ETH9829

title: Demonstrators barricade roads in Tsakane, South Africa, protesting water shortage
description: On September 18, hundreds of demonstrators in Tsakane, Ekurhuleni, Gauteng, South Africa, barricade roads with burning tires and rocks to protest a water shortage, stoning and damaging a Home Affairs office and police vehicles.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF19805

title: Demonstrators in Inchanga, South Africa protest electricity and water shortages, resulting in five injuries from shooting
description: Demonstrators block roads in Inchanga (eThekwini, KwaZulu-Natal), South Africa to protest electricity and water shortages when unknown assailants open fire, injuring five people. Victims suffer leg gunshot wounds, with one also sustaining stomach and head injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF19484

title: Demonstrators in Johannesburg block roads and loot trucks, demanding water and sanitation
description: Demonstrators in Johannesburg, Diepkloof, barricade roads with burning tires and loot trucks, demanding water and sanitation, prompting police to fire rubber bullets to disperse the crowd.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF19321

title: Demonstrators torch truck and assault driver in Gqeberha, South Africa over water shortage
description: Demonstrators torch a truck in Gqeberha, Nelson Mandela Bay, South Africa to protest water and electricity shortages, forcibly removing the driver and three passengers, and assaulting one passenger.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF19471

title: Desalination plant in Gaza bombed by Israel
description: In December 2023, the Eta Water company reports at least one of its desalination plants in Gaza has been bombed by Israel.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Baba and Neurman 2023

title: Destruction of water and water infrastructure in Gaza cuts off water services for over a million Palestinians
description: As of October 12, 2023 following the Israeli invasion of Gaza at least six water wells, three pumping plants, one reservoir, and one desalination plant, serving over 1.1 million people, have been damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN OCHA 2023a

title: Dominican Republic closes border with Haiti to pressure halt on canal construction
description: On September 15, all borders between Haiti and Dominican Republic are closed, and military are deployed, to pressure Haiti to stop canal construction on the Massacre River, with visa suspensions and entry refusals for labeled provocateurs.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. DOM533

title: Dominican Republic partially closes Haiti border to halt canal construction on shared Massacre River; military deployed
description: On 6 September 2023, in Dajabon, the Dominican government announces the partial closure of the border with Haiti in order to pressure Haiti to stop construction of a canal to take water from the Massacre River, shared by both countries. Soldiers, machinery, and armored vehicles are deployed in the area and borders are temporarily closed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. DOM533

title: Dozens hospitalized after consuming poisoned water in Farah religious school
description: Nearly 40 female students from a religious school in the Naw Abad area of Qala-i-kah district, Farah, are hospitalized after consuming water contaminated with poison, with the reason and perpetrators of the incident remaining unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. AFG66658

title: Drinking water system in Nepal is vandalized
description: An unidentified group vandalizes properties of the Roshnidanda-Rumaldev-Gadakha Lifting Drinking-Water Program, in the Chamunda Bindrasaini municipality, Nepal. The drinking-water project served more than 350 consumers in the municipality.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NEP23286

title: Drone attack in Myanmar kills one soldier and injures another during water tank transport
description: A drone attack is carried out by the Myaing People's Defense Force and an unknown local defense force on military forces transporting a water tank in Hpa Lan Kaing village, Pauk township, Magway region, Myanmar. The attack results in the death of one soldier and injuries to another.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR46218

title: During violence between gangs and the police in Mariani, Haiti, the National Directorate of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DINEP
description: During violence between gangs and the police in Mariani, Haiti, the National Directorate of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DINEPA) facilities are assaulted and occupied. One fatality and several injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. HTI5446

title: Eastern Cape's Raymond Mhlaba residents block road with stones and burning tires to demand water after pump station vandalism
description: In Raymond Mhlaba, Eastern Cape, residents block road near Fort Beaufort with burning tires and stones, demanding water due to the vandalism of a water pump station by criminals.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF18187

title: Ede minority protest in Cu Kuin, Vietnam over contaminated water; police response leaves seven injured, twelve arrested
description: Ede ethnic minority citizens stage a protest in Ea Bhok, Cu Kuin, Vietnam, against failures of the water-sewage system, alleging contamination of natural water sources in Dak Lak's Cu Kuin district. Police beat the protesters, resulting in at least seven injuries, and twelve protesters are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. VNM581

title: Environmental activists vandalize Beaumont-Saint-Cyr golf course and irrigation systems over water use during drought
description: During a lunch break of the SLT-organized 'Water Convoy' bicycle parade in France, 15 to 40 masked environmental activists cut through a fence and vandalize the Beaumont-Saint-Cyr golf course near Jaunay-Marigny, Nouvelle-Aquitaine. They tear up the lawn, damage the irrigation system, and paint slogans and the SLT logo, protesting water use for golf courses during droughts.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. FRA27309

title: Explosive device hits civilians at a water pump in Tin Rhassane, Burkina Faso, killing 21, likely targeting IS Sahel militants
description: Civilians who regularly fetch water from a water pump in the village of Tin Rhassane, Tin-Akoff, Burkina Faso, are hit by an explosive device, likely targeting IS Sahel militants who regularly come to refuel at this fountain, resulting in the death of 21 men, women, and children.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID.BFO9972

title: FAMa and Wagner forces in Mali kill civilians and destroy water towers and blow up wells in the village of Ersane
description: Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and Wagner forces in Mali kill 17 Tuareg civilians including elderly men and children in the village of Ersane (Bourem, Gao). They also destroy water towers and blow up wells in the village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MLI30979

title: Farmers and herders clash over water and land in northern Cameroon, with two deaths and many injuries reported
description: Between 6 and 7 October 2023, Kotoko farmers clash with Arab Choa herders over water and land in Makary, Goulfey, Amdagalgui and Ngouma (Logone-et-Chari, Far North, Cameroon) leading to at least two deaths and 20 injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; International Crisis Group 2024

title: Farmers in Guerrero, Mexico cut off a pipeline water supply to demand improved government response to Hurricane Otis
description: Farmers around Acapulco de Juarez, Guerrero, Mexico disrupt pumping equipment of the Lomas de Chapultepec pipeline to demand better federal government response to the rural impacts of Hurricane Otis. The disruption cut off a water supply to the region.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX86014

title: Farmers protest electricity cuts blocking water supply in Viransehir
description: Around 300 farmers gather on the Sanliurfa-Viransehir road in Viransehir district to protest electricity cuts that prevent them from watering their lands, blocking traffic and burning tires. Gendarmerie and police intervene with tear gas and water cannons, detaining 20 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. TUR30367

title: Farmers stealing water from a canal assault Irrigation Department Team in Hansi City, Haryana, India
description: Farmers assault an Irrigation Department Team at Mujadpur village in Hansi City, Hisar, Haryana, India, when the team discovers that the farmers are stealing water from the canal and try to stop them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND129213

title: Farming community leader attacked in Hambantota, Sri Lanka for addressing water shortage, the second such attack in a month
description: An unidentified group attacks a farming community leader in Mayurapura, Hambantota city, Sri Lanka, for helping farmers solve a water shortage problem, the second such attack in a month.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SRI7114

title: Farming community leader attacked near Bopele Tank, Sri Lanka for addressing water shortage
description: An unidentified group attacks a farming community leader near Bopele Tank in Mayurapura, Hambantota city, Sri Lanka for helping farmers address a water shortage problem.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SRI7113

title: Fatal clash between Baiki and Tangi tribes in Khost, Afghanistan, over road construction and possible water dispute
description: A violent clash occurs between Baiki and Tangi tribes in Khost's Spera, Afghanistan, over road construction and a possible dispute over water. One Taliban member dies, two to four civilians are injured, and seven are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. AFG66161

title: Fatal confrontation over the distribution of water resources claims life near New Manik Wah in Tando Bago, Pakistan
description: Confrontation over the fair distribution of water resources between Athela and Kaloi factions near New Manik Wah in Tando Bago, Sindh, Pakistan results in the death of an individual.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK82051

title: Fishers are killed in a dispute in Mali over management of a water pond
description: On October 29, fishers are killed in a dispute over management of a water pond near near the village of Troh, Segou, Mali.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MLI31228

title: Flood-stricken citizens of Volos, Greece, protest waterway damming, mayor confronts protesters
description: On 30 September 2023, flood-stricken citizens in Volos, Greece, protest in Ali Meria against damming a waterway without required studies. The mayor confronts protesters and hits one who insults him, while police do not intervene.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GRC4593

title: Former police officer fires at villagers protesting water pipe construction in Walasmulla, injuring three
description: Former police officer fires at villagers protesting against the digging of a well near his house for the construction of a water pipe in Walasmulla, Hambantota, Southern, injuring three.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SRI6990

title: Greenpeace activists cut of the water supply to a Spanish water agency in protest over water pollution
description: In December, Greenpeace activists cut off the water in the office of the hydrographic confederation in Laguna de Duero (Castilla y Leon, Spain) to demand the cessation of nitrate pollution.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. ESP15151

title: Groups clash over water extraction in Pharaya Malwala, India resulting in one death
description: Two groups clash with sticks and guns in Pharaya Malwala, Punjab, India over water extraction from fields, resulting in one death and three injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND136417

title: Groups clash over water tank construction in Khempur, India, resulting in one death
description: Around 30 August, two groups led by a Pradhan and a former Pradhan clash with stones and gunfire in Khempur village, Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, India, over cutting trees to construct a water tank, resulting in one death and six injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND137773

title: Groups clash over watering fields in Bannu, Pakistan, resulting in one death and three injuries
description: On 5 October 2023, two groups exchange fire over a dispute about watering fields in Miryakhel police limits in Bannu town, Pakistan, killing one person and injuring three others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK136349

title: Gunmen shoot and kill a senior South African municipality water and sanitation official
description: Gunmen shoot and kill a senior eThekwini municipality water and sanitation official Mandeni, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. The victim also served as the manager for Plants and Logistics in the Water and Sanitation Unit.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF20086

title: Hackers gain access to computers in water and wastewater systems in seven US states, forcing some to switch to manual operations
description: Cyber Av3ngers hackers gain access to computers in US water and wastewater systems in seven states, posting anti-Israel messages and forcing some to shut down their systems and switched to manual operations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Office of the Director of National Intelligence 2024

title: Hezbollah militants attack a water tanker in Israel killing the driver
description: Hezbollah militants fire an anti-tank missile in the Shoshan base area near Yiftah, Israel hitting an Israeli water tanker and killing the driver.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. ISR37964

title: Houthi forces assault workers and shut down a water factory in Yemen
description: Houthi forces assault workers at the Shamlan Mineral Water Factory in Shamlan, Hamdan, Sanaa, Yemen. They demolish parts of the factory, close it, and block the entry and exit for employees and trucks. The attack is allegedly due to the factory owners' refusal to share revenues with a Houthi figure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM79583

title: In Colombia, residents block highway over water service outages, and a confrontation with police results injuries
description: In San Juan Nepomuceno, Bolivar, Colombia, residents block the Western Highway in response to a ten-day water service outage. Colombian National Police riot control forces use tear gas to disperse protesters, and police officers fire their guns, resulting in injuries to four demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. COL19464

title: In Myanmar, military claims Kachin Independence Army and People's Defence Force destroyed vehicles, water tanks, and windows
description: In Mabein township, Mongmit district, Myanmar, the military alleges that the combined force of the Kachin Independence Army and local People's Defence Force destroy building windows, a motorcycle, a fire truck, a water truck, doors, and water tanks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR47316

title: In November 2023, the second largest water testing laboratory of the Gaza municipal water utility is destroyed by Israeli forces
description: The second largest water testing laboratory of the Coastal Municipalities Water Utility in Gaza is destroyed by Israeli forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Water and Development Partnership Program 2025

title: In a dispute between the regions in India over irrigation and drinking water, police take control of a dam and release water
description: In India on November 30, about 700 police personnel from Andhra Pradesh (AP) clash with Telangana state special police forces guarding the Nagarjunasagar dam on Krishna River in Nalgonda district in a long-standing dispute over water sharing and releases of irrigation water. AP police take control over the dam and irrigation officials start releasing water into Andhra Pradesh.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND145511 ; Apparasu 2023

title: Indigenous Rights Group marches to Zocalo in Mexico City, Mexico, denounces water and land dispossession
description: In Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc, Mexico, members of the Front for the Defense of the Rights of the Indigenous Peoples and Neighborhoods of the Anahuac Basin (FDDPBOCA) demonstrate and march to the Zocalo against the dispossession of water and land and the registration system established by the Political Constitution of Mexico City. Demonstrators attack police officers with sticks and strip them of radios. Injuries unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX80184

title: Indigenous women block National Route 86 in Tartagal, Salta, demanding water supply restoration
description: Indigenous women and children from the Wichi, Guarani, and Toba communities block National Route 86 in Tartagal, Salta, Argentina (September 11), demanding the restoration of their water supply. Protestors are attacked by an unidentified group at night.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. ARG14014

title: Iranian schoolgirls targeted with poison at school water systems in multiple incidents
description: Iranian schoolgirls are targeted in spate of poisoning attacks on school water systems. In Qom on February 14, more than 100 students from 13 schools were taken to hospitals after what the state-affiliated Tasnim news agency described as “serial poisonings.” Poisonings in other cities were also reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shahla 2023 ; Moshtaghian et al. 2023

title: Israel shells the Kawkab dam in Syria in response to attacks from this area on the Golan
description: Israeli forces shell the Kawkab dam in rural western Dara, Syria in response to unidentified shelling originating from the area targeting the Golan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR120857

title: Israel threatens full water cutoff to Gaza; water supply halts on October 30 amid blockade on electricity, food, and fuel
description: On October 9 2023, Israel threatens a complete cutoff of water to Gaza. Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant says that “no electricity, no food, no water, no fuel” would be allowed into Gaza. Water supply from Israel to southern Gaza comes to a halt on 30 October and for some time no water is provided to Gaza from Israel.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kershner et al. 2023 ; UN OCHA 2023b

title: Israeli aircraft strike a water supply tank in the Gaza Strip, causing damage and killing several dozen people
description: Israeli military airplanes strike a main water supply tank east of Rafah in the Gaza Strip, causing damage and killing several dozen people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE40372

title: Israeli airstrike destroys a water desalination plant in Jabalya, Gaza
description: On December 22, Israeli artillery shell Jabalya town in Gaza Strip, killing an unspecified number of Palestinians and injuring several others. Warplanes strike a house, kill six, and destroy a water desalination plant.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID.. PSE44092

title: Israeli airstrike kills two and injures several others filling water in Khan Yunis, Gaza
description: Israeli airstrikes kill two Palestinians and injure several others filling water in Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE43950

title: Israeli airstrike on a car belonging to the Gazan Water Authority kills three.
description: Israeli warplanes carry out airstrikes in Khan Yunis, Gaza, including an attack on a car belonging to the Gazan Water Authority, killing three.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID.. PSE44023

title: Israeli attack on southern Lebanon disrupts water supply for Tair Harfa.
description: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon in November 2023 destroy a solar-energy project that supplies electricity to operate the water well in Tair Harfa, Lebanon, disrupting its water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN ESCWA 2023

title: Israeli fighter jets strike a water project on the outskirts a town in Lebanon
description: Israeli fighter jets strike a water project on the outskirts of Taybeh, Marjayoun, Lebanon on November 19.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. LBN16319

title: Israeli forces bulldoze the main water pipeline in the West Bank
description: Israeli forces bulldoze the main water pipeline in Kisan, near Bethlehem, West Bank, on November 9.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE40264

title: Israeli forces clash with Palestinian protesters in Qarawat Bani Hassan, Salfit, West Bank, during a raid to seize a water tank
description: Israeli forces clash with Palestinian protesters in Qarawat Bani Hassan, Salfit, West Bank, during a raid to seize a water tank vehicle. Rubber-coated bullets and tear gas canisters are used by the Israeli forces. Three protesters sustain bullet injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE33112

title: Israeli forces damage and destroy several water systems in an agricultural area in the West Bank
description: In a week-long series of attacks in May 2023, Israeli military forces damage and destroy water pipes, water tanks, water-distribution systems, and wells along with many crops and other agricultural equipment at multiple locations in the West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE33608, PSE33586, PSE33585, PSE33643, PSE33891, PSE33912, PSE33262

title: Israeli forces demolish the water line to a refugee camp in the West Bank
description: Israeli forces demolish the main water line for the Jenin - Mukhayyam refugee camp, houses, and infrastructure in the West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38798

title: Israeli forces destroy Palestinian water containers, water lines, and more near Jenin, West Bank
description: On November 30, Israeli forces demolish Palestinian-owned residences, water containers, solar panels, and electricity and water lines in Firasin, Jenin, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE41925

title: Israeli forces destroy a Palestinian water reservoir, water pipeline, and olive plantings in Yuta, West Bank
description: On November 20 Israeli settlers demolish housing, a school's water tanks, a water pipeline, and uproot 70 olive seedings in Yuta, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE41345 ; Middle East Monitor 2023

title: Israeli forces destroy a Palestinian water well and agricultural road near Bethlehem, West Bank
description: On December 11, Israeli forces bulldoze an agricultural road and demolish a Palestinian-owned water well in Artas, near Bethlehem, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE43465

title: Israeli forces destroy a water network and water tanks in the Birin area, Hebron, West Bank
description: On November 27, Israeli forces destroy two houses, three dunam of agricultural lands cultivated with olive trees, and a water network and tanks in Birin area, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE41968

title: Israeli forces fire at a water transportation truck in Qab al Janib area in Hebron, West Bank
description: Israeli forces open fire at a water transportation truck as it was approaching the checkpoint in Qab al Janib area in Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38505

title: Israeli forces pour concrete into Palestinian well in Hebron, West Bank to stop irrigation
description: Israeli forces raid Palestinian farmland in occupied Hebron, West Bank, and pour concrete into the water sources to stop agricultural irrigation in an area that serves 25 families.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Middle East Monitor 2023

title: Israeli forces seize Palestinian water tank and agricultural equipment near Al Hadidiyah, West Bank
description: Israeli forces seize Palestinian-owned agricultural equipment, a water tank, and two vehicles east of Al Hadidiyah village (Tubas, West Bank) (October 25).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38591

title: Israeli forces seize wastewater pumping truck in Nablus, West Bank
description: On September 10, Israeli forces seize a wastewater pumping truck in Burqah, Nablus, West Bank, citing the reason of it operating in Area C -- an area under Israeli control.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE36058

title: Israeli military demolishes Palestinian-owned facilities and water tanks in As Sawahira ash Sharqiya
description: Israeli military forces demolish Palestinian-owned facilities, including water tanks belonging to Bedouins in As Sawahira ash Sharqiya, Al Quds, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE35124

title: Israeli military demolishes Palestinian-owned water well in Hablah Village, citing building permit absence
description: An under-construction water well owned by Palestinians in Hablah village, Qalqilya, West Bank, is destroyed by Israeli military forces, who claim the absence of a building permit as the reason.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE31105

title: Israeli military demolishes Palestinian-owned water well in Hebron
description: Israeli military forces demolish a Palestinian-owned water well in Al Baqaa, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE35021

title: Israeli military demolishes Palestinian-owned water well in Kafr Laqif, Palestine, due to permit issue
description: The Israeli military demolishes a Palestinian-owned water well in Kafr Laqif, Qalqilya, West Bank, due to a lack of required permit.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE31052

title: Israeli military destroys Palestinian lands and water wells near Hebron
description: Israeli military forces raze Palestinian-owned lands and destroy water wells in al-Hejrah, south of Hebron near Dura town, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE35276

title: Israeli military fires warning shots at Palestinian wastewater vehicle in Gaza Strip
description: On September 16, Israeli military forces on the security fence fire warning shots at a Palestinian wastewater vehicle east of Khan Yunis, Gaza Strip, to keep Palestinians away, with no reported casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE36209

title: Israeli military forces demolish a water well in Hizma Village, West Bank
description: Israeli military forces raze a road and demolish a water well in Hizma village, Al Quds, West Bank, claiming they were constructed in areas controlled by Israel.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE34280

title: Israeli military forces demolish foundations of Palestinian water pond in Bethlehem, West Bank, Palestine
description: On September 27, Israeli military forces demolish the foundations of a Palestinian-owned water pond in Artas village, Bethlehem, West Bank, Palestine, claiming it lacks a building permit.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE36425

title: Israeli military forces demolish water well in Kafr ad Dik Village, Plestibe, citing permit absence
description: On January 10, 2023, Israeli military forces demolish a water well in the village of Kafr ad Dik, Salfit, West Bank, Palestine, citing the absence of building permits as their justification.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE30901

title: Israeli military forces destroy Palestinian water supply network in Hebron, West Bank, Palestine
description: On September 28, Israeli military forces destroy a Palestinian water supply network between Samu and Khirbat Susiyah village in Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE36449

title: Israeli military operation in Jenin damages main water-supply network
description: Israeli military forces damage the main water-supply network during an operation in Jenin, including Mukhayyam Jenin refugee camp and Jenin city. Israel's stated intent of the operation is the defusing of explosives and IEDs.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE34718

title: Israeli military shells the main water tank in Lebanon
description: Israeli military forces shell the main water tank of Yarine (Tyr), Lebanon (October 11).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. LBN15223

title: Israeli military shoots six Palestinians filling water at the Al Shifa Hospital, Gaza
description: Israeli snipers shoot and injure six Palestinians filling water in Al Shifa Hospital in Gaza City, Gaza Strip.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE43605

title: Israeli military uproots Palestinian olive trees to build water network for settlements
description: Israeli military forces uproot numerous Palestinian-owned olive trees in Kifil Haris village, Salfit, West Bank, to build a water network for the Barkan and Ariel settlements.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE35007

title: Israeli police confiscate water tank in West Bank, citing license issue near Al Quds - Isawiya
description: In Cisjordânia, east of Al Quds - Isawiya, West Bank, a water tank is confiscated by the Israeli police who allege lack of license.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE31104

title: Israeli police demolish Palestinian dwelling and confiscate water tanks in Al Quds
description: Israeli police demolish a Palestinian-owned dwelling in Wadi Abu Hindi east of Al Quds, West Bank and confiscate four water tanks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE34722

title: Israeli settler damage water tanks and destroy trees in Ain Al Baydha, Palestine
description: On 26 October 2023, armed Israeli settlers raid Ain Al Baydha, east of Yuta, Hebron, West Bank, Palestine, damaging over 200 commercial trees, water tanks, and other infrastructure, and looting farming equipment.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE39402 ; PSE38559

title: Israeli settler rioters chop down Palestinian olive trees and destroy water meters in Jenin, West Bank
description: Israeli settler rioters chop down Palestinian-owned olive trees and destroy water meters for agricultural lands in Khirbat al Makhal, southwest of Jenin, in the West Bank on December 31.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE42987

title: Israeli settler rioters destroy water infrastructure in Jalud, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers destroy olive trees, water containers, and irrigation lines in Jalud, Nablus, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE43492

title: Israeli settlers and forces storm villages, demolish water reservoirs in Hebron, West Bank, Palestine
description: On October 14, Israeli settlers, supported by Israeli forces, storm At-Tuba, Isfey at-Tahta, and Maghayir al Abeed villages in Hebron, West Bank, Palestine. They demolish water reservoirs, throw stones at houses, and loot solar panels and batteries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38471

title: Israeli settlers and military cut the main water line that feeds the town of Bayt Lid, West Bank
description: On 3 November, Israeli settlers protected by Israeli forces cut the main water line to Bayt Lid (Tulkarm, West Bank) that feeds the whole town with water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE39569

title: Israeli settlers and soldiers destroy water systems and an outhouse in Khirbat Susiyah, West Bank
description: On 16 October 2023, Israeli settlers and soldiers block all entrances to the village of Khirbat Susiyah (Hebron, West Bank), destroying three main water cisterns, cutting irrigation pipes, and causing a water shortage affecting four dunams of farmland. The settlers also raze olive groves, demolish a stone wall, cut a home's power cable, seal a livestock feed cave, and demolish an outhouse.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE52667

title: Israeli settlers assault Palestinian shepherds and block water access in Mosafer Yuta
description: Israeli settlers, protected by soldiers, assault Palestinian shepherds in Tuba, Mosafer Yuta, and set up a tent near a water well to prevent Palestinians from using the water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE35372

title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinian shepherd and restrict access to a water pond in Ayn al Bayda, West Bank, Palestine
description: A group of Israeli settlers attack a Palestinian shepherd and restrict access to a Palestinian-owned water pond in Ayn al Bayda, Tubas, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE31523

title: Israeli settlers attempt to seize the Ayn Bliebel spring from Palestinian farmers, Tubas, West Bank
description: In an attempt to seize the spring that is used by Palestinian farmers, Israeli settlers carry out construction activities at the water spring of Ayn Bliebel east of Ayn al Bayda, Tubas, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE32342

title: Israeli settlers contaminate Palestinian water resources in Hebron City, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers pollute water resources in Hebron City, West Bank, by spraying chlorine into the water used by Palestinians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE32688

title: Israeli settlers cut down 70 olive seedlings, demolish water wells, and damage Palestinian lands in West Bank
description: Israeli settlers cut down 70 olive seedlings, cut barbed wires, and demolish three water wells on Palestinian owned lands in Khirbat Susiyah (Hebron, West Bank). Soldiers and settlers in military uniform are present at the scene.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38005

title: Israeli settlers damage Palestinian water pipes in Qusra Village, West Bank, Palestine
description: On January 11, 2023, Israeli settlers destroy water pipes that belong to Palestinians in the village of Qusra, Nablus, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE30832

title: Israeli settlers damage Palestinian-owned agricultural equipment, fence, and water tanks in Al Masoudiyah, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers engage in the destruction of Palestinian-owned agricultural equipment and cause damage to a fence and water tanks in the Al Masoudiyah area near Burqah village, Nablus, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE31366

title: Israeli settlers damage Palestinian-owned solar cells, cars, and water tanks in Tubas, West Bank, Palestine
description: Individuals from the Israeli settler community damage solar cells, agricultural equipment, and water tanks owned by Palestinians in Khirbat al Malih village, Tubas, West Bank. They assault a Palestinian before soldiers arrest them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE31987, PSE31986

title: Israeli settlers damage water pipeline to At Tuwani villagte, Hebron, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers raided At Tuwani village (Hebron, West Bank) on November 10 and attacked Palestinian farmers harvesting olives. The settlers also damage the main water pipeline in the village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE40146

title: Israeli settlers damage water tanks and water pipes in Ar Rakiz and Al Mafqara villages, near Hebron, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers raid Palestinian houses in Ar Rakiz and Al Mafqara villages in Mosafer Yuta, near Hebron, West Bank, damaging water tanks, water pipes, solar panels, and car tires.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE40131

title: Israeli settlers demolish a water tank in Ayn al Bayda (West Bank) and cut a water line
description: On October 27, Israeli settlers demolish a water tank in Ayn al Bayda (Tubas, West Bank) and cut a water line.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38800

title: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian almond trees and seize water containers and pipelines in the Al Tabaq area of the West Bank
description: On December 10, Israeli settlers from the Tekoa settlement uproot 15 Palestinian-owned almond trees, cut fences, and seize water containers and pipelines in Al Tabaq area in Tuqu, Bethlehem, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE43457

title: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian property, including water containers and contaminate water wells in West Bank
description: Israeli settlers from the Avigail settlement destroy 30 olive trees and grape vines, water containers, and solar energy power lines, and contaminate water wells in the Umm Turait Bedouin community near Shaab al Butm in Massafer Yuta (Hebron, West Bank)
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38821

title: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian water containers in Hebron area of the West Bank
description: On December 13, Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian water containers in the Shaab Al Batm and Wadi Abu Juhaish area in Massafer Yuta, Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE43471

title: Israeli settlers destroy a Palestinian water well in Massafer Yuta, West Bank
description: Israeli forces demolish houses, a sheep pen, and a water well in Shaab al Batm and Main areas in Massafer Yuta, Hebron, West Bank on November 22.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE41302

title: Israeli settlers destroy agricultural resources, pollute water well, and damage trees on Palestinian land in Shufah, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers from Avnei Hefetz settlement destroy agricultural resources and pollute a water well on a Palestinian-owned land in Shufah, Tulkarm, West Bank. Settlers also destroy fig, grape, and olive trees.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE32727

title: Israeli settlers destroy almonds and olives seedings and irrigation pipelines and loot a water pump in the West Bank
description: On October 27, Israeli settlers cut 2,000 almonds and olives seedings, destroy irrigation pipelines and loot a water pump in Al Thaala near Yuta in the West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38799

title: Israeli settlers destroy an irrigation network and water tanks in Qaryut, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers storm agricultural lands in Qaryut village, Nablus, West Bank and demolish irrigation network and water tanks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE39468

title: Israeli settlers destroy water lines to several Palestinian communities near Yuta, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers destroy main water lines that feed the Al Asfa, Maghayer Al Ubied, and At Tubah communities near Yuta, Hebron, West Bank on December 3.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE42529

title: Israeli settlers destroy water main feeding Khirbat al Thaala, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers from the Karmiel settlement destroy a main water line that feeds Khirbat al Thaala in Mosafer Yuta in Hebron, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE40928

title: Israeli settlers destroy water networks in the West Bank village of Khirbat Tana
description: Israeli settlers destroy two kilometers of water networks in Khirbat Tana village, Nablus, West Bank, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE35597

title: Israeli settlers destroy water supply network in Khallet al-Homur, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers from Maale Amos destroy a water supply network in Khallet al-Homur, near Bethlehem, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE35775

title: Israeli settlers destroy water systems on Palestinian lands in Jalud, West Bank
description: On December 24, Israeli settler rioters chop down 60 olive trees and destroy water containers and irrigation lines on Palestinian-owned lands in Qitaa Kamel in Jalud, Nablus, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID.. PSE43492

title: Israeli settlers from the Maale Amos settlement destroy water pipelines supplying Arab ar Rashaydah, Bethlehem, West Bank
description: On October 11, Israeli settlers from the Maale Amos settlement destroy water pipelines in Arab ar Rashaydah, Bethlehem, West Bank, Palestine, disrupting the town's water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE37022

title: Israeli settlers in Bethlehem, West Bank, destroy water-supply network and vandalize crops in Husan village
description: Israeli settlers in Husan village, Bethlehem, West Bank, destroy a water-supply network belonging to Palestinian farmers and uproot trees and vandalize crops.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE33157

title: Israeli settlers loot water tank in a village in the West Bank
description: Israeli settlers loot water tank in Umm Safa village, Ramallah and Al Bireh, West Bank
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE34445

title: Israeli settlers physically assault a Palestinian in Khirbat Ar Ratheem, West Bank and damage water tanks and pipes.
description: Five masked Israeli settlers in military uniforms physically assault a Palestinian in Khirbat Ar Ratheem (Hebron, West Bank) and damage water tanks and water pipes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE51294 ; PSE50987

title: Israeli settlers pump sewage water onto Palestinian farm near Nahhalin
description: Israeli settlers from Baytar Illit pump sewage water onto a Palestinian-owned farm in Ayan Fares near Nahhalin village, Bethlehem, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE35093

title: Israeli settlers pump wastewater on Palestinian agricultural lands, damaging olive trees and crops
description: Israeli settlers from Shaarei Tikva pump wastewater onto Palestinian agricultural lands east of Qalqilya, near Atmat Bayt Imrin and Azzun village (September 24), causing damage to olive trees and crops.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE36357

title: Israeli settlers raid Palestinian homes in West Bank damaging water tanks
description: Israeli settlers raid Palestinian-owned homes in Isfy (Isfey at-Tahta), Hebron, West Bank, damaging water tanks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38016

title: Israeli settlers raid Palestinian properties in West Banck, cutting down olive trees and looting water pipes
description: On October 22, Israeli settlers from Avigayil settlement raid Khirbet Umm Thret near Sha'ab al-Batum in Hebron, West Bank, Palestine, cutting down olive trees, destroying electricity lines, and looting agricultural equipment and water pipes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE39412

title: Israeli settlers raid and assault Palestinians in West Bank, injuring a man and two children, and damaging water pipes and tanks
description: Israeli settlers raid and assault Palestinians in Sudat Al Thula area east of Yuta, West Bank, injuring a Palestinian man and two children, and causing material damage to water pipes and tanks in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38019

title: Israeli settlers seize water sources and build networks in West Bank, causing extensive damage to Palestinian lands
description: In the Sahel Al-Baqiaa area, east of Tammun town, Tubas, West Bank, Israeli settlers appropriate water sources and construct water-supply networks, resulting in the extensive damage to Palestinian agricultural lands.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE31772

title: Israeli settlers seize water well in Mosafer Yuta, Hebron, and prevent Palestinian access
description: Israeli settlers seize a water well in Mosafer Yuta, east of Yuta in Hebron, West Bank in early June, preventing Palestinian shepherds from reaching it. Settlers also destroy Palestinian-owned crops.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE34165

title: Israeli settlers set fire to a Palestinian-owned house and destroy 800 meters of water pipelines in West Bank
description: Israeli settlers set fire to a Palestinian-owned house and destroy 800 meters of water pipelines in Al Awja (Jericho, West Bank) that feed thousands of dunams of agricultural lands.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE37988

title: Israeli settlers steal Palestinian water pumps and cut pipes in West Bank
description: On October 22, Israeli settlers from the Suseya settlement steal two water pumps and cut water pipes belonging to Palestinians in Khirbat Susiyah, Hebron, West Bank, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE40006

title: Israeli settlers take over water well on Palestinian lands in Hebron, West Bank, Palestine
description: On October 23, Israeli settlers set up tents and take over a water well on Palestinian lands in the Sha'ab al-Batum area in the southern hills of Hebron, West Bank, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE39998

title: Israeli settlers trespass on Palestinian agricultural lands and contaminate water tank in Jericho
description: Israeli settlers move their sheep onto Palestinian agricultural lands in Al Muaarajat al Fawqa, west of Jericho city, and contaminate a water tank with an unknown material.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE34965

title: Israeli settlers vandalize water supply networks in Palestinian Village
description: Israeli settlers vandalize water-supply networks and steal property belonging to Palestinian farmers in the Al Sahel area of Turmus Ayya village in the West Bank (June 3).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE34183

title: Israeli settlers vandalize water supply networks of Palestinian farmers in the Al Sahel area of the West Bank
description: A group of Israeli settlers vandalizes water supply networks belonging to Palestinian farmers in the Al Sahel area of Turmus Ayya village, Ramallah and Al Bireh, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID.PSE34183

title: Israeli settlers, attack homes in Kifil Haris, West Bank, disrupting water supply; clashes injure one, arrest made
description: Israeli settlers, protected by Israeli forces, attack Palestinian homes and properties in Kifil Haris, Salfit, West Bank, causing property damage and disrupting the water supply.
