Palestinian residents retaliate with stone-throwing, and Israeli forces respond with stun grenades and tear gas, injuring a woman. A Palestinian is also arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PSE33013

title: Israeli systems that monitor irrigation and wastewater treatment are hit by a cyberattack, affecting water for farms
description: In April 2023, Israeli systems that monitor irrigation and wastewater treatment in the Hula Valley, the Jordan Valley, and the Galil Sewage Corporation’s are hit by a cyberattack, affecting water for at least ten farms.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Waqas 2023b

title: Israelis destroy water supply line in Al Minya, West Bank
description: On December 22, Israeli forces destroy water supply line network in Al Minya, Bethlehem, West Bank, that supplies water to the village.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE44154

title: Ituru residents in Kenya vandalize Karimenu dam pipeline in protest over lack of access to water for their homes
description: Residents of Ituuru village, Gatundu South, Kiambu, Kenya, vandalize the Karimenu dam water pipeline in a protest over the unsuccessful delivery of water into their taps, and demand an immediate supply of water to their homes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KEN10925

title: JNIM militants destroy water dam with explosives in Boni, Mali
description: On 28 August, JNIM militants set off explosives to destroy a water dam in Boni, Douentza, Mopti, Mali.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MLI30757

title: Jamali community protests in Tando Bago, Pakistan after youth dies in water rights clash
description: Family members and relatives of the Jamali community protest in Tando Bago town, Sindh, Pakistan after a youth dies in a clash over water rights rotation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK134439

title: KRRS members storm a water pumping station, Karnataka, India seeking compensation for lands damaged by a dam
description: Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha (KRRS) members protest and storm the Thumbe water pumping station in Thumbe town, Karnataka, India demanding compensation for farmers whose lands are damaged due to water releases from the dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND147146

title: Kenya security forces conduct airstrike in Saakow, Somalia, injuring two civilians and destroying water facility
description: On September 3, Kenya security forces conduct an airstrike in Saakow, Middle Juba, injuring two civilians and destroying a water company facility and buildings.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SOM42161

title: Kilgoris boys high school students set fire to buildings in protest over water shortage in Kenya
description: Kilgoris boys high school students in Transmara West, Narok, Kenya set fire to a dormitory, dining hall, and classroom to protest a water shortage, leading to the arrest of 10 students and the school's indefinite closure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN12256

title: Kurdish militia (QSD) members prevent water tanks from entering Al Tirwaziya village, Syria
description: Kurdish militia (QSD) members prevent water tanks from entering Al Tirwaziya village in ar Raqqa province, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR116454

title: KwaMaqoma, South Africa residents barricade road demanding safe drinking water, leading police to use teargas and rubber bullets
description: About 1,000 KwaMaqoma residents in Raymond Mhlaba, Amathole, Eastern Cape, including students and school staff, barricade Mbewu Road with burning tires and rocks demanding safe drinking water, leading police to use teargas and rubber bullets as demonstrators retaliate with stones.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF19510

title: Local indigenous opposition to a dam in Brazil that could flood a reserve results in two injuries
description: Indigenous people block access to a dam in Jose Boiteux (Santa Catarina), Brazil by setting obstacles on fire to demonstrate against the closing of the dam over concerns it would flood part of their Indigenous reserve. Military police use tear gas bombs and rubber bullets to disperse the demonstrators, injuring two.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BRA75976

title: Local resident fatally shoots Houthi supervisor in Al Arim village over ownership of a disputed water well
description: A local resident shoots and kills a Houthi supervisor in Al Arim village in Uzlat Bani Mahalhal region, Sanaa, Yemen, after repeated attempts to seize a water well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM80197

title: Local terrorist attack on hydroelectric facilities in the United States
description: A man in Idaho, United States is charged with two counts of destruction of an energy facility after federal prosecutors said he shot a rifle at Hells Canyon Dam and Brownlee Dam electrical systems on the Snake River, damaging both. The dams produce, transmit, store and distribute electricity to Washington, Idaho, and Oregon and the shooting caused over $100,000 in damage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Associated Press (AP) 2023

title: Local women and INC members protest waterlogging in Joshiyara, India and clash with police
description: Local women and INC members protest flooding in Joshiyara village, Uttarakhand, India raising slogans and black flags. They stop the convoy of a cabinet minister and clash with the police.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND136291

title: Man assaulted and killed near Ghazipur, Uttar Pradesh, India over water pipe dispute
description: On October 12, Patidars (landowners) assault and kill a man near the Foxganj area in Ghazipur city (Uttar Pradesh), India over an issue related to drawing a water pipe through the fields.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND142144

title: Man poisons drinking water supplies for soldiers in Barnaul, Altai, Russia
description: Around 20 September 2023, a man in Barnaul, Altai, Russia, poisons the drinking water supplies intended for conscripted soldiers. The Federal Security Services allege that he does this to prove his desire to help Ukrainian war efforts.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS11797

title: Many injuries reported at massive protests in Sainte-Soline, France to stop construction of water reservoirs
description: In late March 2023, as many as 200 protesters and 50 police officers sustain injuries in a battle in Sainte-Soline, France to stop the construction of giant water "basins" to irrigate crops. Protesters throw projectiles including improvised explosives; police respond with tear gas, water cannons, and rubber bullets.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; France 24 2023a ; Gounden and Byers 2023 ; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. FRA24671

title: Maya group seizes aqueduct and dam near Zaragoza, Guatemala; water cut off, clashes reported with police
description: Near Zaragoza, Chimaltenango, for the second consecutive day, members of the 48 Cantones de Totonicapan (Maya indigenous group) take over the Xaya Pixcaya Aqueduct and the El Tesoro dam and cut off the water supply to demand the resignation of the Solicitor General and the head of the Special Prosecutor Against Impunity (FECI). Clashes between participants and officers are reported. Police regain control using tear gas, and the dam is returned to government control on 15 October.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GTM7723 ; GTM7469

title: Mexican residents in Rincon de Tamayo, Guanajuato protest water mismanagement, leading to clashes, injuries, and arrests
description: Mexican residents in Rincon de Tamayo, Guanajuato, protest against the Municipal Water and Sewage Board over water mismanagement, leading to clashes with personnel and police that results in injuries and arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX69621

title: Migrants' protest for water in Ciudad Juarez, Mexico, detention center ends in at least 39 fatalities
description: Migrants detained in Ciudad Juarez, Chihuahua, Mexico, set fire to mattresses in protest of their deportation, poor living conditions, and lack of drinking water. The fire escalates, resulting in the deaths of at least 39 migrants and injuring 29 others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX72530

title: Militants in Burkina Faso attack a village causing multiple fatalities and destroying a water tower at medical center
description: Militants from Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin attack volunteer fighters and civilians in Bilguim-Doure village near Ouargaye, Burkina Faso resulting in multiple fatalities and the destruction of a water tower at a medical center.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO9798

title: Military forces set fire to betel nut farm, destroy water pumps, and property in Ka De Village, Myanmar
description: Military forces burn a betel nut farm, two tents, two water pumps, a tractor, and other property in Ka De village, Palaw township, Myeik district, Tanintharyi region, Myanmar.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR46181

title: Militia positions are shelled at a water station in Thiban, Syria
description: Tribal and clan forces shell Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) militia positions at a water station in Thiban, Deir ez Zor, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR120360

title: Missile attack damages water supply in Kharkiv, Ukraine, cutting water to hospital and homes; 2 injured
description: A water-supply system in Kharkiv, Ukraine is damaged in an enemy missile attack, cutting water to a hospital and private homes, injuring two, in late September.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ukrinform 2023

title: Mob attacks Qhara Qhara indigenous community members in Sucre, Chuquisaca, Bolivia, over water dispute
description: On September 3, in the rural area of Sucre municipality (Chuquisaca), Bolivia 11 to 15 local farming syndicate members attack members of the Qhara Qhara indigenous community with sticks, knives, and stones in Estancia Chullchuta, La Paz municipality. The syndicate members, backed by the local MAS political party, have a long-standing water dispute with the indigenous community.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BOL4869

title: Mobapane residents in Gauteng, South Africa take officials hostage over illegal water disconnections, block reservoir exit
description: In December, residents of Mobapane, Gauteng, South Africa take officials from the Water and Sanitation Department and Tshwane Metro police hostage and threaten them with violence when the officials came to disconnect illegal water connections at the local reservoir. Residents blocked the reservoir exit with rocks, temporarily trapping the officials and police.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF20318

title: Mothers and children protest food and water shortages in Guantanamo, Cuba, leading to violent clashes
description: In Maisi, Guantanamo on October 23, a group of mothers, together with their children, hold a demonstration against the national regime and decrying the lack of water and food. Demonstrators block roads with empty water tanks and police forces intervene, leading to violent altercations. Injuries and arrests are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CUB1017

title: Multiple clashes on the Iran-Afghanistan border over water rights and access; deaths, injuries reported
description: In late May 2023, violent encounters between Iranian and Afghan forces along the border occur related to a water rights dispute on the Helmand River leading to multiple deaths and injuries. In Sasuli, Sistan, and Baluchestan, Taliban forces enter Iranian territory and seize military equipment. Fighting leaves two Iranian police officers and one Taliban militant dead and several other civilians injured. In Makaki village, Kang district, Nimruz, several Taliban fighters, Iranian military, and civilians are killed, and many others are wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID.IRN23337, AFG66609 ; Gambrell 2023

title: Myanmar military launches airstrikes on War Ri Khu Village, damaging religous buildings and water storage
description: The Myanmar military carries out airstrikes on War Ri Khu village in Pekon, damaging the Me Taw Gu Christian religious buildings and water-storage facilities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR45374

title: One death and one injury reported in water dispute in Sabih village, Yemen
description: A dispute over a natural water pool that is filled with rainwater leads to one man shooting and killing another man and injuring his brother in Sabih village in Al Hada district, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM80536

title: One death during protests over water shortages in Mpumalanga, South Africa
description: A protest over water shortages near Piet Retief in Mkhondo, Gert Sibande, Mpumalanga, leads to road blockades with burning objects; police use shots to disperse the crowd, fatally injuring a 17-year-old.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF18196

title: One person killed in explosion of water well mined with an IED by JNIM militants in Sorga, Burkina Faso
description: A water well mined with an IED by JNIM militants (a subgroup of Katibat Mouslimou formed in Burkina Faso) explodes in the area of Sorga, Bogande, Burkina Faso, killing one.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BFO11249

title: Ongoing major armed clashes in Sudan damages water plant and other water infrastructure and kills more than 220 people
description: Armed clashes between Sudan Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces with heavy and medium artillery and anti-aircraft shells in Bahri, Khartoum, Sudan, damages the Bahri water plant and other water infrastructure. At least 220 people, including civilians and soldiers, are killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SUD19739, SUD19712 ; Human Rights Watch 2023

title: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf activists clash with police during demonstrations in Karachi, Pakistan, setting fire to water tankers
description: During demonstrations in Karachi - Shah Faisal, Pakistan, a large number of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf activists throw stones at police personnel and set fire to two water tankers. Police respond with batons and tear gas shells to disperse the demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK83460

title: Pastoralists and Douar Azaghar residents clash over water access in Toumliline, Morocco
description: Pastoralists and Douar Azaghar residents clash in Toumliline, Sidi Ifni, Guelmim-Oued Noun, resulting in two injuries after locals prevent access to water tanks in late August.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MOR7777

title: Police arrest gang leader for killing environmentalist opposing hydroelectric project in Tela, Atlantida, Honduras
description: An environmentalist who advocated for water rights and opposed a hydroelectric project on the Mezapa River that would affect water access for around 30,000 residents is killed in Tela, Altanida, Honduras. Police arrest a Los Conrados gang leader in late August.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. HND8846

title: Police at an environment protest in Panama over the impacts of a copper mine kill four and injure hundreds
description: A protest over the environmental impacts of a major copper mine in Panama, including severe impacts on rivers, is met with violence by local police. Hundreds are injured and four killed over a month of protests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Con las manos en la data 2024

title: Police beat and arrest La LUCHA protesters in Tshikapa, DR Congo over water cost increase
description: Police beat and arrest 10 La LUCHA protesters in Tshikapa (Kasai) Democratic Republic of Congo demonstrating against the public water cost increase by REGIDESO.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. DRC30163

title: Police repress LUCHA protest over water connection fees in Tshikapa, Kasai
description: Police in Tshikapa, Kasai, repress a LUCHA protest, beat and arrest protesters demanding a reduction in the water connection fee, which increased from 220 to 320 USD.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. DRC29826

title: Political dispute in Tamil Nadu, India, over misuse of drinking water leads to violence and one death
description: A Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam councillor and eight of his relatives attack two soldiers on leave near Pochampalli village, Tamil Nadu, India due to an altercation over the misuse of drinking water, killing one of the soldiers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND126508

title: Presumed Islamic State Sahel militants kill civilians at a water well in Burkina Faso.
description: Presumed Islamic State Sahel militants kill four civilians in Lipsi and 13 civilians at a water well in Mira, Sampelga, Burkina Faso.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BFO10800

title: Presumed JNIM militants kill village chief and destroy water tower in Diabatou, Piela, Gnagna
description: Presumed JNIM militants kill the Diabatou village chief, demolish a water tower, and order residents to evacuate within 48 hours.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BFO10149

title: Prison inmates clash over water in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh
description: Prison inmates clash over water in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, resulting in two inmates being injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND132849

title: Pro-Kannada activists protest water release at KRS Dam in Karnataka, India
description: Over 100 pro-Kannada activists from Bengaluru protest and attempt to lay siege to the Krishna Raja Sagara Dam reservoir in Srirangapatna, Mandya, Karnataka, India (August 26), against the state government's decision to release Cauvery river water to Tamil Nadu. Police use force to stop protesters from pushing through barricades and detain them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND139196

title: Protest in Evaton, South Africa, over water shortage leads to one fatality
description: Residents in Evaton, Gauteng, South Africa, barricade roads with burning tires, rocks, and debris to protest water and electricity shortages. A 22-year-old man is fatally shot during the demonstration.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF18463

title: Protest in Fatehabad, India over water barrier construction, gunshots reported
description: Some people protest in Fatehabad district (Haryana), India over the construction of a barrier to stop water from flooding into the village, with gunshots fired during the protest.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND136059

title: Protest in Yauri, Cusco, Peru escalates with mining facility breach and attack on a community water tank
description: A four-day protest against Peru's president Dina Boluarte in Yauri, Cusco, Peru, escalates as demonstrators breach Antapaccay mining facility, targeting a vital water tank supplying local communities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PER5913

title: Protest over water supply issues in Hubballi, India, turns violent as councillors of two parties clash
description: Indian National Congress council members protest inside Hubballi Dharwad Municipal Corporation in Hubballi city, Hubli, Dharwad, Karnataka, India, against water supply issues, but violence ensues as members of the Bharatiya Janata Party physically attack them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND127631

title: Protesters in Azerbaijan block Baku highway demanding irrigation water, resulting in injuries and arrests
description: Villagers from Nabatkend and Orta Mugan, Azerbaijan, stage a protest, blocking the highway to Baku, demanding irrigation water to address the significant crop damage. Police use rubber bullets, causing two protesters to be hospitalized, and arrest around 10 demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID.AZE18096

title: Protesters in Ethiopia demand water and are met with violence from local military, resulting in fatalities and injuries
description: Residents of Welkite, Guraghe, Ethiopian, block a road and throw stones at the Water and Sanitation Office to protest the lack of drinking water, which has been shut off in some parts of the city for over a month. Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples' Region forces fire live bullets at the rioters, killing at least three and wounding 30 people. Several dozen people are later arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. ETH9774, ETH9794

title: Protesters in Guinea block roads, burn tires, and destroy army office demanding water, electricity, roads, and jobs
description: Demonstrators in Dubreka, Guinea block the road and burn tires to demand water, electricity, roads and jobs. They also attack and destroy a local army office. Some arrests are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GUI2681

title: Protesters in Liben, Amhara, Ethiopia stage road blockade demanding water and electricity access. Security forces fire live bull
description: For several consecutive days, young individuals in Liben, West Gojam, Amhara, Ethiopia, block roads with burning tires, stones, and wood, halting vehicles to protest the lack of drinking water supplies and electricity for more than six months. Security forces fire live bullets, killing one and injuring three others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. ETH9836, ETH9837, ETH9838

title: Protesters in Swellendam, South Africa barricade roads and torch municipal office over water and electricity rate hikes
description: Demonstrators in Swellendam, Overberg, Western Cape, South Africa barricade roads with burning tires and torch the municipal head office, protesting increases in municipal rates for water and electricity. Rioters loot and damage shops, clashing with police while armed with sticks and improvised weapons. Police arrest more than 100 suspects on charges of public violence, malicious damage to property, and arson.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF19723

title: Protestors and police clash at a protest over a water treatment plant in Puebla, Mexico
description: In Santa Ana Xalmimilulco, Puebla, Mexico, municipal police, state police, and demonstrators clash at a protest over the construction of a new water treatment plant. The protesters feel the plant will harm the aquifers of the community in Colonia Los Tanques. Six state police are injured and at least eight environmental activists are arrested. According to residents, the police shoot at the rioters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX82388

title: Protestors block road in Chaco, Argentina demanding water access and police respond with rubber bullets
description: In Chaco province, Resistencia, San Fernando, Argentina protestors from the October 27 Social Movement cut off National Route 11 to demand water, electricity, and housing access, and police intervene with rubber bullets to disperse them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. ARG13791

title: Protestors in Mexico face eviction and assault by police during demonstration against farming that contaminates water sources
description: In Sitilpech, Yucatan, Mexico, over 100 residents face eviction and physical assault by more than 150 state and municipal police officers after a protest over farming practices that cause environmental contamination and damage to water sources. The protests continue for two weeks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MEX70925, MEX71452

title: Protests erupt in Bengaluru, India, against release of Cauvery River water to Tamil Nadu; one farmer attempts suicide
description: On September 26, pro-Kannada activists, Kannada Rakshana Vedike members, and farmers protest in Bengaluru, Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka, India, against the state government's decision to release Cauvery river water to Tamil Nadu. One farmer attempts suicide at Freedom Park, and police detain the protesters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND141501

title: RSF cuts off water and electricity supply in Ombada, Khartoum, Sudan
description: The Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group in Sudan, is accused of cutting off the water and electricity supply in Ombada, Um Bada, Khartoum, Sudan, September 18.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD22577

title: RSF militants loot generator from water well station in Omdurman
description: RSF militants loot an electricity generator from the Jaden al-Takamol water well station in Omdurman, Khartoum, and fire shots in the air to disperse residents confronting the looting. No injuries are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD20728

title: RSF militia seize dam near El Fasher, imposing water fines and blocking tanks; Sudan Armed Forces retaliate
description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia seize Goro dam and reservoir near El Fasher (Al Fasher, North Darfur) (November 8) and begin imposing fines on civilians attempting to fetch water. They also prevent water tanks from entering the city after the water supply is cut off. Sudan Armed Forces airstrikes target Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on November 13, with numerous deaths reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD23724 ; SUD23805 ; SUD23716 ; SUD23693

title: RSF shelling in Shambat, Khartoum, Sudan, cuts off electricity and water supply
description: The Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group in Sudan, targets civilians with artillery in Shambat, Khartoum North - Shambat, Bahri, Khartoum, Sudan (October 8) cutting off electricity and water supply. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD23034

title: RSF shells Al Manara water station in Karari, Khartoum, Sudan
description: On 21 October 2023, Rapid Support Forces, a paramilitary group, shelled Al Manara water station in Karari, Karrari, Khartoum, Sudan, causing the station to temporarily go out of service.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD23354

title: Reports that Russia destroys a dam on the Mokri Yali River
description: A dam on the Mokri Yaly River is blown up by Russian forces in mid-June 2023, causing flooding on both banks. Reports are the dam was destroyed to slow down Ukraine’s counteroffensive.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Borger and Sabbagh 2023 ; Brennan 2023 ; BBC News 2023

title: Residents block road in San Antonio, Valparaiso, Chile, demanding municipal drinking water
description: On September 25, in San Antonio, Valparaiso, Chile, residents from the Maranata neighborhood block Road G-82 to demand drinking water deliveries from the municipality. This follows a halt in deliveries after drivers were attacked and injured on September 5th. Demonstrations continue at least until September 28th.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CHI10940

title: Residents clash in Sullana, Peru, over access to water amid prolonged service disruption
description: Residents in Sullana, Piura, Peru, clash outside the EPS Grau water company facilities trying to access potable water due to prolonged service disruption.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PER8133

title: Residents clash with Exaltacion de Colcapirhua board over water well construction amid ongoing border conflict in Bolivia
description: In a border conflict, Sirpita residents clash with Exaltacion de Colcapirhua board during a demonstration against a water well construction in Tiquipaya, Cochabamba, Bolivia. The well is destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BOL4051, BOL4050

title: Residents in Acahuizotla, Guerrero, close water supply valves to demand infrastructure works
description: Residents in Acahuizotla, Guerrero close the pumping valves of the water system supplying the capital, demanding authorities start infrastructure works, and shut down the water system until the construction of the second stage of their water system begins.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX75713

title: Residents in Ciudad de Mexico protest outside National Palace over killings and water access denial
description: On September 21, residents of Xacaxomulco in Ciudad de Mexico - Cuauhtemoc protest outside the National Palace to demand justice for the killing of two men by local leaders. Protesters claim that these leaders have denied them access to water unless they participate in political campaign events.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX79320

title: Residents in Divandarreh, Iran protest drinking water outage, and clash with police
description: Residents in Divandarreh city, Kurdistan, Iran rally in front of the water and sewage department over a three-day drinking water outage, and police use tear gas and arrest some protesters to disperse them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRN23814

title: Residents in Dominican Republic hold a demonstration demanding water supply, higher wages, and a reduction in the cost of living
description: Residents in San Francisco de Macoris, Duarte, Dominican Republic, demand water supply, higher wages, and lower living costs in a demonstration with burning tires and road blockades. Police intervene with firearms, injuring one protester.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. DOM476

title: Residents in Guinea clash with law enforcement over demands for 24-hour electricity and water supplies, resulting in injuries
description: Residents in Boffa, Boffa-Centre, Boffa, Boke, Guinea, block a road with trunks and stones and clash with law enforcement, demanding 24-hour electricity and water supplies while denouncing corruption among the elite and mining companies; three demonstrators are injured by live ammunition fired by special forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GUI2612

title: Residents in Indwe, South Africa, demand water supply and police use rubber bullets injuring 16
description: Residents in Indwe, Emalahleni, Eastern Cape, South Africa block roads using burning tires, demanding water supply and service delivery. The police respond by firing rubber bullets, injuring 16.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF18335

title: Residents in Naranjos, Veracruz, Mexico, block highway to demand water
description: On September 19, around Naranjos, Veracruz, Mexico, more than 300 residents protest for the second day, demanding water and blocking the Tuxpan-Tampico highway near Buena Vista. State police intervene, forcibly evicting residents with pushes, insults, and tear gas. Protesters also report warning shots being fired.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX79351

title: Residents in Omiltemi, Mexico cut off water to the municipality in protest over failure to receive water services or other benef
description: Residents from Omiltemi in Chilpancingo de los Bravo, Guerrero, cut off the pumps that supply water to the municipality to demand compensation for the failure to receive any water, fire protection, or other benefits for 50 years.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX81860 ; Arista 2023

title: Residents in Taizz, Yemen, protest against military over a water well controversy, resulting in four injuries from an armed atta
description: Residents protest in Al Nashmah, Al Maafer, Taizz, Yemen, against former military police for digging water wells near drinking water sources. Armed men fire at protesters, injuring four.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM80081

title: Residents in Yurimaguas, Peru, demand potable water outside the provincial government building and clash with police
description: On September 19, in Yurimaguas, Alto Amazonas, Peru, residents and members of the local Highway Defense Front gather at the provincial government building to demand potable water. Conflicting reports suggest possible clashes between rioters and police and the use of tear gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PER8760

title: Residents protest lack of water access in Castilla, Piura, Peru
description: In Castilla, Piura, Peru, residents throw rocks and reject officials inspecting water works due to the lack of access to water infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PER6466

title: Residents protest water price hike by taking over El Ceibal purification plant in Rocafuerte, Manabi, Ecuador
description: On September 13, residents in Rocafuerte, Manabi, Ecuador, take over the El Ceibal water purification plant to protest a proposed water price hike, causing nearly 400,000 Manabi residents to lose drinking water service until pumping could resume.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. ECU3336

title: Residents protest water shortage in Case Noyale, Mauritius, blocking road, damaging police vehicle, and disrupting water supply
description: 100 residents protest inadequate drinking water supply, blocking a major road with concrete blocks and damaging a police vehicle in Case Noyale - Black River, Mauritius. Water supply disruption is attributed to a damaged pipe.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MUS342

title: Residents resist Houthi forces seizing dam for military use; 72 civilians, including 15 children, abducted, villages blockaded
description: Local residents attempt to resist Houthi forces who are trying to seize a nearby dam to divert water to their military sites. In response, the Houthi forces abduct 72 civilians, including 15 children, and impose a blockade on villages in Shib al Maahirah, Jabal al Mukaydam, and Al Kharabah.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. YEM80513

title: Rioters clash with police in Al Islah district, Thi Qar, Iraq, over water scarcity
description: Clashes erupt between rioters and police in Al Islah district, Thi Qar, Iraq, triggered by water scarcity. Police reinforcements are deployed and use live ammunition to disperse the riot. Tires are set on fire by the rioters. Casualties unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IRQ45205 ; Crisis 24 2023

title: Rioters in Bangladesh set fire to a water tanker during a clash between opposition parties and police forces
description: Rioters set fire to a water tanker in Shajahanpur, Bangladesh during a clash between opposition parties and police forces, demanding resignation of the Awami League government.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BGD25742

title: Rioters in Iraq protesting the lack of jobs shut down water projects in Thi Qar, Iraq and fire on security forces, killing one
description: Dozens riot in the Bada area of Shatrah district, Thi Qar, Iraq over lack of jobs. The rioters close water projects in the area and when security forces try to disperse the riot and reopen the water projects rioters open fire at the security forces killing one and injuring another.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRQ49717

title: Russia again attacks the Dnipro hydropower plant in February 2023
description: The Dnipro hydropower plant near Zaporizhzhia is attacked by Russia in February 2023.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; BBC News 2023

title: Russia attacks a dam in Terny, Donetsk, Ukraine
description: On 1 November 2023, Russian forces conduct an airstrike near a dam in Terny, Donetsk region, Ukraine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR140000

title: Russia attacks a water pumping station in Vovchansk, Ukraine
description: Russian forces shell Vovchansk, Kharkiv, Ukraine, damaging two generators of the local water pumping station.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR137429

title: Russia attacks the water supply system of Nikopol, Ukraine
description: Russian forces launch four drone strikes and shell Nikopol, Ukraine, damaging the water supply system on November 22.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR137351

title: Russia destroys the dam of the Karliv reservoir in Donetsk region of Ukraine
description: Russia destroys the Karlivka dam of the Karlov reservoir in Donetsk region of Ukraine, northwest of Pervomaisky, May 25, 2023.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Top War 2023 ; Kesaieva and Hallam 2023

title: Russian airstrikes in Idleb, Syria, target HTS positions and water station, killing two
description: On 22 August, Russian warplanes target Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) militants and an old water station used by displaced families near Array village in Idleb countryside, Syria, killing two and injuring three others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR116170

title: Russian forces damage water pumping station in attack in Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine
description: Russian forces damage a water pumping station in an attack to the Chervonohryhorivka community in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR89685

title: Russian forces shell Druzhkivka, damaging residential area and water supply networks
description: Russian forces shell Druzhkivka, Donetsk, damaging water supply networks along with residential areas, two multi-story buildings, two private houses, and road surfaces; no casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR109905

title: Russian forces shell Kharkiv, damaging infrastructure and a water pipe
description: Russian forces again shell Kharkiv, damaging residential buildings, a gas station, water pipe, and cars, with no reported casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR106763

title: Russian forces shell Kharkiv, damaging water pipe
description: Russian forces shell Kharkiv on June 5, damaging water pipe and buildings.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR106626

title: Russian forces shell Kherson region, inflicting damage on civilian infrastructure, water pipelines, and industrial facilities
description: Russian forces shell Kherson region, damaging civilian infrastructure, water pipelines, and an industrial enterprise in 10 separate attacks. One civilian is killed and one is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR102722

title: Russian forces shell Marhanets, Ukraine, disrupting water supplies for 35,000
description: Russian forces shell Marhanets in the Dnipropetrovsk region, Ukraine, damaging private houses, a gas pipeline, and a power line connected to the water pumping station, resulting in water-supply disruption for 35,000 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. UKR92941

title: Russian forces shell Uhroyidy in the Sumy region, Ukraine, damaging a water tower
description: Shelling by Russian forces in Uhroyidy in the Sumy region, Ukraine, damages a water tower and other civilian structures.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID.UKR105624

title: Russian missile strike hits bottled water warehouse, killing seven civilians
description: Russian forces fire cruise missiles at Kryvyi Rih, Dnipropetrovsk, hitting a bottled water warehouse and killing seven civilians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR107579

title: Russians manipulate the water levels in the reservoir behind Kakhovka Dam, affecting civilian and agricultural water supplies
description: Russian forces manipulate water releases from the Kakhovka Dam in February 2023 to hinder Ukrainian military operations and threaten the water supplies for the cities of Enerhodar, Melitopol, and Berdiansk, which rely on water from the reservoir. Water supply for irrigation and power plant cooling at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant is also threatened.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Brumfiel et al. 2023

title: Shelling in Idleb Province, Syria, injures civilians and damages water truck
description: Syrian regime members shell residential neighborhoods and a market in Jisr-Ash-Shugur city, Idleb province, Syria, injuring seven to ten civilians, including two children and two women, and causing material damage, including to a water truck. No fatalities are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR118476

title: Sinaloa Cartel in Mexico cuts off water and electricity to force community into joining roadblocks in territorial dispute
description: Members of the Sinaloa Cartel in Chiapas, Mexico cut off water and electricity in the community to pressure community members to join roadblocks and participate in a dispute over territorial control.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX82425

title: Soldiers destroy water pump at Mahar Myat Muni pagoda in Kyauktaw, Myanmar
description: Four soldiers stationed at Mahar Myat Muni pagoda in Kyauktaw township, Myanmar destroy a water pump.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. MMR44916

title: South African residents barricade roads with burning items in Parys, Ngwathe, Free State, protesting water shortage
description: Residents in Parys, Ngwathe, Free State, South Africa, barricade roads with burning items to protest water shortage, resulting in property damage by rioters; police intervene, arresting five for violence.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF18185, SAF18186

title: South Sudan Accedes to Nile CFA
description: South Sudan accedes (ratifies) to the Nile Basin Cooperative Framework Agreement in 2024, expanding the upstream bloc and further marginalizing Egypt's and Sudan's historical veto position over Nile development.
countries: South Sudan, Ethiopia, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Republic of South Sudan National Legislative Assembly Ratification of Nile CFA (2023).

title: Sudanese militia (RSF) work to prevent Chadian refugees from accessing a nearby water source in Central Darfur, Sudan
description: Sudanese militia (RSF) work to prevent Chadian refugees in Um Shalaiya IDP camp from accessing a nearby water source in Central Darfur, Sudan after clashes between RSF and the area's residents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD23088

title: Supporters clash in Kerugoya, Kenya over county water project vandalism
description: On August 22, supporters of the Kirinyaga governor clash with supporters of the Kirinyaga women's representative and a Baragwi member of the county assembly (MCA) in Kerugoya, Kenya, pelting stones as the representative goes to answer police summons over county water project vandalism, resulting in injuries to the representative, the MCA, and several supporters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN12365

title: Suspected Jama'a Nusrat ul-Islam wa al-Muslimin members destroy two water pumps in Barsalogho, Burkina Faso
description: Individuals believed to be associated with the Jama'a Nusrat ul-Islam wa al-Muslimin destroy two water pumps in the town of Barsalogho, Sanmatenga, Burkina Faso.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO9271

title: Suspected Kuki militants fire at Meitei farmers collecting irrigation water in Bishnupur, Manipur, India
description: Suspected Kuki militants fire at Meitei farmers heading to Phubala Maning High Canal in Bishnupur, Manipur, India to collect irrigation water amid ongoing ethnic violence, firing from bunkers between Haotak Khullen and Chingfe Ching villages, with no casualties reported. Water-supply systems are also sabotaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND134427 ; IND132818

title: Suspected group for support of Islam and Muslim militants sabotage power lines in Gayeri, Burkina Faso, disrupting water system
description: Around January 8, 2023, suspected Group for Support of Islam and Muslims militants sabotage power lines in Gayeri, Burkina Faso, disrupting water systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID.BFO8976

title: Suspected militants from Islamic State Sahel vandalize water pump station, causing water scarcity in Dori, Burkina Faso
description: Suspected militants from Islamic State Sahel vandalize the water pump station located at the dam in Yakouta, Dori, Burkina Faso, resulting in a water scarcity affecting the town of Dori.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BFO9522

title: Taliban militants kill water suppliers to security check posts in North Waziristan, Pakistan
description: On August 21, Taliban Pakistan (TTP) assailants shoot dead two water suppliers at security check posts in Hamzoni village, North Waziristan, Pakistan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK134773

title: Teacher assaults Dalit student over drinking water from teacher's camper in Bayana, Rajasthan, India
description: In caste-based violence in Bayana town, Rajasthan, India, a Gujjar caste teacher assaults and injures a Dalit student for drinking water from a teachers' camper. This prompts another protest by family members, villagers, and Bhim Army members and the teacher is assaulted.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND141112 ; IND141193 ; IND140082

title: The Balochistan Liberation Army attacks a water transport tractor at Hazara dam construction area in Harnai district, Balochista
description: The Balochistan Liberation Army orchestrates an improvised explosive device attack on a tractor transporting water to workers at the Hazara dam construction site in Harnai district, Balochistan, Pakistan. The driver is fatally wounded, and three more individuals suffer injuries as a result of the incident.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. PAK81842

title: The Iraqi army damages Kurdish irrigation pipes and supplies and orders villagers not to cultivate crops in a repeat of an event
description: In a repeat of an incident from June 2023, the Iraqi army raids Balkanah village in Kirkuk damaging irrigation supplies and pipes in August. The army detains two workers and their guards and the Iraqi commander in charge instructs villagers not to cultivate their crops.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRQ48350

title: The Iraqi army destroys Kurdish irrigation equipment and supplies and orders villagers not to cultivate crops
description: Iraqi army soldiers destroy irrigation equipment belonging to Kurdish farmers in the Balkanah village of Kirkuk. The farmers are not allowed to irrigate the fields and only do so at night to avoid their equipment being confiscated by the army.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRQ47032

title: The Israeli military begins pumping water into tunnel complexes in Gaza
description: The Israeli military begins pumping seawater into Hamas' tunnel complex in Gaza in an effort to destroy them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Jerusalem Post 2023

title: The Syrian military shells the Jeb ad Dam near Aleppo
description: Syrian military shells the Jeb ad Dam in rural western Aleppo with artillery.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR118229

title: The city of Odesa, Ukraine loses water supply after Russian attacks on energy and water systems
description: The entire city of Odesa, Ukraine population 1 million, is temporarily left without water in late January 2023 after Russian attacks on energy and water systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UNHCR 2023

title: The cutoff of fuel and destruction of energy facilities in Gaza forces the closure of the last remaining ocean desalination plan
description: The last remaining seawater desalination plant, out of the four servicing central and southern Gaza, shuts down on October 15 due to lack of fuel. Gaza’s only remaining operational wastewater treatment plant (out of five), which relies on solar energy, is also forced to shut down. Untreated sewage is being discharged to the sea and most of the 65 sewage pumping stations are not operational.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN OCHA 2023a

title: The hactivist group Cyber Av3ngers claims to have hacked 10 water treatment stations in Israel on October 30
description: The hactivist group Cyber Av3ngers claims to have hacked 10 water treatment stations in Israel on October 30.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Waqas 2023a

title: The massive Kakhovka Dam on the Dnipro River is destroyed, causing massive upstream and downstream consequences
description: The massive Kakhovka Dam on the Dnipro River is destroyed on June 6, 2023, presumably by Russian occupying forces, causing massive flooding, more than 50 deaths, and ecological devastation downstream, and cutting off water supply for cities, power plants, and irrigation systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; New York Times, The 2023

title: The water supply for the village of Troitskoye, Russia is damaged by Ukrainian shelling
description: Ukrainian military shells the village of Troitskoye (Korenevskiy, Kursk), Russia, damaging the water tower and cutting water supply for 300 people (October 31).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS12537

title: Three fishers disrupt desalination plant construction in Valparaiso, injuring one worker
description: Three fishers disrupt construction of Aconcagua desalination plant between Puchuncavi and Quintero communes in Valparaiso, throwing stones at machinery. This follows eviction of Bahia Narau Quintero-Puchuncavi Fishermen's Federation members on August 3, who block access to area for 86 days over environmental concerns. One worker sustains injury; no fatalities occur.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CHI11036

title: Tiquipaya residents protest against water-treatment plant relocation in Bolivia
description: Police clash with residents of Tiquipaya, Cochabamba, Bolivia, protesting the relocation of a water-treatment plant.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BOL4270

title: Townspeople in Rachaya al Foukhar, Lebanon protest attacks on water station facilities
description: Townspeople in Rachaya al Foukhar (Hasbeiya, Lebanon) demonstrate outside the water station, condemning repeated attacks on its facilities, after unknown persons destroy a building and the electricity generator, stealing its contents and disrupting water pumping to the town and agricultural sector.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. LBN15058

title: Tribal and clan forces attack QSD positions at Al-Hawayij water station in Deir ez Zor
description: On October 11, 2023, tribal and clan forces attack QSD positions at a water station in Al-Hawayij town, Deir ez Zor countryside, with rocket shells and machine guns. Casualties remain unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR119367

title: Tribal families clash over water dispute in Al-Hasakeh, Syria injuring two
description: Clashes over a water dispute between two tribal families who are cousins erupt in Khashman neighborhood in Al-Hasakeh city, Syria involving roadblocks with burning tires, resulting in two injuries and no fatalities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR115827

title: Tribesmen clash over control of Marbun water dam in Al Said City
description: Al Yaslim and Al Bazaal tribesmen clash in Al Said city's market, Shabwah, over control of the Marbun water dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM80912

title: Tribesmen clash over water source in Amran, Yemen leaving two dead and eight injured
description: Tribesmen from Al Abraq and Qaynah villages clash over a water source in Jabal Salil, Amran, Yemen following disputes over water supply, resulting in two dead and eight injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM81197

title: Turkish drone attacks on Syrian power stations cut water supplies to a million Syrians
description: Electricity systems in northeastern Syria are attacked by Turkey, cutting power and water to a million Syrians. The attacks extend from October 2023 to January 2024.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Khoshnaw et al., 2024 ; Human Rights Watch 2023

title: Turkish fighters shell the Khan Eljabal water station in rural Al Hasakeh, Syria
description: On October 7, Turkish fighters shell the Khan Eljabal (Khan Siri) water station in rural Al Hasakeh, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR119213

title: Two civilians are injured in groundwater pumping dispute in Iraq
description: An intra-tribal clash over groundwater injures two women in the Shatra district, Thi Qar, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID.IRQ46662

title: Two families clash over water distribution in Mahmood Raqi, Afghanistan, wounding six
description: Two families clash over drought-affected water distribution in Mahmood Raqi, Kapisa, Afghanistan wounding six.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. AFG66773

title: Two soldiers in Benin killed by JNIM militants as they go to fetch water
description: On December 12, an IED likely planted by JNIM militants (a subgroup of Katibat Mouslimou formed in Burkina Faso) kill two Benin soldiers who were going to fetch water in the vicinity of Bako Maka, Alibori.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BEN1260

title: Ukraine attacks a Russian military outpost at an occupied water tower in Donetsk, Ukraine
description: On November 26 Russian military forces occupy a water tower in Horlivka, Donetsk, Ukraine, which is then attacked by Ukrainian forces, destroying a machine gun position and ammunication depot.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR138097

title: Ukraine intercepts a Russian missile attack on Kryvyi Rih dam
description: On 22 June 2023, Ukrainian military forces intercept Russian air-launched 'Kinzhal' missiles over the Dnipropetrovsk region aimed at the dam near Kryvyi Rih.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR109065

title: Ukrainian drone strike damages water tower in Dolgoe, Belgorod, Russia
description: Ukrainian forces use a drone to strike the village of Dolgoe, Valuyki I Valuyskiy, Belgorod, Russia, damaging a water tower on September 16.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS11697

title: Ukrainian forces shell Gordeevka, Kursk, damaging power lines and water main
description: Ukrainian forces shell Gordeevka, Kursk, September 14, damaging power lines and a water main.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS11545

title: Ukrainian forces shell Novaya Tavolzhanka, Belgorod, Russia, damaging water tower and electricity supply lines
description: Ukrainian forces shell Novaya Tavolzhanka, Shebekinskiy, Belgorod, Russia (September 26), with seven artillery rounds, damaging electricity supply lines, a water tower, and a house. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS11974

title: Ukrainian forces shell village in Kursk, Russia, damaging water tower and infrastructure
description: On 29 September 2023, Ukrainian forces shell the village of Gogolevka, Sudzhanskiy, Kursk, Russia, causing damage to houses, a former school, a maternity ward, electricity lines, and a water tower. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS12016

title: Ukrainian military shells Belgorod, causing casualties and water pipes damages
description: Ukrainian military shells Belgorod with over 13 rockets, killing one man and damaging houses, cars, and gas and water pipes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS13308

title: Ukrainian military shells damage a water tower in Russia
description: Ukrainian military shell the village of Novostroyevka-Pervaya, Belgorod, Russia damaging a water tower, November 8.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS12638

title: Unidentified armed individuals attack water tanks in Bzal, Akkar, Lebanon, over clan feuds
description: Unidentified armed individuals attack a house and vehicle with grenades and fire at water tanks and solar panels in Bzal, Akkar, Lebanon, likely due to old clan feuds (September 27). One grenade explodes causing material damage, but there are no casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. LBN15120

title: Unidentified militia invade and vandalize Kaakong Primary School, including water tank, in Kibish, Turkana, Kenya
description: A group of unidentified militia carry out acts of vandalism on buildings and equipment, including the water tank, at Kaakong Primary School in Kibish, Turkana, Kenya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. KEN11061

title: VASKI staff and police assault residents and headman over water issue in Ipekyolu, Turkey
description: Van Metropolitan Municipality Water and Sewage Administration Directorate staff and police officers physically assault the headman and residents of Kecanis neighborhood during a visit to Ipekyolu, Van, to address a water problem.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. TUR30089

title: Vandalism of Aguas del Altiplano pipe causes water cut for 7,000 in Iquique, Chile
description: Unidentified individuals vandalize an Aguas del Altiplano pipe in the Tadeo Haenke area of Iquique, Tarapaca, Chile cutting water to over 7,000 people for several hours.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CHI10792

title: Villagers clash over water drainage and river diversion in Sirsa, Haryana, India
description: Villagers from Farwai and Vaidwala clash with those from Panihari and Burj Karamgarh near Panihari village, Haryana, India over opening an underpass to drain water and divert the Ghaggar river, resulting in four injuries. Police deploy to control the situation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND135978

title: Villagers in Bazhou, China, clash with police over flood response and compensation
description: On 22 August, villagers in Bazhou city (Langfang, Hebei, China) break windows and barge into a government office after learning that police beat women from their village who were protesting on August 8, prompting police to attack the demonstrators, hospitalizing two and causing injuries to others. The demonstration with around 3,000 participants protested government responses to typhoon-induced floods that destroyed homes, killed at least 29, and were worsened by the discharge of excess water from Beijing and Xiongan, with villagers demanding adequate government compensation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CHN13600 ; CHN13651

title: Villagers protest in Gaobeidian, China over flood response, clash with police, with at least one injury reported
description: Villagers in Gaobeidian city (Hebei, China) protest outside the local government's office over the flood response. Police beat one resident and arrest at least one demonstrator. The protests follow typhoon-induced floods that destroyed homes and killed at least 29. Villagers are angry at the media's downplaying of the disaster and the central government's discharge of excess water into their village, demanding adequate compensation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CHN13610

title: Violence between Meiteis and Kuki communities in India include attacks on the Maphou Dam
description: Armed Kuki assailants attack villages near Maphou Dam located in Thoubal River and Meitei villages, India. The Gorkha regiment of the Indian army and local police forces retaliate with several rounds of firing. Numerous injuries are reported. The dam has been at the center of disputes between Meiteis and Kuki communities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND145943 ; Bordoloi 2024

title: Violence in Sudan cuts water supplies and electricity to Khartoum
description: Violence between the regular Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) cuts electricity and water supplies to large portions of the city of Khartoum (June 2023).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; France 24 2023b

title: Violent clash between Hawazmah-Baggara and Nuba clans in Sudan over access to water kills as many as nine and injuring others
description: The Hawazmah-Baggara and Nuba clans in Sundan clash when Nuba prevent the pastoralists from watering livestock and limit access to water sources in Al Tabldiat and Abu Zaid neighborhoods in Dilling. Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) shell the region killing as many as nine and wounding eight more, destroying houses and displacing residents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD24061

title: Violent clash over water resources in Muzabd, North Kordofan, Sudan claims two lives and injures seven
description: Two rival ethnic groups engage in a violent confrontation in Muzabd, Gharb Bara, North Kordofan, Sudan, due to a conflict over access to water resources. The clash results in two deaths, including an off-duty police officer, and leaves seven individuals injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SUD19440

title: Violent ethnic clashes claim seven lives in Tulu Guled, Ethiopia, over grazing land and access to water
description: Violent ethnic clashes erupt in Tulu Guled, Ethiopia, resulting in seven fatalities and numerous injuries. The conflict is rooted in disputes over grazing land and water resources. In response, the Oromia regional government initiates a restructuring of the contested land, dividing it into two administrative district to accommodate the Oromo and Somali pastoralist communities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. ETH9834

title: Violent protest and military deployments over the construction of a canal along the Massacre River and a dispute over the border
description: In Ouanaminthe, Nord-Est, Haiti residents protest the presence of Dominican soldiers at the Haitian-Dominican border during a dispute over the construction of a canal on the Massacre River. Military are deployed in the area and during the demonstration, rioters set up barricades of burning tires, dig a ditch, and attack the departmental head of the Protected Areas of Surveillance Brigade (BSAP) as he intervened to prevent the rioters from throwing stones at the soldiers. The Dominican soldiers try to remove the barricades and point firearms at the rioters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. HTI5476 ; ID. DOM624

title: Wagner mercenaries attack the village of Lougui, Mali, killing seven and destroying the water tank
description: Wagner mercenaries attack the village of Lougui (Niono, Segou), Mali, killing seven civilians including the chief of the village and a marabout. The mercenaries also destroy the water tower and houses, and loot goods.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MLI31092

title: Wagner mercenaries kill three pastoralists watering livestock at a well in the village of Inbogitane, Mali
description: Wagner mercenaries kill three pastoralists at a well in the village of Inbogitane (Kidal), Mali. The pastoralists were watering their livestock when they were killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MLI31007

title: Water allocation conflict erupts between villagers in Chilaura Nowapara Village, Sylhet, Bangladesh
description: On January 4, 2023, a dispute between villagers over the allocation of water for cultivation erupts in Chilaura Nowapara village, Jagannathpur upazila, Sunamganj, Sylhet, Bangladesh.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. BGD23466

title: Water collection dispute triggers clash in Baglung Municipality, Nepal, and residents attempt to destroy water tank
description: A water collection dispute sparks a clash between hundreds of locals from two districts in Baglung municipality, Baglung district, Nepal. Residents of Ratnechaur, from Beni municipality of Myagdi district, try to destroy Baglung's water tank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. NEP21608

title: Water containers are booby-trapped with explosives by IS militants in Iraq
description: Popular Mobilization Forces defuse five booby-trapped water containers in Ramadi, western Al Anbar, Iraq. The booby traps contained TNT and other high-explosives and were left behind by IS militants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRQ51000

title: Water defender shot and killed by armed men in Guapinol, Colon
description: In Guapinol, Colon, unidentified armed men shoot and kill a water defender, the brother of another environmental activist killed earlier in the year.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. HND8576

title: Water dispute in Chupki village leads to violent clash
description: In Chupki village, Ludhiana, Punjab, three people clash with two others using lathis, crude weapons, and a gun after being confronted about diverting water supply to their fields, resulting in all five individuals sustaining injuries, including a bullet wound.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND133927

title: Water drainage conflict sparks clash between families, leaving five injured in Jammu and Kashmir, India
description: A confrontation erupts between two families in the Khalis Kullian area of Miran Sahib block, Jammu district, Jammu and Kashmir, India, due to a dispute over water drainage. The clash leaves five individuals injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND127686

title: Water pipe dispute escalates to armed clash in Nassriya, Iraq, resulting in one fatality
description: On September 27, a dispute over a water pipe escalates into an armed clash between cousins in Nassriya city, Iraq, resulting in the death of a Thi Qar Oil Company employee. Police arrest one person involved in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRQ48844

title: Water pipelines in Port Sudan are attacked
description: A water crisis worsens in Port Sudan, Sudan after attacks on the city's water pipelines by unknown persons. The neighborhoods of Shargi, Hadal, Salbouna, and Abu Hashish are worst affected.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Dabanga 2023

title: Water pipes in Umm Tuba, West Bank are destroyed by Israeli settlers
description: On 27 October, Israeli settlers storm the Umm Tuba neighborhood, Al Quds, West Bank and demolish water pipes in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE38825

title: Water shortage protest in Lichtenburg, South Africa, leads to truck burning and 24 arrests
description: In Lichtenburg, Ngaka Modiri Molema, North West, South Africa, residents burn trucks and loot amid water shortage protest, leading to 24 arrests.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. SAF18203

title: Water supplies in three districts in Ukraine are cut off by attacks on civilian infrastructure
description: In late February 2023, water supplies in the Druzhkivka, Mykolaiv, and Bashtanka districts are only available irregularly and are regularly cut off by direct damage, attacks on electricity systems, and inability to repair infrastructure damaged by the war.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Left Bank Analytics 2023

title: Water tanker and machinery set on fire by People's Liberation Front of India members in Ranchi district, Jharkhand, India
description: People's Liberation Front of India members set fire to construction equipment, including a water tanker, near Orga railway station in the Ranchi district, Jharkhand.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IND125522

title: Water treatment factory and infrastructure destroyed in Gaza City during the Israeli attack on Gaza
description: Fire destroys the Abdul Salam Yaseen Water Company factory on the outskirts of Gaza City during the Israeli invasion of Gaza. This water treatment plant produced domestic, agricultural, and industrial water and wastewater pumps and equipment for large-scale water desalination units and plants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Zwijnenburg 2023a ; 2023b

title: Water truck is attacked near the Romo gold mines in Kenya, killing two
description: Suspected Turkana ethnic militia shoot at a truck ferrying water to the Romo gold mines at Chepiririch, Kenya by the Turkwel River killing two and wounding three others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN12800

title: West Papua National Liberation Army damages water pipes and disrupts access to clean water in Oksibil District, Indonesia
description: Disruption of the clean water supply to the Oksibil district in Papua province, Indonesia, results from an attack on a water pipe by the West Papua National Liberation Army.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID. IDN11341, IDN11342

title: Workers at a water station in Sudan are abducted resulting in a water shortage
description: A group called Rapid Support Forces abducts water station workers from Soba Water Station in Khartoum - Soba West, Sudan, resulting in a water shortage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al 2010 ID.SUD20473

title: Workers protest Arazati drinking water plant project in Montevideo
description: Unionized workers at the State Sanitary Works (OSE) company in Montevideo demonstrate against the Arazati drinking water plant project, alleging it doesn't ensure water supply, is unconstitutional, and privatizes the water service. Demonstrators clash with police, vandalize the OSE building, and throw smoke bombs.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. URU391

title: 10 Palestinians killed while filling water near mosque in Gaza City, Palestine
description: 10 Palestinians are killed, likely by Israeli artillery shelling, while filling water near the Al Shamaa mosque, Gaza City, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE55116

title: 10 killed in water dispute between clan militias in Ceel Dheere, Somalia
description: Militias from Hawadle and Abgal clans clash over water sources in Ceel Dheere, Somalia, killing 10 people and leaving several others injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SOM47264

title: A Russian-linked group launches cyberattack on Texas water utilities, USA
description: In April 2024, a Russian-linked "hactivist" group attempts to disrupt operations at several Texas utilities, including the Muleshoe water utility, temporarily disrupting their operations and causing a water tank to overflow.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lyngaas 2024

title: A Sudanese nomad watering cattle is killed at water source in Unity, South Sudan
description: Armed youth attack and kill a Sudanese nomad watering his cattle in Pan-Akuach, Unity. The assailants flee when security forces arrive at the scene.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SSD12959

title: A clash over the lack of water services in the eThekwini Municipality township in South Africa injures many protesters
description: During a protest over the lack of water services, about two dozen residents of the Phoenix township in South Africa are injured in a confrontation with the South African Police Service (SAPS) and Durban Metro Police. The protest was planned by the Voice of Phoenix, a civic movement concerned with the failures of water service delivery in the eThekwini Municipality township.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Naidoo 2024

title: A device detonates in a water truck in Hama, Syria, killing one and injuring two
description: An explosive device planted by unknown gunmen in previous clashes detonates in a water truck near Shakkushiyah, Hama countryside. A man is killed, and his wife and sister are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR133677

title: A pro-Russia hacktivist group gains control over computers at Texas, USA water and wastewater systems causing flooding
description: On 18 January 2024, a pro-Russia hactivist group accesses control systems at two Texas water facilities and tampers with water pumps and alarms, causing water to run past designated shutoff levels and overfill storage tanks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Office of the Director of National Intelligence 2024

title: A protest over control and access to water between Delhi and Haryana, India turns violent with police response
description: A protest in front of the Delhi Jal Board (DJB) filling pump in Okhla against the water crisis in Delhi is met by police using water cannons on the protestors. At the same time, Delhi Water Minister Atishi launches a fast alleging Haryana is failing to release Delhi's rightful share of water in Yamuna, and the BJP is ramping up protests over water shortages and the black marketing of water in Delhi.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; India Today Video 2024

title: A series of Russian missile attacks on the water systems of Donbas region of Ukraine cut water supplies to 260,000 people
description: Russian forces cause significant damage to two water facilities of the Donbas region of Ukraine, cutting water to Slovyansk, Kramatorsk, Druzhkivka, Kostyantynivka, and surrounding settlements affecting access for 260,000 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ANTIKOR 2024d

title: A union leader is killed in dispute over control of drinking water pipes in Solidaridad, Mexico
description: Armed assailants kill a man in Valle de Chalco Solidaridad, Mexico. Authorities link the attack to an ongoing rivalry between labor unions competing for control over drinking water pipelines.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX82977

title: A water pump is stolen and equipment damaged during a clash with police in Napeitom, Kenya
description: Unidentified assailants clash with police, destroy a water pump, and steal equipment in Napeitom, Kenya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN13508

title: A water treatment facility in Kansas, U.S., experiences a cybersecurity incident disrupting operations
description: The water treatment facility in Arkansas City, Kansas experiences a cybersecurity incident on 22 September 2024, leading to a temporary switch to manual operations. Despite the incident, there was no disruption to the water supply or service delivery.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nair 2024

title: A water-management facility in Gaza is attacked, damaging the plant and killing the town's mayor
description: Air strikes by Israel hit a water-management facility serving Nuseirat municipality in Gaza, damaging the plant and killing the town's mayor who was in the plant at the time.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nishin 2024

title: A woman is injured in a water access protest in Ecatepec de Morelos, Mexico
description: Residents in Ecatepec de Morelos, Mexico, protest to demand drinking water services. During the protest, a car strikes a female demonstrator, who receives medical care and the driver is arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX83193

title: Abducted Water and Sanitation deputy director found dead in Pretoria, South Africa
description: The deputy director of the Water and Sanitation Department in Pretoria, South Africa, is carjacked and abducted by unknown assailants. Police trace the vehicle to Johannesburg and arrest a 53 year old suspect. The victim is later found dead.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF21593 ; Mlangeni 2024
