title: Mother and daughter assaulted by neighbors over water dispute in Panvel, India
description: A mother and her 18-year-old daughter are stripped and assaulted by their neighbors over a water dispute in Panvel, India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND173290

title: Municipal water truck driver injured during labor strikes in Durban, South Africa
description: Unknown suspects attack a municipal water truck driver in Phoenix, Durban, during strikes led by the South African Municipal Workers' Union. The driver is hospitalized.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF20820

title: Municipal water truck set on fire, driver hospitalized amid threats to mayor in Piura, Peru
description: Unidentified suspects torch a municipal water truck in La Union district, Piura, injuring the driver who is taken to hospital. Police state the attack is linked to threats against the district mayor, which have been ongoing since 2023.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PER10113

title: Municipal workers sabotage water infrastructure in Durban, South Africa, amid wage strike
description: Members of South African Municipal Workers' Union in Durban vandalize and sabotage water infrastructure during five days of protests over wage increases.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF20774, SAF20743, SAF20820

title: Myanmar military abducts men digging water well in Minhla Township, Myanmar
description: Four men digging a water well in Shwe Zan Pyayt village, Minhla Township, are abducted by the Myanmar military.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MMR86344

title: Myanmar rebel group kills three soldiers fetching water in Monywa, Myanmar
description: A rebel group, Brave Heart Army, ambushes Myanmar military troops from the Baw Di Ta Htaung camp in the town of Monywa as they go to collect water. Three Myanmar soldiers are killed, and weapons and ammunition are seized.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MMR81489

title: Myanmar soldier fleeing border police attacks villagers fetching water in Maungdaw Township, Myanmar, injuring one
description: A Myanmar military soldier fleeing border police throws a grenade at locals collecting water from a pond near Kan Thar Yar village in Maungdaw Township, Myanmar. One person is injured in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MMR85695

title: Myanmar troops injured in ambush while collecting water in Tilin Township, Myanmar
description: Fighters from the People’s Defence Force (PDF) ambush Myanmar soldiers from the Yae Myet Ni police station in Tilin Township, Myanmar, while they fetch water. Two soldiers are injured after exchanging fire for around 15 minutes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MMR81575

title: National Defence Forces (QDW) member executed after attempt to poison water tanks in northern Homs, Syria
description: A National Defence Forces (QDW) member is executed by firing squad after being captured attempting to poison regime-affiliated water tanks in rural northern Homs, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR123469

title: Naxal-Maoist rebels abducted four Jal Jeevan Mission drinking water scheme workers in Sukma, India
description: Naxal-Maoist rebels abduct at least four workers involved in the Jal Jeevan Mission drinking water scheme in a forest in the Sukma district of Chhattisgarh, India. The armed rebels also seized a JBC machine used for excavating, obstructing the development project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND150290 ; O.rganiser 2024

title: Neighbors kill farmer with axe over construction of water channel in Gujarat, India
description: Neighbors attack and kill a farmer with an axe in Ranigam village in Gujarat, India, during an argument over building a water channel on his farmland.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND162309

title: Nigerian airstrikes kill ISWAP fighters and destroy water vessels in Marte, Nigeria
description: The Nigerian Air Force conducts airstrikes on Islamic State – West Africa Province (ISWAP) sites in Marte, in Borno State, Nigeria, killing over 40 fighters including five commanders. Vehicles, water vessels and a dispensary are destroyed in the attacks.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIG38188

title: Nile CFA Enters into Force with 5 Ratifications
description: The Nile Basin Cooperative Framework Agreement formally enters into force after receiving its sixth ratification (South Sudan), creating a new legally binding institutional framework for the Nile while Egypt and Sudan remain outside.
countries: Ethiopia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nile River Basin Commission (NRBC) Constitutive Entry into Force (October 13, 2024).

title: Officer injured in clash between farmers and activists at demonstration against water reservoirs in Sainte-Soline, France
description: In Sainte-Soline, France, 30 members of the Stop Megabasins collective rally to oppose large water reservoirs and celebrate a Bordeaux court ruling that declared four of them illegal. Tensions flare when farmers supporting the reservoirs stage a counter-demonstration, leading to clashes. Gendarmes intervene to separate the groups, and one officer is slightly injured in the process. A 26-year-old activist is later arrested and charged with assaulting the officer.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. FRA37173

title: On two days in April 2024, a pro-Russian hactivist group attacks two US wastewater systems
description: On 20 and 24 April 2024, a pro-Russian hactivist group posted videos showing an attacker remotely manipulating settings on human-machine interfaces (HMIs) in two US wastewater systems and one US energy company.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Office of the Director of National Intelligence 2024

title: One injured as police detain protesters over waterlogging in Charkhi Dadri, India
description: A protester is injured while being detained by police during a demonstration against waterlogging in Charkhi Dadri, India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND168599

title: One killed in clash over water drainage in Jalil Pur, India
description: Two groups fight with sticks in a dispute over water drainage in the village of Jalil Pur, India. One person is killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND170187

title: One killed, seven injured in dispute over water entering fields in Gothana, India
description: Two groups fight with sticks in the village of Gothana, India, in a dispute over water entering fields. A school headmaster is killed and seven others are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND171643

title: One person injured as Moruleng residents protest for water in North West, South Africa
description: Residents in Moruleng village in North West, South Africa, protest to demand access to water from the municipality. Witnesses say a protester is injured after falling from a truck amid disputed accounts of whether the driver tried to run over the crowd.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF21739

title: One person injured in protests by residents over water shortages in Retreat, Jamaica
description: Residents of Retreat, Jamaica, protest lack of water by blocking the main road between New Hope and Negril with debris. A motorcyclist crashes into tree trunks that were placed on the road and is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. JAM2480

title: Orma militia attack Degodia herders at water point in Bura, Kenya, killing five and injuring others
description: Suspected Orma militia ambush Degodia herders at a water point near El Niqa, in Bura, Kenya. Armed with arrows and machetes, they kill five people, including a child, and injure others. The attack is linked to tensions following the arrest of Orma community members.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN15519

title: Palestinian family fetching water from spring attacked by Israeli settlers and dogs in Jericho, Palestine
description: A Palestinian family fetching water from a spring is attacked by Israeli settlers in Jericho, West Bank, Palestine. The settlers hurl stones at the family and set their dogs on them before stealing their belongings.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE58643

title: Palestinians clash with Israeli settlers after water pipeline destroyed in Ramallah and Al Bireh, Palestine
description: A clash breaks out between Palestinians and Israeli settlers in Ramallah and Al Bireh, Palestine, after dozens of Israeli settlers destroy water pipelines that supply Palestinian houses. The settlers withdraw from the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE55428

title: Police beat protesters in Delfan, Iran, during demonstration over textile factory's impact on water resources
description: Residents and farmers from the villages of Hasanabad and Aliabad, in Delfan county, Iran, protest at the Red Crescent Delfan textile factory construction site against the loss pastures and the drying up of water resources. Police beat the protesters with batons in response. Several people are taken to hospital for their injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRN26376

title: Police fire shots at protest over water shortage in Boane, Mozambique
description: Residents in Boane, Mozambique, block a road over water and power shortages. Police intervene with dogs and fire shots. A young man leading the protest is detained for several hours; police tear his shirt and he is left with bruises.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MZM4215

title: Police injure Tibetans during protest over dam project that will displace villagers in Dege County, China
description: Over 300 Tibetans protest outside a local town hall in Dege County, China, demanding the government withdraw its plans to build a dam that will displace residents of at least two villages and affect six monasteries. Police disperse the crowds with electronic batons, pepper sprays and water cannons, causing injuries. More than 100 demonstrators are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CHN14666

title: Police kill militiaman after shooting of a boy collecting water in Gwadabawa, Nigeria
description: After Sokoto militia shoot a boy in the leg while he is collecting water, the police and vigilantes engage the militia in a firefight on the outskirts of a village in Gwadabawa, Nigeria. The battle results in the death of one militiaman.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIG34999

title: Police officer injured in protest over water shortages in Antananarivo, Madagascar
description: Residents in Antananarivo, Madagascar, stage a protest over water shortages and load shedding affecting their neighborhood. They block roads with burning tires, damage cars and throw stones at police officers, injuring at least one.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MAG4054

title: Police officer injured in violent protest over lack of potable water and poor sanitation in Jalandhar, India
description: A police officer is injured during a protest at the Jalandhar Municipal Corporation office, condemning them for their failure to provide clean drinking water or resolve ongoing problems with sewerage and drainage systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND167614 ; Hindustan Times 2024

title: Pro-Iran militias shell water station in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: Local pro-Iranian militia members shell a water station in Sfireh Tahtani, rural Deir ez-Zor, Syria. The station burns but no casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR128504

title: Pro-regime militias fire rocket at water drilling rig on the Euphrates river in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: Pro-regime militias fire a rocket at a Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) water drilling rig on the Euphrates river bank near Thiban water station in Deir ez-Zor, Syria. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR133733

title: Protest against a water supply project in Kerala, India, leaves official injured
description: Indian National Congress members, including two members of the Legislative Assembly, protest against a Kerala Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation (KINFRA) water supply project in Aluva, Kerala. Demonstrators assault KINFRA officials, leaving one with minor injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND151543

title: Protest against company over contaminating and looting water supplies in Veracruz, Mexico, turns deadly
description: Residents and farmers in San Antonio Limón, Veracruz, Mexico, rally against a company accused of polluting aquifers and stealing large volumes of water. Police move to disperse the crowd and gunfire is reported. Authorities confirm two deaths, with farmer groups claiming three, and multiple people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX88135

title: Protest erupts in Meerut, India, after three killed in farm irrigation dispute
description: Relatives and residents block the Muradnagar–Ganganahar bridge in Meerut, India, protesting the recent shooting deaths of three people in a farm irrigation dispute.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND160855

title: Protest over construction of the Kikar-Navgaon drinking water scheme injures police and guard in Himachal Pradesh, India
description: A demonstration against the Kikar-Navgaon drinking water scheme in a village in Himachal Pradesh, India results in seven policemen and one home guard being injured. Around 400 locals associated with the Ali Khud Bachao Sangarsh Samiti (Save the Ali River Tributary Struggle Committee) pelt stones and machinery at the police, claiming the scheme would deprive other areas of drinking water. The police and guard are injured when they try to stop protesters from entering the construction site of the water scheme.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND150815

title: Protest over poor water services leaves one hospitalized in Ataq, Yemen
description: Residents in Ataq, Yemen, march to the governor’s house in protest over poor water service. Guards intervene with force, with a protester requiring hospital treatment for their injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM86273

title: Protest over water shortages and power cuts injures two in Ambohibao, Madagascar
description: Residents in Ambohibao, Madagascar, block roads and burn tires to protest water shortages and power cuts. Protesters throw stones at gendarmes who respond with tear gas. At least two people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MAG4037

title: Protesters and motorists clash during roadblock demonstration over month-long water shortages in García, Mexico
description: Residents of García, Mexico, block an intersection to protest water shortages in their neighborhoods that have lasted for over a month. The roadblock causes long traffic delays, and some vehicles are reportedly damaged as drivers attempt to use the shoulder. Protesters refuse to clear the road until authorities restore the water supply, sparking confrontations and fights with motorists.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Cuevas 2024

title: Protesters block railways and detain railway staff over water access in Chapulco, Mexico
description: Protesters block railways and detain railway staff in Chapulco, Mexico, to protest the railway company's impact on a local well and water access.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX93678

title: Protesters block water flow in protest over leaks from poor quality infrastructure in Jerusalen area, Mexico
description: Protesters in the vicinity of Jerusalen, Mexico, block water flow in a demonstration over water leaking onto their lands as a result of poor quality infrastructure and the failure of the federal government and CONAGUA (National Water Commission) to meet commitments made with users of a local irrigation scheme.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX95755

title: Protesters clash with police during demonstration over chemical pollution of stream in Ludhiana, India; one injured
description: Thousands gather in Ludhiana, India, to protest the discharge of chemical waste into the Buddha Nala stream, demanding the closure of common effluent treatment plants at dyeing units. A counter-protest is staged by thousands of dyeing unit employees. Over 2,000 police are deployed, who use network jammers to restrict communication and baton charge the protesters. One person sustains a head injury and 150 people are detained.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND173043 ; Kaur 2024

title: Protesters detain mayor and block highway over pork producer's water use in San Antonio Limon, Mexico
description: Residents and farmers in San Antonio Limon, Mexico, detain the mayor during a fourth consecutive day of protests against pork production company 'Granjas Carroll' and its use of water from sources along the Veracruz-Puebla border. Members of the Movement in Defense of the Water of the Free-Eastern Basin block a highway with stones, banners and vehicles, demanding justice for two farmers killed during clashes at a protest last week.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX89389

title: Protesters in Carraipia, Colombia block access to water plant, disrupting water supply to Maicao
description: Residents near Carraipia, La Guajira, Colombia, block the Jordan Water Treatment Plant for three days to protest service fees and energy systems, disrupting water supply to Maicao.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. COL26936

title: Protesters injured in clash over access to water and electricity in Durban, South Africa
description: Students and residents barricade streets with burning tires and throw objects at the police over water and electricity shortages in Durban, South Africa. Police arrest five demonstrators and some are left injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF20846

title: Protesters injured in clash with police over lack of water and services in Free State, South Africa
description: Residents block a highway in Botshabelo, Free State, demanding water, electricity and basic services. Police disperse the crowd with rubber bullets and arrest 12. A community leader says some protesters were beaten, and there are allegations live ammunition was used.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF20748 ; Semela 2024

title: Protesters set fire to water facility in demonstration against general election results in Chokwe, Mozambique
description: Supporters of the Optimist Party for the Development of Mozambique (PODEMOS) set fire to a state-owned water facility in Chokwe, Mozambique, to protest the election of the Mozambique Liberation Front (FRELIMO) in the 2024 general election. They also set fire to the home of a police officer and FRELIMO supporter.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MZM4575

title: Protesters shut water valves at Morbe Dam, cutting water supply to the city of Navi Mumbai, India
description: Villagers from multiple communities in Maharashtra, India, force entry into the Morbe Dam premises. During the demonstration, they close valves to cut off the water supply to Navi Mumbai. The action is part of a protest over compensation and employment.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND161293

title: Protesters threaten self-immolation over lake encroachment clearance in Chennai, India
description: Several residents threaten to set themselves on fire during a protest against the Water Resources Department’s drive to clear structures encroaching on Retteri Lake in Chennai, India. The protesters strongly oppose the court-ordered clearance, which is part of a plan to transform the lake into a source of drinking water. Police officers intervene to prevent self-immolation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND162755

title: Protesters violently detained outside municipal palace while demanding access to water in Ixtaczoquitlan, Mexico
description: A group of 16 residents, including a disabled youth, protesting for water access in front of the municipal palace in Ixtaczoquitlan, Mexico, are violently detained by police. They are released after four hours following further demonstrations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX86986

title: Protesters who demand access to adequate drinking water services in Tabasco, Mexico, are attacked and beaten by security forces
description: Residents of Dos Montes and La Palma, Tabasco, Mexico, block the Villahermosa-Macuspana highway demanding access to adequate drinking water services. In efforts to try and reopen the roads, officials from the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection use tear gas and beat the protesters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX85898

title: QDW fighters and pro-Iranian militias attack QSD water station checkpoint in rural Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: National Defence Forces (QDW), pro-Iranian militias from Al Hafl and Tribal and Clan Forces, attacks a Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) position in a water station in rural Deir ez-Zor, Syria, sparking clashes and causing material damage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR136057

title: QSD forces detain civilian over alleged water station breach in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) arrests a civilian in Basira village, Deir ez-Zor, Syria, accusing him of helping facilitate breaches at the town’s water station.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR133030

title: QSD forces shell water station and farm in rural Aleppo, Syria, injuring two
description: Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) shells a water station and a farm near the town of Rasm Abbud Jaftalak in Aleppo, Syria, injuring two civilians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR138674

title: QSD forces shell water station in rural Aleppo, Syria
description: Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) shells a water station in the town of Al-Khafsa, in rural Aleppo, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR138727

title: QSD seizes control of Babiri water station following clash with JWS in rural Aleppo, Syria
description: Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) makes advances in northern Aleppo, Syria, taking control of Babiri water station in Jirah Airbase after clashing with Syrian National Army (JWS) members.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR137434

title: Qush Tepa canal project employees killed in office attack in Sheberghan, Afghanistan
description: Gunmen kill an engineer and a cleaner working for a private contractor in Sheberghan, Afghanistan. Although linked to the Qush Tepa canal project, the Taliban claims the victims were not involved.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. AFG67949

title: RSF commander injured as SAF reclaims control of reservoir in Khazan Golo, Sudan
description: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), with the support of Darfur Joint Forces (JSAMF), launches airstrikes and retakes Khazan Golo water reservoir from Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Water pipes are reopened. An RSF commander is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD28112

title: RSF destroys water sources and attack civilians in Wad Abu Salih, Sudan
description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) attacks residents of Wad Abu Salih, Sudan, forcing them out of their homes and destroying their water sources. One civilian is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD31499

title: RSF seizes water resources and kill civilians during attack in Sidraha, Sudan
description: During a raid in Sidraha, Sudan, Rapid Support Forces (RSF) takes control of water resources, cuts communications, loots property and livestock and kills seven civilians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD27616

title: RSF shelling in Khartoum kills two and damages Al Manara water station
description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) targets Al Manara water station in Al Jarrafa, Khartoum, Sudan. The attack leaves two dead and damages the water station.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD27167

title: RSF shuts down water supply in North Darfur, Sudan, after clashes between RSF and SAF
description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and allied Arab militias battle Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) near Khazan Golo in North Darfur, Sudan. RSF captures the reservoir and closes water pipes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD28100

title: Rebel forces kill two Myanmar soldiers pumping water in Zin Bar village, Tanintharyi, Myanmar
description: Joint forces of the Dawei National Liberation Army (DNLA), Kaw Thoo Lei Army (KTLA), and Shwe Be Lone PDF (SBL) attack 10 Myanmar soldiers pumping water in Zin Bar village, Myanmar. Two soldiers are killed and one injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MMR81558

title: Refugees injured in clash over water access at migration center in Agadez, Niger
description: Ivoirian and Sierra Leonese refugees fight over water at an International Organization for Migration office in Agadez, Niger. Both groups sustain injuries. Police intervene with tear gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIR31159

title: Regime airstrikes target water station and other infrastructure in Idlib, Syria
description: Regime warplanes launch airstrikes on the city of Idlib, Syria, targeting a water station, schools, and other infrastructure while regime fighters attack the city with missiles. Four civilians are killed and 19 are wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR136756

title: Regime fighters target civilian vehicle and water tank with guided missile in Idlib, Syria
description: Regime forces fire a guided missile near Maaret Al Naasan in northern Idlib, Syria. A civilian vehicle and a water tank are struck, causing material damage but no casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR128466

title: Resident shot dead by Houthi supervisor during dispute over water project in Ar Rujum, Yemen
description: A resident of Ar Rujum, Yemen, dies after being shot five times by a Houthi supervisor in a row over a water project. The incident takes place at the home of a sheikh and is witnessed by tribal mediators who had been attempting to resolve the dispute.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM94509

title: Residents and farmers break dike in protest over water shortages in Paita, Peru
description: Over 500 farmers and residents from several localities in Paita, Peru, gather at a water company site and break a dike supplying water to the La Huaca district, redirecting it to irrigate their crops and nearby areas. The action is part of a protest against regional water shortages, with demonstrators calling on the government and the Ministry of Agriculture for assistance.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PER10840

title: Residents beaten by police during protest over water reconnection in Oaxaca, Mexico
description: Residents of colonia Benito Juarez in Salina Cruz, Oaxaca, stage a protest to demand reconnection to a municipal drinking water pipeline. Military and municipal police intervene violently, beating demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX84191

title: Residents block highway and clash with police in Talara, Peru, after 10 days without drinking water
description: Dozens of residents in Talara, Peru, block a highway with burning objects to protest being without drinking water for 10 days and the lack of water tanks to supply their area. Clashes break out when police arrive to clear the road, with protesters alleging they were assaulted by officers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PER10843

title: Residents brawl and riot over water shortages in Garcia, Mexico
description: Residents of Garcia, Mexico, close a road and protest water shortages in the Paseo de Capellanía, Riberas, and Bugambilias neighborhoods which have reportedly lasted more than a week. The protest turns violent when cars begin to drive through the blockade, leading to brawling and rioting.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Estrada 2024

title: Residents in Altamira, Mexico, attempt to lynch suspected water thieves
description: Residents of Altamira, Mexico, detain three people accused of water theft in an apartment building. They begin destroying their vehicle in an attempted lynching. The suspects flee the scene.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX88615

title: Residents in Jharkhand, India, tie public health contractor to pole during protest over water supply
description: Giridih residents in Jharkhand, India, demonstrate against the irregular water supply. During the protest, they tie a Public Health Engineering Department contractor to a pole for over an hour. The contractor is released after an executive engineer promises improvements.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND160222

title: Residents irrigating fields attacked over water dispute in Etah, India
description: Residents from the village of Tajpur Tigra are suspected of attacking people irrigating their fields in Nagla Mali, India, in a dispute over water supply. They throw stones and fire weapons, leaving six injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND169763

title: Residents of Ludhiana, India, protest for two days over water shortages and assault municipal worker
description: Residents in Ludhiana, India, demonstrate against water shortages for two days. During the rally, protesters burn an effigy and assault a municipal employee.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND158620, IND158621

title: Residents of Saint Albans, South Africa, protest lack of water services; police respond with rubber bullets and tear gas
description: Over 200 residents in Saint Albans, South Africa, block a road with burning debris to protest inadequate electricity, water, and sanitation facilities. Demonstrators torch a signboard and hurl rocks at a truck that forced its way past the roadblock. Police disperse the crowd with rubber bullets and tear gas.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF21603

title: Residents protesting water shortages beaten by police in Boyeros, Cuba
description: Residents block traffic in Boyeros, Cuba, protesting week-long blackouts and water shortages. Police intervene and beat some of the demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CUB1256

title: Residents' demands for drinking water lead to physical altercations with police in in Naucalpan de Juarez, Mexico
description: Residents of several Colonias in Naucalpan de Juarez, Mexico, block a road demanding access to drinking water. There are some reports of physical altercations as state police intervene, surrounding and dispersing the protesters.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX92760 ; Gonzalez 2024

title: Rocket fire from Lebanon damages water infrastructure in Metulla, Israel
description: Hezbollah missiles and shrapnel hit Metulla, Israel, damaging homes and water and power infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. ISR42195

title: Russia attacks Dnipro Dam again
description: In another attempt to destroy Ukrainian energy and water systems, Russia launches another attack on the Dnipro Hydroelectric Power plant near Zaporizhzhia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Macalpine 2024

title: Russia attacks Kyiv Dam with drones and missiles
description: In an attack on Ukrainian energy infrastruture, Russia attacks the Kyiv Dam resulting in civilian casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Macalpine 2024

title: Russia attacks the Dnipro Dam on World Water Day causing massive damage and power outages
description: Ukraine's largest dam, the Dnipro Dam, is attacked by Russia, causing massive damage and leading to extensive blackouts in Ukraine. This attack falls on World Water Day.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR152844 ; British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) 2024

title: Russia destroys a bridge in Ukraine, cutting water supply and ending operation of a filtration plant
description: Russia destroys a bridge between Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad, Donesk region of Ukraine, interrupting the water supply and ending operation of a modular filtration plant.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR174286 ; ANTIKOR 2024b

title: Russian airstrike damages water supply infrastructure in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine
description: Russian forces carry out an airstrike on a rural settlement in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine, damaging water supply infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR155239

title: Russian airstrike destroys water pumping station in Lyman, Ukraine
description: Russian forces use a reconnaissance drone to guide an airstrike targeting a water pumping station in the city of Lyman in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine. The pumping station is destroyed in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR220375

title: Russian airstrike destroys water station in rural Idlib, Syria; two workers wounded
description: Russian forces carry out an airstrike on a water station in in rural Idlib, Syria, wounding two workers and destroying the facility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR134473

title: Russian airstrike disrupts water supply in Bilopillia, Ukraine
description: Russian forces carry out an airstrike on Bilopillia, Sumy. The strike damages a critical component of the city's water supply system, leading to water outages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR153448

title: Russian airstrikes hit water station in Idlib, Syria
description: Russian aircraft strike the town of Upper Sheikh Sindyan and a water station in the Idlib countryside. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR130108

title: Russian attack on Kryvyi Rhi, Ukraine cuts power and water throughout the city
description: Energy infrastructure in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine is attacked by Russian missiles, cutting power to pumping stations and water networks and cutting water to the entire city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ANTIKOR 2024f

title: Russian attack on oil depot leads to major oil spill into the Nemyshlia River, Ukraine
description: More than 3,000 tons of oil spill into the Nemyshlia River in the Kharkiv Region after a Russian attack on Ukrainian energy systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Menshikova and Grebinik 2024

title: Russian attacks Kremenchuk hydroelectric station in Ukraine
description: Russian missile attack damages the Kremenchuk hydroelectric station in Ukraine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ANTIKOR 2024e

title: Russian attacks in Kharkiv, Ukraine leave many without water or electricity
description: Water systems are cut off by a wave of Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure in Kharkiv, Ukraine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Segura 2024

title: Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy systems disrupt water supply in the city of Nikopol
description: Due to Russian attacks, an overhead power line is severed, the water supply station is cut off in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast and disruptions in the water supply in the city of Nikopol are recorded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ukrainska Pravda 2024

title: Russian drone strike on Kherson, Ukraine, damages water facility and injures two
description: Russian forces carry out a drone strike on a rural settlement in Kherson, Ukraine, damaging a water supply facility and injuring two civilians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR166239

title: Russian drone strikes damage water infrastructure leading to widespread outages in Sumy, Ukraine
description: Russian drone strikes in Sumy, Ukraine, damage power and water infrastructure, causing widespread water outages across the city. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR184094

title: Russian forces destroy Ternivska Dam at the Kurakhove Reservoir, flooding villages in Donetsk, Ukraine
description: Ukraine reports that Russia has attacked and severely damaged Ternivska Dam at the Kurakhove Reservoir on the Vovcha River, causing flooding downstream.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Kulakova 2024 ; Varga 2024

title: Russian forces hit Ochakiv, Ukraine, with incendiary weapon; water supply disrupted
description: Russian forces carry out a strike on Ochakiv, Ukraine, using an unidentified incendiary weapon. The attack sparks fires and disrupts water services. Casualties unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR179467

title: Russian missile attacks cut water and electricity to 280,000 people in the Rivne region of Ukraine
description: Russian missile attacks cut water and electricity to the Rivne region of Ukraine, affecting 280,000 people.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ANTIKOR 2024h

title: Russian missile strike damages power plant, interrupting heat and water supply in Ivano-Frankivsk, Ukraine
description: Russian forces carry out a missile strike on Burshtynska thermal power plant in the Ivano-Frankivsk region of Ukraine. The strike disrupts heat generation and hot water supply and injures an employee.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR153488

title: Russian missile strikes damage critical infrastructure in Hlukhiv, Ukraine, disrupting water and power
description: Russian forces launch missile and drone strikes on Hlukhiv in Sumy, Ukraine. The attack damages infrastructure, disrupting water and electricity services.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR182395

title: Russian rocket attack on Odesa, Ukraine cuts water and power to the city
description: A Russian missile attack on Odesa, Ukraine cuts water and power to the city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ANTIKOR 2024g

title: Russian shelling and drone strikes damage water pipeline in Chuhuiv, Ukraine
description: Russian forces carry out drone and missile strikes on Chuhuiv, in the Kharkiv region of Ukraine, damaging medical and residential buildings and a water pipeline.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR162823

title: Russian shelling damages water filtration plant near Karlivka, Ukraine
description: Russian forces shell an area near Karlivka, in the Donetsk region of Ukraine, damaging a water filtration station.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR145760

title: Russian shelling disrupts water and power and injures two in Kherson, Ukraine
description: Russian shelling damages infrastructure in Kherson, Ukraine, leading to water and power disruption. Two civilians are wounded in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR171217

title: Russian shelling kills a civilian and damages water facility in Sumy, Ukraine
description: Russian shelling in Sumy, Ukraine, damages a water facility, medical facilities and a school. One civilian is killed and another wounded.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR151466

title: SAF airstrikes in North Darfur, Sudan, destroy water sources, kills five civilians and cattle
description: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) carries out airstrikes in Koma, North Darfur, Sudan. Five civilians are killed, water sources are destroyed, and over 150 cattle perish in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD29468

title: SAF airstrikes kill seven and destroy water station in Koma, Sudan
description: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) carries out airstrikes on Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Koma in Sudan's North Darfur State, destroying a water station and killing seven civilians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD31337

title: SAF airstrikes kill six and destroy water sources in Kebkabiya, Sudan
description: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) launches airstrikes on Kebkabiya, North Darfur, destroying water sources and killing six civilians.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD31584

title: SAF airstrikes target water station in Abu Hamira, Sudan
description: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) carries out airstrikes on Telis water station in Abu Hamira, Sudan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD29411

title: SAF drone strikes damage Tuti Island water station in Khartoum, Sudan
description: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) conducts drone strikes on Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Khartoum‚ Sudan, damaging a water station in Tuti Island. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD30206

title: Separatists destroy water supply machinery in Kech, Pakistan
description: Unidentified assailants (possibly Baloch separatists) use explosives to destroy water supply equipment in the Tagran Maskingar area of Kech, Pakistan, which they claim is used by military forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK145426

title: Settlers assault Palestinian and seize water containers in Ayn Samiya, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers beat a Palestinian in Ayn Samiya, Palestine, and confiscate 15 tons of animal feed, water containers, and a vehicle.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE52065

title: Settlers attack Palestinian homes and empty water containers in Arab al Mlihat, Palestine
description: About 15 Israeli settlers raid homes in the Arab al Mlihat community in West Bank, Palestine, emptying seven water containers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE51307

title: Settlers under protection of Israeli forces destroy main water pipelines in Umm al Khayr, Palestine
description: While under protection of Israeli forces, Israeli settlers destroy pipelines that supply water to houses in the village of Umm al Khayr in West Bank, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE55727

title: Seven Frontier Corps personnel ambushed and killed while fetching water in Kurram, Pakistan
description: Militants linked to the Pakistani Taliban (TTP) ambush Frontier Corps personnel near the Barani River in Central Kurram, Pakistan, as they fetch water, killing seven and wounding two.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK145870

title: Seven injured during protest over water diversion in Damavand, Iran
description: Residents of Aru, near Damavand, Iran, rally against plans to divert their spring water to other towns. Police clash with villagers. One civilian sustains a gunshot wound and six officers are injured as villagers throw stones. At least 15 protesters are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRN27696

title: Seven injured in clan dispute over water sources in Xalfooley village, Somalia
description: Hawadle and Abgal clan militias fight in the village of Xalfooley, Somalia, over water sources and grazing pastures. Seven Hawadle members are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SOM47189

title: Shelling damages water pipelines and injures one in Nova Kakhovka, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian forces shell the occupied city of Nova Kakhovka, Ukraine, damaging water and gas pipelines and injuring one civilian.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR216746

title: Shelling injures six and damages hospital water tanks in Beit Lahiya, Palestine
description: Israeli forces shell Kamal Odwan Hospital in Beit Lahiya, Palestine, damaging water tanks and injuring six children.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE63036

title: Siblings fatally shot on return from fetching water in Matswale, South Africa
description: A brother and sister on their way home from fetching water are shot and killed by an unknown assailant in Matswale, South Africa. The attack occurs amid water shortages in the area which have left residents without consistent water supply to their homes. Locals report that water is sometimes available only at night, forcing people to make the journey in darkness and leaving them vulnerable to attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Chiguvare 2024

title: Six injured in clash over distribution of agricultural irrigation water in Tando Muhammad Khan, Pakistan
description: Members of the Lashari and Nizamani groups fight in Shah Bukhsh Lashari village in Tando Muhammad Khan District, Pakistan, during a dispute over farm water allocation. Six people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK143103

title: Six killed in airstrike on water filling point in Jabalya, Palestine
description: An Israeli airstrike targets a group of people fetching water in Jabalya, Palestine, killing six.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE62069

title: Solar energy for water stations looted during clash in Babanussa, Sudan
description: Solar energy systems for water stations are looted during a battle between Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Babanussa, Sudan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD25940

title: Soldier killed in JNIM attack on water truck in Intahaka, Mali
description: JNIM (Salafi-jihadist group) militants attack a Malian military vehicle transporting water in the village of Intahaka, Mali. One soldier is killed and militants seize the vehicle.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MLI33356

title: South African water and sanitation employee is shot while working on a water-supply reservoir
description: A water sector worker for the eThekwini Municipality in South Africa was shot while working on a reservoir providing water to the community, in what is thought to be a "water mafia" attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Democratic Alliance 2024

title: Strikes damage water pipes in Shebekino, Russia; one killed, two injured
description: Ukrainian drones and artillery hit Shebekino in Belgorod, Russia, damaging gas and water pipes. One civilian is killed and two others are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS23970

title: Students in Analamanga, Madagascar, protest water and power shortages with road barricades; one injured
description: Students in Antananarivo, Madagascar, block roads with burning tires to demand improved water and electricity services and infrastructure. Police disperse the crowd with tear gas; one student is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MAG3792

title: Students injured during protest over poor infrastructure and water supply in Vontovorona, Madagascar
description: Students protest outside their university campus in Vontovorona, Madagascar, to demand the university make improvements to campus infrastructure, including drinking water supply, electricity and internet connection. They barricade the campus entrance with burning tires and tables, and throw stones at gendarmes who respond with tear gas. Several students are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MAG3826, MAG3818, MAG3827, MAG3828

title: Sudanese Armed Forces airstrikes destroy farms and water wells in Kebkabiya, North Darfur
description: Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) conducts airstrikes on Kebkabiya, Sudan. Farms and water wells are destroyed in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD27753

title: Suicide drones target water truck on Afes axis in Idlib, Syria
description: Regime forces in Syria launch four suicide drones along the Afes axis in rural Idlib, hitting civilian and rebel positions. One drone targets a water truck, and another drone is shot down by rebels.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR130022

title: Syrian Democratic Forces shells water stations and depots in Jarablus, Syria
description: Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) attacks water depots and stations with heavy machine guns in Jarablus, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR124346

title: Syrian rebel group attacks and abducts farmer over failed water delivery in northwestern Aleppo, Syria
description: Armed militants from the 9th Division, a Syrian rebel group, accost and attack a farmer in Kura village in northwestern Aleppo, Syria, after accusing him of failing to deliver water to the group's headquarters. They abduct the victim, whose whereabouts remain unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR128609

title: Syrian regime forces shell water station in Deir ez-Zor countryside, Syria, injuring one
description: Syrian regime forces shell a water station in Abu Hardoub village in Deir ez-Zor, Syria. One civilian is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR132615

title: Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan militants kill a security guard while he collects water in Dera Ismail Khan, Pakistan
description: Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) militants fatally shoot a security guard in the town of Drazinda in Dera Ismail Khan District, Pakistan. The guard is attacked while fetching water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK138698

title: The "water tanker mafia" in Kwa-Zulu Natal, South Africa is accused of actively sabotaging water infrastructure
description: The "water tanker mafia" in Kwa-Zulu Natal, South Africa is accused of actively sabotaging water infrastructure to continue and prolong contracts with municipalities to deliver water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Jacobs 2024

title: The Bani Saeed water pipeline from Israel to Gaza is shut down due to damage from military activities
description: The Bani Saeed Mekorot water line from Israel to Gaza is shut down for 10 days after sustaining damage due to military activities, cutting expected water supply to zero.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Water and Development Partnership Programme 2025

title: The Coastal Municipalities Water Utility headquarters and main water testing laboratory are destroyed by Israeli bombs
description: The Coastal Municipalities Water Utility headquarters and main water testing laboratory are destroyed by Israeli bombs.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Water and Development Partnership Programme 2025

title: The Cyber Army of Russia hacks the computer systems of the Tipton Wastewater Treatment Plant, Indiana, USA and posts video
description: The Cyber Army of Russia hacks the Tipton Wastewater Treatment Plant, Indiana, United States and posts a video showing the attack. The utility switched to manual operations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Nye 2024

title: The Southern Gaza Desalination Plant is shut down for four days after damages from military actions
description: The Southern Gaza Desalination Plant serving the Deir al Balah, Khan Younis, and Rafah governorates is shut down for four days due to attacks on power lines to the plant. Operations resume after repairs.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Water and Development Partnership Programme 2025

title: The city of Kalush, Ukraine is left without heat and water after a Russian missile attack
description: The city of Kalush, Ukraine loses water and power on Christmas after a Russian missile attack cuts power to treatment plants and pumps.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ANTIKOR 2024j

title: The main warehouse of the Coastal Municipalities Water Utility in Gaza is destroyed and seven people are killed
description: The main warehouse of the Coastal Municipalities Water Utility in Gaza is destroyed, seven people are killed, and $9 million in water equipment and supplies are destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Water and Development Partnership Programme 2025

title: The towns of Burshtyn and Demyaniv, Ukraine lose heating and water supplies after Russian missile attacks
description: The towns of Burshtyn and Demyaniv, Ukraine lose heating and water supplies after Russian missile attacks on Ukrainian energy systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ANTIKOR 2024i

title: Three dead and water distribution systems destroyed during clash between military and PDFs in Sagaing, Myanmar
description: More than 100 security forces, including military soldiers and police, open fire on local People's Defence Force (PDF) vehicles arriving to the Min Kun village in the Sagaing region of Myanmar. Three people are killed, including a police officer and a Pyu Saw Htee. An airstrike by the security forces ensues. They set fire to multiple buildings and destroy the water distribution system and electricity lines and hinder firefighting. Mu Airstrikes and arson follow, burning shops and homes; flames spread to Mya Thein Tan pagoda. Multiple residents, including a Buddhist monk and teacher are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MMR65130

title: Three injured in Israeli drone attack on hospital water tanks in Beit Lahiya, Palestine
description: Israeli forces use drones to attack water tanks at the Indonesian Hospital in Beit Lahiya in North Gaza, Palestine, injuring three.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE64354

title: Three-fifths of 350 US/British utilities surveyed report cyberattacks with a majority suffering serious disruption
description: Over three-fifths of 350 US and British water and electricity firms surveyed report being targeted by cyberattacks in 2024 with a majority suffering serious disruption or permanent corruption or destruction of data or systems.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Muncaster 2025

title: Tribal and Clan Forces attacks QSD water station in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: Tribal and Clan Forces attacks a Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) water station in the Deir ez-Zor countryside, Syria, sparking armed clashes. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR134319

title: Tribal and Clan Forces shells QSD water tanks, injuring two in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: Tribal and Clan Forces shells Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) water tanks in Deir ez-Zor, Syria. Two QSD members are wounded in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR134074

title: Tribal and Clan Forces shells QSD-linked water facilities and neighborhoods in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: Tribal and Clan Forces, regime troops, National Defence Forces (QDW) fighters, and pro-Iranian militias fire mortars at Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD)-linked water facilities and neighborhoods in Basira, Deir ez-Zor, Syria. QSD reinforces positions along the Euphrates and orders civilian evacuations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR131802, SYR131799, SYR131800, SYR131801

title: Tribal and Clan Forces targets water station in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: A water station is attacked by Tribal and Clan Forces in the village of Al-Hawayij in Deir ez-Zor, Syria. Four members of the Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR134938

title: Turkish airstrike destroys livestock water project in Duhok, Iraq
description: A Turkish airstrike destroys a livestock water project near Belave village in Duhok, Iraq.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRQ52251

title: Turkish drone attacks water facilities in a rural village in Syria
description: Turkish drones target a water station and water storage facilities in the village of Shirk in rural Al Hasakeh, Syria. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR123419

title: Turkish drone strike hits QSD positions and water tank in Al Hasakeh, Syria
description: Turkish forces launch a drone attack on Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) positions and a water tank in Shakar Khaj village in rural Al Hasakeh, Syria. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR131526

title: Turkish forces fire on DFNS maintenance team while repairing water station in Shuyukh village, Syria
description: Turkish troops open fire on a Democratic Federation of North Syria (DFNS) Water Department team as they repair a water station in Shuyukh village in rural Aleppo, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR131909

title: Turkish forces shell village water station in rural Ar Raqqa, Syria
description: Turkish forces, together with the Syrian National Army (JWS), shell a water station in the village of Fatsa in Ar Raqqa, Syria, causing material damage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR138568

title: Two PHED officials held hostage during water shortage protest in Hisar, India
description: Residents of Dhad village in Hisar, India, stage a protest over water shortages. Demonstrators take two Public Health Engineering Department (PHED) officials as hostages and force them to sit in the sun until their concerns are acknowledged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND160225

title: Two Rand Water executives shot dead in Johannesburg, South Africa
description: Unidentified gunmen open fire in City of Johannesburg, South Africa, killing two Rand Water executives and injuring the city’s chief whip along with two others, in what has been described as mafia-style incidents around disputed control of water, water utility corruption, and competition over service delivery.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; The Water Diplomat 2024 ; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF20521 ; Ngcobo 2024

title: Two girls killed, several injured fetching water in Jabalya, Palestine
description: Israeli forces target Palestinians filling water containers in Jabalya, Palestine. Two girls are killed and several others are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE63231

title: Two injured as residents clash over unpaid water bills in Tehuacan, Mexico
description: A fight breaks out between residents of a housing unit in Tehuacan, Mexico, after the president of the municipal water committee discloses the names of households that had not paid their water bills. The non-payments led the committee to cut off the area’s water supply. A woman and a girl are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX93521

title: Two injured by gunfire during protest in KwaDukuza, South Africa, over lack of water services
description: Residents of KwaDukuza, South Africa, protest outside the ward councilor’s home over the lack of water services. Demonstrators throw stones and try to force the gate. Bodyguards fire live rounds, injuring two protesters - one in the ankle and one in the shoulder.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF21784

title: Two injured in Antananarivo, Madagascar, during student protest over poor water supply infrastructure
description: University students in Antananarivo, Madagascar, demonstrate, demanding better infrastructure, including water and electricity, and unpaid scholarships. Police fire tear gas; students respond with stones and bricks. During the clash, one student and a passerby are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MAG3625

title: Two killed in JNIM attack on water station in Tangayiri, Burkina Faso
description: A water station in Tangayiri, Burkina Faso, is attacked by JNIM (Salafi-jihadist group) militants. Two employees are killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BFO12883

title: Two killed in clan clashes over access to watering spot in Pathai Payam, South Sudan
description: Rival Lou Nuer sub-clans clash at Nyanuai cattle camp in Pathai Payam, South Sudan, over access to a communal watering spot for animals. Two people are killed and one injured before security forces arrive.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SSD13165

title: Two men killed, 10 arrested and water towers destroyed during FAMa raid in Bourem, Mali
description: Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) loots property and destroy houses, water towers and a mosque in Bourem, Mali. They kill two civilians and arrest 10 others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MLI31998

title: Two protesters are killed and 12 injured during protests against a mining company over lack of water services in Lero, Guinea
description: Following 10 days of protests against a mining company and demanding water and other basic services, security forces in Lero, Guinea, kill two residents, injure 12, and destroy homes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GUI2827

title: Two young men lynched by residents of Maharashtra, India, over alleged theft of motor-operated water pump
description: Two men in their twenties are lynched with bamboo sticks by residents as they allegedly attempt to steal a motor-operated water pump, in Maharashtra, India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND151156 ; Khan 2024

title: Ukrainian artillery fire leads to power and water outages in occupied Enerhodar, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian artillery fire leads to power and water outages in the occupied city of Enerhodar, Ukraine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR216909

title: Ukrainian drone attacks disrupt power and water supply in a village in Kursk, Russia
description: Ukrainian forces conduct drone strikes and drop explosives in the village of Snagost, in the Kursk region of Russia. Power lines are damaged and water supply is disrupted. There are no casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS20471

title: Ukrainian drone strike damages water pipes in Belgorod, Russia
description: Water pipes are damaged when the village of Golovchino in Belgorod, Russia, is shelled and struck by a Ukrainian drone. The strike also damages houses, cars and a gas pipe. No casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS14965

title: Ukrainian drone strikes damage water facility in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian forces carry out drone strikes on Donetsk People's Republic (DPR) positions in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine. A water pumping station is damaged in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR144082

title: Ukrainian drones target water delivery vehicle in Donetsk region, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian drones strike a vehicle transporting water to Oleksandrivka, in the Donetsk region of Ukraine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR216820

title: Ukrainian missile strike in Belgorod, Russia, injures civilians and damages water, gas, and electric lines
description: Ukrainian forces fire five missiles in Belgorod, Russia. Three civilians are injured. Homes, cars, as well as electricity, gas, and water infrastructure are also damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS17302

title: Ukrainian shelling damages infrastructure in Enerhodar, Ukraine, leaving city without water
description: Ukrainian forces shell Enerhodar, Ukraine, causing damage to hydraulic infrastructure. Part of the city is left without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR217387

title: Ukrainian shelling damages water pipeline and injures two in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian forces shell Donetsk People's Republic (DPR) positions in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine. A water pipeline is damaged and two civilians are wounded in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR170583

title: Ukrainian shelling damages water supply generator in Lyubymivka, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian shelling in Lyubymivka village (Kherson Oblast), Ukraine, damages a generator that powers the local water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR217431

title: Ukrainian shelling in Horlivka, Ukraine, leaves 60,000 without water
description: Ukrainian forces shell Donetsk People's Republic (DPR) positions and substations in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine, leaving 60,000 residents without electricity, water, or heat.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR193911

title: Ukrainian strike in Belgorod, Russia, damages water supply system
description: Ukrainian forces carry out a drone strike and shell two sites in the Krasnoyaruzhskiy district in Belgorod, Russia. During the attack, part of a water supply system is damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS18645

title: University student shot during demonstration over poor university sanitation in Ongata Rongai, Kenya
description: Students in Ongata Rongai, Kenya, block a road with burning tires in a protest over ongoing issues at Multimedia University, including poor sanitation. Police intervene by hitting and kicking the protesters, and use a water cannon and tear gas to disperse them. One student sustains a gunshot wound and another student is injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN15787

title: Unknown assailants attack Water Resources Department workers in Al Shomaly, Iraq, injuring four
description: Unknown assailants attack employees of a water resources department as they clear encroachments from tributaries in Al Shomaly, Iraq. Four employees are left injured and three perpetrators are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRQ56558, IRQ56542

title: Unknown assailants open fire at herders near water point in Bambo, Kenya, amid inter-clan fighting
description: Unidentified ethnic militia open fire at two herders near a water point in Bambo, Kenya. Police and reservists intervene, killing two of the attackers while the rest of the group manage to escape. The violence occurs amid ongoing Degodia–Murule clan disputes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN14552 ; Yahya 2023

title: Violent clash over water source destroyed by illegal mining activities in Apowa, Ghana; several seriously injured
description: An armed clash breaks out between residents and illegal miners in Apowa, Ghana, after mining activities destroy a community water source. Two residents are shot and left seriously injured, while another person, thought to be a miner, has his hand severed by a machete.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GHA2360

title: Violent clashes between police and protesters over lack of water service in Ixtaczoquitlan, Mexico
description: Residents of Ixtaczoquitlan, Mexico, clash with police during a demonstration over water supply issues. The protesters throw stones at the city hall, break windows and torch a palm tree as well as a parked vehicle. Police attack the protesters with stones, sticks and broken flower pots. Powder from fire extinguishers is discharged and police allegedly administer slaps, shoves and blows to disperse the crowd.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX87856 ; Castillo 2024 ; Castukki 2024

title: Violent protests erupt during World Water Forum events in Denpasar, Indonesia
description: Members of the Bali Community Joint Alliance demonstrate at the World Water Forum in Denpasar, Indonesia, opposing the event as unrepresentative of local needs. They seize banners and violently clash with several forum participants.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IDN16938

title: Violent riots erupt in the central Algerian city of Tiaret as taps run dry and people are forced to queue up for water
description: Violent riots erupt in the central Algerian city of Tiaret as taps run dry and people are forced to queue up for water. The region is plagued by extreme heat, and local reservoirs are drying up as temperatures rise and rain diminishes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Water, Peace, and Security Partnership 2024 ; Associated Press 2024a

title: Water agency worker shot dead while inspecting well in Tehuacan, Mexico
description: An employee of a drinking water agency is shot dead by armed assailants on motorcycles while inspecting a well in Tehuacan, Mexico.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX95580

title: Water and electricity infrastructure damaged in Ukrainian attacks on 10 locations in Belgorodsky, Russia
description: Ukrainian forces attack 10 locations in Belgorodsky, Russia, using drones, mortar and (likely) missiles. The attacks damage water and electricity lines, two apartment buildings, six outbuildings and eight cars.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS17624, RUS17640, RUS17642, RUS17649, RUS17654, RUS17656, RUS17661, RUS17662, RUS17664, RUS17667, RUS1

title: Water and power lost in cities after 20kg of explosives used to blow up critical canal in Zubin Potok, Kosovo
description: 20 kilograms of explosives planted at the Ibar-Lepenac canal in Zubin Potok are detonated, destroying critical infrastructure and cutting water and power to cities across Kosovo. The canal supplies water to a number of cities and supports the operation of three power stations, including the country's main coal-fired station. Kosovo officials Kosovo officials called it a “terrorist act” conducted by Serbia and deem it the worst attack on its critical infrastructure since the 1998-99 conflict.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. XKX1092 ; Bytyci and Sekularac 2024 ; Dimadick 2025 ; Zhinipotoku and Semini 2024 ; Associated Press 2024b

title: Water borehole destroyed in Montepuez, Mozambique, amid election protests
description: A water borehole is destroyed by a group of people in Nanune village in Montepuez, Mozambique. The incident is reportedly linked to protests over general election results.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MZM4697

title: Water company worker assaulted over water network leak in Cartagena, Colombia
description: A group of people in a residential complex in Cartagena, Columbia, temporarily detain and assault a water company worker over a leak in the water network which had not been repaired. They seize his motorcycle keys and damage his phone before police intervene to protect him and restore order.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. COL25574

title: Water offices and vehicles torched, two left injured during anti-government protest in Petit-Goave, Haiti
description: Residents in Petit-Goave, Haiti, protest against Prime Minister Ariel Henry, burning tires and setting fire to the National Directorate of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DINEPA) office and two of its vehicles. Police intervene with firearms, injuring two demonstrators.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. HTI6808

title: Water outages in Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine, after Russian missile debris damages energy infrastructure
description: Several settlements across Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine, are temporarily without water after debris from Russian missiles crashes into energy infrastructure.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR195836

title: Water pipeline targeted with explosives in Tuban, Yemen
description: Unidentified militants in Tuban, Yemen, target an Al-Baytarah - Al Fayush water pipeline, detonating an explosive device which causes material damage.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM91106

title: Water shortage protest in Mirgund, India, leads to clashes and injuries
description: Demonstrators in Mirgund, India, block a road over drinking water shortages and clash with police and security staff. Two security officers are injured and a vehicle is damaged. Police fire shots in the air to disperse the crowd.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND162012

title: Water suppliers protest pump removals that cut off water supply in Mandi Buchiana, Pakistan
description: Water suppliers in the town of Mandi Buchiana in Punjab, Pakistan, demonstrate against the irrigation department’s dismantling of canal-side pumps, which they say cut residents’ water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK143030

title: Water supply facility damaged in Ukrainian strikes on Valuyskiy, Russia
description: A water supply facility building is damaged following Ukrainian drone strikes and shelling across the Valuyskiy district of Russia, including the villages of Dolgoe, Kukuevka and Nizhniye Melnitsy. There are no casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS25624, RUS25700, RUS25746

title: Water supply is cut by workers protesting unpaid salaries in Kohat, Pakistan
description: Water and Sanitation Services Company workers in Kohat, Pakistan, suspend water supply during a protest over unpaid salaries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK140006

title: Water supply system damaged and four injured during strikes on Russian-backed separatist forces in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian forces target Russian-backed separatist forces with drone strikes and shelling in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine. Four civilians are injured and a water supply system is damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR189657

title: Widespread corruption over water tanker contracts leads to the murder of a water employee in South Africa
description: A water employee for the eThekwini Municipality in South Africa is murdered as part of widespread corruption and fights for water tanker contracts. As many as eight employees have been killed in recent years over issues related to water provision and management.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Magubane 2024

title: Woman and son assaulted in Bareilly, India, after drinking from a water tap
description: In Chaubari village in Bareilly, India, a group attacks a woman and her son, likely from the Dalit community, after the young man attempts to drink from a field tap. The assailants use caste-based slurs and tear the woman's clothes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND160921

title: Woman injured in armed clash over water drainage in Shaheed Benazirabad, Pakistan
description: A violent clash between two groups from the Otho community breaks out in Dolo Otho village in Shaheed Benazirabad District, Pakistan, over the drainage of water from an alley. A woman is injured when shots are fired.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK144983

title: Woman killed while fetching water from stream near Ajebo, Nigeria
description: An unidentified armed group kills a woman fetching water from a stream in Mile 7 community, near Ajebo in Ogun State, Nigeria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIG40173

title: Woman seriously injured in explosion while attempting to access booby-trapped well in Essouk, Mali
description: Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) and Wagner forces burn Tuareg huts in Essouk, Mali, and trap the door of a water well with an improvised explosive device, leaving a woman seriously injured after she attempts to access the well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MLI33498
