title: Women protesting the impacts of mines on water systems in Bolivia are attacked
description: Environmental activists in Bolivia are targeted with death threats and bombings after speaking out against mining operations contaminating water resources in Oruro, Bolivia. Women protesting the harmful impacts of mining are attacked, their campsites burned, and miners allegedly throw dynamite into their homes.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Radwin 2024

title: Youths and political party members injured during rally against rising water tariffs in Dharan, Nepal
description: Youths and political party members are injured during a rally against the rising water tariffs in the city of Dharan, Nepal. The protesters attempt to enter the office. The police try to stop them and some protesters are injured in the process.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NEP24683

title: 11-year-old girl attacked while fetching water at roadside tap in Bahawalpur, Pakistan
description: An 11-year-old girl fetching water from a roadside tap in Bahawalpur, Pakistan, is attacked and raped by a man thought to be responsible for several other attacks on young girls in the area. The suspect later dies by gunshot wound during a police raid in which the suspect's accomplices open fire on officers, reportedly shooting the suspect in the process.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; The Current 2025

title: 20 injured, five seriously, in armed mob attack after community water supply is cut off in San Juan Sacatepequez, Guatemala
description: An armed mob attacks and beats indigenous authorities in El Pilar 2, San Juan Sacatepequez, leaving 20 people injured (five seriously). The violence erupts following ongoing tensions with the mayor, who cut off the indigenous community’s water supply and is accused of inciting the mob. At the time of the attack, the indigenous people had entered a building occupied by supporters of the mayor in order to reconnect the water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GTM8884

title: A drone attack by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in Sudan damages Merowe Dam cutting water, pumps, and power to a city
description: Omdurman, a city north of Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, loses drinking water after a drone attack by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on the Merowe Dam, one of Africa’s largest hydropower projects. The attack disrupts electricity and renders Nile water stations and wells inoperable.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ganot 2025

title: A water tanker is attacked during a dispute over access to water in Knysna, South Africa
description: A water tanker is attacked during protests over disruptions of water supply in Knysna, South Africa. Water was cut off after a main water pump broke, leaving extensive areas without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Payne 2025

title: Access to water for up to 80,000 people in Gaza is cut after Israel issues displacement order
description: Israeli authorities issue displacement orders for two neighbourhoods in Khan Younis, Gaza, where up to 80,000 people had been living, cutting their access to the Al Satar reservoir – a critical hub for distributing piped water from Israel.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; UN News 2025

title: After a terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir, India restricts flows of Indus River water to Pakistan
description: In May 2025, after a terror attack kills 26 Hindu tourists in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir. Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India restricts flows to Pakistan through two dams on the Chenab River causing unprecedented drops in water levels. These actions are outside of the agreements established by the Indus Water Treaty, a treaty that both countries have honored since 1960, and Pakistan responds by threatening internationl legal action and states that "Any attempt to stop or divert the flow of water belonging to Pakistan...will be considered as an act of war."
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ganai and Khajuria 2025 ; Ahmed et al. 2025

title: Aid workers report people are killing each other over access to water in Gaza after Israel cuts off aid deliveries
description: Aid workers in Gaza report "people are fighting for water… people are killing each other over water" after Israel cuts off all humanitarian aid.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; France24 2025

title: An Iranian missile strike targeting Israel intelligence headquarters damages a nearby wastewater treatment plant
description: An Iranian missile strike targeting Mossad, Israel's intelligence headquarters, damages a nearby wastewater treatment plant in Herzliya.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Conflict and Environment Observatory 2025

title: An Israeli airstrike hits a desalination plant in Deir El Balah, Gaza
description: An Israeli air strike on April 13 hits the Deir El Balah desalination facility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Care 2025

title: An Israeli missile attack on Iran ruptures a major water pipeline, cutting water to thousands of people
description: An Israeli missile attack on Iran ruptures a major water pipeline, cutting water to thousands of people in Tajrish, northern Tehran
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; McKenzie and Goudarzi 2025

title: Armed group shoots and kills water well guard in rural Homs, Syria
description: A water well guard in the village of Mahfura, Syria, is shot by an unidentified armed group for unknown reasons.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR142818

title: Around eight dead, 12 injured in clash between farmers and herders over land and water resources in Agana, Chad
description: Clashes erupt between farmers and herders in Agana, Chad, leaving between seven or eight people dead and 12 injured. The violence is driven by disputes over land and water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CHA2031

title: Artillery fire destroys hospital water tanker, disrupts patient water supply in Al Fasher, Sudan
description: A UNICEF water tanker stationed at Saudi Hospital in Al Fasher, Sudan, is destroyed by artillery fire during clashes between Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF). Around 1,000 severely ill patients are left nearly without drinking water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD35257 ; Arab News 2025

title: At least 40 killed in attack on fishers and irrigation farmers amid ISWAP factional clash near Baga, Nigeria
description: Suspected Islamic State – West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters kill at least 40 fishers and irrigation farmers in attacks on villages near Baga in Nigeria’s Borno State. The victims had been working under a protection agreement with one ISWAP faction to continue irrigation farming, but another faction attacks them and kills the farmers under protection. Nearby Boko Haram members pursue the attackers but do not clash with them. They also help evacuate the wounded and recover bodies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIG40326

title: Attack on occupied Makiivka, Ukraine, causes water outages
description: According to Russian sources, Ukrainian forces carry out an attack (likely shelling) on the occupied city of Makiivka, Ukraine, leading to water outages in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR219694

title: Attacks by Turkish forces on the Tishrin Dam in Syria kill and injure hundreds and cut water for more than 410,000 people
description: Many civilians are killed in Turkish attacks on the Tishrin Dam and surrounding areas. The dam is a flashpoint in fighting between the Syrian National Army, Turkish-backed rebel groups, and the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces. Attacks on the dam have cut access to water and power for more than 410,000 people and raised concerns about the safety of the dam.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Syrians for Truth and Justice 2025 ; Waller and Abbas 2025 ; Abdo and Martany (AP) 2025

title: Attacks on water and energy systems in Goma, DR Congo cut water to hundreds of thousands of people
description: Attacks on energy systems and water infrastructure in Goma, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) cut water supplies to 700,000 people in January 2025.
basin: Democratic Republic of the Congo Havzası
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Horn Observer 2025

title: Ballistic missile strike on Kyiv, Ukraine, kills four and damages water supply system
description: A Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv, Ukraine, leaves four dead, injures three and damages a water supply system. The damage leads to flooding and prevents water from reaching residents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR204547 ; ANTIKOR 2025a

title: Body of missing water shortage activist found in Amatitán, Mexico
description: The body of a woman activist threatened for her work against the water shortage in El Arenal is found near Guadalajara-Tepic highway in Amatitán, Mexico. She had been reported missing about 10 days prior to the discovery.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX103698

title: Citizens and activists in Kandhkot, Pakistan, clash with police during protest over Indus River canal project
description: Citizens, together with political and religious activists, stage a sit-in in Kandhkot, Pakistan, to oppose plans to build six new canals along the Indus River. Police launch tear gas and baton charge the protesters, who throw stones at the police in retaliation. The tear gas causes some demonstrators to faint.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK151818

title: Clash between protesters and gendarmerie leaves eight injured in demonstration over water price increases in Paoscoto, Senegal
description: A protest over increased water costs leads to violent clashes in Paoscoto village, Senegal. At least six female protesters are attacked, and one is taken to hospital for her injuries. Two gendarmes also sustain injuries. The gendarmerie launches over 300 canisters of tear gas at the crowd before arresting 34 demonstrators, including minors and the elderly.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SEN2125

title: Clash over agricultural water in Umerkot District, Pakistan, kills two, injures five
description: Shar and Mari community members armed with guns clash in Umerkot District, Pakistan, over an agricultural water dispute. Two people are killed and five injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK151536

title: Clash over children's water tanker dispute injures several in Indore, India
description: A dispute between children over a water tanker in Indore, India, escalates into a clash between members of the Indian National Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party, leaving several people injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND183190

title: Clash over sewer water disposal injures four in Matikunda, India
description: Two factions of the Trinamool Congress clash with bricks, sticks, and sharp weapons in a dispute over sewer water disposal in Matikunda, India. Four people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND178182

title: Clashes erupt over alleged water and electricity theft in Anthili, Greece
description: Residents of Anthili, Central Greece, clash with Roma after reporting them for alleged water and electricity theft. A community leader claims a Roma tried to run him and two others over, while the Roma accuse the residents of throwing rocks. Both sides file lawsuits.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GRC6217

title: Clashes over water network reconnection injure police and minors in Ixtapaluca, Mexico
description: In Ixtapaluca, Mexico, over 200 Colonia Luis Cordova residents and members of the National Torch Movement clash with residents of Colonia El Mirador and municipal workers reconnecting the area to the water network. The violence erupts over claims the reconnection would reduce supply to other neighborhoods. Stones, bricks and other objects are thrown, injuring at least five police officers and several minors.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX101000, MEX101001

title: Demonstrators cut water supply in Nashik, India, protesting alleged Jal Jeevan Mission corruption
description: Elgar Kashtakari Sanghatana members halt the supply of water from Vaitarna Dam in Nashik, India, while protesting the implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission. They claim officials are negligent and that contractors are profiting from the scheme.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND183995

title: Doctors Without Borders report an attack on Gaza citizens waiting for a water truck
description: The non-governmental aid organization, Docotors Without Borders, reports that at least two people are shot and wounded, including one child, while waiting for a water truck in Khan Yonis in the Gaza strip. Water and food distribution sites have repatedly been places of vulnerability for Palestinians who have few other options for acquiring basic necessities during the ongoing war with Israel.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ottens-Patterson 2025

title: Drone debris damages water supply infrastructure in Belgorod, Russia
description: Ukrainian forces carry out 34 drone strikes across the Valuyskiy district of Belgorod, Russia. In Dolgoe, one civilian is injured and part of a water supply system is damaged, likely from falling debris.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS33670

title: Drone debris hits wastewater treatment plant, severely injuring one in Lipetsk, Russia
description: Debris from an intercepted Ukrainian drone falls on the Lipetsk wastewater treatment plant in Russia, severely injuring an employee.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS31549

title: Drone strike damages water infrastructure object in Kyrylivka, Ukraine, says Russia
description: According to Russian sources, a Ukrainian drone strike on the occupied town of Kyrylivka in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, damages a water infrastructure object.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR217492

title: Drone strike destroys schools and water storage tank in Kyauktaga Township, Myanmar
description: A drone strike carried out by the Myanmar military drops bombs in the village of Hpyan Tha Lin in Kyauktaga Township, Myanmar. Two schools and a water storage tank are destroyed in the attack. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MMR89442

title: Drone strikes kill two civilians and disrupt water supply in Kherson, Ukraine
description: A Russian drone attack on Kherson, Ukraine, kills two civilians and disrupts the city's water supply, heating, and electricity.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR207723 ; ANTIKOR 2025b

title: Farmer injured in protest over quarry pollution in Manchenahalli, India
description: Villagers, farmers and environmental committee members stage a protest in Manchenahalli, India, over the construction of a road for the purpose of transporting quarry stones, citing concerns around air and water pollution. Protesters throw stones at the quarry owner who retaliates by firing his revolver, injuring a farmer in his leg.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND183551

title: Farmers protest for water rights in Isfahan, Iran; police use tear gas and fire warning shots
description: Farmers rally in Isfahan, Iran, demanding water rights and access to the Zayandeh Roud River for agriculture. Police disperse protesters with tear gas and warning shots. The demonstration is one of many in an ongoing dispute between farmers and officials over water rights and access in the area, with drought and river diversions threatening crops. Some protests have reportedly been met with brutal attacks by Special Guard forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRN30843 ; National Council of Resistance of Iran 2025

title: Farmers sabotage water pumping stations in Varzaneh, Iran, demanding water rights and access
description: Farmers in Varzaneh, Iran, rally at pumping stations serving nearby industries, demanding agricultural water rights and access to the Zayandeh Roud River. The protest escalates with stations set on fire and a water transmission pipeline cut.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRN30841

title: Farms and water wells damaged in SAF airstrikes in Um Hajaleig, Sudan
description: Airstrikes carried out by Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) damage farms and water wells in the Um Hajaleig area of Al Fasher, Sudan.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD34567

title: Fishermen and pastoralists clash over watering hole in Wacham, Cameroon
description: Between April 1, 2025, and April 20, 2025, fishermen and pastoralists in Wacham, Cameroon, clash multiple times over the fishermen’s accusations that the pastoralists are letting their livestock destroy their fishing nets in a watering hole. Five fishermen are injured with knives in this period.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. CAO16781, CAO16803, CAO16825, CAO16840

title: Five injured in dispute over irrigation in Khulna, Bangladesh
description: Villagers staging a protest over an irrigation dispute clash with Awami League supporters in Khulna, Bangladesh. Five people are injured, including a Jubo Dal member who was attempting to mediate between the groups.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BGD30556

title: Four injured in machete attack over water pans and grazing land in Mandera North, Kenya
description: Members of the Degodia community in Mandera North, Kenya, are ambushed by suspected Murule militia, who attack them with machetes and sticks during a dispute over water pans and grazing land. Four people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN17510

title: Four people are killed in Maharashtra region of India in a dispute over water sharing from a well for irrigation
description: A long-running family dispute over sharing water from a well turns violent and four people are killed and several injured in the Maharashtra region of India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Akhef 2025 ; Clarion India 2025

title: Gunmen attack Thiban water station in rural Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: Unidentified gunmen use rocket-propelled grenades to attack a water station in rural Deir ez-Zor, Syria.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR139588

title: Gunmen clash over water well digging in Yarim, Yemen
description: Gunmen from Al Dakhla and Aboum villages exchange fire during a dispute over water well digging in Yarim, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM96582

title: Gunmen open fire at water point, killing one and seriously injuring two in Lomelo, Kenya
description: Three gunmen open fire at a water point in Lomelo, Kenya, killing one woman and leaving two others with gunshot wounds. The gunmen are thought to be Pokot militia who have previously attacked people in the area. The motivation for the attack is unclear.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN17643

title: Gunmen open fire on water tanker in Al Abr, Yemen, killing one and injuring another
description: Unidentified gunmen open fire on a water tanker belonging to Yemen's National Shield Forces between the Al Muthalath and Ba Haj checkpoints in Al Abr, Yemen. One soldier is killed and another injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM97042

title: Houthi forces abduct more than 10 villagers and shoot at houses over water sanitation project in Ar Ribat, Yemen
description: Houthi forces abduct over 10 residents and raid houses in Ar Ribat, Yemen. The attack is aimed at forcing residents to give up their land for a water sanitation project proposed by a Houthi investor. Houses are shot at but no casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM96451

title: Houthi forces blockade village, steal water well solar panels and open fire in Harf Sufyan, Yemen
description: A large Houthi military crew blockades the village of Al Thamathima in Harf Sufyan district, Yemen, and seizes solar panels from water wells. They also destroy crops and shoot randomly at houses.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM97512

title: Houthi shelling damages water tank in Taizz, Yemen
description: Houthi forces fire mortars at a residential area in Taizz-Ash Shamasi, Yemen. The attack damages a house and a water tank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM97379

title: Houthi snipers open fire on children fetching water from well in At Ta'iziyah, Yemen, injuring two
description: Houthi snipers shoot and injure two children, aged 14 and 12, as they fetch water from a well in At Ta'iziyah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM99192

title: IRG shelling hits water well in Al Jabalayn, Yemen, injuring two civilians
description: Yemen's Internationally Recognized Government (IRG) fighters shell a water well in Al Jabalayn, Yemen, injuring two civilians who were grazing sheep nearby.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM98960

title: Irrigation canal dispute leads to armed clashes in Nisab, Yemen
description: Two tribes armed with weapons clash over the use of an irrigation canal in Nisab, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM96587

title: Israel halts electricity to a desalination plant in Gaza, cutting off water supplies
description: Israel cuts off the electricity supply to Gaza, affecting a desalination plant producing drinking water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lidman and Magdy 2025

title: Israeli airstrikes on an aid center in Gaza damages water and sanitation facilities
description: On April 12 an Israeli airstrike on an aid center in Gaza City damages water and sanitation facilities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Care 2025

title: Israeli airstrikes on schools in Gaza City kill 30 people and destroy latrines and desalination units
description: On April 3, Israeli airstrikes on two schools in Gaza City kill 30 people, injure more than 70, and destroy five mobile latrines and a solar-powered desalination unit that were delivered and installed in October 2024 as part of an EU-funded project.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Care 2025

title: Israeli missile strikes a water distribution site in Gaza, killing six children and injuring 17 others
description: An Israeli missile strikes a water distribution site in the al-Nuseirat refugee camp in Gaza, killing six children and injuring 17 others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al Mayadeen English 2025 ; Jerusalem Post 2025

title: Israeli settlers assault Palestinian family and damage water truck in Nablus, Palestine
description: Israeli settler rioters assault a Palestinian family in Nablus, Palestine. They also puncture the tires of a water transportation truck and destroy solar panels.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE73233

title: Israeli settlers attack water pump on Palestinian-owned land in Bayt Illu, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers target a water pump on Palestinian-owned land in Bayt Illu, West Bank, Palestine. They also target an agricultural greenhouse and spray anti-Arab sentiments.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE69453

title: Israeli settlers attack water well and torch guard’s vehicle in Burqah, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers storm the town of Burqah in West Bank, Palestine, and attack a water well. They set fire to a number of Palestinian-owned vehicles, including the vehicle belonging to the well’s security guard.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE73873 ; Kestler-D’Amours, Marsi, and McCready 2025

title: Israeli settlers cut water pipelines supplying homes in Al Awja, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers cut several water pipelines in Al Awja, Palestine, disrupting residential drinking water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE72952

title: Israeli settlers damage water line and tanks in Tubas, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers damage a water line and two Palestinian-owned water tanks near the Tayasir checkpoint in Tubas, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE72793

title: Israeli settlers damage water pipelines near Jericho, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers damage Palestinian water pipelines and solar panels near Jericho in West Bank, Palestine. Tents are also targeted, and the settlers seize 70 sheep.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE73245

title: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian water containers in Suseya, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian water containers and attack houses and vehicles in the village of Suseya in West Bank, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE67440

title: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian-owned water pipelines and puncture water tanker tires near Tubas, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers destroy Palestinian-owned water pipelines and puncture the tires of a water tanker in Al Mayita village near Tubas, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE73868, PSE73868

title: Israeli settlers destroy irrigation pipelines in Tubas, West Bank
description: Israeli settlers in the village of Bardalah, Tubas, West Bank, destroy irrigation pipelines on Palestinian-owned land. On the same day Israeli settlers destroy parts of a water pipeline in the village of Khirbat Yarzah, Tubas, West Bank.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE72802, PSE72688

title: Israeli settlers destroy solar panels and water pumps in Khirbet al Deir, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers destroy solar panels and water pumps belonging to Palestinians in Khirbet al Deir in West Bank, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE73243

title: Israeli settlers destroy water collection well and olive trees in Nablus, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers destroy a water collection well and chop down olive trees on Palestinian-owned land in the Bayta district of Nablus, Palestine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE66928

title: Israeli settlers destroy water pipeline supplying water to Palestinian communities near Khirbat Yarzah, Palestine
description: A water pipeline near Khirbat Yarzah in West Bank, Palestine, is destroyed by Israeli settlers, disrupting water supply to nearby Palestinian communities.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE73639

title: Israeli settlers destroy water tanks and hurl stones at Palestinians in Hebron, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers throw stones at Palestinians in Hebron, West Bank, and destroy their water tanks and solar panels.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE70043

title: Israeli settlers in the West Bank accused of damaging a Palestinian water system
description: In the West Bank Israeli settlers are seen breaking a water pipline from the Ein Samiyah spring that supplies water to around 110,000 people. The water system staff were able to get the supply back online.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Arab News 2025

title: Israeli settlers seize Palestinian water tanks and agricultural equipment in Salfit, Palestine
description: Israeli settlers target Palestinian-owned land in Salfit, West Bank, seizing water tanks and agricultural equipment and uprooting around 100 olive trees.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE70125

title: Israeli settlers seize a spring in the West Bank and damage a water system that provides water to 30 Palestinian villages
description: Israeli settlers seize the Ein Samiya spring in the West Bank and vandalize Palestinian pumping stations that supply water to 30 villages in the Ramallah area, diverting the water to a nearby pool.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Shezaf 2025

title: Israeli warplanes strike vehicle transporting water in An Nusayrat, Palestine
description: Israeli warplanes strike a moving vehicle carrying water in An Nusayrat, Palestine. Injuries are reported but the number is unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE71716

title: Israeli warplanes target water desalination plant in east Gaza, Palestine
description: The Ghababin water desalination plant in east Gaza City, Palestine, is targeted by Israeli warplanes. Israeli artillery fire is reported in the same area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE71358

title: JNIM militants attack multiple locations in Sourou, Burkina Faso; at least 100 dead, dozens abducted and water station destroyed
description: JNIM (Salafi-jihadist group) militants attack the areas of Di, Lanfiera and Guiedougou in Sourou, Burkina Faso. At least 100 people are killed, dozens are abducted, and a water station is destroyed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BFO13546, BFO13545, BFO13547

title: Karachi Bar Association president injured in targeted attack over Indus river activism in Karachi, Pakistan
description: Six unidentified men carry out a targeted attack on the president of the Karachi Bar Association in the Saddar area of Karachi, Pakistan. The victim is reportedly hospitalized for serious injuries. The attack is thought to be motivated by his opposition to plans for six new canals on the Indus River.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK150775 ; The News International 2025

title: Kyrgyzstan-Tajikistan-Uzbekistan Summit on Water
description: Presidents of Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan meet in Khujand and jointly declare all outstanding territorial and water-access disputes resolved, launching a new era of Central Asian water cooperation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bishkek Joint Declaration on Water-Energy Consortium in Central Asia (2025).

title: Landmine damages water tanker in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: A landmine planted by an unidentified armed group during a previous conflict detonates in southern Deir ez-Zor, Syria, damaging a water tanker.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR143446

title: Lawyer sit-in over Indus River canals sparks violent clashes in Karachi, Pakistan
description: Lawyers protesting plans for six canals along the Indus River clash with police in Gulshan-i-Hadeed, Karachi, Pakistan. Protestors throw stones at police, injuring eight people, including two police officers and a lawyer. A police vehicle is also set on fire. Six demonstrators are arrested.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK151815, PAK151816

title: Lebanese militias linked to Hezbollah shell water station in rural Homs, Syria
description: Lebanese clan militias linked to Hezbollah shell the Ain Al-Tanoura water station Homs, Syria, halting its operations. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR142286 ; SNHR 2025

title: Man opens fire during protest over water shortages in Mexico City, Mexico
description: During a demonstration over residential water shortages in Mexico City, Mexico, a man fires shots into the air while a woman beats a protester. The man then opens fire at police officers before being arrested. There are conflicting reports on the incident, with some stating there was no clash with police.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX102660

title: Man shot dead fetching water from a pump in The Bahamas
description: A man fetching water from a pump in The Bahamas is shot dead by an unknown assailant in a vehicle.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Bailey 2025

title: Man shot while fetching water in Liloan, Philippines
description: A construction worker fetching water for his workplace is shot in the neck by a man on a shooting spree in Liloan, Philippines. The suspect later dies from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Lauro 2025

title: Mass Russian drone attack cripples power and water supplies in Odesa, Ukraine
description: Russian forces attack Ukraine's Black Sea port city of Odesa with a massive drone strike, leaving most of its residents without power, water, or heating.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Hindustan Times 2025 ; ANTIKOR 2025c

title: Militants ambush Niger military escorting Kandadji dam workers; 12 dead, six kidnapped in Tillaberi
description: The Niger military is ambushed in the vicinity of Dangala, Tillaberi, while escorting workers to the Kandadji dam in Niger. The militants kill 12 soldiers and kidnap six workers. The Islamic State – Sahel Province (ISSP) claims responsibility for the attack. The Kandadji dam is a key infrastructure for electricity generation and water management in Niger.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIR31548

title: Military forces armed with machine guns open fire on water station workers in rural Aleppo, Syria
description: Syrian military forces armed with machine guns open fire at workers maintaining a water station in rural Aleppo, forcing them to flee the site. The water station is damaged in the attack but the workers escape without injury.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR143691

title: Mob attacks two men accused of tampering with water pipeline in Kithimani, Kenya
description: A mob beats two men in Kithimani, Kenya, who are accused of tampering with a public water pipeline and illegally siphoning water. Police intervene and place the men in custody. The extent of the injuries is not reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN17657

title: Mob torches water tankers and beats up drivers in Karachi, Pakistan
description: A mob torches five water tankers and assaults their drivers during a demonstration near Jail Chowrangi, Karachi, Pakistan. The protest erupted after a speeding dumper truck hit and killed a motorcyclist.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK149323

title: Municipal delegate assaulted over water shortages in Rincon de Tamayo, Mexico
description: Residents in Rincon de Tamayo, Mexico, beat and injure a municipal PVEM (Ecologist Green Party of Mexico) delegate over water shortages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX102989

title: Nine injured in BNP clash over canal lease in Khulna, Bangladesh
description: Two factions of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) clash with bricks in Chalna, Khulna, during a dispute over a canal lease. Nine people, including three police officers, are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BGD31697

title: Occupiers cut off water supply to Donetsk residents who refuse Russian documents
description: Occupiers in Donetsk, Ukraine, cut off water supply to residents who refuse Russian documents, declaring their homes as "ownerless".
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Khlyudzinsky 2025

title: One killed, nine injured in BNP clash over embankment construction in Barisal, Bangladesh
description: A clash between two rival factions of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) over the construction of an embankment by the Water Development Board leaves one dead and at least nine injured in Barisal, Bangladesh.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BGD31005

title: One killed, several injured and water access restricted in militia attacks on villages in Sokoto State, Nigeria
description: A Sokoto militia attacks the villages of Aliya and Layinna in Sokoto State, Nigeria, killing one and injuring several others, and restricts access to water in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIG41375, NIG41376

title: Pakistani Army Chief warns India of missile strikes on dam if built in breach of Indus Treaty
description: At a black-tie dinner in the United States, Pakistani Army Chief Asim Munir is said to have warned that Pakistan would retaliate against any perceived violations of the Indus Waters Treaty, saying a dam built by India would be destroyed "with 10 missiles", according to several attendees at the event.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; India-West News Desk 2025

title: Pakistani Taliban militants blow up water tanker; one dead in North Waziristan, Pakistan
description: Pakistani Taliban (TTP) militants use improvised explosives to carry out an attack on a military vehicle used for carrying water in Spinwam in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa District. A Frontier Corps personnel is killed in the blast.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK148328

title: Palestinian water tanks seized by Israeli forces in Bethlehem, Palestine
description: Israeli forces operating in Khirbat an Nahlah, in Bethlehem, West Bank, seize water tanks and woodworking tools from a Palestinian-owned house. The windows of the house are smashed by Israeli settlers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE69950

title: Physical fight breaks out at community meeting in Knysna, South Africa, over housing, water and sanitation services
description: Residents clash during a meeting at a community hall in Knysna, South Africa, over demands for subsidized housing, electricity, toilets and water. A physical fight breaks out and police are called. The extent of injuries is unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF22901

title: Poland thwarts major cyberattack on critical water infrastructure
description: Poland's deputy prime minister reports that a major cyberattack on critical infrastructure that would have left a large Polish city without water has been thwarted.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Reuters 2025

title: Police assault a journalist and committee chairman protesting corruption over Indus canal projects in Mirpur Sakro, Pakistan
description: A journalist and the committee chairman of Mirpur Sakro, Pakistan, are left badly injured by police after being arrested for leading protests against plans to construct six new canals on the Indus River. The journalist sustains fractures to his hands and arms and is taken to a nearby hospital for urgent medical treatment.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK151541 ; Khawaja 2025

title: Police fire pepper spray during protest over water shortages in Paita, Peru
description: Over a hundred residents gather outside the offices of a water company in a protest led by the mayor of Paita, Peru, over water shortages disrupting supply to more than 180,000 people. The company invites the mayor inside to a meeting, but as residents attempt to follow they are stopped by riot police who fire pepper spray at them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ruesta 2025

title: Police fire tear gas and rubber bullets in protest over two-month water outage in Buffalo City, South Africa
description: Protesters use rocks and burning tires to block the N6 highway in Buffalo City, South Africa, demanding an end to water outages that have persisted for nearly two months. A police vehicle catches fire during the demonstration. Tear gas and rubber bullets are used to disperse the crowd.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF22928

title: Police officers in Nentón, Guatemala, targeted by at least 50 armed individuals in dispute over water resources
description: At least 50 armed individuals target eight police officers carrying out a judicial proceeding relating to the reinstatement of water at Chacula treatment plant in Nenton, Guatemala. One officer and a local community leader are beaten and detained by the group. The incident is connected to ongoing conflict between the El Aguacate and Chacula communities over the use of land and water resources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. GTM9081

title: Police response to water shortage protest results in severe injuries in Matadi, Democratic Republic of Congo
description: A "brutal" police response to a peaceful demonstration over a shortage of drinking water leaves a dozen people injured, some severely, in Matadi, Democratic Republic of Congo. The circumstances around the violence are unclear.
basin: Democratic Republic of the Congo Havzası
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. DRC35410

title: Police strike protesters with rubber bullets during demonstration over water shortages in Johannesburg, South Africa
description: Residents of Coronationville in Johannesburg, South Africa, stage a protest over water shortages which they say have been ongoing for eight years. Police disperse the crowd with teargas and shoot several people with rubber bullets.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; eNCA 2025

title: Police use stun grenades to disperse residents demanding water in Johannesburg, South Africa
description: Hundreds of residents blocking a road to demand water in the Lenansia South suburb of Johannesburg, South Africa, are dispersed when police launch stun grenades into the crowd.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SAF22926

title: Protester and journalist run over by vehicle during drain demonstration in Hermosillo, Mexico
description: Residents from Colonia Santa Isabel in Hermosillo, Mexico, block traffic to protest a drain installed parallel to a canal. A vehicle runs over a woman who is protesting, as well as a journalist covering the protest. Both sustain injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MEX100319

title: Protesters clash with police during violent protest over Indus river canals project in Karachi, Pakistan
description: Police personnel in Karachi, Pakistan, are attacked by protesters during a demonstration against the construction of six new canals on the Indus river. The protest, attended by around 500-600 people, turns violent when some of the protesters beat police workers and hit them with sticks and stones. Many are injured during the clash but the exact number is not reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK149539

title: Protesters damage water canal during demonstration over death of person displaced by Bokaro steel plant, India
description: 5,000 people gather under the banner of Visthapit Apprentice Sangh, an association representing the interests of those displaced by the Bokaro steel plant, in a demonstration over the death of one of its members. They block roads, burn vehicles and damage a water canal.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND181657

title: Protesters shut off water pipeline in Tontouan, Indonesia
description: Dozens of residents stage a protest in the village of Tontouan, Indonesia, over road damage caused by the vehicle of a water supply company. During the protest they shut off the main valve of the company's water pipeline.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IDN20193

title: Protesters torch water tanker after dumper truck hits motorcyclists in Karachi, Pakistan
description: Residents in Karachi, Pakistan, set fire to trucks and a water tanker after a dumper truck crashed into several motorcyclists. Three people are injured, and a firefighter sustains a head injury.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK150983

title: QSD drone strike on water station leaves one dead and two injured in rural Aleppo, Syria
description: Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) carries out a drone strike on Al-Khafsa town's water station in rural Aleppo, Syria. Three people are injured, including the station manager and an electrical engineer who were trying to fix previous damage to the station. One victim dies from their injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR139095

title: QSD forces shell Al-Khafsa water station in rural Aleppo, Syria
description: Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) launches rockets at the Al-Khafsa water station in Aleppo, Syria, targeting Syrian National Army (JWS) positions.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR139731

title: QSD forces shell water station in Big Habbuba, Syria
description: A water station is shelled by Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) in the town of Big Habbuba in rural Aleppo, Syria. The attack causes material damages; casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR139732

title: QSD member injured in armed attack on Thiban water station military post in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: A Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) member is injured in an attack on a QSD military post in Thiban water station, Deir ez-Zor, Syria. The unidentified assailants were armed with rocket-propelled grenades and machine guns.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR143078

title: RSF floods villages in Al Jazirah, Sudan, after killing woman and demanding ransom
description: A woman with special needs is assaulted and killed by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Tayba Al Naim in Al Jazirah, Sudan. The RSF demands a ransom for her body and then opens irrigation channels, flooding the village and neighboring Hasab Allah.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD33141

title: RSF shelling damages water sources at Abu Shouk IDP Camp, Sudan; 40 killed, over 100 wounded
description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and allied militia shell Abu Shouk IDP (Internally Displaced Persons) Camp in Al Fasher, Sudan, damaging water sources. 40 people are killed and more than 100 injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD34887

title: RSF snipers shoot at engineers assessing water station damage in Khartoum, Sudan
description: A group of engineers assessing conflict-related damage to Bahri water station in Khartoum North, Sudan, are shot at by Rapid Support Forces (RSF) snipers. There are no casualties.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD33419 ; Sudan Tribune 2025

title: RSF soldier killed in dispute over water station in Abu Karaynka, Sudan
description: A clash erupts in a refugee camp in Abu Karaynka, Sudan, after a Rapid Support Forces (RSF) soldier fires shots and blocks the operation of a water station, claiming it was built on his farm. The soldier is killed.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD33193

title: RSF threatens to cut off water supply in Golo, Sudan
description: Rapid Support Forces (RSF) claims to have overtaken Golo in North Darfur, Sudan, and threaten to cut off water from Al Fasher during clashes with Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD33245, SUD33266

title: Rapid Support Forces destroys $1 million water lab in Khartoum, Sudan
description: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces (RSF) destroys a water laboratory worth $1 million in Khartoum, Sudan, official say. The lab is used to analyze river and well water and is the main water analysis facility in the state.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Sudan Tribune 2025

title: Rapid Support Forces shells Al Manara water station in Karrari, Sudan
description: The Al Manara water station in Sudan's Karrari District is shelled by Rapid Support Forces (RSF) fire.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD32923

title: Refugee camp food and water shortages spark violence in Kakuma, Kenya
description: A demonstration attended by thousands of refugees over food and water shortages at Kakuma refugee camp, Kenya, turns violent when stones are pelted at police and protesters attempt to storm the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees offices. Police throw tear gas canisters and fire live bullets to disperse the protesters. At least three refugees, as well as three police officers and a local administration officer sustain injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN17229

title: Refugees protest reduced access to basic needs at Kakuma camp, Kenya; police use tear gas, several injured
description: Refugees at Kakuma camp in Turkana, Kenya, stage a protest over reduced access to food, water and healthcare following a freeze on United States foreign aid. Police use tear gas to disperse the crowd. Several refugees are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN17801

title: Remnant landmine in water well kills one and injures another in Idlib, northwestern Syria
description: One civilian is killed and another injured after a remnant landmine detonates in a water well in rural Idlib, Syria. The landmine, planted by former regime members, exploded while the victims were cleaning the well.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR143626

title: Resident clashes with maintenance worker over water shortage in Ghaziabad, India
description: A fight breaks out between a resident of a high-rise housing complex in Ghaziabad, India, and one of it's maintenance workers during a dispute over a water shortage. The resident reportedly approached the worker to complain, leading to a heated argument. The resident pushes the worker, who retaliates by punching him in the face and continues the assault until witnesses intervene.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; HT News Desk 2025

title: Residents punch and beat firefighters due to lack of water in Manila, Philippines
description: Residents of a burning building punch two volunteer firefighters and beat them with wooden planks in Manila, Philippines. They are angry that there is no water available and that they will have to wait for a supply to arrive.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; KAMI 2025

title: Residents take over water station in Puerto Badel, Colombia, and disrupt water supply to Cartagena
description: Residents protesting the state of roads leading to their communities take over a water pumping station in Puerto Badel in Bolivar, Colombia, disrupting drinking water supply to the nearby city of Cartagena.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. COL30091

title: Riot police beat indigenous people protesting water outages in Tabasco, Mexico
description: Indigenous people from Tamulté de las Sábanas in Tabasco, Mexico, block a federal highway in protest of power and water grid failures. Riot police push and beat them in response.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Peréz Marin 2025

title: Rioters protesting water price increases torch infrastructure at water offices in Chokwe, Mozambique
description: During a demonstration over water prices, rioters break and torch infrastructure at water offices in the town of Chokwe, Mozambique, prompting the district administrator and mayor to flee the area. Police open fire to disperse them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. MZM4922

title: Russia launches large-scale attack on Ukrainian infrastructure, killing a child and disrupting water supply
description: Over several consecutive nights, Russian forces carry out a large-scale attack on Ukraine, using cruise missiles and suicide drones to target the country's energy infrastructure. Electricity and water supplies are lost in parts of Kharkiv and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi. In Zaporizhzhia, a child is killed and the Dnipro hydroelectric plant is closed as a precaution.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Danishevska 2025 ; Ukrinform 2025

title: Russian attack on Lozova, Ukraine, disrupts water supply, kills one and injures 10
description: Russian forces attack the city of Lozova, Ukraine, targeting critical infrastructure which disrupts water supply. Residential areas are also hit, leaving one dead and 10 others, including children, injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Balachuk and Diakonov 2025

title: Russian drone strike hits water supply vehicle in Stepnohirsk, Ukraine
description: Russian forces carry out a drone strike on a water supply vehicle in Stepnohirsk in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR221567

title: Russian drone strikes disrupt water supply in Dnipropetrovsk, Ukraine
description: Russian drone strikes near Malomykhaylivka in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine, damage power lines and disrupt water supply.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR217691

title: Russian drone strikes interrupt water supply in Sumy, Ukraine
description: Drone strikes carried out by Russian forces damage houses and lead to water supply disruptions in the Sumy village of Pishchane, Ukraine.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR205837

title: Russian drone strikes on Kupiansk, Ukraine, leave city without water
description: Russian forces carry out airstrikes on Kupiansk, Ukraine, in a prolonged attack on infrastructure in the area. A water pipeline is targeted, leaving the city without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Oleniak 2025

title: Russian drone strikes on water tanker injure emergency workers and officials in Donetsk, Ukraine
description: Two State Emergency Service of Ukraine (SESU) workers delivering water in Dontesk, Ukraine, are injured when a manually piloted Russian drone targets the SESU tanker. A second drone targets the evacuation crew who had come to rescue the workers, injuring two police officers and the head of the local administration.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR208525

title: Russian missile strike destroys water intake facility in Trostianets, Ukraine
description: A Russian missile strike on Trostianets in Sumy Oblast, Ukraine, destroys the city's water intake facility, leaving around 100 residents without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Danishevska 2025

title: Russian shelling in the Zaporizhzhia region cuts water to 3,000 residents
description: Russian shelling in the Zaporizhzhia region cuts electricity and water to 3,000 residents in three frontline villages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; ANTIKOR 2025d

title: Russian shelling on infrastructure in Sumy, Ukraine, disrupts water supply and injures three
description: Russian forces shell civilian infrastructure in the city of Sumy, Ukraine, damaging a water intake which leads to water outages in surrounding areas. Three people are injured in the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mezha 2025

title: Sabotage of borehole leads to water outages in South Corfu, Greece
description: Unknown individuals use axes to cut the power supply cables to a borehole in South Corfu, Greece, leaving residents of surrounding communities without water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Enimerosi Corfu News 2025

title: Sabotage of electricity transformers in Zanzibar, Tanzania, results in severe water supply disruption
description: In June 2025, four electricity transformers are vandalized and stolen across several sites in Zanzibar, Tanzania, including water distribution facilities, resulting in severe disruptions to water supply in surrounding areas. According to Zanzibar’s Ministry of Water, Energy and Minerals, the incidents are deliberate acts of sabotage designed to impede the government's effort to provide essential services to residents.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Suleiman 2025

title: Security forces injured during protests over drinking water quality in Basra, Iraq
description: Residents of Basra, Iraq, stage protests over several days over poor drinking water quality due to the flow of saltwater into the city. They block roads with burning tires and scuffle with security forces, leaving several personall injured. Severe drought in Iraq has affected the flow of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, allowing saltwater from the Shatt al-Arab to extend further into the city.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; The New Region 2025 ; Shafaq News 2025

title: Several farmers are injured during a conflict over water rights between cities and farms in Isfahan, Iran
description: Several farmers are injured in a violent clashes with Iranian security forces in a revival of conflict over water rights between cities and farms in Isfahan, Iran.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; IranWire 2025

title: Several injured in violent clash over water in Dwarkapura, India
description: Several people are injured when two groups clash in a dispute over water in Dwarkapura village, India.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND182550

title: Shelling damages water supply system in occupied Nova Kakhovka, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian shelling damages a water supply system as well as power lines, a gas pipeline and four apartment buildings in occupied Nova Kakhovka, according to Russian sources.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR217322

title: Shelling damages water supply system in occupied Shevchenko, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian forces shell occupied Shevchenko, Ukraine, damaging power lines and a water supply system.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR217080

title: Shelling in Horlivka, Ukraine, kills one, injures six; water supply facility damaged
description: According to Russian sources, Ukrainian shelling in the occupied city of Horlivka, Ukraine, leaves one person dead, six injured and damages a water supply facility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR224786

title: Six injured during protest over water shortages in Antananarivo, Madagascar
description: Anti-government protesters march through Antananarivo, Madagascar, in a mass demonstration over power and water shortages. Security forces use armored vehicles to charge the protesters who respond by throwing stones. At least four people are injured by rubber bullets and two others by stun grenades. In nearby Anosibe, a man is left unconscious after police chase and severely beat him.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Arab News 2025

title: Strike debris damages water supply infrastructure after Ukrainian drones shot down in Belgorod Oblast, Russia
description: Water supply infrastructure is damaged following Ukrainian drone strikes across the Belgorodskiy district of Belgorod Oblast, Russia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS36376

title: Striking shipyard workers in El Natahoyo, Spain, set fire to a water treatment plant during protests over employee dismissals
description: Striking shipyard workers in El Natahoyo, Spain, set fire to a water treatment plant during protests over employee dismissals. Police respond with smoke canisters and rubber bullets. 30 people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. ESP19908

title: Students injured in violent clash during Indus River development in Sindh, Pakistan
description: A student protest against the construction of water channels to facilitate irrigation of Punjab land using Indus River water turns violent when police fire tear gas and baton charge the crowd. The students retaliate by throwing stones, breaking the windows of two police vehicles. Many students are injured in the clash.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK149774

title: Suspected RSF drone targets water treatment plant in Kosti, Sudan
description: A water treatment plant on the White Nile River in Kosti, Sudan, is targeted by a fighter drone. The drone is suspected to be linked to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) due to similar incidents in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD34715

title: Systematic sabotage puts Bahri water station out of service in Khartoum, Sudan
description: The Khartoum State Water Corporation makes a press statement announcing that Bahri water station has been put out of service following systemic sabotage of equipment, including extensive damage to electrical transformers, cables, dashboards, pumps, laboratory equipment and tanks, which has rendered the station inoperable. The station is one of Khartoum's largest, and its closure occurs amid a severe water crisis which has led to clashes between the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). The following month, engineers assessing damage to the station are shot at by RSF snipers.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Al-Taghyeer 2025

title: TTP abducts Frontier Corps personnel, torches water tanker in North Waziristan, Pakistan
description: Armed Pakistani Taliban (TTP) assailants abduct a Tochi Scouts member of the Frontier Corps in Hassan Khel, North Waziristan, as he returns from the market. The attackers also seize two government-owned water tankers and set fire to one of them.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PAK148578

title: Taliban governor shoots father and son over water dispute in Sang-e Atash, Afghanistan; victim in critical condition
description: A father and son are wounded after being shot by the Taliban deputy district governor over a water dispute in the village of Sang-e Atash in Takhar, Afghanistan. One victim is hospitalized in critical condition.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. AFG69795

title: The city of Port Sudan, Sudan loses access to water after attacks on fuel supplies
description: Attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Port Sudan, Sudan leave the city without the diesel fuel needed to power groundwater pumps for the water supply, raising the price of water from vendors and cutting supplies.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Osman and Sippy 2025

title: Three killed while collecting water in RSF attack on Khartoum water distribution point, Sudan
description: The Rapid Support Forces (RSF) targets Al Nil city, including a water distribution point in the Al Thawra district of Khartoum, Sudan. The shelling kills three civilians who were lining up to collect water.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD32926

title: Tiv woman accused of polluting water in Awe, Nigeria, killed by Fulani pastoralist in machete attack
description: A young Fulani pastoralist attacks and kills a Tiv woman with a machete in Imon village in Awe, Nigeria, after accusing her of polluting the water where she was fishing.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIG41627

title: Tribal disputes over village water supply leave three dead and four injured in Osmanabad, India
description: Two groups clash over water supply in the village of Bavi, Osmanabad, India. Three people are killed and four others injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IND175863, IND176535

title: Turkish forces and JWS target water tanker in rural Al Hasakeh, Syria
description: Turkish forces use drones and artillery to target a water tanker in rural Al Hasakeh, Syria. The attack is carried out in conjunction with the Syrian National Army (JWS).
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR139009

title: Turkish forces strike water station in rural Aleppo, Syria
description: Turkish forces carry out an airstrike on a water station in the village of Upper Shyookh in Aleppo, Syria, causing material damages.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR140549

title: Two die in dispute over well water in Benue State village, Nigeria
description: Armed pastoralists, thought to be Fulani, attack and kill a woman and a Roman Catholic Church leader during a dispute over the use of community well water in Ayua village in Benu, Nigeria. Some residents flee the community in response.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIG41739

title: Two injured in protest over water outages in eMalahleni, South Africa
description: Two people are injured during a protest over water outages in eMalahleni, South Africa, due to broken pipes serving the area. A woman is engulfed in flames and thrown into the air after a motorist, blinded by smoke from burning tires, runs her over as she crosses the road. Meanwhile, another motorist is assaulted by a man who accuses him of bumping his vehicle.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Goldswain 2025

title: Two killed, three injured in clash over irrigation water in Maysan, Iraq
description: Gunmen from two unidentified tribes clash with light weapons in Al Abyad village, in Maysan, Iraq, after a dispute over irrigation water. Two people are killed and three injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. IRQ62490

title: Two teenagers injured, water reservoir damaged in armed attack on civilians in Torodi, Niger
description: Armed militants suspected to be linked to JNIM (Salafi-jihadist group), attack civilians in Garbangou village in Torodi, Niger. Two teenagers are injured and the village water reservoir is damaged.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIR31500

title: US strikes on Water & Sanitation Foundation in Al Mansuriyah, Yemen, kill four and injure two
description: Four workers are killed and two injured following United States military strikes on the Water & Sanitization Foundation in Al Mansuriyah, Yemen.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. YEM98035

title: Ukraine strikes military water pipeline in Vladivostok, Russia
description: Ukrainian forces strike a water pipeline supplying Russian military facilities in Vladivostok, in Russia's far east, cutting off drinking water to garrisons in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Ivanyshyn 2025

title: Ukrainian drone strike damages water infrastructure object in Belgorod, Russia
description: A Ukrainian drone strike damages a water infrastructure object at an inactive enterprise in the village of Krasnyi Oktyabr in Belgorod, Russia.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS34762

title: Ukrainian drone strikes damage water infrastructure in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian forces carry out drone strikes and shell an unknown target in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine. Water infrastructure is damaged during the attack.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR206245

title: Ukrainian drones strike oil pumping station in Krasnodar, Russia, damaging water tank
description: Ukrainian drones strike an oil pumping station in Krasnodar, Russia, damaging a water tank and disrupting operations.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS31836

title: Ukrainian shelling and drone strikes damage water treatment plant and injure three in occupied Horlivka, Ukraine
description: Ukrainian forces launch drone strikes and shell Russian separatist forces in occupied Horlivka, Donetsk. The attack injures three civilians and damages a water treatment facility.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. UKR206390

title: Unidentified gunmen open fire at water station military point in Deir ez-Zor, Syria
description: A Syrian Democratic Forces (QSD) military point in a water station in in rural Deir ez-Zor, Syria, is targeted by unknown assailants with machine guns. Casualties are unknown.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SYR141290

title: Unidentified hackers succeed in taking over a Norwegian dam's control systems, spilling millions of liters of water
description: In April 2025, unidentified hackers succeed in taking over a Norwegian dam's control systems, spilling millions of liters of water from the Lake Risevatnet Dam, near the city of Svelgen in Southwest Norway.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mous 2025

title: Violent clash erupts between villagers over land irrigation in Natore, Bangladesh, injuring at least 15
description: Residents of the Kadamkuri area of Natore, Bangladesh, clash with firearms in a dispute over the irrigation of a paddy field. At least 15 people are injured.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BGD30622

title: Violent dispute at waterpoint leads to death of woman in Rumbek, South Sudan
description: Five unidentified women suspected to be from an Agar Dinka clan attack a woman at a waterpoint in Rumbek, South Sudan. The victim, from another Agar Dinka clan, later dies from her injuries.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SSD14826

title: Violent protests over plans to divert Indus River water to Pakistan kill at least two and set a house on fire
description: At least two people are killed and other injured in massive protests in Sindh province, Pakistan over plans to divert Indus River water to Punjab. Protesters also attack and burn down the local minister's house.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Khan 2025

title: Water pipes and meters targeted in Lydenburg, South Africa
description: A number of businesses and households in Lydenburg, South Africa, have their water pipes and meters stolen or tampered with by unknown individuals.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Engelbrecht 2025

title: Water pipes set ablaze in demonstration over water tariff increase in Othaya, Kenya
description: Protesters storm the Othaya-Mukurweini Water Service Company compound in Othaya, Kenya, and set fire to water pipes in a demonstration over increased water tariffs. Police deploy tear gas to disperse the group.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN17377

title: Water rescue volunteer dies in arson attack on tent in Moscow Oblast, Russia
description: Unknown individuals set fire to a tent in a forest park in Dzerzhinskiy, Moscow Oblast, killing the man inside. The man had been volunteering with a group from a water rescue organization attempting to stop further construction work in the forest when his tent was targeted. The group accuses the local government of being behind the attack and a number of others.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS35525

title: Water stations are targeted by RSF drone strikes in Shuwak, Sudan
description: Water stations are targeted by Rapid Support Forces (RSF) drone strikes in Shuwak, Sudan. A number of civil defense personnel are injured trying to extinguish flames.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. SUD32915

title: Water supply infrastructure damaged by drone debris in Belgorod, Russia
description: Ukrainian forces carry out 41 drone strikes across the district of Valuyskiy in Belgorod, Russia. Part of a water supply system is damaged, likely caused by falling debris after 37 drones are shot down by Russian forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS32367

title: Water tower damaged by Ukrainian shelling in Belgorod, Russia
description: A water tower in the village of Terebreno in Belgorod, Russia, is damaged by shelling from Ukrainian forces.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. RUS31772

title: Water truck triggers improvised explosives in Tillaberi, Niger
description: An improvised explosive device planted by an armed group, likely JNIM (Salafi-jihadist group), explodes as a water truck passes near Mine de Samira in Gotheye, Tillaberi, Niger. The truck sustains minor damage; no casualties are reported.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. NIR31401

title: Water wells lose only power source after refrigeration unit damaged in Israeli strike in Khan Yunis, Palestine
description: A solar-powered refrigeration unit is damaged after being struck by Israeli artillery in the village of Qizan an-Najjar in Khan Yunis, Palestine. The damage disrupts the agricultural sector as the unit was the only source of power to water wells in the area.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. PSE73575

title: Woman murdered by armed group while fetching water in Atacora, Benin
description: An unidentified armed group slits the throat of a woman fetching water alone in the village of Nanagade in Atacora, Benin. Local residents find her body the following morning and alert police.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. BEN1732

title: Woman shot dead, child injured fetching water in Turkana, Kenya
description: Women and children fetching water from the Suguta River, Turkana, are ambushed by armed assailants. One woman is shot dead, while another woman and a boy sustain injuries. The attackers, thought to be Pokot militia, flee the area when police are called.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Raleigh et al. 2010 ID. KEN17441

headline: Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan Northern Aral Sea Restoration Treaty
title: Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan Northern Aral Sea Restoration Treaty
description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan finalize historic treaty guaranteeing minimum ecological flows into the Northern Aral Sea and joint Kokaral dam elevation.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Treaty on Transboundary Water Cooperation and Ecological Restoration of the Northern Aral Sea, Astana (2026).

headline: Mekong Commission Enacts Mainstream Dam Cascading Rules
title: Mekong Commission Enacts Mainstream Dam Cascading Rules
description: The MRC Council agrees on legally binding cascading flow release rules for upstream mainstream hydropower projects during El Nino drought periods.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Mekong River Commission (MRC) Joint Operational Protocol on Mainstream Cascading Hydropower and Flow Regulations, Vientiane (2026).

headline: Turkey-Iraq Operational Drought Protocol Signed
title: Turkey-Iraq Operational Drought Protocol Signed
description: Turkey and Iraq conclude operational drought protocol under the 2024 Framework Agreement, locking in guaranteed releases and digital hydrometric verification.
source: Pacific Institute Water Conflict Chronology; Operational Annexes to the Turkey-Iraq Framework Water Agreement for Severe Drought Periods, Baghdad (2026).
